It kept recalculating constantly. Honestly, it was more stressful than actually driving. I ended up relying on good old-fashioned map reading in the end. Remember those, George? Vividly. But at least you knew where you were with a map. This thing just wanted to take us to the middle of nowhere. And the language settings! I accidentally set it to Flemish once. Utterly pointless. Oh, that sounds dreadful. Have you considered upgrading? I just got a new phone, and the maps app on it is incredible. It even shows traffic updates in real-time. A new phone, eh?

Honestly, David, I’m not sure about this paprika. It’s a bit… assertive, isn’t it? It's overpowering the tomatoes. Assertive is good, Eleanor! A bit of spice livens things up. Remember that disastrous shepherd’s pie you made last year? No spice whatsoever. Like eating wallpaper paste. That was one time! And I was experimenting with a new recipe. This is supposed to be a simple Tuscan stew. Not a volcanic eruption in a pot. Are you  sure  you wouldn’t prefer I leave it out? No, no. Trust me. Just let it simmer. It'll mellow. Speaking of trusting people, have you seen what Fiona posted on Facebook? She's claiming she baked a three-tiered cake for her nephew’s birthday. Looks suspiciously like she bought it from Marks & Spencer, if you ask me. Oh, Fiona! Always trying to portray a perfect life. Honestly, the pretense some people engage in… It's exhausting. Speaking of exhausting, these roses from the market are looking a bit peaky. Should I put them in water with that flower food? Floralife, is it? Yes, definitely. Don’t want them drooping before guests arrive. Did you tell Sarah we're having them over on Saturday? I messaged her, but she didn't reply. Probably lost in that labyrinthine legal document she's working on. I did, but I’ll ping her again. It's rather lovely to have them over, isn't it? It feels like ages. I was thinking of lighting the fireplace on Saturday evening – a bit of autumn ambience, you know? Although, remembering last time, it took me a good hour to get it going and nearly set off the smoke alarm. I'll handle the fireplace this time. Promise. I've been watching those YouTube videos on proper kindling techniques. Turns out, you can't just shove any old wood in there and expect it to ignite. There's a… science to it. A science to kindling? Really, David? You're applying administrative precision to fire starting! I never thought I'd see the day. Hey, it's all about optimization. Less smoke, faster ignition, maximum coziness. Efficiency is key, El. Besides, your perfume is lovely tonight. What is it? Something floral? It’s a new one I got. "Midnight Bloom” by Jo Malone. It's supposed to be pear and freesia. It’s quite subtle, I thought.

Well, you see, back in my day, a good double-breasted suit screamed “power.” Especially in Manchester. You needed to look the part, even if you were just shuffling papers. It was all about projecting an image. My company, Harrison & Croft, we practically built our reputation on sharp dressing. We even had a tailor on contract, flew him out to Hong Kong regularly. Can you imagine? Extraordinary. I always found them rather… restricting. I preferred something a bit simpler, more comfortable. Not that dress codes were ever a big concern for me, of course. Teaching English to Japanese businessmen – they were far more concerned with getting the grammar right than looking like they'd stepped out of a Savile Row window. Aye, that's true enough. In Sheffield, we'd say, "Look sharp, but don't look like you're trying too hard." It's a subtle difference, int it? A Yorkshireman's elegance is understated. Not flash, like some of those Southerners! Southerners! Don’t get me started. They think they invented good tailoring. Proper Yorkshire steel, now  that's  quality. Speaking of quality, did you ever consider the financial implications of a trip like this, Margaret? Australia, that is. It's not cheap. No, it's not. I've been looking into it. A small bank loan, perhaps. Just enough to cover the flights and initial accommodation. My pension doesn't stretch quite far enough, and, well… things haven't been easy these last few years. A bank loan, eh? You should be careful with those, love. Interest rates are ripping people off something awful. I’ve seen colleagues bury themselves in debt trying to get ahead. What are you planning to do out there, Margaret? I was considering teaching, actually. Plenty of demand for experienced EFL teachers, especially in Queensland. Apparently, there’s a huge influx of Asian students. It could be a fresh start, you know? Somewhere warm, somewhere different. It’s just a pipe dream at the moment, really. Queensland! Beautiful part of the world. We’ve got a nephew living just north of Brisbane, fantastic weather. Though the snakes… you have to be careful of the snakes. They're surprisingly brazen. I remember young David got a bit too close to one once… nearly gave him a heart attack. Oh, the creatures! They’re everywhere, aren’t they? Similar to the pigeons in Sheffield, mind you.

Honestly, this is incredible! I didn't think vegan food could taste this…substantial. Poland surprised me, didn't it? Though, I’m still slightly baffled by the pierogi situation. Everything’s got cheese! It is rather lovely, isn't it? And yes, Poland is proving...interesting. A lot of cheese, definitely. It's a bit of a shock to the system after being so rigidly vegan for so long. Reminds me of trying to navigate a wedding buffet. Difficult. But back to pierogi, you know, I was trying to explain the concept of “comfort food” to a Romanian student the other day, and pierogi, in their traditional form, seemed to fit the bill perfectly. Oh, you were? That's a good point. I can see that. Though, for me, comfort food is a cheese toastie and a really, really strong cup of tea. Utterly calorific, obviously. Have you been following that new documentary on Netflix, ‘The Social Dilemma’? It's properly unsettling. Vaguely. I’ve been trying to reduce my screen time, you see. Part of a new…project. It’s already proving rather difficult. All the algorithms and persuasive design... It’s practically psychological warfare, isn’t it? I read something about it in  The Guardian  a while ago; something about dopamine loops and manipulative advertising. Right? It’s terrifying! They’re literally engineering addiction. I mean, I know it, logically, but it's still shocking to see it laid out so clearly. I've actually started setting timers on my phone for social media - 20 minutes max a day, and it  works . Eventually. The withdrawals are real though. I nearly threw my phone across the room yesterday. I can imagine. I confess, I’ve reverted to more…analog pursuits. I’ve started listening to podcasts again. Remember how we used to obsess over Serial? Oh my god, yes! I totally forgot about Serial! I was devastated when that wrapped up. I’ve been deep into ‘Crime Junkie’ recently. It’s a bit… sensationalist, perhaps, but I find it strangely comforting. Like, knowing things have gone horribly wrong for  other  people makes my life seem a little less chaotic, you know? A morbid sort of reassurance. I understand completely. I've been listening to ‘Stuff You Should Know’. It’s incredibly random, but fascinating. Last week it was the history of rubber ducks. Really quite diverting, actually. Do you ever feel… overwhelmed by everything?

Right, swimming lessons sorted for Saturday then. Pippy, are you excited? Yes! Can we build the thing on page 42, Mummy? The rocket! Dinosaurs need swimming lessons too! Rawr! Your dinosaur doesn’t need swimming lessons, Leo. Though, he might enjoy a splash. This rocket is ambitious, isn’t it? We'll need a lot of kitchen roll. Speaking of ambitious, Anon was telling me about her circus. Anon’s circus! Will the dancing elephant be there? I’m not sure about an elephant, darling, but apparently it's got acrobats and clowns and… a very talented poodle. Anon says it’s touring down near Cambridge next month. Fancy going? Poodle! Can I feed the poodle dinosaur snacks? No, Leo. Poodles don't eat dinosaur snacks. They eat… poodle food. We need to think about pictures first though, don’t we? For your Blue Peter badges. We promised we’d get them both done this weekend. I want a good picture! Not one where I’m making a funny face. Of course, darling. Serious face. Big smile. Right. And then, passports. We absolutely need to renew yours, Leo. It expired last year. Expired? Does that mean I can’t see the poodle? No, Leo, it doesn’t mean that. It just means we need to get a new little book with your picture in it. It’s a bit boring, I know. Right, let’s talk about pocket money. You've both been ever so helpful this week. Can I have five pounds? Please, Mummy? For the bits and bobs for the rocket? I want five pounds too! To buy a sparkly hat for the poodle! Alright, alright. Two pounds fifty each. And you can earn a little extra by helping me tidy up your toys. Anon mentioned she's teaching you both some new circus tricks too, hasn't she? She's teaching me to juggle! But it's really hard! The beanbags keep falling. I’m learning to balance on one leg! Like a flamingo! That’s brilliant! Anon’s really wonderful with you both, isn't she? It's lovely she’s agreed to babysit again next week. It’s just… her stories are sometimes a bit… unusual. Like the one about the Chinese who eat old eggs! Yes. That one was… a bit out there, wasn't it? Rest assured, darling, it’s not true. Don't go telling everyone you meet that Chinese people eat old eggs.

Right, so… you actually  said  that to Mark? Honestly, El? Well, yeah! What? He asked! He was being, you know… inquisitive. And I wasn’t going to lie to him. It’s important to be honest, isn't it? Honest about what, exactly? That your ex, five years ago, had… problems? It’s a bit of a bombshell to drop on a first almost-date, isn't it? I mean, love, you’re a southern softie, but sometimes you need to keep some things to yourself! Especially things that could make someone feel awkward. He wasn't awkward! He actually seemed… interested. He started asking questions about it. Like, what kind of problems? Did it affect… well, everything? Oh, bless. Mark. He’s a good lad, he genuinely is, but he’s a bit… literal. He probably just wanted to know if he'd be expected to, you know, perform some kind of circus act. Honestly, El, you're playing with fire. Don’t be mean! I just thought it was important for him to understand. He kept going on about how important communication is in a relationship. And this is part of that, right? Being open, even about difficult things. Aye, communication is important, lass. But there's a time and a place for everything. Dumping your past romantic backstory and medical history on someone before you’ve even had a proper cuppa is… not ideal. It feels a bit… overshare-y. So, what would you have done? Lied? That feels wrong. Not lied, exactly. Just… deflected. Said something like, "Oh, we all have our baggage, don’t we? Let’s focus on getting to know each other." You know, something light and fluffy. Like you Cambridge girls are good at. Okay, fair point. I’m not exactly known for my subtle social graces. But he seemed… genuinely concerned. He started researching it! That’s what freaked me out. He sent me a link to some article about erectile dysfunction! Oh, good grief! He  did ! That’s brilliant! Poor Mark. He probably thinks he’s got to become some kind of miracle worker. It’s not funny! It made me feel awful. Like I’d unknowingly burdened him with some kind of… responsibility. And his brother, Ben, got involved. Ben's a doctor, you know. He started giving Mark advice! Ben the know-it-all! I should have known. So, what did Ben say?

Honestly, I’m starting to feel like a walking Slimming World leaflet. Cauliflower cheese  and  roast dinner? It's a miracle we’re losing weight at all. It is a miracle, isn't it? But a delicious miracle. And hey, at least it’s healthier than takeaway. Did you manage to get any of the Hex A bars today? Those are my Healthy Extra this week. Managed to snag the last two! They were practically fighting over them at the pharmacy. People are serious about their Healthy Extras. I was thinking about having one with my tea. Speaking of tea, could you put the kettle on? Absolutely. Lemon and ginger? Or something more exciting? I'm feeling adventurous. Thinking about adding that 0 calorie syrup – raspberry is divine in tea. Though, you know, the artificial flavour still bothers me a bit. Don’t start with the artificial flavour lecture, please! It’s a small price to pay for a sweet cup of tea when you've been counting every single ‘syn’ all day. Did you check your syns for that granola this morning? It’s surprisingly high. You’re right to remind me. I forgot! Blast it. Okay, going to log it now… Right, logged. Speaking of syns, I was reading this article about how even seemingly ‘healthy’ foods can be packed with hidden sugars. It's madness. It makes you question everything. Tell me about it. I was looking at some Quorn mince the other day, and the seasoning mix they add in has more sugar than I thought. The supermarket ranges are getting better though, aren’t they? I genuinely think Tesco has the best Quorn selection now. Definitely. And have you tried those proper frozen veg boxes? The ones that deliver weekly? I put an order in last week and it was brilliant. Loads of stuff we wouldn’t normally buy - butternut squash, sprouting broccoli… got a massive bag of double peas in the freezer too - future dinners sorted! I've been thinking about that. Saving money is the main thing, isn't it? With tax coming up, and trying to save for a holiday… Oh, don't remind me about tax! It's looming. We need to get organised. Have you updated the calendar with ‘Treat Day’ Saturday? Cheesecake, definitely cheesecake is mandatory. Yep, it's in there. I even asked Siri to remind me. She’s being a bit glitchy today though.

Greece again? Seriously, Mark? We went last year. It was lovely, don’t get me wrong, but… But what? It was sun, sea, and olives. What's not to love? And they've got those amazing tavernas. Remember that moussaka we had in… what was that place called? Symi? Symi was wonderful, yes. But I was thinking… something different. Something a bit more… adventurous? I saw this documentary about Iceland. The landscapes were just incredible. Ice caves, geysers… Iceland? In October? You’ll need a parka and crampons, love. It’s not exactly beach weather. Remember the Algarve in February? We froze! Okay, fair point. But I’m just saying, a bit of adventure would be nice. We’ve been doing the “sun and sand” routine for years. I'm starting to feel like an automaton. Order a G&T, apply sunscreen, repeat. You’re being dramatic. I thought you enjoyed building those sandcastles with Chloe. She did, and it was lovely seeing her happy. But  I  need something more than sandcastles. Besides, she’s getting too old for sandcastles. She’s obsessed with history now. She wants to go to Rome. Rome, eh? Now you’re talking. Colosseum, the Forum… definitely beats shivering in Iceland. It wouldn't be quite the relaxing getaway, though. Think of the crowds! That's true. I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed by the thought of navigating Roman traffic. But perhaps… what about a writing retreat? Somewhere quiet, with stunning scenery? I’ve been meaning to actually  write  something for ages, you know. Finish that short story. A writing retreat? You? You barely have time to respond to emails from Mr. Hawthorne, let alone churn out prose. That's not entirely true! And it would be good for me. Just a week, somewhere remote. Imagine, just me, a laptop, and a view. No spreadsheets, no urgent requests for coffee, no… Mr. Hawthorne. Alright, alright. I see your point. A change of scenery  might  inspire you. Still, Rome’s tempting. We could get those little leather sandals Chloe's been eyeing up. You’re impossible. So, Rome or Iceland? Or... a tiny cottage in the Lake District? I saw one online with a fireplace and a window seat overlooking a lake… a perfect spot for a writer. Lake District? Too rainy. And full of sheep. Remember that time we went hill walking and got chased by a ram?

…and then Brenda said, "Are you  sure  you want haggis with custard?" I nearly choked on my whisky! Honestly, some people. It’s a national treasure, haggis! Brenda's palate evidently has...distinct preferences. The postcard, though, was lovely. That view from Skye… absolutely breathtaking. You really captured the light. A far cry from grey Nottinghamshire, wouldn’t you say? Aye, a world away. Though I do love a bit o' rain now and again – reminds me of home. So, weekends… have you given any thought to what we're doing? David’s birthday is looming, isn't it? He’ll be… what, fifteen? Seems like only yesterday he was building Lego castles. Indeed. Fifteen is a significant milestone. I was thinking we could do that escape room he's been desperate to try. "The Lost Pharaoh," I believe it's called. It's rather cleverly designed, apparently. Hmm, escape rooms. Not entirely my cup of tea, but if David wants it... Right. So, escape room Saturday afternoon. What about Saturday evening? I was thinking we could have a barbecue. The weather forecast looks reasonably promising. A barbecue sounds delightful, dear. Much better than another evening wrestling with his algebra homework. We could invite the Millers, couldn't we? Sarah and David get on so well. Excellent idea. I’ll give them a ring tomorrow. They’re having a bit of trouble with the new puppy, apparently. Chaos, pure chaos. Speaking of chaos… did you catch the latest polling figures on Scottish independence? I did, unfortunately. It seems considerably tighter than I’d hoped. It's unsettling, isn’t it? The potential ramifications for the entire Union... Unsettling is putting it mildly. It worries me, honestly. I grew up in a working-class mining town – Harworth. We relied on the stability the Union offered. The thought of Scotland pulling away… it feels like a fragmentation of everything. Precisely. Although, one could argue that the current Union  is  inherently unstable, given the way Westminster has treated Scotland over the years. The oil revenues have certainly complicated matters. It's a complex political landscape. Aye, complex alright. But fundamentally, I think a fractured Union is a weaker one. For everyone. What about Sunday? Just thinking ahead. I was hoping we could finally tackle that overgrown rose bed in the front garden. It's become a jungle. Oh, the rose bed. A project I've been strategically avoiding.

Right, so I’ve sketched out a basic chair shape here. Not brilliant, I know. It's proving harder than I thought to convey 'chair-ness' effectively. Do you think it looks… chair-y, Leo? It looks like a squiggly! Can it fly, Mummy? No, darling, it’s not a flying squiggly. It’s meant to be a chair. For people who don't have one. Remember we talked about the Syrian refugees? They've lost everything, haven't they? Lost… houses? Yes, sweetheart. Lost their houses, their toys, sometimes their families. And they need chairs. This charity, "Helping Hands," wants us to draw pictures of chairs – simple ones – for them to use in their welcome packs. They give these packs to families arriving in the UK. A visual representation, they said, to show them we're thinking of them. Why not just  give  them chairs? That’s a very good question, love. And of course, they need real chairs! But it's a way to show kindness and support. It’s about showing we care, even if it’s a small thing. Leo, help me think. What  kind  of chair would be good? A big one! Like for giants! Giants, right. Not quite, darling. Something practical. What about a wooden chair? Like at Grandma’s? Like the one I sit on to eat my dinner! But with stripes! Stripes are brilliant! Colourful chairs would be lovely. Maybe we could draw a few different kinds. A wooden one, like you said, Elodie. And one with cushions - a comfy armchair! It needs legs! It’s just… a seat! You're absolutely right! Good eye, Leo. Need to add legs! See? I knew I needed your expert chair design skills. It's harder than it looks. School today was a bit… stressful. They’ve announced a mock exam next week. It's all about fractions, which frankly, I'm not sure even I fully understand! Tests are silly. I don’t like tests. I know, sweetheart. Adults don’t always like tests either! It's just something we have to do sometimes. Right, back to chairs. What about a rocking chair? Would that be helpful? No! It will fall over! Good point! Maybe not. See? You're a lifesaver, Leo. Okay, simple, sturdy, wooden chairs then. And maybe a colourful armchair for when they want to relax. It's a nice thought to brighten their day, isn't it?

Honestly, I’m starting to feel like everyone we know is either pregnant, has a baby, or is actively trying. It's relentless. Remember when we were the "young and free" couple, scoffing at the whole baby thing? Vaguely. It feels like a different lifetime, doesn't it? Though I don’t think we scoffed  that  much. Just…prioritised academic freedom. Which, let’s be honest, feels slightly ridiculous now. Sarah just texted about her scan. Looks like it’s definitely a girl. A girl! That's wonderful for them. And slightly terrifying for me. Another female force in our orbit. She’ll probably be lecturing me on sustainable living within five years. You’ll survive. And you'll be a brilliant Uncle. Honestly, have you seen the photo of Mark and Chloe’s little Leo? He’s already trying to climb out of his highchair. Total chaos, but utterly adorable. Leo is a menace, I'm convinced. Chloe looked utterly exhausted last time I saw her, bless her. She was talking about sleep regression and the existential dread of baby-led weaning. It sounded…challenging. Makes my grading load seem positively luxurious. True, marking essays on Dickens is significantly less stressful than navigating the complexities of purée consistency. Although, I had a particularly insightful one today - a student actually connected the themes of social injustice in  Great Expectations  to contemporary housing policy. Really made me think. See? That's the joy of teaching. A little spark of genuine understanding. It's worth the madness. Did you manage to get through the Henderson submissions? Those were brutal. Just about. Henderson's always a struggle. He just doesn't grasp the nuance. I think I’ll have to schedule a one-on-one with him. Sometimes they just need that little nudge, that targeted feedback. How's your Medieval History seminar going? Are they still debating the legitimacy of the Angevin Empire? You know it! They're locked in a constant battle of interpretation. It’s actually quite engaging, in a frustrating sort of way. I’m thinking of assigning them some articles on postcolonial theory and see how they react. Ooh, risky. But potentially brilliant. You’ll unleash a week of passionate arguments, I suspect. Don't let them overrun your office hours though. They'll be camped there all day. I’ll need reinforcements. Maybe a strategically placed sign saying “Quiet Zone - Angevin Empire Discussions Strictly Prohibited.”

Honestly, the sheer terror on Mrs. Higgins’ face when she thought I was going to hex her prize-winning marrow… priceless. Absolutely priceless. You  did  sort of set her up, didn't you? Bringing up all that folklore about warding off slugs with rosemary and then dramatically sprinkling it around her vegetable patch… It was for comedy, darling! A bit of lighthearted fun. She needs to lighten up. She’s obsessed with those marrows. It's bordering on unhealthy. And the village fete judges are probably terrified of her. Well, they should be. She’s won for the last five years running. I think she’s got a deal going with the local garden centre or something. The size of those things… defies logic. Exactly! It’s all a conspiracy. Anyway, it reminded me of that time we were kids and I convinced old Mr. Peterson that wearing a hat inside would bring bad luck. He spent the entire summer indoors! Oh, you were a menace! You and your superstitious nonsense. Remember when you tried to convince me that policemen were actually disguised fairies? They  looked  suspicious! All in dark uniforms and observing everything. Perfectly believable, really. Besides, you bought it, didn't you? For a good week, you were constantly looking over your shoulder, terrified they were going to turn into pixies and steal your sweets. I was eight! And you were terrifyingly persuasive. It was around the same time you insisted on throwing salt over your shoulder every time you spilled something, to ward off evil spirits. It worked! I never had any bad luck after that. Coincidence, obviously. But still. It’s interesting, isn’t it, how these beliefs stick around? Even in a modern, supposedly rational society. It is. I was reading an article for my folklore module – ironically enough – about how superstitions actually serve a purpose. They give people a sense of control in a world that often feels chaotic. Right. Like Mrs. Higgins feeling she can control the weather and the slugs with her rosemary ritual. It's…affirming. Speaking of chaotic, did you hear about the entire debacle with Professor Davies and the university newsletter? Don't even start. The publicity team really put their foot in it, didn't they? Running that picture of him looking utterly bewildered in his Hawaiian shirt at the departmental summer party? They claimed it was meant to be “accessible” and “friendly” to prospective students.

Honestly, Dad, this new phone update is awful. Everything’s moved around. I can't even find the camera quickly anymore! It’s so frustrating when they “improve” things and it just makes it more difficult. A new phone, eh? Fancy that. These things are all too complicated for me, love. Just want to be able to ring people and that's about it. Remember when a phone was just a phone? All dials and a cord stretching halfway across the room? Simpler times, that was. They really were! Anyway, I was thinking about it… moving house is going to be a nightmare. We absolutely  need  to get a van. Have you started looking into quotes? Quotes? Not yet, no. Been a bit busy, you know. Fixing this old boat. Found it in the attic, belonged to your grandad. He was a keen fisherman, he was. Used to take us all down to Margate. Lovely day out, that was. Remember the fish and chips? Vaguely. I mostly remember getting sand everywhere! Right, van then. I was looking at some online, and it looks like about £300-400 for a day. A bit steep, isn’t it? Maybe we could ask Uncle Barry if he'd be willing to lend his. Barry? He’s always got some contraption or another. Probably wouldn't fit all your bits and bobs in his little thing. Besides, he'd want a tenner an hour for it, wouldn't he? Cheeky devil. Best to get a proper van, I reckon. What about that Great Dorset Steam Fair? Fancy going this year? They've got some proper antiques there - might be a bargain to be had. The Steam Fair! I’d love to, Dad! It’s been ages. But moving is taking up all my time and energy. We need to prioritize, you know? I was thinking, maybe we could get the whole family together for a Sunday roast once we’re settled in the new place? Mum's been saying she misses everyone. A Sunday roast… that’s a good idea. Your sister, Sarah, might be busy though. She's always playing those computer games, y’know. Consumes her whole life, it does. Don’t know what they’re all about, space ships and whatnot. Give your brain a rest, eh? I play them too, sometimes! It’s a nice way to unwind. But yeah, we’ll have to see about Sarah.

Honestly, Eleanor, this council… they’re unbelievable. Demolishing the library? It's a bloody disgrace. A Victorian building, Eleanor! A  Victorian  building! I know, David. It’s just… short-sighted, isn’t it? What are they going to put there instead? Another bland block of flats? It’ll ruin the character of the whole area. I signed the petition, of course, but I doubt it’ll make a difference. It has to make  some  difference. We need to rally people. I was thinking of writing to the local paper, highlighting the architectural significance. Did you see that article about the old mill down in Bramblewood? They’re insisting on keeping the facade, preserving the original stonework. It’s a good precedent. I did, yes. That was encouraging. Though I suspect Bramblewood has a lot more money floating around than we do. Still, we have to try. This library… I practically grew up in that library. Remember all those rainy Saturdays? Of course. You were always buried in some fantastical novel. Me, I was trying to avoid homework. Seems a lifetime ago. Still, it's more than just memories, Eleanor. It provides a vital service. Think about the children, the pensioners… Where will they go? Exactly. And what about the history? It's not just the building itself, it's the stories held within those walls. I was just transcribing some old parish records the other day, fascinating stuff about families who lived here centuries ago. Imagine that all being lost. Right. Speaking of losing things, are you still wrestling with that upholstery fabric for the armchair? You've had about twenty swatches out this evening. I am! It’s proving surprisingly difficult. I want something that feels… comforting. Something that will last. I’m leaning towards this, but the colour is a little bold, don't you think? Perhaps too… 80s? Teal can work. It depends on the light. And the cushions you use. Don't go too matchy-matchy. A bit of contrasting texture would be good. We saw that lovely linen at the market last weekend, remember? Yes, but that was incredibly expensive! And I’m trying to be sensible with the budget. Although, I did see a peculiar article online... about financing home improvements through crowdfunding. Have you heard of it? Crowdfunding for an armchair? Now that  is  a new one! Seriously though, I am familiar. It's becoming quite popular.

Honestly, Dad, you’re playing Abba again? It’s Christmas Eve! Can’t we have  something  a bit more… festive? Like, I don't know… Mariah Carey? Festive? This  is  festive, darling. Abba are timeless. Besides, it’s a good backdrop for present-wrapping. Keeps the mood light. Speaking of which, have you wrapped yours yet, Chloe? Nearly finished, Dad. Just proofreading a last-minute edit. This article on the resurgence of vinyl records is surprisingly compelling. It’s a bizarre little niche hobby, isn't it? Collecting physical media in the age of streaming. Vinyl, eh? My nephew’s gone completely mad for it. Says it's about the sound quality, the ritual. Makes you feel connected to the music. Got him a fancy turntable for his birthday, actually. Cost me a pretty penny. Sounds expensive! I've been thinking about getting back into painting. I used to love it at school, but haven’t really touched a brush since. Just feels like something relaxing to do away from the salon. That's wonderful, Chloe! You always had a good eye. Remember that watercolour you did of the lavender fields in Provence? Absolutely stunning. You should definitely pursue it. Provence? That sounds amazing. I'm itching to travel. I’ve been slogging away at work, proofreading endless articles, my brain feels completely fried. A proper holiday is desperately needed. Well, Sarah, you deserve one! Long hours, all that screen time… you’ll need to unwind. Any particular destinations in mind? Honestly? Anyplace warm. Somewhere with sunshine and good food. Maybe Italy? Or Greece? I've been researching some tiny, secluded islands. Ooh, Greece! That sounds idyllic. Painting landscapes overlooking the sea… you'd be in your element. I'm dreaming of a beach somewhere sun-drenched. I’ve got loads of clients booking blow dries for New Year's Eve, it’s going to be mad. Speaking of New Year's... have you two decided what you’re doing? We’re thinking a small gathering at home, just close family. Perhaps a bit of charades after dinner. Charades sounds good. Though I suspect I'll be utterly hopeless. I’m notorious for getting the clues wrong. Last Christmas, I spent ten minutes trying to mime ‘The Godfather.’ Utter chaos. I remember that! You were practically performing a one-man opera. Maybe we should just skip charades then? Though, watching Dad attempt to act… that's entertainment in itself.

Right, that's it! Absolutely ridiculous. £1800 a year to insure this thing? Are they having a laugh? Now, now, lad. Don't get yer knickers in a twist. It's a powerful car, a lovely car, mind, but it’s a powerful car. Insurance ain't free, is it? But Mum! It’s near on the price of a used Fiesta! And a Fiesta’s, like, a grandma car. I’m seventeen, I need something… sporty. Sporty doesn’t pay the bills, does it? An' sporty attracts more attention, more accidents. Remember what yer dad always says, “Keep it sensible, lad, keep it sensible.” He was right about most things, tha knows. Dad’s not here to say anything! And he drove a Rover P6! Hardly exactly a speed demon. Aye, he did. But he kept it on the road, didn’t he? Now, let’s have a look at this quote properly. Which company were ye lookin’ at? Elephant. They seemed to have the lowest initial quote online. Elephant, eh? Alright. Did ye put your details in properly? Honest mileage? No dodgy habits like… frequent late-night drives with the engine roarin’? Mum! I’m a responsible driver. Well, mostly. I mean, I’ve only stalled it twice this week. Twice? That’s a bit more than “mostly responsible,” isn’t it? Now, tha know, honesty’s the best policy with these things. They’re clever, these insurance companies. They’ll find out if yer fibbin’. Okay, okay, I might have added a few miles less than I actually do. It was just… a little bit. A little bit ain't good enough, love. It’s fraud, basically. They’ll penalise you, or worse, cancel your policy. And then where will you be? Walkin'? Fine, fine. I’ll put the real mileage in. But it’s still extortionate! Tha needs to look at different options. Have ye tried comparison sites? Confused.com, GoCompare, that kind of thing? Yeah, I did. They all come up with about the same price. I thought about adding me as a named driver on Dad’s car, but he said no. He's right to, to be fair. It’d bump up his premium too. An’ addin’ a seventeen-year-old driver, even a grandkid with a good head on their shoulders, will always cost. We could… well, I could maybe get a quote through my work, see if we can get a corporate discount.

This curry's… okay. Bit dry, innit? Okay? Liam, it’s from Happy Dragon. It’s  always  okay. It's consistently okay. The chicken’s always a bit… rubbery, isn't it? Like they've been keeping it in the freezer too long. Honestly, Colin, it’s perfectly fine. Don’t be so picky. At least we’re eating together. Things have been a bit hectic lately. Hectic is an understatement, Siobhan. My boss is breathing down my neck about this new server migration. It's just relentless. I swear, the stress levels are through the roof. I feel like I’m going to explode. I keep catching myself grinding my teeth. What even is a server migration? Sounds boring. Boring for you, maybe. It's moving all our company’s data to a new system. Millions of emails, files… everything. If it goes wrong, well, let’s just say I’ll be looking for a new job. You should try some mindfulness, love. Even ten minutes a day can make a difference. I’ve been listening to a podcast about it, actually. Quite calming. Mindfulness? Siobhan, I’m chasing fire extinguishers half the time. Mindfulness doesn’t exactly fit into the schedule. Though… I suppose you’re right. I just feel so… responsible. It's a scary thing, this partnership. Everything relies on it. Partnership? You two aren’t married, are you? Mom, are you and Uncle Colin getting married? Not quite, Liam. ‘Partnership’ in Colin's world means his IT business is doing well – relies on him, you see? He feels a big responsibility to it. It’s a figure of speech. Exactly. And it's a massive responsibility. Especially with everything happening here in Ireland. Did you hear about the vote? The equality vote? You mean… about the gay marriage thing? Yeah, I read about it. It was a landslide, wasn't it? It was. A real show of progress. Proof that things  can  change. Makes me hopeful, you know? Keeps me going. Sometimes, when I’m drowning in spreadsheets, I think about how far things have come. It's beautiful, isn't it? The whole country got behind it. So much more tolerant now than when I was a child. Do you think everyone’s really tolerant, though? Or just saying they are? That’s the tricky bit, isn’t it? Surface-level acceptance versus genuine understanding.

Speaker_1 trailed off, gesturing emphatically with a hand. "Aye, sounds like old Mr. Henderson. Always was a bit peculiar, that one. Though I can't say I blame him entirely, pigeons are a menace. Right, Liam, put your phone away, love. Your mum's talking.” "I was just checking the football scores, Mum. Man U lost. Again." "Lost? Already? Well, that’s hardly surprising, is it? They haven’t had a decent keeper since Gordon Banks. Anyway, talking about losing things… did anyone else follow that story about the nudist colony down in Cornwall?" “You’re having a laugh, aren’t you? A nudist colony? What's Cornwall doing with a nudist colony, eh? Sounds proper wild!" "Don't you go encouraging him, Elodie. It's just a bit of news. Reminds me of that documentary Terry Wogan used to host, about unusual places to live. He'd be missed this year, wouldn’t we." "He would. Anyway, the point is, they lost a rather valuable painting. Apparently, a Constable. Stolen right from under the noses of the… well, the unclothed residents. Police are baffled." “Maybe a bear got it, like Bear Grylls. He could have climbed in and snagged it. He’s good at that sort of thing, surviving and stealing stuff.” "Liam, you're being ridiculous! Bear Grylls wouldn’t steal a Constable. Besides, he’d be freezing his bits off in Cornwall. Speaking of freezing, this weather’s getting a right cheek, innit? Proper proper gloomy. Should’ve waited another week for this trip to the Lakes." "It’ll be fine, pet. A bit of drizzle never hurt anyone. Remember that time we went to Hawkshead when you were little, Liam? Absolutely pouring rain, but we still had a grand time exploring the village. Lovely little place, Hawkshead. All those cobbled streets..." “Hawkshead’s nice, yes. Though I still think the drive through the Dales is far more impressive. You get a real sense of scale, don’t you? It’s just… different when you’re used to London. Everything feels so… flat." "Flat? London’s alright, I suppose. But give me a proper hill anytime. You can see for miles from up there. You know, it makes you think about how far a mile actually  is , doesn't it? All these kilometers and miles mixed up... it’s confusing." "Aye, it is. And then they try to get you with them grams and kilograms.

…and honestly, the texture was…weird. Like, convincingly meat-like, but  weird . I tried that cultured chicken thing last week, remember? It was in that article I sent you, Elara. Yeah, vaguely. I remember you being very dramatic about it. Was it awful? You’re always so intense when you try new food. Not awful! Just… unsettling. It made me think about how much we take for granted, you know? Like, we just assume meat is  this  thing we can always get, but it’s all so… artificial. It’s fascinating and terrifying at the same time. It's progress, though, isn't it? Less reliance on actual animals. I mean, look at the environmental impact of cattle farming alone. It's monstrous. I agree with that. The environmental thing is huge. But still, the idea of eating something grown in a lab… it just feels… wrong, somehow. Almost like some dystopian sci-fi film. But is it  more  wrong than the current system? Think about those factory farms, Elara! The sheer cruelty… the confinement... It’s oppression on a scale we can barely comprehend. It’s practically medieval. They’re sentient beings suffering for our convenience. I know, I know. Animal cruelty is awful. That’s why I’m vegetarian, obviously. It just feels like a different kind of disconnect with synthetic meat. At least with a carrot, you know where it came from. You can  see  the plant. True. But think about hunting as opposed to abattoirs. One's a quick kill in a natural environment, the other is mass processing, anxiety, dread, and a completely unnatural death. Surely cultured meat could be a step closer to the former, ethically speaking. Exactly! And imagine a world where we don't  need  to raise and slaughter animals. Think of the land liberated. We could rewild massive areas. Okay, you're painting a very pretty picture. I’m still not sure I’m sold, but I can see the potential. What about the nutrients, though? I always worry about getting enough B12 and iron. That's where the vitamin tablets come in! We’re all pretty diligent about those, right? I've been taking that algae-based B12 supplement; it's surprisingly good. You’re the only one who actually  likes  taking supplements, Jamie! I feel like a science experiment whenever I swallow those things. I tend to forget. I probably need to set a reminder on my phone.

Honestly, this film's rubbish. Absolute dross. What even  is  the point? Aye, it's a bit slow, isn't it? But I’m enjoying relaxin’ after lectures. At least it's quiet. No lads from halls shoutin’ their heads off tonight. Quiet’s good. My head's still poundin' from that history seminar. Professor Davies goes on and on about the Treaty of Versailles like it's the most exciting thing ever. Versailles? Sounds boring. I’d rather be playing FIFA. You wouldn’t believe the deal I got on a new controller online. Proper bargain, that was. Twenty quid off! Twenty quid? Where’d you find that? I'm needing a new one, mine's on its last legs. Keeps driftin’ on me. Amazon. Spent ages lookin’. Had to go through loads of dodgy websites first. You know how it is. Always gotta be careful online, full of scammers. Used a voucher, too – remember me mum’s birthday this year, remember! Oh, you saved your money for an Amazon voucher. Very selfless. Speaking of birthdays, have you two thought about Mum’s Christmas present yet? It’s creeping up fast. Christmas already? Feels like I just finished taking the decorations down last year. I was thinkin’ about gettin' her that fancy electric blanket she’s been lookin’ at. Good shout, that. She’ll love that. Keeps her warm, especially with the heating bein’ what it is these days. I’m still stuck. Maybe a new phone cover? She’s always droppin' hers. She needs a whole new phone, honestly. Hers is older than all of us combined. I was lookin’ at some flights to Gran Canaria online. Thought we could all go for a week over Christmas. Just a little sunshine to brighten things up. Gran Canaria? That’d be brilliant! Uni probably won't let me off that much, mind. Got exams in January. Gotta knuckle down, I suppose. Though sunshine... tempting. Really tempting. Flights are expensive though, aren’t they? Plus, I haven't been doin' much. Struggling to even pay for train fare down to the job centre, let alone a holiday. Don't be like that, Liam. We'll figure something out. We always do. It'd be good for you to get away, honestly. A bit of sun might do you good. Clear your head. Aye, Liam. You need a break. You’ve been wearin’ the same jumper for a week straight.

…and then the pigeon just landed right on his head! Full-on, gray fluff and cooing. Honestly, Dad's face was priceless. He looked like he’d seen a ghost. Oh, bless him! My Gran would’ve sworn it was a sign. You know how she is. Every bird, every cloud, it’s all got some deep meaning. Did you manage to get a picture? Of course! Instant family classic. I’ve already sent it to Aunt Carol. She’s threatening to get it printed onto a mug. You know how obsessed she is with photo gifts. So, how was your family’s trip to Italy, then? You were raving about it beforehand. Venice, wasn't it? It was  incredible . Absolutely breathtaking. The canals, the architecture… completely lived up to the hype. Mum was in her element, snapping photos of everything. Dad, predictably, complained about the heat. He just doesn't do 'romantic European getaway.’ Though, even he had to admit the gondola ride was something special. Sounds lovely! We need to do something like that. My parents are talking about maybe going to Greece next year. Just a relaxed beach holiday, nothing too adventurous. Greece would be brilliant. We should all try and synchronize holidays sometime. It would be so good to all be together, wouldn't it? Though coordinating three families is proving to be a logistical nightmare, even for someone like me who’s used to managing complex data sets! Tell me about it. Trying to schedule a simple Sunday lunch with them feels like negotiating a peace treaty. Right, back to work, I suppose. Alumni Day has been surprisingly busy this year. The Head of the Faculty gave a really interesting talk this morning about the expansion of legal aid. Oh, really? I missed that – I was stuck in a meeting about updating our linguistic databases. Thrilling stuff, as you can imagine. What are you working on at the moment, beyond keeping the alumni happy? Anything exciting? We’re starting a new project looking at the impact of social media on legal language. Apparently, the way lawyers communicate online is vastly different from formal court documents. It’s fascinating, actually, seeing how much jargon gets simplified, or completely replaced with emojis. Emojis! That’s brilliant! We could incorporate that into our linguistic analysis framework. It would give us a really unique insight into how language evolves in professional settings.

Honestly, Liam, I’m ready to chuck my laptop out the window. This Modernist Literature module is killing me. Killing me, I tell ya! Dramatic, much, Maisie? You've only got three essays left. And you were banging on about Virginia Woolf last week, practically quoting her at the dinner table. That was  last  week! Now I’m wrestling with Joyce’s stream of consciousness and it's like trying to grab smoke. I read a paragraph five times and still don’t know what the blooming heck is going on. Professor Davies keeps saying it's about 'finding the underlying anxieties of post-war society' but all I find is a headache. Okay, okay. What's giving you the most trouble specifically? Maybe I can…attempt to decipher it. I did a whole module on literary theory, remember? Though, mostly about the Romantics, I'll admit. Still, some principles are universal. You and your literary theory! Always throwing those big words around. It's this bit in  Ulysses  where he’s…wandering around Dublin, I think? And he’s thinking about… bread? And then about his dead mother? It’s just…random. Utterly random! Right, the Lestrygonians’ episode. It  seems  random at first, but Joyce is layering in symbolism. The bread represents… well, it’s complicated. But it's linked to sustenance, to survival. And his mother, naturally, is tied to themes of loss and dependency. See? Not just random. It’s clever! Clever and confusing. I need something to ease my brain after this. Fancy getting a massage? I saw a place online, 'Serene Hands' or summat. They do student discounts. Foot and back massage would be heavenly right now. A massage does sound good. My back's been playing up something fierce since I’ve been trying to finish this research paper. But haven't you just spent all your student loan on that vintage coat? It was a bargain! And I deserve a treat. Honestly, Liam, you’re so stingy sometimes. Besides, think of it as an investment in my academic performance. A relaxed mind is a focused mind, right? That's a new one. Alright, alright, you've twisted my arm. But you're paying for my coffee afterwards. And don’t go booking the full works, mind. We’re on a student budget, remember? Deal! So, Serene Hands it is. Book it for Saturday? Saturday afternoon?

Right, everyone, lunch is served! I made a big batch of this Mediterranean salad – lots of cucumber, tomatoes, feta, olives… hopefully that's to everyone’s taste. Smells alright, love. Bit light on the meat though, isn't it? A man needs protein, you know. Though, I suppose that’s asking a lot these days with prices the way they are. Oh, Colin, you’re always complaining about the lack of meat. It’s a salad, not a Sunday roast! Besides, it’s good for you. And I brought that sourdough bread from the bakery – still warm! Exactly! It's about balance, Dad. And I promise, there's chicken skewers for dessert – I marinated them in lemon and herbs. Chicken skewers... that's more like it. Though, seeing as we're talking about prices, I saw something in the paper this morning about the migrant crisis over in Calais. Dreadful state of affairs, isn't it? It is heartbreaking. The conditions those people are living in… it’s absolutely appalling. And the rhetoric around it, too. It’s just… awful. They’re trying to create a bigger fence, apparently. A taller one. Which feels like solving a problem with more walls, you know? It's just pushing it further down the line. I keep thinking about those children. How are they supposed to have a decent life? Used to be, there were proper solutions. People helped each other. Now it’s all about borders and bureaucracy. Back in my day… well, things were different. Colin, dear, “back in your day” often involves a selective memory. Things weren't always better for everyone. And focusing on what  was  doesn’t help these people  now . What do you think we can  do , realistically? I've been looking into donating to some of the charities that work directly with the refugees there. Small amounts, consistently. It feels like a drop in the ocean, but… A drop in the ocean's better than nothing, I suppose. Still, the politicians... they're all the same, aren't they? Promise the world, deliver nothing. Let's not get into a political argument over lunch, eh? It’ll ruin the appetite. How’s Amelia doing with her exams, Sarah? She’s actually doing really well! Finished her mock exams last week. Her Biology paper was brilliant, apparently. She's thinking of applying for Oxford. Oxford, eh? Fancy that.

Honestly, Alun, this whole bathroom renovation has been a complete and utter fiasco. A fiasco, I tell you! I thought, you know, having lived in London for so long, I'd be accustomed to the…challenges of coordinating tradespeople. Turns out, dealing with London builders is like herding cats. Aye, I can imagine. London builders have a reputation, don’t they? Tredegar lads are a different breed. More straightforward, you see. Less… flair. More getting the job done. What’s gone wrong, then? Leaky pipes? Wrong tiles? All of the above, actually! The tiler insisted on this incredibly obscure pattern – he called it 'wave-like contemporary' – and it looks more like a child has thrown noodles at the wall. And the plumber...don't even get me started on the plumber. He promised, explicitly, that he’d install a rainfall showerhead. Rainfall! I pictured a gentle cascade. What I got was a jet engine. My wife nearly took out the mirror. A jet engine, you say? Good heavens! That  is  a bit dramatic. Rainfall showerheads can be tricky, though. Need proper pipework, you see. I had a similar issue with Dewi, a friend of mine, when he put one in at his daughter's place. Had to call in a specialist. Did you get any quotes for the initial work? Of course! I’m not entirely naive. But everything is dependent on the previous stage being completed, naturally. And each stage is perpetually delayed. And the bill…well, let’s just say it’s significantly exceeding the initial estimate. It’s making me reconsider my entire approach to home decorating. I was thinking of redoing the kitchen next, a nice, minimalist design… but now? Now I’m seriously contemplating just leaving everything as it is. I understand that feeling perfectly. We had a nightmare with the kitchen extension a few years back. The joiner – Gareth, a lovely man but… a bit optimistic about deadlines – kept adding “little details" he thought would be nice. Eventually, the whole thing was three months overdue and cost a fortune. My wife, Bronwen, nearly had kittens. "Little details"? That's exactly it! This tiler kept suggesting different shades of grey. Grey! As if my bathroom needed more grey. It's supposed to be a sanctuary, a place of relaxation. Not a monochrome study in despair. Bronwen is a stickler for colour. She turned our hall a shade of teal that nearly blinded the postman.

Right then, who’s feeling brave enough for another one? That Vindaloo was a proper kick in the teeth, wasn't it? Nearly took the wallpaper off. Yeah! It was amazing! Could feel it right down to my toes, Mr. O'Connell. It was, like, intense. Intense is one word for it, Liam. I'm fairly certain I can still feel the heat radiating from my throat. I’m sticking with water, thanks. Maybe a tiny bit of vanilla ice cream later. Goo! Goo! He wants more curry, the little scamp. Doesn't seem to have a pain receptor in his system at all. I swear, he'd eat a tin of nails, wouldn't he, Oran? Seriously? You think he’d eat metal? That’s, like, a superpower! Super-stomach! Don’t encourage him, Finn. He’ll be trying to chew the radiator next. Besides, we’ve already established he’s not going to be a superhero. He’s more of a pint-sized tornado of chaos. True enough. Though a bit of super strength wouldn't go amiss, particularly when wrestling him into his pajamas. Thinking about superpowers… remember that article I read about bio-luminescence? Natural, you know, in jellyfish and fireflies? Imagine having that! No need for candles! Dude, that would be epic! Like, you could just glow in the dark! Perfect for sneaking out. Finn! Absolutely not. And Liam, dear, let's focus on birthday arrangements, shall we? Oran's turning five next month, and I'm completely overwhelmed. Do we stick with the park again? It was lovely last year, but… The park’s grand. Good space to run around. We could look at getting one of those bouncy castles. A bit pricey, mind you. Speaking of pricey, I was thinking of getting a little something stashed away for Oran’s future. Maybe invest in a… night deposit box. A bit old-fashioned, I know, but safer than keeping it under the mattress. A night deposit box? That's like, straight out of a heist movie! Do you think we’d need a getaway car? Finn, honestly! Liam's just trying to be responsible. Although, I do remember my grandfather had one. Said it was the safest place for his savings during the war. All a lot of drama, as it turns out, because the bank was robbed anyway. Horrible history, isn’t it? Aye, it is.

"Fractions, eh? Never did get the hang of them myself. Always preferred a nice bit of practical work. You know, fixing things. That was always my forte." "Now, Arthur, don’t go starting on about that shed again. Remember last Christmas? The whole thing ended up collapsing under a pile of tinsel and fairy lights." "It weren't the tinsel's fault, Brenda, it were a dodgy beam! Should’ve known. Should’ve checked it proper. Costessey weather, you know. Damp gets into everything." "Right then. Halloween. My Year 8s were obsessed, absolutely obsessed. One kid brought in a rubber spider the size of his hand. Sent Mrs. Peterson into a right state, she did. Kept shrieking." "Said it reminded her of something from a horror movie." "It was so cool, though! We’ve been planning our costumes for weeks. I'm going as a spooky rider, you know? Like, a ghost on a horse.” "A spooky rider? That sounds lovely, dear. Are you still going riding lessons, then? Miss that little pony of yours." "Yeah! Rosie’s getting so much better. She used to be really skittish, but now she's really calm. I’m teaching her some new jumps. It’s hard work, but it’s worth it.” "Horses are good for you, girl. Good company. Quiet. Unlike some people I know." "Oh, hush you. You're just jealous you can’t get on and off anymore. Remember when you tried to ride Mr. Henderson's prize-winning Shire? That was a sight to behold!" "That was a long time ago, Brenda. And I nearly did it! Just a bit of a stumble. Henderson wouldn't let me back on, though. Said I weren’t ‘suited’ to a Shire horse." "Talking about places, have you all been to that new café down by the river in Norwich? ‘The Willow’s Nest’ it’s called. Excellent scones. Honestly, some of the best I've had in years." "Oh yeah! We went there after the school fair last week. Their hot chocolate is amazing. They have these little marshmallows on top." "Sounds lovely, John. Maybe we should all go next weekend. A bit of a treat. We could do with it." “Might be a bit much for me, Brenda. My knees aren’t what they used to be, you know. All that walking around…" “You could sit and relax, Grandad. I’ll do the walking.

Honestly, this traffic is ridiculous! I thought coming this early would avoid the worst of it, but look at this queue. It’s barely moving. Aye, it's always like this going to the Steam Fair. Been coming for, must be, forty years now. You youngsters never twig, do ya? Takes time, these things. Patience, love. Patience. Tell me about it, David. I was almost late getting here, thanks to a flooded road near Harlow. Honestly, the council needs to get a grip on the drainage. At least the radio’s on, eh? Drainage is a nightmare, Mum’s right. It’s not just Harlow, is it? Everywhere seems to be crumbling. Speaking of crumbling, did you see that article in the paper about the waiting list for elderly housing down in Ashford? It's terrifying. Waiting lists are always long. It's just the way of things, innit? Though, you know, back in my day, council housing was… well, it was a lifeline for a lot of people. Now? Don’t even get me started. It  was  a lifeline, David. My nan lived in a council flat for forty years. Safe, warm, affordable. Now they’re all being sold off, aren’t they? And nobody’s building replacements. It’s dreadful for those on fixed incomes. Exactly! And it's not just the cost, it's everything. My grandma's been looking at some of those retirement villages. Lovely, on paper. But the service charges? They’re insane! And she’s perfectly capable of looking after herself, just needs a bit of support. Retirement villages… fancy that! My mum ended up in one of those. Not by choice, though. Needed care, you see. Cost an arm and a leg. Felt a bit…soulless, to be honest. Like a hotel for sad people. I see it every day at work. Wonderful places, some of them, but they're not for everyone. And frankly, they're just a plaster over a much bigger problem. We need more affordable, accessible housing for older people, not just these glorified care hotels. Absolutely. And disability parking too! I was thinking about that. Have you seen how crazy it gets at events like this? People with mobility issues, struggling to find spaces… They'll be queuing for ages, alright. Remember that fella last year? Had a blue badge, but some bloke in a shiny sports car parked right across it.

Honestly, 0321, your little patch is looking lovely! You've managed to get so much in, even with the unpredictable weather we've been having. Thanks, Chloe! It's a bit of a labour of love, this. I’ve been experimenting with companion planting – the basil seems to be really helping the tomatoes. It’s mostly for the novelty of it, really. I don’t need to grow that much food. But it's so relaxing. I know exactly what you mean. That's a big part of why I'm so keen on getting an allotment. The programme I manage at the charity is…well, it's stressful, to put it mildly. Something grounded, something tangible, feels essential right now. Absolutely! I was saying just the other day that it’s like, the only time I properly switch off. So, you're still set on applying for one at the Willow Creek site then? Definitely. I’ve been looking at the website. The sizes seem reasonable, and apparently, they’re really supportive there – lots of workshops and things. Did you have a particularly rough time getting yours sorted? I heard allotment waiting lists can be brutal. They can be, yeah. I was lucky, I think. Someone had to give theirs up unexpectedly, and I was already on the list. Though it took about six months, that's fairly standard around here. The waiting list at Willow Creek is notoriously long. Don't get disheartened if it takes a while. Right, that’s good to know. I was bracing myself for a year or more. What are you thinking of growing, if you actually  did  get a larger plot? Apart from basil and tomatoes, naturally. Ooh, if I had a bigger plot... I'd definitely do some proper weeding. Honestly, maintaining this little space is enough work. But beyond that… I'd love a proper raspberry patch. I’m always craving fresh raspberries. And courgettes! Everyone says they're easy, but I’ve never had much luck. Maybe I’d try a few pumpkins too, for Halloween. It's a bit ambitious, I know. Courgettes  are  sneaky. They explode overnight! You need to be constantly harvesting them when they're small – like, baby courgettes. Tiny ones are delicious grated into pasta sauces. I'm thinking more vegetables for me initially. Things I actually use regularly – potatoes, carrots, onions, leeks… the basics.

…and then, honestly, Mr. Henderson just  stared  at me. Like I’d grown a second head! I was asking about the deadline for the essay, perfectly reasonable question, right? And he just… blinked. Oh, bless him! Some lecturers are just robots, aren't they? My Professor Davies looks like he hasn’t slept since the invention of the internet. Aye, they’re a funny bunch. So, tell me, are you still seeing Liam? You were a bit vague last time we spoke. It’s… complicated. We had a proper heart-to-heart on Sunday. Things got a bit intense. Intense how? Don't tell me he’s started reciting poetry again. That always ends badly, doesn't it? Remember that Wordsworth phase? No poetry, thankfully. It’s just… we have different ideas about the future. He wants to settle down, like,  now . Marriage, kids, the whole nine yards. Blimey. And you don’t? Not yet. I’m still figuring things out, you know? University, career... I don't want to feel like I'm rushing into anything just because he’s ready. He said I was being “unrealistic” which, frankly, felt a bit unfair. Unrealistic? He’s being a bit precious, then, innit? You're young! It's good to have your own ambitions. Don’t let him pressure you. Honestly, at 21, I’m still trying to decide what to have for dinner most days, let alone plan a lifetime. Exactly! But his mum's already started hinting about grandchildren. It’s all a bit much. Oh, mums. Always keen on the grandkids. Right, well. Forget about him for a bit. We're going to that festival next month, aren't we? The one in Leeds? Yes! I was just thinking about it. Did you manage to get tickets for Saturday? I know they're selling out fast. Managed to snag ‘em! Got four. You, me, Chloe and… well, you can invite someone if you like. If you're not fussed about dragging Liam along, that is. Definitely not dragging Liam. This is a Sophie-and-Me thing. Chloe’s definitely in, then? Aye, she’s dying to go see ‘The Lunar Echoes’. She’s been listening to them non-stop. You’ll be hearing it for weeks, mark my words. Good, I love a bit of music. Honestly, just thinking about getting out of Doncaster for a weekend is making me feel a lot better.

Aye, that was a right dodgy save, wasn’t it, Liam? Honestly, I thought we were goners there. Proper panic set in. Dodgy? That was atrocious! The keeper just… froze. Luckily, it bounced to Ben, didn't it? Saved our bacon. Though, still 2-1 down, innit? This is stressing me out. Relax, Liam. It's just a game. And honestly, are you two getting  that  worked up about a Sunday afternoon kickabout? I’m trying to find a decent playlist for the party next week. A party? Seriously? After last time? Remember what happened with the glitter bomb? Nana was  not  pleased. Right proper mess that was. Your Grandma's carpet never forgave us, did it, Jay? Still, good laugh though. We need to apologize, though. Apologize? We offered to pay for the cleaning! She just kept going on about "the disrespect." Drama queen, that one. My mum’s the same. Everything's a potential tragedy. Anyway, playlist. What vibe are we going for? Honestly, I'm leaning towards early 2000s nostalgia - Pop Punk anthems mostly. Pop Punk? Nah, you’re havin’ a laugh, Ellie. Give us some Oasis, summin' with a bit of proper grit to it. Like ‘Wonderwall.’ Gets everyone singin’. Oasis? Seriously, Josh? That’s so… dad. Let’s throw in a bit of grime, you know? Keep it fresh. Something like Stormzy. I’d be happy with something instrumental, honestly. Allows me to focus on my figurines. I'm trying to recreate the entire cast of Star Wars, Episode VI. It's proving… challenging. Jay, you are the most dedicated Star Wars nerd I know. How's Yoda coming along? Is he miniature and wise? I've sculpted his ears perfectly. Took me hours. The challenge is the cloak. It needs to have that flowing, ethereal quality. I’m thinking felt. What do you think? Felt's risky. It might look a bit… cheap. Maybe something more textured, like a woven fabric? Though, that'll be harder to work with. Fabric would look better, yeah. You got a proper eye for detail, Jay, that’s for sure. Reminds me of when my Grandma used to knit. She could make anything, she could. Proper little wizard with the needles. Speaking of grandmas, mine’s been on a right one since she saw that new  Bridgerton  series. Says it’s “scandalous.” She keeps asking me if I think true love is real.

Honestly, Sarah’s wedding photos are  amazing . You’d barely recognise her, she looks so… grown up! And Mark, bless him, is just beaming. They look so happy. Cor, Sarah, is it? My, seems like only yesterday she were a little nipper, playing in me garden. Always climbing the apple tree, that one. Didn't listen to a word I said, mind you. Typical girl. She definitely had a rebellious streak. I think she really needed that stability with Mark, though. He's a good egg. Are you planning on sending a gift? I was thinking something from that little pottery place in town, you know, the one with the quirky mugs? A gift, eh? Right. Pottery. I'm not sure about pottery, dear. Feels a bit...fussy. Though, you're right, I should get something. What about one of those nice picture frames from John Lewis? She’s always taking pictures, Sarah is. Could put a photo of 'er and Mark in it. That’s a really lovely idea, actually! Much more her style than a mug. I'll pop down and have a look. Oh, have you seen 'Everything Everywhere All at Once'? 'Everything Everywhere…'? Sounds a bit silly, doesn't it? Like one o’ them sci-fi things. I'm not keen on sci-fi, love. Too much bangin’ and flashin’. Give me a good weepie any day. No, no, it's not  just  sci-fi. It’s bizarre, definitely, but it’s also incredibly moving. It's about family, and regret, and… well, it’s hard to explain. Michelle Yeoh is brilliant in it. You wouldn't expect it, but I think you'd genuinely like it. Michelle Yeoh, is it? She were in 'Tomorrow Never Dies', weren't she? With Pierce Brosnan. That were a good film. Proper action film. But family and regret, you say? Sounds a bit…down. I just want a bit o’ escapism, dear. Me knees ache somethin’ awful today. It has escapism too! It's just wrapped up in this crazy, multiversal package. Think of it like… like a really, really clever puzzle. Remember that film, 'Sliding Doors'? That kind of feeling. The ‘what ifs’. 'Sliding Doors'! Oh, I loved that film! Gwyneth Paltrow, weren’t it? That were a proper cry. I remember blubbin' me eyes out on the sofa after watchin' that. Right then, you’ve piqued me interest a bit.

Honestly, this drizzle is making me question all my life choices. A spa day sounds  amazing  right now. Remember that one we did in Bristol? The seaweed wraps... bliss. You and your seaweed. It's a bit… much, innit? Still, a spa trip would be nice. A little pampering is definitely required after the week I’ve had. The linguistics conference was a right headache. Too many people arguing about vowel shifts. Did someone say spa? Can I come? ANON! You're always lurking! Of course you can, love. Though I’m not sure how a full seaweed wrap would suit you… She seems to manage alright with everything else. Seriously though, how was the interview, Elin? You were dreading it, weren't you? At  The Stylist ? It was… intense. Loads of questions about repurposing content for different platforms, SEO strategies, and apparently, knowing the latest TikTok dance craze is a vital skill for an editor these days. A vital skill! I felt utterly prehistoric. Right mess, that. They do lean heavily on the social media stuff, don't they? I had a similar experience for a research project presentation. They asked me to explain complex linguistic theory using emojis. Emojis! Is there cake? Because I require sustenance after enduring the suspense of knowing whether I’m being included in your spa plans. There’s lemon drizzle. You’ll be right as rain. So, the TikTok thing... did you mention your expertise in long-form articles and deep dives? I tried! I stressed my experience with crafting compelling narratives and building readership. But they seemed fixated on reels and challenges. The interviewer kept asking about “engagement metrics.” It’s all so superficial. Honestly, I came home wanting to crawl under a duvet and watch  The Undateables . Oh, don’t even start with  The Undateables . I cried last night watching that episode with the chap who collects porcelain thimbles! He was so lovely and genuine. It’s more real than half the stuff you see on reality TV. Actually, speaking of DVDs, have you seen that documentary about obscure board games? I got it in on offer. Board games? Seriously, Lottie? After a soul-crushing interview you want to talk  board games ? I need therapy, not Settlers of Catan. Actually, ANON has a point. A board game night might be just the thing. Distract me from the existential dread of being deemed unfit for the world of online magazines.

Right, so, this washing machine. It’s possessed, I swear. Absolutely possessed. It’s been makin' this awful racket, like a badger trapped inside, and now it's not drainin' proper. Proper soaked the kitchen floor, it has. A badger, eh? Sounds exciting. Let me guess, you tried the usual things? Checked the filter? Aye, checked the filter. Clean as a whistle, it were. Tried tellin' it off, too. Didn’t work. I’m startin' to think we need an exorcist, not a repairman. You've been fiddlin’ with your microscope all day, haven't you? Don't tell me you've forgotten what a normal domestic appliance is supposed to do. A little bit, perhaps. Been deep in the world of algae, you see. Not a lot of badger noises involved. But look, I’ll have a look at it later. It’s probably just a blocked pipe somewhere silly. Speaking of silly, did you hear from Mum and Dad? Just this mornin'. Dad’s still trying to convince them to get a Yorkshire Terrier. He thinks it'll cheer Gran up, poor lass. They’re makin' a right fuss about it though, sayin' Gran's already got enough fuss with her floral arrangements. Honestly, that man will chase after anything with a wagging tail and a bit of fluff. He does, doesn't he? A true terrier enthusiast. Reminds me of that time he tried to rescue a squirrel from the bird feeder. Ended up with a scratched face and a very smug squirrel. Oh, God, I'd almost forgotten about that! He looked like he'd been wrestling a badger, actually. And Gran was fair cryin' with laughter. It was gold, pure gold. What about you? Any exciting algae revelations? Surprisingly, yes. I think I might be onto something with the chlorophyll absorption rates. Could have implications for biofuel research… it’s all very preliminary though. Don’t want to get ahead of myself. What are you fancying for tea? I'm thinkin' something hearty. This laundry drama must have worked up an appetite. Starving, to be honest. How about that lentil stew you made last week? That were belting. Proper warming. Or… …that new film, ‘Everything Everywhere All at Once’? Fancy a watch later? I've been hearin’ good things. Lentil stew it is! And yes, absolutely. I’ve seen the trailer, looks brilliant. A bit chaotic, but brilliant.

Honestly, the sheer scale of it is just… unbelievable. Another emissions scandal. This one’s about VW fitting defeat devices to their cars again, apparently. Remember the first one? Felt like the world ended for a week. Aye, well, a bit dramatic, love, wasn’t it? Though, it  was  a right shocker at the time. Big companies get away with a lot, don't they? Always have. Oil industry, banking… it's all the same game, really. Just different toys. Defeat devices? So they were… cheating, deliberately? How could they even  get  away with something like that for so long? It’s just so dishonest. You know, I spent my life trying to instill a sense of integrity in young people. To be truthful and honest. And then you see this? It’s complicated, apparently. They programmed the cars to detect when they were being tested and then switch to a cleaner setting. But on the road, they were emitting far more pollutants. So, yeah, blatant cheating. And they got away with it because… well, regulatory oversight wasn’t as robust as it should have been. And apparently, it was going on for years. They’ve been fined, of course, but… Fined? That’s a slap on the wrist for a company that size. They’ll likely make that back in a week. What’s really galling is the impact on the environment. All those extra pollutants, pumping into the air… it's just irresponsible. It's exactly why I’m so relieved to be retired, honestly. Dealing with the world’s problems seemed rather overwhelming when teaching advanced calculus. This feels… remote. Like a shadow of something bigger. Speaking of bigger things, how's the house hunt going, darling? Have you seen anything promising in Hunsonby yet? It's… moving. Slowly. The prices here are surprisingly high. I thought Cumbria would be a bargain compared to the South, but… even with the current market, people are paying a premium. Apparently, the "escape to the countryside" trend has really driven prices up. You'll find that everywhere now. People fleeing the southerly nonsense. We saw it ourselves when we moved up here. Used to be, folks down south looked at the Midlands like we were on another planet. Thought we were all living in some Dickens novel. Now they’re flocking here, driving up prices, and then complaining about the accents.

Honestly, Doris, I don’t know  what  gets up his tree these days. Just…everything. Seems to find something to be riled about. Arthur, you're talking about David again, aren't you? He's always been a bit like that, hasn’t he? A bit prickly. A sensitive soul, really. Sensitive? I was merely pointing out the planning application for those new houses on the old apple orchard is a disgrace! They’re cramming ‘em in like pigeons! No green space, no consideration for the local infrastructure...it's utterly chaotic! Is that being sensitive? Is pointing out incompetence “riled,” as you put it? Oh, here we go. The apple orchard. You’ve been going on about that orchard for nigh on ten years, David. It was a scruffy old orchard, full of windfalls and wasps. Scruffy, yes, but  characterful ! It was part of the landscape, Arthur. Part of Costessey’s history! Now it’s going to be a soulless estate of identical boxes. And they don’t even need that many houses! It's just developers lining their pockets. Now, David, don't get yourself worked up. It’s done now, isn't it? Can’t change it. And a few new houses might bring a bit of life to the area. More people, more opportunities… Opportunities for what, Doris? Overcrowded schools and gridlocked roads? The council hasn’t upgraded anything to cope. Honestly, these people in charge...they wouldn’t know a level from a plumb bob. Don’t get started on the council, David. Remember that fiasco with the road resurfacing on Meadow Lane? Took ‘em six weeks to patch a few potholes! Six weeks! And they did a dreadful job! I had to go and have a word with Mr. Henderson, the foreman, and  he  admitted they were using the wrong grade of tarmac. Couldn’t believe it, honestly. Said he'd been told to save money. Upsetting people with their cut corners. It's a constant cycle of upsetting people. Speaking of upset, Arthur, have you heard anything more from the pension office? You've been waiting forever to sort out that overpayment. Still nothing. Sent another letter last week. Keeps saying “further investigation required.” Investigation into  what ? I’ve sent them every document they asked for! It’s like banging my head against a brick wall. I was thinking of complaining to my MP.

Honestly, this biology project is going to be the death of me. Evolution? Seriously? Feels like we're just memorising facts to regurgitate. Tell me about it. Mrs. Davies expects us to  understand  it, not just know what Darwin said. Like, how do you even  begin  to grasp timescales that big? It’s mind-blowing. Well, Ms. Davies did that analogy with the finches last week. Remember? How their beaks changed based on the food available? That actually helped a bit. It felt less like abstract theory and more like… well, observation. Yeah, but it missed the key part, didn’t it? She didn’t explain  how  the beaks changed. Like, what’s the actual mechanism? Selective pressure is all well and good, but the genetic mutation bit is where it gets tricky. Exactly! And the way some people still argue against it! It's like, hello, there’s mountains of evidence. My uncle keeps sending me these dodgy YouTube videos about creationism. Drives me insane. Classic. My grandma’s the same. “It’s all in God’s plan,” she says. It’s a bit difficult to engage in constructive debate about evolutionary biology with someone who genuinely believes the Earth is 6,000 years old. It’s frustrating, because it highlights the whole problem with faith versus reason, doesn't it? Like, you can believe what you want, but dismissing scientific evidence based on religious belief seems… irresponsible. It’s bigger than just religion, though, isn’t it? It’s about confirmation bias. People only seek out information that supports what they already believe. Look at that whole ‘manosphere’ thing online. Crazy. Oh god, don't even get me started. I saw this viral TikTok the other day… some guy going on about how feminism has ruined men. Like, seriously? Ruined? We're literally just fighting for equality. It’s ridiculous. They always resort to victimhood. "Oh, we're the oppressed ones now because women can vote and have careers." It's just… exhausting. It's definitely a weird manifestation of insecurity, I think. Feeling threatened by progress. And the way they weaponize online anonymity to spread this stuff... it's scary, actually. Remember that debate we had in history about systemic racism? It’s the same principle, just reframed. People get defensive about any suggestion that established systems benefit some groups over others. Absolutely. It’s easier to deny the problem than to address it.

Speaker_1 exclaimed, gesturing emphatically with a biscuit. Speaker_2 : "Oh, love, that's rotten, it is. Doctors, eh? Never listen, do they? Remember old Mr. Higgins? Went in about a cough, they said it was just a bit of a tickle. Turned out to be pneumonia! Poor man. You gotta trust your gut, Eleanor. Are you taking that penicillin they gave you last time?"
