I’m a bit nervous to be honest, but I really think it could be useful, especially with the kids who struggle to communicate sometimes. Plus, it’s something just for me, you know? A bit of a challenge. That’s wonderful, love. You'll be brilliant at it. You're always so patient and empathetic. It’s a really good idea, Chloe. You're always thinking of ways to help them. I'm thinking of a pottery class myself, something crafty to de-stress. It's so hectic at the store; it's nice to think about doing something different. Pottery! That's lovely, Sophie. Maybe we could do it together? It would be nice for us to have a regular girls' outing. Sounds good. Speaking of outings, have you all booked for Amelia’s birthday dinner next Saturday? I called the Italian place earlier.

Honestly, this quinoa is aggressively bland. Did they just… steam it? Cambridge catering. What can you do? It's more about the atmosphere than the culinary excellence, innit? Besides, at least it's not that weird chicken casserole they served last Tuesday. I’m still having nightmares. You’re being generous. The "atmosphere" is fluorescent lighting and the faint smell of printer ink. I’d honestly prefer the chicken casserole at this point. It was a  choice . This is… beige. I'm actually fine with it. I’m trying to be healthy, you know? My mum would be so proud if she saw me eating this. She's constantly on at me about antioxidants. Your mum? Right. You've mentioned her a few times. Very… focused on Swedish efficiency, isn’t she? Well, yes. She wants me to be successful and… well, efficient. It’s a cultural thing. Everything has to be ordered and productive. Even lunch. I can imagine. I'm a bit of a chaotic mess myself. My flat looks like a bomb went off, but my research is usually… mostly… organized. Mostly. I know the feeling. My desk at the publishing house is a disaster zone. My boss keeps threatening to assign me a “desk tidy consultant.” Can you imagine? Like, a professional organiser for a publishing assistant? The irony! That’s brilliant! You should document that, seriously. Aspiring writers need to know the realities of the industry. It's not all glamorous book launches and literary festivals. It’s beige quinoa and desk tidy consultants. You're right. I should. I'm always looking for examples for my linguistic analysis. Mundane interactions, colloquialisms… you'd be surprised how much you can learn from seemingly ordinary conversation. I'm currently researching regional dialect shifts in younger generations. Oh, really? That’s fascinating! So, the way I say “loo” is potentially a vital piece of data? It absolutely is! Your pronunciation, your use of slang… everything contributes. It's less about correctness and more about observing how language evolves. Whereabouts are you from, then? No offence, but your accent is a bit... neutral. That’s kind of the point. I've floated around a bit. Grew up mostly in Hertfordshire, but my dad's from Cornwall and my mum's from Yorkshire. It's a linguistic melting pot, apparently. See, that explains it. I'm a bit of a mixed bag myself.

Right, so, visa applications. Absolute nightmare, innit? I've been staring at this form for three hours and I still don't know if they want my mum's maiden name or not. It's like they're deliberately trying to confuse ya. Tell me about it. I’ve started mine, but there’s a section on “previous travel history” that's just a black hole. Do I list  every  trip I've ever taken? Even that weekend in Skegness when I were twelve? Skegness counts! Defo gotta put Skegness. Gotta show 'em you’re a seasoned traveller. Though, to be fair, that was mostly just chips and arcades. Not exactly preparing me for the Gobi desert, is it? True, true. I'm leaning towards listing everything over the last five years, just to be safe. What about proof of funds? Have you sorted that? My bank account’s looking a bit…sparse at the moment, thanks to student life. Yeah, got that done. Mum kicked in a bit, which I’m eternally grateful for. Told her it’s for a good cause, you know, helping underprivileged Mongolian yak farmers. She bought it hook, line, and sinker. Yak farmers? Seriously? Well, someone’s gotta help ‘em! It sounds good, right? Gets the sympathy flowing. We need every penny we can get. Speaking of, have you had any luck with the donations? That Gumtree ad I put up hasn’t exactly set the world alight. Not really. A few curious clicks, but no actual pledges. I think it needs a better picture. Maybe something more than just a picture of us grinning like idiots outside the Arndale Centre. Aye, you're right. We need something… evocative. How about a blurry photo of a travel brochure showing Mongolia? Classically misleading! I like your thinking. I’ll see if I can find a decent one. What about the passport photos? Mine look like I’ve been squashed by a badger. I need to get some proper ones done. Aye, I need to do mine too. That photo booth down by the market gives you five for a quid, but they're all horrific. I ended up looking like a startled owl. Five for a quid? Tempting. But I’m terrified of ending up with owl-face. Maybe Boots? They're a bit more reliable. We should do it together – makes it less stressful.

Honestly, I'm knackered. That after-party went on way too long. Didn't even realise it was that late when I finally crawled back. Tell me about it. Though, my knackeredness is a bit… different, innit? Still feel properly ropey from last night. That hospital visit wasn’t exactly the best way to end the evening. How are you feeling? Still aching? I brought you some tea. Honey and lemon. Sounds cliché, I know, but it’s gotta be good for something, right? Cheers, El. It’s… better, I s'pose. The pain's dulled, but I'm just completely drained. And embarrassed. Imagine, being carted off to A&E because I tripped over a rug. Proper clumsy, I am. Don’t be daft, ANON. Accidents happen! You've got better things to be worrying about than falling over. And besides, it's a good story. "Remember that time ANON ended up in hospital after a house party?" Classic. Exactly! And apparently, it was chaos at the hospital. Liam was practically running around trying to find you. He was proper stressed. Oh, stop it! He just came to make sure I was alright. He’s been… lovely, actually. "Just"? Don't play coy with us, love. Everyone knows Liam's got a massive thing for you. He was mooning over you at the party, couldn’t take his eyes off you. He's a nice lad. Just… complicated, you know? He's got that whole "long-distance relationship" thing happening with his girlfriend back home. It’s all a bit messy. Right. University and relationships. A minefield. I'm trying to steer clear entirely this year. Focusing on my thesis is hard enough without adding romantic drama. Wise choice, El. Honestly, I'm trying to do the same. Though, I did fancy that lad from the History Society… but he keeps quoting obscure philosophers at me. It’s a bit much, even for me. Sounds like you need someone to just… buy you a pint. Simple. Not analyze your soul. Exactly! It's exhausting. So, back to your arm. Did they do anything at the hospital? They did an X-ray. It’s just a sprain, apparently. Nothing broken, thankfully. They gave me some painkillers and told me to rest. Hence, the copious amounts of tea and lounging in bed. Good. At least it’s not worse. Right, I’m off to make some toast.

…and then Auntie Maureen, bless her cotton socks, tried to tell Uncle Derek that his prize-winning marrow was looking "a bit peaky." Can you believe it, lad? Peak-y! After all the fuss he makes. He nearly choked on his scone, honest he did. Typical Auntie Maureen. She never misses an opportunity to wind him up. Did she at least apologise? Apologise? Maureen apologising is like snow in July, love. She just patted his arm and said, "Now, Derek, don't get your knickers in a twist." Honestly! The whole table went quiet. You could’ve heard a pin drop. Sounds like it. Was Grandad alright? He seemed a bit tired last time I saw him. He was surprisingly chipper, actually. He kept telling everyone how proud he was of you, going on about your A-Levels and how clever you are. Nearly burst with pride he did. Kept saying, "Look at 'im, a scholar! Better than me playing footie in the mud, wasn’t I?" He’s always got to bring up the footie, hasn't he? Yeah, he does. He still thinks he's capable of scoring a goal, doesn’t he? Did he mention anything about the cricket scores? He’s been obsessed with the Test matches lately. Oh, aye. Every five minutes, eh? “England’s looking a bit shaky, lad. They need to sort out their bowling.” He wouldn’t shut up about it. Honestly, at one point, I thought he was going to start shouting at the telly. Though, to be fair, England  were  looking shaky. They always do. Still, it was good to see him laughing, though. It’s been a while since he’s really seemed… himself. It has. And that's what's important, isn't it? Seeing family together, laughing, forgetting about all the bother. Your grandma looked lovely, too. That blue dress really suited her. She was beaming ear to ear. I thought so too. She looked really happy. It must’ve been nice for her, having everyone there to celebrate their anniversary. 50 years, that's incredible. It is, isn't it? A true testament to… well, patience, mostly, I reckon! But honestly, they’re a good match. They bicker like cats and dogs, but they wouldn’t be without each other. Your grandma couldn't manage without his cups of tea and his bad jokes, and your grandad gets a proper kicking if he tries to change the channel during her favourite shows.

“Right, Dad. How much longer 'til we’re clear of this… this snarl? It’s like M62-squared.” “Now, now, love. Dramatic as ever, aren’t ya? Just a bit of traffic, that's all. Happens. We’ll be through it soon enough. Got your water bottle?” "Yeah, got it. Though I'm already thirsty. You know, you really need to get one of them fancy filtered ones. Proper hydration, Dad. It’s science.” “Fancy filtered ones? I’m trying to save a bit of dosh, lass. Got all the pens you need though, didn’t I? Remember last year when you couldn't find a pen for your crossword in Devon? Near caused a family crisis, that did.” "Don't remind me! I was practically having a meltdown. Seriously, though, what are we thinking for supper tonight? Cornwall’s meant to have decent fish and chips. Or should we cook somethin’ at the cottage?” “Fish and chips sound grand, to be honest. Let’s not fuss with cookin’ already. It’s a long journey and I'm feelin' a bit...well, you know. IBS acting up again.” "Oh, Dad. Honestly, you and your gut. Did you take your tablets? And are you sure you wouldn't prefer a proper cuppa? Maybe some ginger tea? It's supposed to be good for that.” "Ginger tea sounds lovely, actually. Maybe later. Right now, just need to concentrate on the road. Been thinking, though… remember how you were worried about all that unpacking we've got to do?" "Yeah? Of course I was! We're basically moving half our lives into that little cottage. And eBay’s been mental with all the furniture we're tryin' to sell." "Well, I was readin' about these flat-pack furniture assembly services. They come to yer house and build it all for ya. Bit pricey, mind you, but could save a lot of stress. Might be worth a look.” "Seriously? I saw some lads on TikTok doin' that! That’s brilliant, actually. Imagine not having to struggle with IKEA instructions for three days. Although, think of the Amazon deliveries though! The postman will be killin' us.” “Aye, he’ll need a delivery truck, not a van. It's like everything is gettin’ bigger, innit? Do you ever think about how different things were even just… fifty years ago? No Amazon, no TikTok, no fancy cat flaps.

A recipe for what, precisely, Margaret? You’ve been muttering about this 'community project' for the last half hour without explaining what catastrophe you anticipate. Eleanor’s right, Mum. You’re being a bit vague. It’s just a nature reserve, Margaret. Near the old quarry. A little bit of rewilding, some walking trails... A nature reserve straddling a geological fault line, David! Have you  looked  at the plans? And the proposed access road? It’ll churn up ancient peat bogs. Peat bogs, David! Centuries of stored carbon, released into the atmosphere! It's dreadful. Now hold on a minute, Margaret. Peat bogs are important, aye, but a few footpaths ain't gonna bring the whole world tumbling down. Besides, the council’s promised to use permeable paving. Less impact. Gwyn has a point, Margaret. Permeable paving is a good start. And it  is  a lovely idea, really. Giving the area some protection, providing a space for local people… Protection? It's blatant land grabbing, Eleanor! They’ll start with a few trails and a bird hide, then they'll be building a visitor centre, a restaurant, and then before you know it, they’ll be wanting to build  houses ! It always starts small, doesn't it? Sneaky, like brambles growing across your path. Mum, you’re being dramatic. It’s a conservation project, funded by grants. They wouldn’t be allowed to build houses there. It’s protected land. Protected today, David. But what about tomorrow? Politicians change their minds like the wind. I’ve seen it happen. I taught generations of them! They promise one thing at the election, and do another the minute they’re in office. Remember the incident with the library extension in 1987? Promises, promises… Margaret, the library extension was a completely different situation – a funding shortfall due to a change in government priorities. This is a carefully considered environmental initiative. They’ve got ecologists on board, David’s been looking at the geological surveys... Aye, Eleanor's right. David's been a busy boy, researching this. He’s not some fool to be swayed by the first shiny proposal that comes along. He's seen firsthand the impact of shoddy construction - spent his life building things properly, you know. Wouldn’t support something that was a mess. Exactly, Gwyn. And the local community is enthusiastic. It'll bring some much-needed opportunities for local businesses.

Right, so pancakes are almost ready. Think they’ll be a success? Little ones are usually very opinionated about breakfast. Mummy, Mummy! Look! I drew you a flower! It's got, like, thirty petals! Mine’s got sparkly glitter, Mummy! It's a  really  good flower! Can I put more glitter? They're both absolutely gorgeous, my loves. Thirty petals is definitely a record! And yes, darling, a little more glitter won’t hurt. Just… not  too  much, alright? We don't want to be finding glitter in the cat's fur later. Sparkle, sparkle! So, Mother’s Day… I was thinking, after breakfast, we could head over to Forest School. It's a bit chilly, but the bluebells are starting to pop up. It would make a lovely change from the usual cards and chocolates. Forest School! Can we build a badger sett? And find a fairy! A  real  fairy! We can certainly try! No promises on the fairy front, but a badger sett sounds like a very worthy project. Your grandma would like that, wouldn't she? Remember how she used to tell us stories about badgers? Yes! She said they were very clever builders. Like Lego! Exactly like Lego, darling. Now, speaking of clever, I was trying to explain an idiom to the class today, and I completely butchered it. Idiom? What's that? It's like, words that don't  really  mean what they say. Like, if I said "it's raining cats and dogs," I don't actually mean animals are falling from the sky. Silly! Exactly! And the one I was trying to explain was "break a leg." I was trying to tell them it means "good luck," and I got so confused explaining why you'd wish someone to  break  their leg that I just gave up. Why do they say that? Good question! Apparently, it comes from theatre, and it's meant to be a way to wish performers well, hoping they’ll have so many curtain calls they practically break their legs. A bit odd, isn’t it? So, it’s like… a funny wish? Precisely! A funny wish. Like saying "butter someone's socks!" Though, I'm not entirely sure  what  that means either. Your Dad always says that. Daddy says it means you're being silly! He does, doesn’t he? He’s rather fond of silly idioms. Right, pancakes are ready!

I know, love. It's a brutal one, isn't it? Losing your mum… it’s a seismic shift, regardless of how prepared you think you were. You were so close. Close doesn’t even cover it. She was my rock. My confidante. I used to call her every morning, just to chat about nothing. Now… silence. Just this awful, echoing silence. And the guilt, oh, the guilt! I felt like I wasn’t around enough these last few years. Always chasing deadlines, building my business… Don't go there, Sarah. Honestly, don't. You were building a life for yourself and your kids. Your mum understood that. She  wanted  you to be happy and successful. She was always so proud of you. Remember that time she told Mrs. Higgins at the school gates that you were going to "conquer the world"? Oh God, yes! She was so mortified afterwards that she’d bragged so much. But she meant well. She always did. I just… I keep thinking about all the things I didn’t say. All the advice I didn't ask for. Now it’s too late. Sarah, you can't beat yourself up about things in the past. Trust me, your mum knew how much you loved her. And she knew you were busy. She never once mentioned to me that she felt neglected. Quite the opposite, actually. She was always praising you for your resilience, for your drive. You spoke to her more than I did these past few months, didn't you? I always assumed… I made an effort. Someone had to. But it wasn’t a secret. And she wasn't complaining, Sarah. She was planning. She was focused on squeezing every last drop of life out of it. Remember the garden? She was determined to get the roses blooming before… you know. That’s right! She was fiercely determined. And look at them, they  did  bloom. Beautiful, vibrant roses. A testament to her spirit, really. You should go and sit with them. Sometimes, just being near something she loved… it can be comforting. I've been avoiding the garden, actually. It feels… too real. Like she should be out there, pruning and fussing over them. I understand. It’s grief, love. It’s messy and complicated. And it’ll hit you when you least expect it. Last night, I found myself wanting to tell her about the cricket scores.

Honestly, this timetable is a nightmare. Professor Davies has scheduled his Linguistics of Korean Morphology lecture  directly  after my Sociolinguistics seminar. It’s physically impossible! Is it, though? You've managed to cram everything in before. You’re pretty good at the logistical juggling act. Have you contacted him? I did. He just sent back this patronising email about "prioritising well-being" and suggesting I “consider my commitments.” Like, thanks, Professor. Very helpful. It implies I'm the one being unreasonable! And the fees... don't even get me started on the fees. They keep creeping up. Yeah, it's ridiculous. Remember when we were talking about looking into postgraduate funding for your research into Korean honorifics? Have you made any headway on that? A little. Found a potential grant, but the deadline is next month and the application is… extensive. It requires a decent chunk of my current writing. I’m half tempted to just abandon the whole thing and get a decent job. Something involving data analysis, maybe? Less Korean, more spreadsheets. Don’t say that! Your research is fascinating. Remember when I said your analysis of the subtle gendered language used in K-dramas was brilliant? Honestly, it's groundbreaking. You'd be crazy to let admin stuff stop you. Did you see that article about the South Korean festival Chuseok? It’s fascinating how their food traditions reflect their beliefs about ancestor veneration. I did! I was reading about it. I’m trying to find a recipe for Songpyeon. It looks… challenging. Speaking of food, are you eating that sugary cereal again? You’ll rot your teeth. It's post-study fuel! Besides, I’m thinking of trying that new Korean BBQ place in Brighton. Fancy it next week? We could celebrate… avoiding existential dread about timetable clashes. Korean BBQ does sound good. But I’m still a terrible vegetarian influence on you. You know I only eat the vegetable sections. Remember that time you tried to sneak mushrooms into my bibimbap in Seoul? I thought I was being clever! You nearly launched that spoon across the restaurant. And the security guard! That was a memorable evening. Honestly, Seoul was incredible. The contrast between the incredibly modern technology and the deep-rooted traditions… it’s mind-blowing. I've been looking at some old photos on my phone. Did you ever finish that game I was trying to sell you, the one based on ancient Chinese mythology?

Ugh, this is exactly what I needed after that disastrous physics tutorial. Honestly, Professor Davies just…lectured at the board for ninety minutes straight. No questions, no engagement. Like we're robots! Sounds about right for Davies. Remember last year when he literally just wrote ‘E=mc²’ fifty times? Aye, and then just stared at us expectantly. Like we were supposed to spontaneously understand the universe. I nearly fell asleep. This pizza  is  good, though. Did you get the spicy one, Chloe? Yeah, I did! Figured we needed a bit of a kick after Davies. Anyone fancy another slice? Definitely! I’m starving. I’ve been buried in that Chaos Walking trilogy all afternoon. Seriously, the third book is insane. Have you guys read it? I tried, but I just couldn't get into it. Too much violence for me, I think. I’m more of a Twilight girl, you know? Don’t judge me! Oh, lass, nobody judges you for Twilight! It’s a classic. I secretly re-watch the movies sometimes. Don't tell anyone though. It’s terribly embarrassing. I'm with Sarah on this one. No shame in a bit of sparkly vampire action. Although, currently, I’m devouring City of Bones. Absolutely hooked. Ooh, that's good! Is it proper twisty? I need something gripping after hours of physics formulas. Everything's twisty in that series. You’ll love it. Speaking of gripping, did you see Sarah got a terrible bruise on her arm? What happened? Don’t remind me! It was the airport scanner. Honestly! Felt like I'd been punched. I swear they’re getting more and more sensitive. And it’s so embarrassing having people looking at you… Seriously? That’s awful! You should report it. I’d be mortified. Maybe it was the flavoured vodka the other night at Sugarhouse? Remember when Liam tried to do a shot and ended up spraying everyone? Don't even! That was a disaster. It tasted like… cough syrup and regret. Honestly, Sugarhouse is overpriced, too. Agreed. Actually, I was thinking… instead of Sugarhouse next Saturday, could we do camping? We haven't done a proper camping trip in ages. I’m in! Fresh air, a campfire… Sounds perfect after being cooped up in Lancaster. Especially considering the flooding last week. That was scary! Camping sounds amazing. Though, I'm terrible at pitching a tent.

Right, so we’re still… fifteen minutes out? Honestly, this countryside is a bit more… rural than I anticipated. I thought ANON lived closer to a decent coffee shop. Well, relax, Liam. It's lovely, innit? Peaceful. And I’ve got coffee in the flask if you’re gettin' the jitters. Besides, you’re used to rush-hour London, this is practically a spa day. A spa day where the only sound is sheep bleating? I'm not complaining, truly, but my brain is wired for concrete and deadlines. And slightly overpriced lattes. You’re a worrier, you are. Seriously, what's got you all tense? Did something go wrong with that bridge project? No, the project's fine, actually. Better than fine. The simulations are showing an unexpected stability increase. It's brilliant, really - we might be able to reduce the reinforcement steel by a significant margin, saving the client a fortune. It’s just… presenting it to the board is always a nightmare. They don't understand the nuances of finite element analysis. It’ll be a whole hour of me explaining stress distribution. Aye, boardrooms. They're a special kind of torture, aren't they? Like, they'd rather listen to someone describe beige paint for an hour than actually understand the important stuff. Reminds me of my grandma trying to understand what I did at university. "So, you count words, pet?" Brilliant. That’s a terrible analogy. But I get it. It's frustrating. What did you end up telling her? I gave up eventually. Ended up just saying I organized computer things. She seemed happy with that. It was easier than explaining linguistic corpora and the intricacies of lemmatization to someone who thinks eBay counts as a ‘research project.’ eBay research! That's gold. So, still loving the corpus work then? Last time we talked you seemed… ambivalent. I am. It's… comfortable. It’s steady. After drifting about for a while after uni, it's good to have that. But I miss writing, you know? Properly writing. Not just tagging verbs and counting occurrences. You could still do it, though. On the side. You’ve always been a good writer. Remember that short story you wrote in sixth form about the lighthouse keeper? It was fantastic. Absolutely haunting. Aye, well, that was a long time ago. And I was dramatic. Everything seemed like a potential novel back then.

Blimey. Everything’s going wrong, isn’t it? Like clockwork, it is. Always at the worst possible moment. Right, in the middle of the Canaries' push...My knees are playin' up somethin' awful today too. Feels like I’ve been runnin’ a marathon. Oh, Arthur, really? Your knees again? Honestly, you need to see that doctor, dear. You've been saying that for…well, years now. And poor Norwich! That’s dreadful timing. At least you had a nice cup of tea to soothe you. It's a bit drizzly out there, isn’t it? Typical Norfolk weather. It  is  a bit grey. I was hoping for sunshine for my walk this afternoon. Having to lecture online is bad enough without gloom and doom hanging over everything. How are your knees, Arthur? Mum was saying you’ve been complaining. They're not gettin' any better, love. Just clicking and groaning, like an old tractor. I've tried the heat, I've tried the cold. Nothin' seems to do a thing. Doctor’s useless, he just tells me to “take it easy.” Easy for  him  to say, sittin' in a warm chair all day. “Take it easy” is doctor speak for “I don’t have a definitive answer and I don’t want to spend more time with you.” It's a classic. And Arthur, you  don’t  take it easy. You're always pottering about, trying to fix things that aren't broken! Well, somebody's gotta do it, hasn't they? Can't just sit around waitin' for things to fall apart. This telly, for instance. I'll have a look at it tomorrow, I reckon. Probably just needs… well, I'm not sure what it needs, but I'll have a poke about. Do you think they still sell those little screwdrivers? You and your screwdrivers, Arthur. You probably need a whole new television. They’re so complicated these days. Remember when you used to get a good, solid picture without all these flashing lights and confusing menus? Honestly, Mum, the technology is beyond my comprehension sometimes. I spent half an hour last night trying to connect my new headphones to my laptop. It was madness! It felt like trying to solve a cryptic crossword. Dad, are you thinking about getting one of those smart TVs? They’re quite handy for streaming things. Smart TVs? What's wrong with a good, old-fashioned telly?

Honestly, I’m still reeling from the photographer’s quote. Ten thousand pounds! For a wedding! Do you believe it? Ten. Thousand. Wow. That  is  a bit steep, isn't it? But I suppose they're capturing the whole day, and editing, and… Right, but ten thousand? I’ve seen documentary wedding photography for less than half that! Liam's mum was saying we should just get someone from Facebook Marketplace. Liam’s mum suggesting a Facebook Marketplace photographer? That’s a visual. Imagine the bride's face! Exactly! And it’s not like we’re asking for anything fancy, just someone who can actually focus and get decent lighting. It’s just… everything’s so expensive. The venue, the dress, the food… it’s a nightmare. I’m starting to panic. You'll be fine. You just need to prioritize. What’s absolutely essential, and what can you compromise on? Remember that amazing florist you found? Maybe allocate more money there. She has a point. Honestly, the flowers are going to be stunning. Those orchids she showed us were incredible. Better than a mediocre photographer, any day. Besides, you can always ask a friend to take some candid shots. Like, ring Sarah – she’s surprisingly good with a camera. Sarah? Really? I didn’t even think of her. You’re right, she’s got a good eye. Okay, okay, let’s explore that. Saves a fortune if we could get away with it. So, speaking of saving money… anyone seen David lately? He’s been MIA. Last I heard, he was backpacking through Southeast Asia with that new girlfriend. Said he needed to "find himself" - classic. "Find himself" while surrounded by beaches and Pad Thai. Sounds rough. Remember when we all thought he’d marry Chloe? Oh my god, Chloe! That was embarrassing. The engagement party with the live ferret. I still cringe when I think about it. Don't remind me! It was a disaster waiting to happen. Honestly, finding a decent boyfriend feels harder than planning this wedding. I mean, at least a wedding has a slightly predictable structure. Tell me about it! It’s just… everyone’s either married, having kids, or desperately pretending they aren’t. Where do you even find normal people anymore? Well, you’re all normal people. We're a collective force of organized chaos. Although, speaking of kids… my sister just announced she’s pregnant!

Honestly, Arthur, you won't believe what young Maisie – my granddaughter – was showing me on that… that tablet thing. Dancing hamsters! Dancing hamsters, Arthur! And little songs afterward. It was quite… distracting, actually. Dancing hamsters, eh? Bless her little socks. My Stanley never 'ad anything like that. Just a wooden train and a tin soldier. Though he used to build the grandest forts out of blankets and chairs, he did. Remember those, Doris? Vaguely. We were all a bit preoccupied then, weren't we? Trying to make ends meet. Though the kids were happy enough. Maisie’s alright, a bit glued to those screens, mind you. Needs more fresh air. It's a double-edged sword, isn't it? Technology. My kids – well, my adult children now – are constantly on their phones. My daughter runs a marketing firm, and her entire working life is conducted through Teams and emails. She says she wouldn’t know what to do without it, but I worry about the isolation. They barely look up! Isolation... that’s the thing, isn’t it? I used to walk down to the village shop every day, ‘ave a bit of a chat with Maggie behind the counter. Proper social time, it was. Now, folk mostly order online, don't they? It's a bit lonely, this place. Even with you two 'ere. Don't you say that, Arthur. We’re here. And remember, Maggie retired last year, she has a lovely holiday home in Spain. It’s not all doom and gloom. Speaking of needing a bit of cheering up, I was thinking of getting a little pony for Maisie. A pony? That's… ambitious, Doris. A considerable expense. Footing the bill would be something else. I know, I know. But she adores horses. Has since she was tiny. We used to take her out to Farmer Giles’s field. She’d stand there, mesmerized, just watching them graze. It would give her something to look forward to. Horses! Wonderful creatures. Had a friend down the road, when I was a boy, kept a beautiful Shire. Big fella, he was. Called him Sampson. Used to pull the milk cart. My dad always wanted a horse. Never had the money, though. He was a coal miner, you know. Harsh work. He’d come home covered in black dust, aching all over. Never complained, though. Just wanted to provide for us.

…and honestly, Amelia, I just don’t see the point of all these new words they’re inventing. "Influencer?" What’s that even  mean ? Back in my day, if you had influence, you were a politician or a headmaster. Not someone posting pictures of avocado toast. I know exactly what you mean, Arthur! It's mad, isn’t it? But that's kind of fascinating from a linguist's perspective, you know? Language is always evolving. New technology, new trends… they all need new ways to be described. I’m teaching my students about neologisms - newly coined words – all the time. It’s amazing how quickly they crop up. Neologisms? Sounds like something out of a science fiction film. I prefer a good, solid word, like "robust" or "reliable." Words with history, you know? Words that have  earned  their place. This "vibe" business...just doesn’t cut it. Well, "vibe" has been around for a while, actually! It’s got roots in jazz music, tracing back to the 1920s. It’s just had a resurgence lately. Speaking of music, I’ve started taking a ukulele class! A ukulele? Heavens above! Is that one of those little Hawaiian things? You? Playing a ukulele? You always were a clever girl, Amelia, but that’s…unexpected. It is rather fun, actually. It’s quite relaxing. And surprisingly tricky! I’m nowhere near playing anything recognisable yet, just a lot of strumming. Are you still pottering about in the garden, Arthur? I saw some lovely roses blooming on your drive last week. I am, yes. Though my back isn’t what it used to be. The roses did alright this year, despite that awful dry spell we had. Got a couple of prize-winning blooms, I did. Entered them in the Village Flower Show. Didn’t win, though. Some young whippersnapper with a perfectly symmetrical dahlia took first prize. Oh, Arthur! You’re always complaining about the younger generation! You should have entered your roses in Birmingham's show! It's much bigger. Birmingham? Too much hustle and bustle for me, dear. I prefer the peace and quiet of Little Aston. Besides, I heard they’re very strict on the rules. Have to have the roses displayed in a certain way, with a particular type of vase...nonsense, I say. I suppose. So, anything exciting happening with the family? How's Margaret doing? Margaret's fine.

Honestly, Liv, Valentine’s Day. What a load of rubbish, innit? Like, the pressure! Everyone all loved-up, posting pictures of roses and overpriced chocolates. It was exhausting just scrolling through Instagram. Tell me about it, Bex! Mum went proper overboard this year. Sent me a card with glitter  everywhere . Like, I’m going to be finding tiny red sparkles for weeks. And she kept asking if I had a date. As if! Right? My nan’s been on at me too. 'You need a nice young man, Bex, a  stable  young man!' Like, thanks, Nan. Really needed the reminder I’m twenty-two and currently subsisting on pot noodles and existential dread. You’re such a drama queen. Pot noodles aren't  that  bad. But yeah, the family pressure is relentless. Did you end up going anywhere? Nah, I just stayed in, watched 'Pride & Prejudice' for the tenth time, and ate a family-sized bag of crisps. Peak Valentine’s Day, yeah? What about you? Did you manage to escape the glitter? I did! Went to see 'Dune: Part Two' with Chloe and Sam. It was brilliant, honestly. Honestly, the visuals, the acting... proper epic. You should’ve come! Ooh, I’ve heard good things! I’m terrible at sci-fi though, you know me. Give me a good rom-com any day. Thinking about it, we should go to the cinema properly sometime next week. Not just as part of some forced Valentine’s Day outing. Definitely! Fancy going to that new Italian place on Brick Lane? ‘Luigi’s Trattoria’ – Chloe raved about their carbonara. Apparently, it’s proper authentic. Luigi’s? Ooh, sounds good. My bank account is currently weeping, but… carbonara does sound rather tempting. Maybe after I’ve finished these essays. Speaking of which… I’m seriously struggling with this history one. It's all dates and battles. My brain’s just refusing to absorb anything. Oh, I know the feeling. Mine’s on Victorian literature. Trying to decipher all the slang is like learning a completely new language. And the expectations! Professor Davies is marking us down for being "too modern" in our interpretations. Ugh, pretentious. It’s like, we’re living in 2024, love. Let us have our opinions. My writing's been awful this whole semester, actually. I think I need to hit up Primark and buy a new notebook. Maybe a fancy pen will inspire me.

Honestly, I’m just… exhausted. Another article about disproportionate stop-and-searches, another report showing how Black men are more likely to be wrongfully accused. It’s relentless, you know? I know. It's awful. I saw that statistic about the fines issued… massively disproportionate. My lecturer mentioned it in the seminar last week, actually. He was quite scathing about the institutional bias baked into the system. Scathing is good. People need to be scathing! It feels like everyone’s just… accepting it now. Normalising it. Like racism is just part of the furniture. It's frustrating, isn't it? I mean, people  say  they're anti-racist, but actions speak louder than words. And the actions… well, the actions aren’t great. It's not just the police, either. It trickles down. My firm had an incident last month – apparently, a senior partner made some truly appalling comments about a potential client’s cultural background. Oh God, what? Did anything happen? They made him apologise publicly. Some training, a lot of awkward conversations. But the underlying attitude… I don’t think it’s been addressed properly. It’s all surface level, you know? Damage control. Exactly! It’s the performative allyship all over again. Look, I’m not even suggesting that everyone’s a secret bigot, but there's a carelessness, a lack of awareness that allows these things to happen. And then when it  does  happen, the response is so carefully calibrated to avoid any actual systemic change. What did you order? These noodles are surprisingly good. I was a little dubious about the Sichuan peppercorns. Avoiding the bigger problems with noodles, are we? I got the veggie ramen. Always a safe bet. You know, it’s funny. I was just reading about how property prices in Kensal Rise have skyrocketed. My mum's talking about maybe downsizing… moving somewhere cheaper. Really? That's heartbreaking. It feels impossible, doesn't it? Owning a place… it’s a lottery. And the system is rigged against so many people. It is. It's disgusting. Like, how can anyone realistically afford to buy in London? It’s pure capitalism gone mad. Landlords raking in the profits while people are forced into tiny, overpriced flats, or being pushed further and further out. My dad keeps saying “pull yourself up by your bootstraps” and telling me to invest in a BTL – Buy-to-Let.

…and Mrs. Hawthorne just said, "Oh, she’ll settle in lovely, dear. Most of them do." Lovely! As if that makes it any easier, does it? Sending Elsie to nursery feels… monumental, you know? Like I'm handing over a piece of my heart. Aye, I get it. But you were saying she seemed pretty happy playing with the other bairns at the open day. Remember? She was chasing that little boy with the red wellies. She was. But that was for twenty minutes, with me right there. What's she going to do when I'm not? I keep picturing her crying all morning, poor love. I feel terrible already. Mum, you're spiralling. She's hardy. Elsie is a little trooper. And it’s only three mornings a week to start with. You need to get back to work, though. You can't put your life on hold forever, can you? I know, I know. It's just… going back. It feels like a lifetime since I was in an office. All that paperwork, the meetings… Remember how stressed I used to get? I don’t want to go back to  that . Well, you're not going back to the same job, are you? You're doing something completely different now. Freelance writing. You said you enjoyed it when you had a chance to do a bit before Elsie arrived. It's just… everything feels so overwhelming. Nursery, work, the weaning! Good heavens, last night she refused everything. Just pushed it all onto the floor. Pure mashed sweet potato carnage. Oh, Elsie! That sounds like our Gran, actually. She used to fling porridge across the kitchen when she was little. You’ll get used to it. Try different things. Maybe less sweet stuff? And a spoon with a brighter colour? They’re obsessed with bright colours at nursery. That's a good point. Bright colours. Anything to distract her from the fact that Mummy’s leaving. Actually, speaking of distractions… have you seen that new series on Channel 4? The one with the detectives in Copenhagen?  Forbrydelsen ? Yeah! It's brilliant, isn't it? Really dark and twisty. I’ve only seen two episodes. Keeps you guessing. Way better than  Love Island , thank goodness. Honestly, I can't bear  Love Island  anymore. It’s all so manufactured. Give me a good Nordic noir any day. We could watch it together next weekend?

Right, everyone dig in. It's not quite Mum's, but it'll do. Feels a bit surreal, doesn't it? Eating a normal meal after… everything. Surreal is one word for it, love. More like… unsettling. Did you give them a proper statement, Sarah? Everything they needed? I did. It was… difficult. Recounting it all again, details I’d been trying to block out. Poor old Mr. Henderson kept peering at me with those worried eyes. He offered me a cup of tea, like that would fix everything. It must have been awful. Did they ask about the security footage? I remember you saying the pub has cameras everywhere. They did. They're reviewing it, apparently. They seemed particularly interested in the angle covering the alleyway. Said it might show something we missed. Honestly, Emily, I just want it all to be over. They’ll catch whoever did it, Mum. The police are on it. Besides, you did exactly the right thing by going down and giving them your statement. They said it was important to establish a timeline. He’s right, Sarah. Don't beat yourself up. You’re a good witness. Though, I still keep thinking, could we have done anything differently? Saw something? Heard something? Don't go down that road, David. There’s no point in “what ifs.” It happened. And it was… frightening. Honestly, even just thinking about walking past the pub now… You’ll get through it, Auntie Sarah. We all will. Maybe a weekend away? Somewhere quiet? That sounds lovely, Em. But I don’t think I can face packing a suitcase just yet. I just… I need a bit of normality back in my life. Speaking of normality, Dad, any luck with that EE phone bill? You’ve been muttering about it all week. Don't even mention it, Mark. They're saying I owe them another £80! £80! For a data plan I barely use. These companies… they're daylight robbers, I tell you. I spent nearly an hour on the phone to them, and they just kept repeating some automated script. Sounds like my experience with the bank last week. It’s infuriating. You need to escalate the complaint. There are ombudsmen for these things. I know, I know. Just haven’t had the time. Between fundraising and… well, this whole situation, it's been a bit overwhelming.

…and honestly, the rosemary was just  wilting  from neglect. Poor thing. Like, visibly drooping. People don’t appreciate a good herb, do they? They just want instant gratification – pop some dried stuff in a ready meal. Sounds like you rescued it from a tragic fate. Good work, Liam. So, ANON's place is surprisingly…tidy. I expected a whirlwind after a wedding. Yeah, ANON’s always been a bit of a neat freak. Better than some of the chaos I deal with in the gardens, honestly. You know Mrs. Henderson? The one with the prize-winning roses? She throws her pruning shears everywhere. It’s terrifying. Not familiar, sadly. Though the rose bushes here are all looking quite robust. Fancy a cuppa? I made a pot of Earl Grey. It’s got a little ginger in it, gives it a bit of a kick. Ginger, you say? You know me too well. Absolutely. Earl Grey's always good. Did you catch that new Spartacus programme? The one they’re doing now? I’ve seen a couple of episodes. So far, so good. It’s surprisingly historically accurate, at least in terms of the politics. Though I do wonder about the romantic liberties they take. All that rippling musculature... Yeah, well, it’s entertainment, isn’t it? Still, it got me thinking - those Romans. Incredible, really. Building that empire, conquering everything. And all that advanced engineering! Aqueducts, roads... makes you think about how short our own lives are compared to the timescale of history. It does. And the sheer brutality of it all. The gladiatorial contests... it's barbaric by modern standards, of course. Think about all the early deaths, too. Disease, battles... no antibiotics, proper healthcare. Exactly! It's wild. Speaking of brutal, remember that time we tried to make hummus from scratch? Back in sixth form? Used a proper mortar and pestle, the whole shebang. How could I forget? It ended up looking like cement and tasting vaguely of despair. We were convinced we’d used too much tahini. We  did  use too much tahini! I think we also went overboard on the cumin. It was a culinary disaster. It’s much easier to grab a tub from the supermarket now. Although, I'm trying to get ANON into growing his own chickpeas. Apparently, he’s resistant. Claims they’re “too fiddly.” Men and their culinary minimalism. I'm working on getting him to appreciate proper bread.

Honestly, Chloe, this English test is going to be the death of me. Mrs. Davies is just  trying  to fail us, isn't she? All those Shakespeare quotes… I can’t remember which one means what! Tell me about it! I spent ages last night trying to work out the symbolism in  Hamlet , and I ended up just feeling confused and wanting biscuits. Did you do the practice questions? Yeah, but I got, like, half of them wrong. And the ones I  did  get right, I’m not even sure I understood  why  they were right. It's just a load of flowery language, innit? It is a bit. Though I actually found the bit about the metaphors in Coleridge’s ‘Kubla Khan’ quite interesting. Did you find that confusing, too? Coleridge? Oh, yeah, the one with the poem about the dream. Honestly, I zoned out about halfway through. My brain just… stopped. Art’s much better, you know? At least with painting, you can just  do  something. True! I love art lessons with Mr. Peterson. He actually let me experiment with charcoal yesterday - it was brilliant! I’m trying to do a sketch of your mum’s cat, Winston. He’s a proper grumpy looking thing. He  is ! And he bites if you get too close. Speaking of lessons, French is utterly hopeless. Madame Dubois just speaks at the speed of light! I heard her saying ‘le chat mange le fromage’ about ten times in a row. I still don't know what it means! It means "the cat eats the cheese." See? Not that hard when you break it down. We need to actually  study  for French, don’t we? I was thinking we could quiz each other after school on Thursday. Thursday? I'm playing clarinet in the wind band that day. Remember? Mr. Harrison's being all serious about the upcoming concert. He wants us to practice our scales  before  every rehearsal. Scales! Who wants to play scales? It's so boring. Oh right! I forgot about that. You're really good though, you know. Everyone says so. Are you playing that tricky solo in ‘Colonel Bogey’? Yeah, and I'm terrified I'm going to mess it up. Mr. Harrison's got that look on his face, you know, the one that says he's about to give you a withering stare if you play a wrong note.

Aye, lass, tell me about it! They're all obsessed with these “outcomes” and “key performance indicators.” Fancy words for nothing much, really. Makes a body want to chuck it all in and go bake scones. Though I’d need the money for the flour, wouldn't I? Speaking of which, how’s things going with you, Brenda? You looked a bit peaky last time I saw you. Oh, just the usual, love. Worrying about the bills, watching Bargain Hunt… the glamorous life! It's getting harder, isn't it? Everything just keeps creeping up. This café's not bad, though. Nice little treat. And the scones  are  lovely. I got one with clotted cream and jam. Proper Yorkshire indulgence. Clotted cream? That’s posh, Brenda. My gran always said jam was the only proper thing to put on a scone. She’d have a right go at you. Your granny was a woman after my own heart, lad. Strong opinions on everything, that one. You're looking well yourself, Ethan. Still playing footy then? Yeah, Miss Davies says I’m getting faster, but I still can’t beat Liam for pace. He’s got a sponsorship deal now with that new sports drink, 'HydraBoost'. Ridiculous branding, if you ask me. All neon green and flashing lights. Makes you feel like you need a sugar crash five minutes later. Sponsorships. Everything's about money these days. Remember when Footie was just… Footie? Now you've got these millionaires throwing themselves about. I saw a statistic the other day… the average footballer earns more than a doctor! It’s madness. It is, Brenda. Utter madness. And the flags... don't get me started on the flags. Everywhere you look, draped over everything. Honestly, it's a bit much. I saw a fella the other day with a England flag stitched onto his trousers. His  trousers ! My dad’s obsessed with the flag thing. He wears an England shirt, an England hat, even England socks! He’s convinced we’re going to win the World Cup. Says it's "coming home." Coming home, aye. Says it every four years. Never seems to actually  come  home, does it? Speaking of home, I was thinking about visiting my sister in Scarborough next month. Fancy coming with me, Maureen? We could go to the seafront and have fish and chips. Oh, that sounds lovely, Brenda. I'd love to.

Unsettling, is it? You’re a lecturer, love, not a rally driver. It’s a car, not a spaceship! My old Ford Transit, now  that  was a proper machine. You knew every nut and bolt. This newfangled nonsense… well, it'll all fall apart eventually, mark my words. It’s not  nonsense , David. It's progress. And it's a lot quieter than your Transit, which was appreciated by the neighbours when you were tinkering with it at six in the morning. Besides, I need to be sensible about my carbon footprint. Sensible? You’re always sensible, love. Though a bit of tinkering never hurt anyone. Your Grandad used to fix everything, bless him. Remember the time he fixed that washing machine with a bit of string and a rubber band? Speaking of things falling apart, did you hear about Mark’s brother? Had to have a knee replacement already. He’s practically half my age! It's all that dodgy takeaway he's been living on. It’s not just the takeaways, Mark. It's the genetics, too, isn't it? There’s a family history of, well, let's just say robust physiques. Dad’s always blaming my Great Aunt Mildred for it. Apparently, she was a woman who believed in feeding people till they were bursting. Bursting! That's a good one. Reminds me of my Nan. Always had a mountain of food on the table. Said it was a sin to let a man go hungry. Wonder if she was religious? Oh, your Nan was fiercely religious. Methodist, through and through. Believed in hard work, honest living, and Sunday school. And feeding everyone! It was all part of the plan, apparently - a loving heart and a full belly. It's fascinating, isn't it? How diet and genetics interact. We're increasingly understanding the interplay of our DNA and lifestyle choices. The epigenetic effect, you see… Mark, darling, please. It's Sunday dinner. Let’s not launch into a lecture on epigenetics. I’m still recovering from Geoff's surgery, and I don’t need a biology lesson on top of it. Geoff’s doing alright then? That operation sounded a bit hairy. Blimey, all that cutting and stitching... He’s recovering well, thankfully. Bit stiff, but the pain is manageable. The surgeon did a fantastic job, really. Restoring his range of motion. It’s made a world of difference.

Right, so I’ve been wrestling with Moodle all afternoon. Honestly, it's like trying to herd cats. The new assignment upload feature… it’s… challenging. Challenging? That's putting it mildly, isn’t it? I spent a good hour yesterday trying to get the video embeds to work properly. Did you manage to figure out the file size limitations? Partially. It seems to be incredibly arbitrary. One file works, the same file compressed slightly differently? Error message. I've been trying to explain it to the students, but getting them to understand that Moodle's quirks aren't  my  quirks is a battle. They just assume I’ve broken something. Welcome to the wonderful world of online teaching. Remember last semester when half the class swore the quizzes weren't grading correctly because they were browsing on their phones? Don't remind me! That was a nightmare. Still, this is different. This feels… fundamentally flakier. I’ve been looking at the documentation, but it’s drier than the Sahara desert and assumes a level of technical proficiency that… well, that I don't possess. I had a similar issue with the Gradebook integration last year. Remember? I ended up contacting their support team. It took three days and involved a lot of jargon, but they eventually sorted it. Three days! I don't have three days! The deadline for that coding assignment is in a week. These students have already missed a significant chunk of the lectures, so I need them to be able to access that material easily. The last thing I need is them getting bogged down in Moodle technicalities. Well, let’s tackle it together. What’s the specific issue you’re running into now? Show me. You’re trying to upload a .mp4, right? Yes, the demonstration code. It's not a huge file, maybe twenty-five megabytes. But Moodle keeps giving me this error: "File exceeds maximum upload size limit." Which is ludicrous. Right. Okay, let's check the server settings. Have you looked at the 'Allowed file types' section? Sometimes, there's a sneaky restriction there. They’re so fond of hiding things. I have, briefly. It looks fine. MP4 is listed. I thought it was just the overall file size limit. Hmm. Is the 'Maximum upload file size' configured correctly? Have you checked  both  the course level and the system level settings? They don’t always line up.

…and then the gate agent just looked at me like I was insane for asking if they had a quiet area. A  quiet  area in Gatwick at five in the morning. Honestly. Sounds about right. You look like you’ve wrestled a small, grumpy dragon. How’s the jetlag treating you? I thought you were handling time zone changes remarkably well on the flight. Remarkably well until I tried to make a cup of tea and ended up pouring hot water on the kitchen counter. That pretty much signaled the crashing point. Little Leo was a saint, though. Slept through the entire journey. That’s good. Not the counter so much, though. I’ll wipe that down later. Honestly, I’m impressed you managed to sleep at all. I only managed about three hours myself, and that was punctuated by the constant fear that Leo would decide to have a full-blown tantrum mid-Atlantic. He's just so… observant at the moment. Every little thing. A dropped crumb, a slightly off-key hum… he notices. It's exhausting, but also kind of brilliant. Absolutely. He's absorbing everything. Speaking of things he’s absorbing, are you feeling up to tackling the washing mountain? I’ve got a lecture to prep and half the house seems to resemble a particularly chaotic playground. The washing mountain…my nemesis. Perhaps we can bribe him with a particularly exciting rattle to keep him occupied while I wage war on the laundry basket. Right, so, about Saturday... The Alcott Players' production of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' – have you looked at the seating plan? I have! I managed to snag a couple of seats in the second row. Right near the stage. Don’t want Leo throwing popcorn at Puck, though, do we? Definitely not. Although, imagining him trying to follow the plot…a tiny, judgmental face critiquing Shakespeare…it’s quite amusing. I’m hoping the music will hold his attention. I’ve heard they have some lovely folksy arrangements. Fingers crossed. It’ll be nice to get out, won't it? Real people, theatre… something other than baby toys and academic papers. I feel like my brain is slowly turning to mush. Precisely! We’re in dire need of cultured stimulation. Although, I'm slightly apprehensive about leaving him with Mum and Dad for the evening. They're wonderful, of course, but I worry they'll spoil him rotten.

…and then my cousin, Khalil, he’s just… frustrated, you know? He's stuck in Erbil. The paperwork for his family to join him is a nightmare. It’s been nearly two years. Two years! And you hear these stories… bureaucratic delays, people changing documents, corruption... It’s just soul-destroying, isn't it? Aye, heartbreaking. It always is. Bureaucracy, it’s a beast anywhere, but especially when it affects families. Reminds me a bit of my own visa struggles back in the day when I came over here. Remember? The sheer volume of forms. It felt like they  wanted  to keep us out. Still, two years… that's a monumental wait. What's the sticking point this time? Apparently, some detail about Khalil’s wife's birth certificate. They say it doesn't match the school records. Honestly, it's probably just a typo, a tiny thing. But they’re treating it like a national security threat. He’s been paying for lawyers, and even  they  are finding it hard to make any headway. The whole system is rigged, isn't it? Especially when you’re dealing with… you know… places where things aren’t always above board. You ever read about the oil pipelines running through Kurdistan? The politics tangled up in it all? It's a geopolitical mess, isn't it? Don't even get me started! Every drop of oil fuels something terrible. Libya, for example. Look at what happened there. All that fighting, all that chaos… and why? Oil. It’s a curse, really. My uncle still lives there. He’s trying to get out, but the situation is unstable. He keeps saying he'll move to Turkey, but... Turkey’s not exactly a haven these days, is it? They've got their own problems. Although, I wouldn’t put it past my mate, Jurgen, to suggest Istanbul. He and his wife moved there last year. Said the cost of living's better, and the culture's vibrant. He's bringing us over for a visit sometime next spring, apparently. Jurgen? Jurgen Schmidt? Good man, Jurgen. He always had a good head on his shoulders. You think moving house is easy? We’re looking at places now. Trying to decide between St. Helens and Orrell. Orrell’s got more green space, but St. Helens is closer to the city centre. Orrell's alright. Quiet, mind you.

Honestly, the way you’ve managed that lamb, Eleanor, it's practically indecent. Every year it gets better. Just falling off the bone. Years of practice, David. And a little bit of cheat's rosemary oil. Don't tell Mum, she'd have a fit. Nonsense, dear. A little shortcut never hurt anyone. It's absolutely delicious. Though, Eleanor, I do think you’ve layered the garlic a bit thick this year. It's…robust. Robust is a polite way of saying overpowering, isn’t it, Margaret? Precisely! But still perfectly edible. Speaking of edible…Have you got any of that Scottish tablet left, David? The kind your sister sends? I believe I have. A small stash hidden away. Wouldn’t want to deprive anyone. Here you go, Margaret. Oh, thank you, dear. Reminds me of my school days, actually. We used to get a box for Christmas from a local shop proprietor – absolute treasure. You know, this house…it’s charming, Eleanor, but putting the television in the dining room isn’t ideal, is it? What else are we supposed to do, Margaret? It's the only room big enough and with a decent signal. Besides, we mostly watch nature documentaries. It’s educational! And occasionally, terribly dramatic period dramas. Don’t forget those, Eleanor. Point taken, David. But seriously, it works for us. It’s a cosy evening routine. Now, how about some tablet? Very well. . You know, I've been thinking about a cruise. Something around the Mediterranean. Just to see a bit of the world. It’s been far too long since I’ve seen sunshine that isn’t grey. A cruise? Sounds lovely! We’ve been looking at some options actually. A bit further afield than the Mediterranean, though. Thinking of somewhere in the Caribbean. Caribbean? Oh, wow! That's quite a jump from the Mediterranean. Do you think we'd be able to manage the heat? I’m not getting any younger, you know. We'll find something that suits us. Plenty of air conditioning, shaded decks... Plus, think of the rum cocktails! You're incorrigible, David. But yes, that  does  sound tempting. How's your back after that racketball session on Tuesday? Still stiff? A little. I need to get back into my workouts properly. All this good food isn't helping, is it? I’m starting to resemble a roast lamb myself. Don’t be silly, dear.

“Right, I’m starvin’. Honestly, this job search is bleedin’ exhausting. Feels like I’ve sent out fifty applications today, and all I get back is nowt.” “Fifty? Seriously, Liam? You need to take breaks, you’ll burn yourself out. And honestly, have you considered broadening your scope a little? All those warehouse jobs aren’t gonna magically appear.” “Easy for you to say, Ellie. You’re off to uni, livin’ the dream. I’m stuck here, in me mam’s, applyin’ for jobs I’m overqualified for. A graduate runnin’ a warehouse? It’s a joke, innit?” "Here you go, love. Earl Grey, just like you like it. And Ellie, stop peerin' at him. He's allowed to feel a bit down. It's not exactly brilliant out there, is it?" "So, Liam, anything interesting come up today? Besides the endless warehouse vacancies, that is.” “Nah, nothin’. One asked for experience with forklift trucks. Forklift trucks! I’ve got a degree in History, for goodness sake! It’s like they don’t even read the CVs, do they?" “Hey everyone! Tea smells amazing, Freya! Liam, cheers for last week’s help with Leo's reading group - they were so pleased. Made a real difference. And Ellie, how’s that essay coming along? The one on Tudor fashion, right?” “It's… progressing. Slowly. Trying to argue that high-status Elizabethan women basically invented athleisure wear. My tutor thinks I’m mental.” “Athleisure wear? What’s that even mean?” “It’s like… sportswear, but fashionable. Basically, fancy leggings and hoodies. Think Duchesses in joggers, Liam.” “Right, well, that’s a bit mad, that. Freya, you look like you've been up all night.” “Nearly was. Just finished my portfolio for art college. Nerves are kickin’ in, to be honest. It’s a big jump, moving to Sheffield.” “You’ll be brilliant, Freya. Seriously. Your work is amazing. And Sheffield's brilliant. Loads of cool galleries, and don’t forget, loads of people who speak the same language as us! You’ll be home for Christmas, though, right? Mam will have the house smelling of gingerbread.” “Aye, Christmas at me mam’s will be mental. Rest assured, the whole clan will be there, arguing about politics and who’s had the biggest portion of brussels sprouts.” “Speaking of Christmas, has anyone thought about what we’re doing for the Christmas Market this year?

Right, so the sugar’s in, butter’s creamed… these biscuits need to be  perfect  for Year 3. They're making gingerbread men, remember? And we’re doing a little lesson afterward on descriptive language. I need them to be really visually appealing. Will mine have glitter? Please, please,  please  glitter! Glitter! Aye! And a pirate hat! Mine needs a pirate hat! Alright, alright, little pirates. Maybe  some  glitter. A sensible amount though, we don’t want anyone choking. And a pirate hat? Hmmm, we’ll see. We're aiming for gingerbread men, not gingerbread pirates. But pirates are cool! They are very cool. Tell you what, we can draw pirate hats on them with icing. Or maybe give them an eye patch. Eye patch! YES! And a sword! A little gingerbread sword! Okay, okay, you’re giving me ideas! Right, so the lesson. I’m thinking we’ll start by describing them – colours, shapes, textures - you know, "round and brown, with a cheerful smile…” Then they have to give their gingerbread man a name and a little story. Can I name mine Captain Sparklebeard? Captain Sparklebeard it is. Lovely name. What about you, Leo? What exciting name will your gingerbread man have? …Sir Reginald the Brave! Sir Reginald the Brave! That’s brilliant! See? Fantastic descriptive words already. We’ll build on that. Now, I'm a bit stuck on how to get them really thinking about texture. Any ideas? Can we rub them? Rub them? You mean… taste them? Yeah! To see how crunchy or chewy they are! Crunchy! Chewyy! You two are geniuses. That’s  perfect ! A sensory exploration! I love it. Okay, that's settled. We’ll let them taste them – under strict supervision, of course - and then they have to describe the feeling. Crunch, crumbly, chewy… brilliant. Mummy, did you remember we’re having a half birthday party later? Of course, poppet! I’ve got the balloons and a miniature cake. We  have  to celebrate these milestones. It’s been six months since… well, you know. Cake! Yes, cake! And remember what we found in Morrisons yesterday? The one with the sparkly cover!  The Unicorn Who Lost Her Sparkle!  It was so pretty! Exactly! I thought that would be a lovely bedtime story for you both. Do you think Sir Reginald the Brave would be friends with a sparkly unicorn? Yes! They could go on adventures!

Honestly, I’m starting to think Facebook is actively  feeding  me adverts for SUVs. It's ridiculous. Is it really? Or are you just… you know… subconsciously looking at a lot of them? It’s a powerful algorithm, but it's not magic, Ben. I’ve noticed the same with travel brochures – I think about Morocco and suddenly my postbox is overflowing. But it's relentless! This morning, I was reading an article about the rising cost of petrol, and within five minutes, I was being shown ads for the latest Discovery Sport. Seriously! It's like they're in my head. Well, you  did  spend a good hour last week looking at reviews of various 4x4s. Loudly. To the cat. Who was completely unimpressed. He doesn't understand the nuances of torque! Anyway, it just feels… targeted. Overly targeted. It’s a bit creepy. You’d think they'd have more respect for privacy. Respect for privacy? From Facebook? Darling, that’s rich. Remember that whole Cambridge Analytica fiasco? Don’t remind me. Still, it's unsettling. I mean, why do they know I'm even  considering  a new car? Are they tapping into my thoughts now? No, they're tapping into your browsing history and your liked posts. Remember that article you shared about responsible off-roading? Boom, SUV adverts. It's basic data mining, Ben. Perfectly predictable. Although, I do find it slightly amusing you're suddenly so concerned about responsible off-roading. You haven't been off-road since… well, since that incident with the hedge in Dorset. That was a momentary lapse in judgement! And the hedge wasn’t  that  bad. Besides, a proper SUV would have handled it better. A lighter car, struggling through mud… embarrassing. The Discovery Sport has all-wheel drive and hill descent control. It's about safety, really. Safety? Or impressing your colleagues at the university? That’s… completely irrelevant. It's also practical. Imagine the family holidays! Room for the dog, luggage, camping gear… We don’t have a dog, Ben. And we haven’t been camping since 2012. Remember the great slug incident of ’12? I’m never willingly sleeping on the ground again. Okay, fair point about the dog. But think of the space! It’s just… useful. Have you seen the new infotainment system? It’s got everything! Wireless Apple CarPlay, Android Auto… you could stream lectures directly from your phone while we’re… driving.

But why did they just  throw  the meatball? It was enormous! Because, love, it was raining meatballs! Remember? That's the whole point of the film. Everything was food! It's a bit silly, isn't it? It  is  silly. But wouldn't it be heavy? Like, really heavy to be raining? And what about the gravy? Did that just... fall from the sky too? Well, it’s a cartoon, isn’t it? Don't get bogged down in the physics of it all. It's about imagination, and the consequences of, you know, wanting everything you want. Too much of a good thing can be bad. Like when I have too many sweets? Exactly! Like that. You get a tummy ache. They overloaded the planet with food, and then… well, you saw what happened. Floods of marshmallows. Marshmallows are okay even if there's a lot of them! True. Marshmallows are always acceptable. Right, so, my shift at Sports Direct today was… a thing. Absolute chaos. Apparently, there was some sort of big football tournament final on, and everyone wanted replica shirts. I spent the whole time trying to stop lads from ripping them off the hangers. Were they being naughty? Properly naughty. Like, rugby tackling each other in the aisles to get to a shirt. Honestly. I’m thinking of applying for a job at a library. Much quieter. Though, explaining the difference between a fiction and non-fiction section to an eleven-year-old would probably be more challenging than dealing with football hooligans. You could just say one’s real and one’s made up. You're very wise, you know that? Wise beyond your years. Speaking of which, did you finish that essay on Sylvia Plath? Nearly. It’s… difficult. Why did she do that? That's a really big question, love. A lot of people have struggled to understand it. But essentially, she was battling with depression, and she felt trapped. She questioned societal expectations for women, you know? The idea that a woman's only purpose was to be a wife and mother. She was a brilliant poet, but she lived a really difficult life. So, like, feminism? Yeah, definitely. It's about fighting for equality, and challenging those outdated ideas. It's not just about women being angry, it's about fairness. It’s about everyone having the chance to be themselves, without being judged.

Speaker_2 finished, gesturing emphatically with his hands, nearly knocking over a precarious stack of papers on the desk. Speaker_1 adjusted his glasses, a bemused expression on his face. "A shambles, Liam? That's rather…colourful, even for you. You're referring to the current administration, of course?" He spoke with a carefully modulated voice, a slight German lilt layered over his Liverpool accent. Liam grinned. "You know it, Klaus. They’re all at it, aren’t they? Promises, promises. Remember New Labour? Everyone thought Blair was the answer, the man who was gonna fix everything. Said he’d change the world. And look at us now." He shook his head. "Same old story, different faces.” Klaus leaned back in his chair, considering. "New Labour… a fascinating period, actually. From an academic perspective, of course. The reinvention of the party, the appeal to the ‘swing voter’… a remarkable piece of political engineering. Though, I concede, the long-term consequences have been… complicated." "Complicated? That’s one way of putting it! My mate, Terry, he’s a builder, right? He swore by them. Thought they were going to bring back proper jobs, build things up. He voted Labour for the first time in his life. Now he's struggling, bills piling up, can't afford to take the kids on holiday. And who's to blame? This lot!” Liam threw his hands up in exasperation. "There’s always more than one factor at play, Liam. Global economics, for example. It's rarely as straightforward as blaming a single government," Klaus countered gently. "But I understand your frustration. Terry's situation sounds incredibly difficult." "Frustration's an understatement, Klaus! It’s anger, more like it. And don’t get me started on the football. Liverpool's been dire this season." Liam slumped down in the chair opposite Klaus's desk, sighing dramatically. Klaus chuckled. "Now  that  is a genuine tragedy. Though I’d argue politics poses a slightly more significant threat to societal stability than a football team's performance.” "Easy for you to say, sitting up there in your fancy office with your fancy degrees,” Liam retorted, though his tone wasn't unkind. “Football’s a release for people, Klaus. A focus. When things are going badly on the pitch, it just mirrors what's going on in real life. Makes you feel even worse.” “A valid point, Liam. There is a certain… symbolic resonance,” Klaus conceded.

Honestly, this Earl Grey is a bit weak, isn’t it, ANON? You’d think living in London, you’d have access to decent tea. Sorry, Rach! I grabbed it from the corner shop. Bit rushed this morning. Been pouring over these BNC recordings, trying to correlate regional dialect shifts with social media trends. It’s fascinating, really. All these slang terms popping up, influencing everything... Fascinating. BNC recordings? Sounds… tedious. What even  are  BNC recordings? Sounds like something my grandfather would obsess about. The British National Corpus. It’s a huge database of written and spoken language – it's been around for ages, basically. But I'm cross-referencing it with current social media usage. Like, seeing how phrases that were relatively obscure, specific to, say, Norfolk, are now used widely online. It's showing how incredibly fast language evolves. Right. Sounds… academic. I'm more focused on catching up with deadlines. My editor wants a piece on the rise of LinkedIn as a dating platform. Apparently, it's a  thing . A thing? Good grief. I can’t imagine. It seems so… calculated. I tried updating my LinkedIn profile last week. Felt deeply unsettling, like I was crafting a brand rather than showcasing my interests. Exactly! And the photos! Everyone's posing in front of inspirational backdrops with their coffee. I think I’ll just stick to Instagram, for now. At least there, you can filter out the existential dread. Filters… Speaking of Instagram, have you guys seen Maya’s pictures from the Maldives? Absolutely stunning. Crystal clear water, white sand… makes you want to chuck it all and move there. Don’t even start, ANON. I saw them. Makes me jealous, but also… terrified. I still get shaky just thinking about flying. Remember that incident on the way to Spain last year? Oh, Rach! I swear, I need to overcome this fear. I’d love to see the whales in Iceland one day, but… the flights. Ugh. Whales… big… You know, there's this cognitive behavioral therapy thing you can do for flying phobias. You slowly expose yourself to the triggers – start with looking at pictures of planes, then watching videos, then maybe a short flight… Sounds like an ordeal.

…Honestly, Mum, I’m still thinking about getting the whole sleeve done. Like, proper dark ink, you know? Not all that watercolour rubbish. A full sleeve, Finn? Really? …and honestly, I think it's the fennel. People either love it or hate it, but it just gives this stew a depth, you know? It’s a trick my mum taught me. Though, I'm also trying to be more sensible about my health. I really need to get back to those Pilates classes. My back has been killing me. Pilates is brilliant for that. Honestly, the smog tonight is a little better than yesterday. Progress, I suppose. Feels good to be walking though, doesn’t it? After those lectures, I was starting to feel like a robot repeating the same phrases. It does. Though my feet are killing me. Finding decent tea, reliable internet, negotiating with the landlord, and now, finding a podiatrist who speaks English. You’ll manage. You always do. You deserve good evaluations. Anyway, that reminds me... have you heard from Sarah and Liam lately? It feels like ages. Not properly.
