…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails alone this week was bordering on the ridiculous. Three different spreadsheets needing reconciling, a potential merger on the table – it’s just relentless. You wouldn’t believe the pressure. Sounds absolutely draining, Mark. I mean, teaching can be demanding, but it's generally a different kind of stress. Less…corporate. More “please, class, no throwing textbooks this time.” Fair point! Though I imagine wrangling teenagers can have its moments. You still teaching French and Spanish? Primarily. I’ve started dipping my toes into Italian as well, just an evening class. It's lovely, actually, the atmosphere's so much more relaxed than the A-Level groups. Speaking of relaxed, did you see that documentary on Netflix about the Royal Family? Oh, the one about Charles's school days? Briefly. Didn't get around to watching the whole thing. Is it worth the commitment? Surprisingly so! It really shed a light on the pressure he was under. But, you know, then you get into the whole thing about suppressed childhood trauma and…well, you know the internet. All the conspiracy theories swirling! Don’t tell me you're buying into the "he's an alien" crowd? No, no, nothing that extreme! But there’s a lot about his upbringing, that emotionally distant parenting style… it makes you wonder about the ripple effect, doesn’t it? It's tempting to apply those psychological frameworks to everything, isn't it? Absolutely. Human behaviour is fascinating and conveniently complex. Makes for good conversation, doesn't it? Though sometimes I wish people would just stick to discussing football. My wife's gone completely obsessed with that new drama, ‘The Silken Knot’. Apparently, it's brilliantly acted. I’ve heard of it! Is it any good? I’m always looking for recommendations. I'm a bit bored with everything on offer at the moment. Everything feels…recycled. Apparently so. Very stylish, apparently. All those costume dramas seem to be having a moment. Speaking of moments, did you catch Billie Eilish's speech at the Grammys? She seemed genuinely overwhelmed. I saw snippets! It was lovely. She’s so genuine. Unlike some of those manufactured pop stars. You know the ones, all perfectly curated Instagram feeds and manufactured controversies. It's exhausting. Tell me about it. My daughter’s obsessed with that Olivia Rodrigo. All the angst and heartbreak... it's something else.

Dad, are we nearly there yet? My phone’s almost dead, and I’ve run out of data. Nearly there, love? We’ve got another three hours, at least! Where's your patience gone? Remember, Cornwall's a fair bit further than Blackpool. And I’ve already told you, I’ll sort the data when we get to a signal. I know, I know. It’s just...grey. Everything’s grey. Even the fields look grey. It’s a bit depressing, innit? Now, that's not fair. Look closer. See the wildflowers by that hedgerow? Purple and yellow, a bit of red poking through. It's not  all  grey, lass. Think of the beach we're heading to! Think bright blue sea and golden sand! Alright, alright. You’re right. It's just a bit… monochrome. Reminds me of Daphne du Maurier's  Jamaica Inn . All storms and grey skies and smugglers. Did you ever read that, Dad? Aye, a long time ago. Pretty grim stuff, that. Not exactly holiday reading, is it? More like something for a bleak winter evening. Proper spine-chiller. Speaking of bleak, look at those wind turbines over there! Like giant, spinning… well, you know. Like something out of  The Wizard of Oz ! All whirly and futuristic. Do you think they talk to each other? Like clever machines? They probably just moan about the wind, pet. Right. Turn off in about five miles, according to this sat nav. Fancy a break for a chocolate bar? I’ve got some proper Cadbury's, not that cheap stuff. Please! And can we listen to some proper music? Everything’s been classical so far. It’s put me right to sleep. Think I’ll text Chloe, she'll be wondering where I've disappeared to. Fine, fine. But no ear-splitting pop music, mind. Something we can  both  tolerate. You know, it's funny. Back in my day, we didn't have phones. We had telegrams! Can you imagine? “Arrived safe, send chocolate.” Short and sweet. Telegrams? What’s a telegram? Was it like a really old text? Sort of. But even slower. And much more expensive! We had telegraphs too, sending messages in Morse code. Dot, dot, dash… Heard of it? Vaguely. It’s like…a secret language, isn't it? Like in  Sherlock Holmes , when he was deciphering those weird codes. Or Lewis Carroll, with his nonsense poetry.

Honestly, Grandad, you’re accusing me of moving the pieces when no one's lookin’?! It’s Scrabble, not a heist! I swear, you’d think I was tryin’ to steal the crown jewels. Don’t be daft, lass. Just seemed a bit…convenient, didn’t it? That ‘Q’ appearing right where it needed to be. Timperley always had a bit of a reputation for dodgy dealings, you know. Not like Sunderland, respectable folk you are. Dodgy dealings are a family trait, apparently. Grandad nearly knocked over the entire board trying to reach for that 'Z' last round, didn’t he? That was a bluster of wind! Honest to goodness. The wind, I tell you. And you two, fussing about like a pair of magpies! Back in my day, we’d play a proper game. No accusations, no dramatics. Just good, honest competition. Aye, well, back in your day, petrol was tuppence a gallon, Grandad. Things change. So, what did you reckon about the cinema prices this weekend, Leo? They're robbin’ ye blind, aren’t they? Saw 'Barbie' and it cost me a fortune. Proper daylight robbery. Absolutely. £15 a ticket! It's ridiculous. I’m starting to think those classic re-releases are the better option. Less commitment, same nostalgia. Did you see they're showing 'Singin' in the Rain' again? Used to go to the Odeon in Altrincham, that was a grand picture house. 11 pence it was then! Eleven! And the programme was a work of art. None of this sticky floor nonsense you youngsters get. Though, I’ll admit, even then, dear old Mum always insisted on sneaking in a flask of tea. Said the refreshments were overpriced. Sounds lovely. Proper cosy. I wish my flat was cosier. Rent’s gone up again, you know. Absolutely scandalous. It’s like they're plannin' to evict us all. That’s the entire problem with Wincanton, isn't it? Beautiful location, but the cost of living is…significant. I'm lucky, being a consultant, I can absorb it a little better. But you, Anya? Don't you worry about me, Leo. I'm scrappin' along. At least the work's interesting. We’re digitising a collection of local dialects this month. So, you can imagine, with my background, it’s a right good laugh, overhearin’ all sorts of pronunciations. Found a fella from Whitby who said "bath" like "bart."

Honestly, love, this is just what I needed. You look absolutely shattered though. Jet lag hitting you hard? Yeah, Mum. Proper brutal. Managed to sleep for, like, three hours last night. Everything feels…off. Luckily, your chips smell incredible, though. Seriously, I’ve missed your chips. Well, you always did have a weakness for them, didn't you? Thick-cut, proper salt and vinegar. Now, about this move… you’ve got a spreadsheet, haven’t you? You always were a methodical one. I do. It's… extensive. I’ve broken it down into categories: essentials, furniture, sentimental, “might need eventually.” The sentimental pile is terrifyingly large. Mostly books, obviously. Books, yes. And photos. Don't you dare throw out any of those old family albums! Your Uncle George would have my hide. He still remembers every detail from Christmas '87. I know, I know. He has a memory like a steel trap. Better than mine, honestly. I can barely remember what I had for breakfast! Though, I  do  remember that awful weaver fish incident on holiday in Cornwall when I was eight… Oh, don’t remind me! That was traumatic for everyone. You were convinced you were going to die. Little drama queen, you were. Luckily, Dr. Peterson was a dab hand with sea urchin spines. He was! I'd completely forgotten about the spines. I just remember the pain. Anyway, back to the move. I’m starting to worry about getting everything sorted before the lease runs out here. It’s only a month. A month is plenty of time, love. Just tackle it bit by bit. Speaking of tackling things, have you told Sarah about the wedding plans yet? Not properly. We’ve mentioned it, you know, casually. But we haven't set a date or anything. It feels… daunting, to be honest. Daunting? Why? It'll be lovely! You two are perfect for each other. You’re a lucky boy. And Sarah's a gem. She's got your dad’s good sense of humour, you know. I know. That's part of why I love her. She gets my silly jokes. But the whole thing... the invites, the venue, the caterers… it’s a lot. It is, but you’ve got me, haven't you? I’ll help with whatever I can. Don't go trying to do it all yourself. And don’t go spending a fortune!

Aye, it does, love. It really does. Remember when we could pick and choose, do stuff we actually enjoyed? Now it’s all just box-ticking. My little cousin’s doing A-Levels now, and she’s proper stressed. All that pressure… it’s not fair on them, really. You’re hitting the nail on the head. The focus seems to be solely on getting those top grades, regardless of what the students are actually learning or developing. It's a performance metric, not education. It’s just… disheartening to see. And the impact on the arts and humanities? Devastating. Exactly! My mam used to say, "Get a good education, lass, so you can  think ." Not just regurgitate facts. This feels like it's breeding robots, not thinkers. Want another biscuit? There’s ginger nuts. Please. And you’re right about the arts. It’s all STEM, STEM, STEM. They’re ignoring the importance of creativity and critical thinking. Speaking of critical thinking, did you see the report about waiting times at the Royal Cambridgshire? Don't remind me. My Auntie Brenda’s been trying to get a hip replacement for months. Months! She's in constant pain, and they just keep giving her appointments that get pushed back. Honestly, the NHS... it’s just crumbling, isn't it? It is. It’s desperately underfunded and overstretched. The staff are working themselves ragged, and the pandemic just exacerbated everything. It’s a tragedy, really. I'm doing some research on healthcare inequalities, and the data is just… bleak. It’s heartbreaking. You read stories, you hear about it from family... it’s just not right. It used to be the pride of the country, didn't it? Now… Now it's clinging on by a thread. You know, I was talking to a consultant the other day, and he said they're considering rationing certain treatments just to keep things afloat. Rationing? That's dystopian, that is. Absolutely bonkers. It’s just… not something I thought I’d see in my lifetime. Right, that's enough depressing talk for one evening. Let's change the channel. Something a bit lighter. Agreed. What about that gardening show? You were saying you’d been meaning to get some new succulents? Aye, I was! I’m thinking of getting a little Echeveria. They're proper hardy, aren’t they? Unlike my last one, which I killed within a week.

Right, so, lecture this morning was… mental. Professor Davies went  completely  off on a tangent about the Black Plague. Like, we're supposed to be discussing marketing strategies, not the bubonic plague! Honestly. Black plague? Seriously, Liv? You’d think universities would have better things to do than revisit historical pandemics. Sounds right miserable anyway. Proper grim. Liv, you and your history obsession. Though, I suppose it’s a tie-in somehow? Marketing? Panic buying? Think about it, the sheer desperation… Well, he was trying to draw parallels! Said understanding historical consumer behaviour can inform contemporary strategies. Bit of a stretch, innit? Anyway, it made me cough. Keeps happening since I started smoking again. You’re still smoking, Liv? After everything we talked about? You said you were quitting. I  am  trying! It's just… uni’s stressful, deadlines are looming… you know. It's a comfort blanket, alright? A smoky, disgusting comfort blanket. Aye, I get it. Stress does that to ya. Remember when I was chain-smoking before my A-Levels? Mum nearly had a heart attack. At least you eventually stopped, Maisie. Liv, you should seriously consider it. Money’s tight enough as it is, surely? I’m practically living on ramen and instant coffee. Trying to balance student loans, rent, and  everything  else is insane. Tell me about it! I had to pick up an extra shift at the cafe this week just to cover my phone bill. And the landlord keeps hinting about a rent increase. How are we supposed to afford to live?! It’s ridiculous. Exactly! It's all well and good them telling us to “follow our dreams” and “pursue our passions” but how are we supposed to do that when we’re constantly worrying about scraping by? It’s a joke, isn't it? Like, feminism is supposed to be about empowering women, but how are we empowered when we're practically slaves to student debt and low-paying jobs? Totally. And the expectations! You're supposed to be networking, gaining experience, and being totally on top of your game,  and  somehow managing to afford to eat. The pressure's unreal. Honestly, sometimes I just want to chuck it all in and open a tiny bookshop somewhere quiet. A bookshop sounds lovely, Chloe. But then, who’d pay the rent? I’ve been thinking about looking into some freelance graphic design work.

Honestly, this is gorgeous. Like,  really  gorgeous. But I’ve been thinking… about something a bit less scenic. Oh? What's been occupying your mind amidst all this California sunshine, then? Right. So, remember Chloe? From university? We used to be inseparable. Friday night drinks, shared flats, the whole shebang. Chloe… yes, I remember. The one who always wore those ridiculously oversized hats. Exactly! Anyway, I just… don’t really want to see her anymore. And that’s making me feel utterly awful. Is that weird? Not weird at all. It’s perfectly natural. People change, relationships evolve. You don’t have to justify it, really. But I understand it  feels  awful. It's like admitting you've outgrown something. But how do you  do  it? Like, just… phasing someone out. It feels so… unkind. I don't want to hurt her feelings, but I also don't want to pretend we're still best friends when we're clearly not. It’s tricky. There’s a spectrum, isn't there? A blunt conversation can be hurtful, but prolonged pretending is exhausting for both of you. I had a similar situation a few years ago, with Emily from my postgraduate course. Oh? What happened? We were very close during the course, supported each other through the stress and everything. But afterwards, our lives just… diverged. She went into academia, I went into translation and editing. Her priorities shifted, mine shifted. Slowly, I started just being less available. Less responsive to messages. Fewer invites accepted. It wasn’t a massive, dramatic thing. But did she notice? Eventually, yes. She messaged me, a bit hurt, asking if I was okay, if I was still our friend. I answered honestly, but gently. I said that I valued our time together and that I appreciated her friendship, but that my life had taken me in a different direction and I didn’t want to give the impression that we were still as close as we once were. I didn't get into details about why. Simplest is often best. That’s… surprisingly diplomatic. I’m terrible with confrontation. I think I’d end up apologizing for having needs. Don't! You're not apologizing for wishing to focus on other parts of your life. It's completely valid. You're allowed to prioritise your own wellbeing. With Emily, she was initially a little sad, of course.

…and honestly, Professor Davies just kept going on about the theoretical implications for weeks. It was good stuff, don't get me wrong, fascinating even. But I just wanted to  do  something with it, y'know? Apply it. He kept saying, “Patience, Leo, patience!” Like I'm some ancient artefact. Oh, academics. They live in a world of their own, don’t they? All those grand theories floating around, detached from the reality of… well, of everything. It's rather like trying to paint the wind. You can describe it, theorise about its currents, but catching it on the canvas? Impossible. Exactly! It’s frustrating. I feel like I'm just spinning my wheels. I mean, the dissertation’s coming along, but…it's draining. Do you remember when you were doing your Masters, Gran? Was it always this… intense? Intense? Darling, it was a completely different beast! We didn’t have computers! Can you imagine? Research meant spending hours in libraries, surrounded by dust and the smell of old parchment. And the professors! They didn’t believe in hand-holding, let me tell you. If you asked a question they deemed foolish, you’d practically be publicly shamed. Blimey. Sounds brutal. I’d last about five minutes. Still, I guess it builds character. It certainly did! Though I preferred building things. My sculpture thesis... that was the thing that really ignited me. A massive bronze figure, representing… well, it’s rather difficult to explain. Something about the enduring nature of the human spirit, despite all adversity. The critics hated it, of course. Said it was ‘lacking in subtlety’ and ‘overly sentimental.’ I bet it was brilliant. And utterly you. You've always been so… bold with your art. I saw that exhibition at the Tate Modern last year – the one of your earlier landscapes. Stunning. Those were simpler times. Vienna, Italy… soaking up the light, the colours… It was a revelation. That’s why I started painting, you know. Seeing the Duomo in Florence, with the sun setting… I felt… transformed. It sounds incredible. Have you ever thought about going back? A little trip? I've been thinking about it, yes. It’s been… far too long. Perhaps next spring? I’d love to see the cherry blossoms again. They're quite spectacular in Vienna. Although… travelling these days isn’t exactly what it used to be. All the security, the bureaucracy… it’s tiring.

Right, so, we’re realistically looking at another two hours, aren’t we? Which means…gym time is going to be tight. I was hoping to get a good solid two hours in before dinner. Two hours? My dear girl, that's a commitment! And after all that driving? You’ll be exhausted. Are you  sure  you need that much time dedicated to pressing weights? Aye, well, I like to. It’s…it’s good for my head, really. Keeps me focused. Plus, I’m prepping for a competition. Small one, local, but still. And I gotta maintain the strength. You wouldn’t understand, would you? Don't be presumptuous, darling. I may not be regularly hoisting iron bars, but I understand the pursuit of a goal. Though, my goals currently involve finding a decent cup of tea and a reasonably comfortable armchair. Did you want to stop somewhere for a bite to eat before we hit Tarnow? We've got ages to spare. Ages? We’ve got  two hours ! And I’m not sure Tarnow is overflowing with gourmet eateries. Besides, I tried to eat something substantial before we left, didn't I? Didn't want to be feeling faint halfway through a squat set. Speaking of, I'm still annoyed about yesterday. Annoyed? About what? The Polish gym etiquette? The reluctance to share mirrors? No, about that bloke. The one who kept interrupting my set to show off his bicep curls. Said he was "helping" me, that my form was "off." Oh, that sort. The classic gym peacock. Exactly! And it was a bloke! A bloke telling me – a qualified TEFL teacher, mind you – how to lift weights. It’s just… frustrating, isn’t it? It’s always the bloke, isn't it? Thinking they know best. Sadly, yes. A rather persistent and tiresome facet of being female, I'm afraid. Part of the endless background noise. Remember when I was trying to learn pottery? The man running the class kept telling me how to  really  wedge the clay. I knew how to wedge the clay! You and your pottery. It was a short-lived passion. But, yeah, it’s the same isn’t it? They just assume you don't know. They think you’re less capable. It’s ingrained, I think. Centuries of it. And trying to dismantle something so deeply rooted…difficult, to say the least.

Aye, it’s a grand day for it, lass. Proper clear after that drizzle earlier. Though, give it ‘til teatime, I reckon it’ll be chuckin’ it down again. Always does. Yorkshire weather, y’know. Never predictable. That’s the truth of it, Mum. You'd think with all the fancy weather apps they have now, they could get it right. This mug's a bit wonky, isn’t it? The potter really struggles with a flat base sometimes. I keep telling him. Wonky’s got character, love. Much better than those mass-produced things. Feels warm in yer 'and. Reminds me of those mugs Mrs. Higgins used to make at the church fete. Proper thick clay, they were. Used to drink lashings of tea from ‘em. Lashings! You always did drink a lot of tea. Still do! Speaking of, did you want more milk with yours? I got that creamy stuff from Bramley, you like it. Oh, that’s lovely of you, dear. Just a splash. You’re always lookin’ after me. Remember that time I spilled a whole jug down me best blouse? Took half the day to get that stain out. Butter, it was. I do! You were mortified. And poor Arthur trying to help with the towels. Nearly created a bigger mess than the spill itself. Gardening's looking good, isn't it? The roses are putting on a right show. I’ve got that climbing one to plant next to the greenhouse still. What do you think – a ‘New Dawn’ or a 'Gertrude Jekyll'? ‘New Dawn,’ definitely. Smells proper lovely. Gertrude Jekyll used to have a house nearby, y’know, when I were a girl. A grand house, it were. All roses and lavender… I used to dream of havin’ a garden like that. Never did, though. Just a few window boxes, mostly. Speaking of gardens, I saw a huge spider in the shed yesterday. Proper beast, it was. Gave me a right fright! I nearly jumped out of me skin. They’re good for the garden, lass. Eats all the greenfly. Leave ‘em be. Besides, you were fussin’ about those aphids on the runner beans earlier. True, true. Though I still don't like them creeping around. Did you hear about poor Elsie Thornton? She had a terrible fall in her kitchen last week. Broke her hip, she did. Neighbours found her. Awful. Elsie? Oh, bless her heart.

Right, so flights are booked, car hire sorted. We’re actually going to do this holiday, aren't we? I still can’t quite believe it after all the planning. Yeah, Mum! It's going to be amazing. Liam said he’s definitely up for coming along with us to Cornwall. He’s been looking at surf schools. Cornwall, eh? Bit touristy for me, love. Give me a good windswept moorland any day. But, a change is as good as a rest, as they say. Good on you, lass. Sounds lovely. Though I hope you've packed your wellies. The weather can be unpredictable. Oh, definitely wellies, Dad! And layers. I've been warned the sea breeze can be brutal, even in July. Are you excited, honestly? Last time we went away, you were moaning about the lack of a decent pub. Well, I'll be keeping my eye out for a proper boozer, that's for sure. But yes, I am looking forward to it. Seeing you two away from the usual routine will be a treat. It's been a quiet few months here, hasn’t it? It has, hasn't it. Sarah and Chloe are both at that festival in Reading, so we’re a bit adrift without them for a while. They've been having everything planned out in advance, sending us pictures of what they're taking. All glitter and crop tops. Honestly, teenagers! It’s like they’re different creatures sometimes. Still, it's good they're having fun. Did you hear back from Liam about the surf lessons? Yeah! He found one near Newquay – apparently it's really good for beginners. He's a bit nervous, actually. Says he's never really done anything like that before. Footing's a bit shaky. Footing shaky, eh? Sounds like somebody needs a bit of Yorkshire grit! Don’t let him get intimidated, love. Just throw yourself into it. You’ll be riding waves like a pro in no time. I remember when I first started playing the trumpet… Dad, darling, let's not launch into another story about your early musical struggles. We're trying to plan a holiday, remember? It’s brilliant he’s trying something new though, isn't it? It's good for him. It is. It’s just… what if he falls over a lot? He gets really embarrassed easily. Falling’s half the fun, lass!

Honestly, Heath Ledger was  insane  in that film. Like, proper mad genius levels of acting. I didn't realise he was that good. Yeah, he was alright. But I thought Julia Stiles was the real star. The way she delivered those lines, all sarcastic and clever... proper cool. You know, like how Miss Davies is when she’s marking essays? Oh, totally! It’s like she’s got a secret little smirk going on behind her glasses. Though Heath was just… intense. I kept expecting him to burst into tears or something. Did you see the poetry scene? The way he looked at her… Right, yeah, that was good. Bit cheesy, innit? But good. Anyway, I was thinking about that essay we have to hand in for English next week. The one on Shakespeare? I’m properly stuck. Tell me about it! I've been staring at  Hamlet  for, like, three hours and all I’ve got is a headache. All that "to be or not to be" is doing my head in. What are you thinking of focusing on? I was thinking about Ophelia, actually. She gets a bad rap, doesn't she? Everyone’s always blaming her for going mad, but I reckon she was completely driven to it. Poor thing! And the whole misogyny thing… it was bonkers even for then! Ooh, that's a good angle! You could do a whole thing on how the men in the play manipulate her, and how it contributes to her downfall. That’s way better than trying to unravel Hamlet’s brooding angst, that’s been done to death. Seriously! Maybe I'll ask Miss Davies if that's a suitable focus. She always says we need to be original. But then, what are you doing for yours? Still struggling with Hamlet? Still wrestling with the ghost, yeah. I thought about doing something on the revenge theme, but everyone seems to do that. I might try something on the political climate of the time, actually. See if I can link it in to modern politics somehow. Bit ambitious, maybe. Sounds proper hard work! You're always thinking big, aren't you? Remember when you tried to build a working model volcano for Science? Don't remind me. That ended with me covered in baking soda and vinegar all over the kitchen. Mum wasn't best pleased. But it  looked  impressive, for a few minutes!

Honestly, Mum, you wouldn’t believe the debate happening on Facebook about whether posting photos of your children online is ethical. It's getting quite heated. Ethical, is it? Blimey. Back in my day, we just snapped a picture with a Polaroids and showed it to the neighbours. No ethics to worry about, just hoping it didn't come out blurry. Are they having a right old row, then? Facebook, eh? Never got the hang of that. Bit too…flashy for me, I reckon. Always been a simpler man, myself. Not fussed with all that technology. Though, Annie , you always did have a nose for a good gossip. You’d have thrived on that sort of thing! Don't you start, Arthur! I just liked to know what was happening. It's just neighbourly, really. Now, this debate…what about the children’s privacy? That's got to be important, hasn't it? It is, absolutely. Data privacy is a huge issue. And the risk of someone misusing those photos, or even exploiting them later…it's a genuine concern. I try to be very careful about what I post about my niece and nephew, ironically enough, because of what I do. Exactly, Mark. Some people are posting their kids’ every accomplishment, every outing…it’s a whole performance, really. And others are arguing about consent – can you really get consent from a two-year-old? All this modern faff. Reminds me of young Timothy down the road. Always had a bit of a nervous disposition. His mum used to make him wash his hands fifty times a day. Proper fixated, she was. Doctor said it was OCD. Oh, poor Timothy. That’s dreadful. It’s awful when you see a child struggling like that. Remember little Sophie, I used to look after? She had it bad with the sorting. Had to arrange her toys by colour and then size. If it wasn't perfectly ordered, she'd get right distressed. It must be incredibly distressing for the child and the parents. It’s often rooted in anxiety, trying to control something in a world that feels chaotic. I did some research on it for a lecture last year – it’s more common than people realise. It’s fascinating from a cognitive perspective, isn't it? The obsessive thoughts, the compulsive behaviours... the neurological basis… All very well, that, but it just sounds awful.

Honestly, Auntie Carol, you’re making it sound like Grandpa was some kind of getaway driver! A two-seater Triumph Spitfire in Germany? What was he even doing? Oh, don’t you dare mock your grandfather! He was a bit of a whirlwind, that man. He worked for a small engineering firm back then, you know, before he got into self-employment. They were sending him over to Germany to sort out a spot of bother with a new machine build. Said it wasn't working properly, needed his ‘magic touch’ as they called it. Magic touch is right! He nearly ended up selling that Spitfire to a chap in Bavaria! He swore it was a better deal than shipping it back. Luckily, your grandmother talked him out of it, Sarah. Can you imagine? Absolutely bonkers! So, he was just driving around Germany, fixing machines in a tiny sports car? Sounds like a film. Did he speak any German? A smattering. Enough to order a pint and complain about the weather, apparently. Your Uncle Michael told me he used to greet everyone with “Guten Tag! Das Auto ist kaputt!” It was a riot. That's brilliant! My German is atrocious, I practically just point and use Google Translate. I'm trying to learn though, for my trip next year. Thinking of going to Berlin. Berlin’s good. I’ve been a couple of times. You need to check out the flea markets, proper treasures you can find. Though, honestly, Emily, knowing a few basic phrases goes a long way. "Bitte" and "Danke" will get you everywhere. You know, I always thought Triumph Spitfires were rather handsome little things. Always loved the lines. Reminds me of my dad's old Austin Healey. He’d spend hours polishing it, you know. Before he… before he got sick. Oh, Geoffrey, don't start. It’s family time, not a trip down memory lane bringing us all to tears. Remember when you tried to 'restore' that Austin Healey yourself? It ended up looking like it'd been through a warzone. That's not entirely fair! I was young and enthusiastic. Learning curve, right? Besides, at least I gave it a go. Your father just complained about the noise it made. Speaking of noise, remember Uncle Barry's insistence on driving his Morris Minor everywhere? That thing sounded like a badger trapped in a biscuit tin.

…so, honestly, the energy of that Arctic Monkeys gig was just insane. Like, nothing compares to being in a crowd that size, all singing along. Did you ever get to see their early stuff live, back in the day? Nah, I missed all that. Too busy, I suppose. Working weekends at the pub, trying to save up for… well, life stuff. I mean, I  listen  to them. 'Whatever People Say I Am, That’s What I’m Not’ is a classic, obviously. But being  there ? That’s a whole different level. You're grinning like a loon, aren’t you? Totally! It's that visceral feeling. And Alex Turner… his stage presence is just something else. I was thinking, have you heard much about Yard Act? Found them recently, proper left-field stuff, but I reckon you'd appreciate their energy. Yard Act? The name rings a bell… vaguely. I've got a pretty full plate with keeping up with current cooking trends, you know? Gastronomy's moving so fast. I was looking at some new fermentation techniques the other day - kombucha cheesecakes, can you believe it?! Kombucha cheesecake? Honestly, you chefs are taking things to the extreme. But yeah, I get it. It’s relentless. Yard Act are a bit more… shouty, a bit more punk. Proper social commentary. You'd probably like the bass lines, they're pretty solid. Shouty, huh? Maybe. I do enjoy a good bass line. Remember Liam’s drumming? He was always so bloody energetic, even back in school. You think he’s still playing? Last I heard he was trying to get gigs around London. I saw him on Instagram actually, a few weeks ago. Apparently, he’s doing session work now. Lots of indie bands, apparently. He seemed pretty happy. Said he'd finally landed a decent paying gig, which is a relief. Remember how stressed he was about finding something? Yeah, poor bloke. He was brilliant though, always had that natural rhythm. Wish I'd stuck with guitar lessons. I gave up when my fingers got too sore. Ended up in the kitchen, easier on the hands, you know? Fair enough. So, what are you cooking these days anyway? Still at the same place? No, not anymore. Left there a few months back. Managed to snag an internship at The Gurnard, down in Torquay. It’s a Michelin-starred place – madness, I know!

Honestly, this place is a bit of a din, isn’t it? Can hardly hear myself think. Did you order your coffee, love? Aye, Mum. Flat white, like always. It's rammed in here, though. Who’d think a Tuesday could be this busy? Folks needing a pick-me-up, I reckon. Work, school... life, eh? Listen, about Durham next weekend… I've had a look at the Cathedral website. They’ve got a special exhibition on Roman history. Fancy a gander? Roman history? Sounds a bit… dusty, Mum. I mean, I like history, but Roman stuff isn't really my thing. What about going to Eldon Square to get a new pair of trainers? Mine are falling apart. Trainers can wait, lad. This is a chance to see something properly historical! Plus, we can grab a bit of lunch in Durham. Remember that little cafe we found last time, with the sticky toffee pudding? Aye, that was good. But I seriously need new trainers. And I’m nearly out of PS5 games too. We need to add them to the shopping list. Milk, bread, trainers, PS5 game… Always thinkin’ about your needs, don't you? Speaking of needs, I need to sort out the sleeping bags and airbeds for the summer holiday. Still can’t believe we're going to the Lake District! It’s finally happening. It is! I'm already planning all the hikes I'm going to do. Though I’m not looking forward to climbing. My legs feel like lead after football practice. You’ll be right as rain. You’re a strong lad. Did you catch any of the football news? Apparently, Newcastle are seriously considering a new business structure, trying to encourage more local entrepreneurs. Sounds promising. I saw a bit. It was on my phone, waiting for the bus this morning. Loads of people are saying it's just talk, though. Like every other year. Maybe. But it's good to hear, isn't it? Someone’s thinking about the future of the toon. It’s just a shame about the state of the country, really. Did you hear about that report on obesity rates? Shocking. Yeah, it was on the radio this morning. My nan was saying she remembers when everything used to be smaller portions. That’s the truth. Everything’s supersized these days. Speaking of radio, I nearly missed my favourite show yesterday because Liam was fiddling with the dial again!

…and then Professor Davies, bless him, just completely blanked. He started lecturing on the subjunctive mood to a room full of freshers who were actively playing Candy Crush! It was glorious. I’m recording this bit for the linguistics podcast, you know? Gotta capture those moments of academic absurdity. Seriously? Davies? Right, that’s peak Davies. Remember when he tried to explain iambic pentameter using a bouncy castle? Proper mental. So, this podcast – is it going well? You said you were starting it to, what was it, “document the glorious decline of the English language”? Something like that! It’s mostly for fun, to be honest. I've had a few listens, decent downloads, nothing monumental. The workload's the killer, blending it with the instructing. Anyway, what brings a Midlands gent all the way down to Sussex? This flat's looking alright, by the way. Bit minimalist, but, yeah. Cheers, yeah, it’s coming along. Mrs. Thompson - you remember her, our auntie Sheila’s sister? – she's had the baby! Little Emily Grace. A whirlwind, apparently. My mum's positively smothered in nappies. Blimey, that’s brilliant news! Auntie Sheila’s going to be thrilled. I'm so pleased for them. And Emily Grace, lovely name. Honestly, though, I’m still reeling from the fact that you're an Assurance Analyst now. Last time I saw you, you were complaining about the merits of Chaucer in the university library. University feels like a lifetime ago now, doesn’t it? It’s… stable. Pays well. My salary's considerably improved, let’s just say. We’re actually looking at opening a joint bank account soon, proper adult stuff. Sarah's started talking about marriage, even. Marriage! Wow! That’s… significant. So, no sudden urge to become a Buddhist monk then? Because that was a genuine threat back in the day. The lure of enlightenment faded, I'm afraid. Although, the cost of living… it’s brutal. Even with my salary, we’re scrimping and saving. Speaking of money, how's the instructing going? Still feeling the pinch? Yeah, still budgeting like a medieval peasant. Honestly, it’s a constant battle. Keeps me grounded, though, I suppose. Have you thought about moving abroad at all? Maybe Korea? You mentioned it once, about wanting to experience a totally different culture. Korea... I have. Sarah’s not entirely convinced. She's worried about a career break, the language barrier.

I can imagine. It’s so hard to find the right kind of support, isn't it? Especially when you're dealing with something as…raw as losing a parent. And knowing it was cancer… that just adds another layer of… everything. It does. Mum was so… strong, right to the end. Fighting. And then, suddenly, she was just  gone . Ben’s struggling, really struggling. He keeps asking why she had to go. At eight, he shouldn’t be worrying about mortality like that. Oh, poor love. Eight is far too young. How's David coping? He always seemed so close to your mum. David's being… David. Quietly grieving. Trying to be the strong one for Ben, I think. But I can see it eating away at him. He's lost his appetite, and he just sits staring into space sometimes. I tried to talk to him last night, but he just said he was tired. Men, eh? Bottling it all up. My dad was the same. He’d go completely silent when something was bothering him. Stubborn as an ox, bless him. Though he wasn’t dealing with anything quite as devastating as you are. How are  you  doing, really? Don't just say you're fine. Honestly? I’m functioning. That’s the word. Functioning. I have to be for the kids, for David. But underneath… it’s just a dull ache. And terrifying, actually. The thought of navigating life without her… she was my rock, you know? My confidante. Who am I going to call now when things go wrong? I know exactly what you mean. It’s that empty space, isn't it? That silence where her voice used to be. You feel utterly adrift. Remember when Gran passed? It took me years to feel… stable again. It feels even bigger, losing a parent than a grandparent. It’s the fundamental building block, isn’t it? The foundation of everything. Absolutely. And cancer… it’s such a brutal thief. It robs you of so much – of time, of peace of mind, of the future you envisioned. I’ve been thinking a lot about my own health lately, since… well, since everything. Just got a bit paranoid. Don't be silly. It's natural. Anyone would be. Are you worried about something specific? No, not specifically. Just… you hear so many stories. My aunt had a lump she ignored for months, and look where that got her.

But Dad, Liam's mate, Josh, did an apprenticeship with Aston Martin and he’s already earning a good wage! He's literally building cars! See, that’s the key, lad. It depends on the apprenticeship. Josh got lucky, landed a good one. It's about choosing the right pathway. You've got to research it properly. Not all apprenticeships are created equal. And that's what worries me, David. Lots of them are just a cheap way for businesses to avoid paying proper wages and training. Remember that article I was proofreading last week? The one about the surge in ‘sham’ apprenticeships? It was shocking. My uncle did one, Matthew’s uncle. He ended up fixing printers. Said it wasn’t brilliant, but it got him a job. Fixing printers? That’s… not Aston Martin. No, it’s not, is it? But it’s a living. Look, the referendum's complicated things, hasn't it? Companies are thinking about moving, about investing, there's uncertainty. Apprenticeships, for some businesses, might be a way to fill gaps quickly, without the commitment of a full-time hire. It’s all so volatile, isn't it? I was reading about a local company wanting to expand but struggling to find investors. They had a brilliant idea for a sustainable packaging business, but couldn't get the funding they needed. It’s heartbreaking to see good ideas die because of a lack of capital. Sustainable packaging? Like, for fruit and veg? Exactly. Completely compostable, even edible bits in some cases. Apparently, there’s a huge demand. That sounds promising. Perhaps you should look into it, Sarah. You're good at spotting a market opportunity. I’ve been thinking about it. It would require a significant investment, though. Much more than I'm comfortable with right now. I'd need to have proper due diligence done, of course. And a solid business plan. Maybe I could help with the business plan! I’m pretty good at writing essays. You'd be our marketing guru, wouldn't you, son? Though I think you've got more pressing matters. How's tennis been going? Coach says you’re hitting the ball better? Yeah, it's going alright. Mr. Henderson says my serve needs work. He's making me do these drills where I have to aim at a specific point on the service box – it’s boring!

Honestly, this rain is relentless. I was hoping for a glimpse of the Lancashire countryside, you know? Something a bit… picturesque. Aye, it's a bit grim, isn't it? Though, you can't blame the weather, can ya? It  is  Lancashire. Still, hopefully, it’ll clear up by the time we get to Lancaster. At least we’re making progress. How's your mum coping with everything? Not brilliantly, to be truthful. Dad's redundancy really hit her hard. He’s trying to stay positive, applying for jobs left, right, and centre, but… you know the feeling. The constant stress. She keeps saying she’ll bake his favourite Victoria sponge to cheer him up, but even that seems like a monumental effort some days. Blimey, that  is  rough. My nan went through something similar years ago. It’s a proper knock to your confidence, isn't it? Still, he’ll bounce back. Lincoln’s a decent place for opportunities, he'll find something. Did he ever mention what he was applying for again? Mainly project management, things like that. He’s always been good with logistics. It’s just… a bit humiliating, after all those years. Anyway, enough about doom and gloom. We’re off on an adventure! Lancaster! Remember when we used to talk about going to the coast from there? Ooh, Fleetwood! Lovely memories. We should definitely try and squeeze in a trip to Morecambe even, if the rain lets up. Remember that whole cockle disaster? Absolutely shocking. Proper headlines, that was. Don’t remind me! Awful business. And then you'd be guaranteed to get proper fish and chips afterwards, to comfort you. Speaking of memories... I was thinking about Lancaster University, actually. I’m starting to seriously consider doing a Master’s. No way! Really? Which area? I remember their linguistics department was pretty solid. That's fantastic, honestly! I thought you were happy being a research administrator. I am, mostly. But I've been thinking… a master's in applied linguistics would open up so many doors. More research opportunities, maybe even something in sociolinguistics. Thinking about the demographics, speech patterns... It feels like a natural progression, you know? It totally does! Have you looked into funding options? I'm pretty clued up on those sorts of things, being in research coordination. I could have a gander for you. It's a competitive market, mind.

…and then Liam tripped  over  his own feet! Right into the cake! It was champion, honestly. Absolutely champion. "Ooh, look at me, graceful as a swan!" Proper pratfall, was it? Liam’s always been a walking disaster, hasn't he? Remember that time he tried to make Yorkshire pudding and set the oven on fire? Aye, don’t remind me! Mum nearly had a stroke. He swore he followed the recipe exactly. Said it was the oven's fault. Bless 'im. Still, that cake incident at Sarah’s birthday… iconic. She was fuming, though. Said he ruined the picture opportunities. Sarah's always been a bit precious about those photos. Honestly, a bit much, isn't she? But fair play to Liam, he owned up to it, didn't he? And he cleaned it up. Mostly. Mostly being the operative word. There was still buttercream sticking to the ceiling fan. Anyway, speaking of iconic, have you heard anything new from The Howling Wolves? Their Instagram’s been suspiciously quiet. Nah, not really. I thought they’d be gearing up for a summer tour, didn't I? They were practically buzzing about it last month. Did you see that little clip of them recording in the studio? Ben’s vocals sounded proper powerful. I did! I sent it to you, didn’t I? You just ignored me. Typical. You're always listening to that dreary folk stuff. Dreary? It’s  atmospheric , lass! And it’s got proper stories to tell. The Howling Wolves just scream teenage angst. Besides, I’m thinking about getting back into photography, proper serious this time. Might try and catch 'em at a gig, get some shots. Better than your angst-ridden rock bands, eh? Photography? Seriously? Thought you were going to take up pottery. Remember all that talk about wanting to "express your inner artist" with clay? Let’s bury that memory, shall we? Turns out, I’m not as artistically gifted as I thought. My pots looked like something a badger coughed up. Photography feels… different, though. I actually see something worth capturing. Fair enough. What about Hannah and Tom? Have you heard from them? They were going on that camping trip to the Lake District. Last I heard, they were battling a swarm of midges the size of small birds. Hannah sent a frantic text complaining about her face being eaten alive. Said Tom was attempting to build a shelter out of pine cones.

Right, that’s it! I'm putting a research station in Atlanta. It’s the logical hub, everyone knows that! Rhys, honestly, you're so predictable. Atlanta's obvious. We need to be thinking strategically. I'm putting mine in Cairo, preempting outbreaks in Africa. It's a much more proactive approach. Proactive? You're playing defensively, Chloe! This isn't about thwarting outbreaks; it’s about containing them. London’s a better bet, massive pop, easily quarantined. Besides, I need to be close enough to get a decent curry later. London's already got a disease hotspot, Ben. Remember last turn? It’s looking precarious there. Cairo makes sense, Chloe. Now, now, children. Let’s not bicker. Remember what happened last time we argued about strategy? We lost. Miserably. We need to work together, like a good team. My station's going in Tokyo – high population, good infrastructure, and plenty of fish. Can't go wrong with fish. Your priorities, Dai, are always... distinctive. Fish are vital, I suppose. Elaine, darling, you're overthinking it. Just put it somewhere useful. Somewhere we can actually  reach  with our actions. Useful, according to whom, Bronwyn? Your definition of useful and Dai's clearly differ drastically. And Rhys, calm down. It's just a game. Although, admittedly, a thrillingly stressful one. It’s not  just  a game! It’s a pandemic survival simulation! The stakes are, you know, theoretically high! Besides, Atlanta is strategically vital for transport. Transport? When the world’s falling apart, who’s flying anywhere, Rhys? We'll be huddled in cottages, rationing biscuits! Actually... biscuits. Anyone want a biscuit? I brought a tin of shortbread. Always thinking about food, aren't you, Ben? I'll have one. Thanks. Shortbread! Wonderful! A little sugar will do us good. It’s all getting a bit tense, isn't it? Reminds me of the flu epidemic in '68. Caused absolute chaos. People hoarding tangerines, you wouldn't believe it. Okay, okay, back to the game. I've got Cairo. Anyone else need to place a station? We’re already getting hits in South America. I'm putting mine in Buenos Aires. Keeps an eye on that quarter of the globe. Elaine, dear, you're right, it’s all a bit stressful. Don't let it spoil your holiday. Right, so Cairo, Tokyo, Buenos Aires... We're leaving Europe a bit exposed, aren’t we?

Right, so, pantomime sorted then! Little Poppy and Finn are absolutely buzzing about the CBeebies one - "Jack and the Beanstalk," wasn't it? Yes! The giant’s big! And funny! He's scary! He’s supposed to be a  little  bit scary, Finn, but it’s all pretend. Remember, it's just actors. And Poppy, you loved the singing, didn’t you? You were trying to do that “Fee, Fi, Fo, Fum” all morning! Fee, Fi, Fo, Fum! I smell the blood of an Englishman! Bless you, love. You're getting the words a little muddled there! That's a very old saying, you know. From the story! We'll go over it again before we go. Anyway, it's next Saturday, right? I’ve booked the tickets and arranged for Mum to pick up the kids from school – you two can have a little treat after. A treat? Ice cream? Maybe! We’ll see how well behaved you are, won't we? Now, speaking of birthdays... Finn, yours is just around the corner, isn't it? The 18th of June. Nearly five! Nearly five! Crikey, where has the time gone? We need to start thinking about that. Poppy’s was lovely last year, but five is a big milestone, isn't it? Any ideas what you'd like to do? Dinosaurs! A bouncy castle! And cake! LOTS of cake! With dinosaurs on it! Dinosaurs and bouncy castles, right. That's a wish list and a half! We might have to compromise a bit. Comberton Village Hall is still available, isn’t it? We could do a dinosaur theme, definitely. And Nana said she’d be happy to bake the cake. She's promised a three-tiered chocolate explosion! Three tiers?! Wow! Cake! Now, bearing in mind it’s summer, we could do something outside too. Perhaps a picnic in the park afterwards if the weather's nice? We can't rely on it, of course. Typical British summer, wouldn’t you know. Remember last year’s World Book Day picnic? We had torrential rain! Rainy picnic… It was a little bit of a disaster, I’ll admit. But we made the best of it! We huddled under the gazebo reading “The Gruffalo.” It was actually quite cosy, in a strange way. Shows you what a good story can do, doesn’t it? It’s amazing how even a rainy day can be enjoyable with a good book.

Honestly, I still can’t believe you’re actually going through with it, Ben. Moving to Birmingham? It seems so… drastic. Drastic? I wouldn't call it drastic, Sarah. It's a logical progression. The job at the robotics firm is incredible. Significantly better prospects, better salary… massively better than what I'm doing now with this tiny engineering consultancy. Plus, the cost of living is a lot more reasonable. My flatshare in London was bleeding me dry. Logistical nightmare, though, isn't it? Boxes, paperwork, saying goodbye to everyone… It’s a huge upheaval. It is. I’m trying to break it down into manageable chunks. First the job secured, then the flat hunt – which is proving surprisingly difficult. Birmingham’s a popular place, apparently! Then the dreaded packing. And your family? Are they happy about you going so far north? My mum's been a bit dramatic, as usual. Crying, saying I’ll never see her again. My dad's just practical; asking about the commute and the football teams. You know him. Very Dad. Listen, about the flat hunting - have you looked at Edgbaston? Apparently, it's got some lovely areas, quite leafy. Might be a bit pricier, but worth a look. I’ve had a quick glance. My budget’s a bit tight, but thanks for the tip. It’s the whole transport thing that's worrying me most. London’s so interconnected. Well, Birmingham’s got a decent rail network, doesn't it? Though I haven't been in years. You'll adapt. It'll be an adventure! What about dating? Are you planning on hitting up the Bumble scene? Don’t even mention it. My last experience with internet dating was… memorable, in all the wrong ways. Turns out, “enjoys hiking” can actually mean “shares pictures of their feet in hiking boots.” Oh, Ben! You are a caution. It  is  a minefield, though. I’ve had a few... interesting encounters myself. Tell her, Chloe! You always have the best stories. It's a long story, involving a man who claimed to be a professional mime artist and a surprisingly aggressive pigeon. Let’s just say I’m sticking to meetups for language exchange for now. Safer that way. A mime artist, seriously? See? It’s a disaster waiting to happen. I'm leaning towards focusing on the job and settling in first. Then,  maybe , cautiously dipping a toe back into the dating pool.

…and then little Timmy, bless his heart, tried to build a fort  inside  the paddling pool! It was utter chaos. Honestly, Mum nearly had a heart attack. Remember those paddling pools, Sarah? The ones with the flimsy plastic sides that collapsed the moment you sat in them? Oh, absolutely! We had a blue one, didn’t we? And my dad would spend ages inflating it with that ridiculously loud hand pump. The neighbours probably thought we were summoning aliens! It’s funny the things you remember. I was just thinking earlier, about those Spirograph toys. Do you recall? Hours spent making those complicated patterns… Spirograph! Yes! I had one! Mine was pink, with all the little gears and coloured pencils. I was obsessed. Used to make cards for everyone at Christmas. My mum used to complain I only ever drew spirals, though. She said I needed to draw proper Christmas trees. Proper Christmas trees? Your mum was a stickler for tradition, wasn't she? Mine was more... ‘as long as you’re happy, love’ kind of woman. Though she did have a thing for doilies. Everything had a doily under it! Seriously. Even the TV remote. Doilies are making a comeback, you know. I saw a lovely set in a vintage shop the other day. They’re quite chic, in a retro sort of way. Anyway, back to childhood... I wonder if my daughter even knows what a Spirograph is these days. Everything’s iPads and apps and… well, it's very different. It is. My nephew is the same. He tried to explain ‘Fortnite’ to me the other day. My brain just short-circuited. It’s a whole new language, isn’t it? Speaking of languages… Sarah, you always had a way with words. Even back then. Always loved hearing you tell stories. That’s kind of you to say, Emily. I think it came from my dad. He was a history teacher, you know, and always reading. He used to recite poetry - Kipling, mostly. I’d pretend to listen, but I was probably more interested in what was for tea. It’s funny how dialects change too. I’ve lived in London for ages now and people pick up on the slight…well, something different about my accent. Gets labelled as ‘posh’ sometimes. Honestly? Sarah, your accent is lovely. It’s just… clear. No offence to anyone, but you can actually  understand  every word you’re saying.

Speaker_3 finished, chuckling heartily. Speaker_2 : "Seriously, Mum? Seagulls that big? Sounds like something out of a David Attenborough documentary, not Scarborough!" He grinned, taking a sip of his tea. Speaker_1 : "Scarborough! That’s where Dad wanted to go, wasn’t it? He was going on about the sea air and the donkey rides for weeks.” Clara said, smiling at Speaker_4 , her father. Speaker_4 : “Donkey rides are timeless entertainment, Clara! Don't you mock me. And the sea air  was  lovely. cleared the cobwebs, it did. Though I was hoping for a bit less… aggressive birdlife, as Maureen so eloquently put it.” He leaned back in his armchair, a contented sigh escaping him. Maureen: “Aggressive is putting it mildly! One landed on the table at the café, David,  on the table!  And stared at us. Like we owed it something.” She emphasised the point with a dramatic wave of her hand. "They were absolute terrors! We had to eat our fish and chips  indoors  to avoid becoming victims.” Liam: "Fish and chips indoors? That practically defeats the purpose, doesn't it?" He chuckled. "Did you manage to see any decent football while you were away? Any highlights?" David: “Not really, lad. The telly was patchy in the B&B. Mostly just talked to Maureen about the footy, mostly complaining about refereeing decisions, as is tradition.” Clara: “Speaking of traditions, did you buy any cheesy seaside souvenirs? Keyrings with plastic crabs? Anything?” She asked with a playful smirk. Maureen: "Now, don't you start, love. I bought us all something. Wait 'til you see!" She reached into a large tote bag and pulled out four small, brightly coloured boxes. "Yorkshire Pudding Mix! I thought we could have a proper Yorkshire Pudding Sunday. It’s a bit of a change from your usual scrambled eggs and toast, Liam." Liam groaned good-naturedly. “Yorkshire Puddings! That’s… ambitious, Mum. Especially for me. You know how I feel about culinary adventures.” David: “Don’t be daft, Liam. Yorkshire Puddings are a staple! Maureen makes a cracking one.” Clara: “I’m in! Yorkshire Puddings sound amazing. Especially if you make your gravy extra rich, Dad.” Maureen: “Right then! Sunday it is. So, apart from the avian assaults and questionable entertainment, how was the seaside, David? Did you get to walk along the beach? Margaret ever manage to relax?" David: “The beach was grand, Maureen. Lovely and sandy. Margaret… well, Margaret managed fifteen minutes of peace before she started worrying about whether she’d remembered to turn off the iron back home.”

Honestly, this Earl Grey is a bit weak, isn’t it, Anon? You’ve let it steep for, what, thirty seconds? Sorry! Brain’s still a bit fuzzy. Saturday morning pancakes require a different level of concentration, you know. It's a serious business. And I’m using proper clotted cream this time, just to elevate things. Clotted cream? Fancy. I'm just hoping I can get a signal on this blasted thing. Keep dropping. Says I've got three bars, then poof, gone. It’s infuriating. You’re still struggling with the phone situation, then? Maybe you should just bite the bullet and upgrade. You know, finally get a 5G handset. Upgrade? With what, exactly? I'm patching up the boiler again next week. That's going to take a chunk out of the budget. It's a nightmare, honestly. I spent half of last night covered in soot, trying to trace a leaking pipe. Engineering is brilliant in theory, right? But in practice... it’s mostly grime and frustration. There you go, sunshine. Fuel for the fight. And don't be so hard on yourself. You’re good at what you do. You keep those heating systems ticking over for all of us. Seriously. You’re a vital cog in the Birmingham infrastructure machine, Liam. Don't downplay it. Besides, you were telling me about that new project at the university, the one with the sustainable energy focus? Sounds pretty exciting. It  could  be exciting. Lots of theory, not a lot of practical application yet. They're keen on these hydrogen fuel cells, but the efficiency is still… well, let's just say it's a challenge. It's a world away from fixing a leaky pipe in someone’s kitchen. Well, both are important, aren't they? So, Zara just sent me a picture of her and Miles in Barcelona. They look ridiculously happy. Oh? Barcelona? That escalated quickly. I thought they were still deciding if they liked each other. Apparently, tapas and sunshine have a powerful effect. She's glowing. Though, she did mention something about Miles trying to order a paella entirely in pigeon French. Bless him. He's always been a bit hopeless with languages. Remember when he tried to order a coffee in Italy and accidentally asked for a plate of snails? Classic Miles. You’d think with Zara being a language teacher, he'd put in a little more effort!

Speaker_1 exclaimed, gesturing wildly with a forkful of chips. Speaker_2 , her partner, chuckled. "Sounds about right with that satnav. Mine directed me into a field once. A  field , Elara! I was covered in mud." Speaker_3 , Liam’s cousin, nodded vigorously. "Yeah, they're useless, innit? Google Maps is better, generally. At least it shows you the roads." Speaker_4 , a burly man with a Liverpudlian accent, leaned back in his chair, a wry smile playing on his lips. “Google Maps, eh? Used to rely on the road signs meself. Can’t go wrong with a good old-fashioned road sign. Builds character, it does.” "Character like, risking ending up in the wrong country?" Elara retorted, rolling her eyes playfully. "Seriously, Dad, you're living in the past! We're going to Saudi Arabia next month, remember? You  need  a decent GPS. No road signs in Arabic are going to help you." Reg raised his hands in mock surrender. “Alright, alright. Just saying. It's a big change, going to Saudi, lass. Proper different, that. You’ve both been studying, got your good jobs, but it’s a different world out there. Make sure you keep your wits about you.” Liam chimed in, "It's just for a year, Reg. It's a great opportunity for Elara's administration work, and I can pick up some serious project coordination experience. They’re really impressed with my skillset.” He puffed out his chest a little. Josh snorted. “Sounds fancy. You’ll be sweating in a suit, while I’m still here digging ditches.” “Hey, there’s nothing wrong with honest work, Josh,” Liam retorted good-naturedly. "And you're saving up for that motorbike, aren't you? Plenty of travel to be had on that, without going to some foreign desert." Elara interjected, "Don't knock it, Josh. Liam's working incredibly hard. And Saudi's no desert to be feared. It’ll be an adventure. Plus, the money will be amazing. We're planning to redecorate the flat when we get back; new kitchen, definitely." "Decorating, eh?" Reg grinned. "Now that's something I know a thing or two about. Just scrapped together the loft conversion last year myself. Proper graft, that was. Took me six months." "You did, didn't you?" Elara said admiringly. "You're a legend, Dad. I’m going to need your advice when we tackle the kitchen. Liam's got some grand ideas, but I want it to be… cozy.

Honestly, this is just… balm for the soul, isn't it? After a term with Year 8s, I need this. Utterly vital for the sanity. Absolutely, Sarah. Stockholm's a good shout for a family break. Bit pricier than the Algarve, mind you, but the air's cleaner. And the gardens… incredible. I wasn’t expecting this level of botanical artistry. Did you know these rhododendrons are a hybrid called 'Pink Perfection'? Quite a name. Pink Perfection is a bit of an overstatement, isn't it, James? They’re lovely, don't get me wrong, but I’ve seen more flamboyant varieties. Still, the scale of this place… impressive. I’m just hoping they've got some good hand sanitizer dotted around. This pollen's doing a number on my allergies. Allergies, eh, Fiona? Still battling the hay fever? You really should try that local honey I bought you. Apparently, it desensitizes you. Remember what the doctor said? I know, I know. "Gradual introduction, Fiona, gradual introduction." I bought a jar, didn’t I? And promptly ate half of it in one go. Didn't help. I’m considering a full-on allergy test. Maybe I’m reacting to something beyond pollen. It’s just a constant tickle and itch. Ugh. You're rather dramatic, as always. Anyhoo, how's your shoulder feeling? Still stiff from that fence post weeding debacle? It's...better. Resting and the ice packs. The physio exercises are a pain, though. Feels like I'm trying to dislocate my own arm. I should probably be doing them  more  frequently, but… you know. Prioritizing. You always do. You prioritize the business over everything. You have to be careful, darling. We don't want you ending up like my Uncle Arthur, who tried to prune a rose bush with a chainsaw. A chainsaw? Seriously? Seriously! Landed him in hospital with a rather nasty gash. Moral of the story: hire a professional. Speaking of, have you looked into someone to manage your Auckland property? It’s been vacant longer than you’d like, hasn’t it? Yes, and it's impacting your cash flow, James. You need to be thinking about that. Apartment management software – have you investigated that? It can streamline things significantly.

"Modern technology, eh? Always causing trouble. Remember when you just had to dial a number and hoped for the best? No voice recognition, no fancy algorithms messing about." He chuckled, a dry, rattling sound. "It’s the way you talk, love. Your accent’s getting thicker. All that time studying up in London probably smoothed it out a bit, didn’t it? But now you're back in Kent and it’s come roaring back." Brenda’s voice was warm but direct, the Essex lilt evident. Chloe: “Well, yeah, probably. I guess I've been talking to Liam more. He’s got a proper London accent these days, it's weird. Makes me feel even more like a country bumpkin sometimes.” "London accents just sound…pretentious, innit?" Mark grumbled, picking at a loose thread on the sofa cushion. "All posh and clipped. Sounds like you’ve got something important to say, but you’re trying not to." "Now, now, Mark. Don't be like that. London's a grand city." Chloe: “It is, but…Liam’s mum keeps giving me looks, you know? Like I’m not ‘proper’ enough for him. It’s just…a lot." She sighed, slumping further into the armchair. "And then there's the custody thing. Sarah's lawyer keeps pushing for stricter visitation rules." "Oh, that’s rough, dear. How’s Sarah doing? Is she handling it alright?" Brenda’s tone softened with genuine concern. Chloe: “She's…resilient. But it’s hurting her, obviously. Seeing me argue with Liam’s mum over every little thing. It's not a good look for either of us." "Boys. Always causing bother. Remember when your dad and I used to… well, never mind. Best not to go there." He trailed off, a shadow crossing his face. "Speaking of bother," Mark said, abruptly changing the subject, "Did you see that new mattress they’ve got in the spare room? It's practically a waterbed. Mum’s putting on weight, isn't she? Not that I’m judging, just…that mattress looks uncomfortable for everyone else." Brenda: “Mark! That’s not a nice thing to say! I'm just getting a little…comfortable. So what? At least I’m trying to stay active. I’ve been riding my bike down to the shops every other day.” Chloe: "You are! That's brilliant, Brenda. Seriously. I need to get back into cycling, actually.

Right, so, Baked Alaska. Seriously, Dad, how do you even  make  one? It sounds… mad. Like, molten ice cream on meringue? It doesn’t make any sense! It does, actually, once you understand the science of it. The meringue insulates the ice cream, stopping it from melting too quickly when you torch it. It's all about rapid temperature change. It’s surprisingly straightforward, really. I made one for your cousin’s wedding, remember? Vaguely. It was a bit… dramatic, wasn't it? All that flaming sugar. Did Aunt Carol nearly set her hair on fire again? Thankfully not this time. Though, she did complain that the meringue was a bit "crunchy." Honestly, some people! It’s meringue, it’s  meant  to be a little crunchy. What about you? Are you grating the cheese for the lasagna? Nearly done. This cheddar is seriously hard though. My knuckles are killing me. Why don't we just buy pre-grated? Because pre-grated cheese is disgusting! It's dry and dusty and doesn't melt properly. Freshly grated cheese makes all the difference. It's a labour of love, darling. Much like this lasagna. Speaking of labour, got any thoughts on the potential candidates for the marketing team? I'm still sifting through the applications. Oh. Right. Work. Um, well, you said you wanted someone with social media experience, right? Like, proper TikTok savvy? Exactly. Someone who understands algorithms and trends. The last candidate was all talk and no substance. Said they knew “a bit about TikTok” - their account had three followers and consisted entirely of blurry cat videos. Sounds about right. My mate Liam’s got a pretty decent TikTok. He does those… dance challenges? Does he, now? And is he employable? Has he got relevant experience? This isn't a popularity contest, you know. Come on, Mum. He's good. He’s actually getting sponsorships. And he's a good worker, generally. He helped me build the set for the school play last year. School play? Right. Well, I suppose getting to see his set building skills would be helpful. It's crucial we find someone who understands the importance of attention to detail. It reminds me of Uncle David trying to build that bird table… A complete disaster. He swore he was a carpenter. Oh god, the bird table! Remember when it collapsed the first week and buried Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning roses?

Honestly, Bronwyn, you wouldn’t believe the state of the bins this morning. The seagulls had  really  gone to town. It was like a feathered feeding frenzy out there. Could practically hear them squawking their delight. Aye, they're a right nuisance, aren’t they? Shipley were bad for ‘em, but nothin’ like this. More people here, more scraps, more gulls. Still, it’s a good sign the bins are gettin’ emptied regularly, eh? Last time I was down here, I thought they'd forgotten about our street completely. They did! For weeks! I was starting to feel a responsibility towards the refuse myself. It was awful. Anyway, enough about the bins. Did you hear back from the flying school about your introductory lesson? I did! Just this morning. They’ve got a slot for me next Tuesday. Early, mind. 8 o’clock. Said it's best to beat the wind. I’m a bit apprehensive, mind you. Up in the air… well, it’s a long way down. But I’m determined to give it a good go. Always wanted to fly, you know? Even considered joining the Women’s Auxiliary Air Force back in the day. Really? You? Little Yorkshire lass, battling it out in the air force? I can totally see it! Though, I bet your mum would have had a fit. She would have! She’d have been worryin’ herself sick the whole time. “Ethel, are you safe? Are you airborne? Are you not fallin’ out?” She was a worrier, my mum. Blessed her cotton socks. Speaking of worrying, are you still getting grief from your sister about that photo you posted of the daffodils? Don’t remind me! She said it was “flaunting” Wales, like I wasn’t Welsh enough already. Honestly, some people. It was just a nice photo of daffodils, Margaret! It was springtime! She's just bein' a bit thick, love. Typical Margaret. Always lookin' for somethin' to grumble about. You should just ignore her. Block her if you have to! Social media... it brings out the worst in folks, doesn't it? Remember when you tried to start that online book club? Don’t even. The passive-aggressive comments about genre choices... the arguments over posting schedules... I closed it down within a week. It was less about reading and more about proving who was the most 'literary'. It was exhausting. Do you ever actually write  letters  these days?

Speaker_1 chuckled, pushing a Scrabble tile around with his finger. Speaker_2 : "Oh, Liam! Seriously? Again? You're practically a legend for tardiness at Cardiff. What was it this time? Overslept?" “Nah, worse. I was trying to understand the etymology of the word 'serendipity'. Had this massive rabbit hole of research on the Persian origins, and completely lost track of time. It’s a fascinating word, though, isn't it? Pure chance leading to something good." Speaker_3 : “Fascinating waste of a morning, you mean. You've missed half the lecture on Victorian Landscape Architecture. You could have at least grabbed a coffee.” Speaker_4 : "Victorian Landscape Architecture? Sounds delightful. Is that part of your course, Liam? Thought you were doing something with linguistics or something?" "It  was  linguistics! But I switched. Figured I needed something a bit more…visual, you know? All those words can be a bit overwhelming. Besides, landscape architecture is surprisingly linguistic. So much depends on the careful choice of words and phrases to describe a space." Chloe: "That's actually quite clever. Speaking of words, I was reading about the spelling of 'queue' the other day. Why is it spelled that way? It sounds nothing like it looks!" Ben: "French influence, obviously. It comes from the Old French 'cue', meaning tail. It's rather delightful, really, the evolution of language." He placed 'QUITE' on the triple word score. “Boom! 27 points.” Sam: "Show off. Seriously, you’re a Scrabble beast, Ben. How do you do it? I swear, every time we play, I get stuck with 'xj' and 'qu'." Ben: “It’s pattern recognition, mate. And knowing your two-letter words. That's key. You focus too much on the big words. Small, strategic placements are what win you games." Chloe: "He’s right, Sam. Ben’s like a Scrabble ninja. Liam, you're no help. Still obsessing over word origins I presume?" “Just thinking! It’s connected, see? Like, have you noticed how many children’s book authors have such a flair for language? Roald Dahl, C.S. Lewis... They play with words in such fantastic ways." Sam: "True. My niece is obsessed with 'The Gruffalo' at the moment. That rhyme scheme is brilliant. It really hooks you in." He looked at the board. “I’m going for 'ZEAL' here. That’ll get me a few points at least.” Chloe: "I remember loving 'The Magic Faraway Tree' when I was little.

Honestly, Arthur, you've been staring at that robin for nearly an hour. It's just a robin. They’re everywhere this time of year. Aye, but 'ee’s a right handsome one, Brenda. Look at 'is breast, all bright red it is. More vibrant than usual, I reckon. Might be a young 'un, fresh off the nest. You always did have a soft spot for the birds. Remember when you tried to build that birdhouse shaped like a miniature windmill? That was… ambitious. Ambitious is one word for it. Ended up lookin' more like a wonky shack, didn’t it? Still, the tits moved in. Blackbirds too. They weren't overly fussed about the architecture, see. Just wanted shelter. They did, bless them. Though I was forever shooing the squirrels away. They were trying to dismantle the whole thing, piece by piece. Like little furry vandals. Did Mrs. Higgins ever come round to see about the garden club again? Nah. Didn’t see 'er after that scare with the wasps. Said she weren’t takin' no chances. Shame, really. Her roses were somethin' special. Better than mine, naturally. I can’t seem to get the hang of them thorny things. Always pokin’ me. You’re a bit clumsy with your hands, aren’t you, dear? Still, you manage perfectly well with a cup of tea and a biscuit. I made shortbread this morning, you know. Still warm. Shortbread, you say? Now that’s a proper treat. Better than that dried-up flapjack you tried to pass off last week, anyhow. Tasted like cardboard. Oh, don’t be dramatic! It needed a bit more syrup, that’s all. I’m still learning, even after all these years. Did you hear from young Thomas? He hasn’t called in ages. No, haven’t 'eard from 'im. Started gettin' a bit distant, that boy. Always busy with 'is... computer things. Says he’s workin’ on some new program or other. Don't seem to 'ave much time for 'is old dad anymore. Young people today. Always glued to those screens. I used to worry about the children I minded, spendin' too much time watchin' telly. Now it’s all phones and computers. Progress, I suppose. Though sometimes I miss the days of skipping ropes and playing hopscotch. Aye. Simpler times, weren't they? Didn’t ‘ave all this… technology. Used to spend me days down the river, fishin’.

Honestly, this is a feast! You've really outdone yourself, ANON. This roasted butternut squash is incredible. Did you add nutmeg, I think I detect a hint of it? Indeed I did, love. A good pinch. Used to make a similar thing for the board meetings, you know. Bit of autumnal cheer to brighten up a gloomy London day. Though, truth be told, I never really enjoyed the meetings themselves. The squash was the highlight. It  is  lovely, ANON. Though I must confess, I’m still slightly overwhelmed by the sheer quantity! I think we’ve got enough leftovers to last the entire week, haven’t we? Particularly pleased with the apple crumble you made. Perfect ending to a lovely holiday. Totally. It’s been such a needed break. I'm feeling properly refreshed. Though, I'm already thinking about getting back into my fitness routine. I downloaded this new app, 'StrideStrong'. It’s supposed to be brilliant for personalized workout plans, adapting to your goals and progress. Have either of you heard of it? StrideStrong, eh? Sounds a bit… modern for me. Competition? Between you and your colleagues? Sounds a bit fraught, doesn't it? A bit of friendly rivalry is one thing, but... It's just a bit of fun, John! Nothing serious! Anyway, speaking of local things… have you heard about the train station finally opening? Oh, praise be! Honestly, it's been a joke, hasn't it? Years of delays and broken promises. I remember reading about it when I was a little girl, wishing for a train station right here in Devon.

…and then the pigeon just  launched  itself at the sandwich! Right out of nowhere, full-on dive. Honestly, I nearly choked on my latte laughing. It was chaos. My English teacher always said he should have just cut it back to the essentials. Remember sixth form, slaving over those essays? Oh god, yes. Trying to decipher what Mr. Davies  actually  wanted. I’m heading to a premier league match next weekend, actually. Arsenal vs. Man City. Ridiculously expensive tickets, but needed a proper football fix. Jealous! Apparently, there’s a "gladiator school" that’s a popular activity now. A gladiator school? That sounds… adventurous, at best. Hope Liam’s got a good insurance policy. Seriously though, Prague is brilliant. Any thoughts on what kind of books you’ve been reading lately? Still into sci-fi? Mostly. Been trying to broaden my horizons, though. Just finished "The Lie" by Ruth Ware. Really gripping, kept me up way too late. You read it? No, I haven’t. Is it good? I’ve been meaning to get back into fiction, properly. Been stuck in a news cycle vortex lately. Politics, Brexit… it’s all just draining. It feels like there's this constant tidal wave of negativity, you know? Tell me about it. It's impossible to escape. They're hammering us with it constantly. Makes you want to just move somewhere completely off the grid.

Honestly, the commute here was a nightmare. Roadworks everywhere. I’m seriously considering moving closer to Cambourne, just to avoid it. Though then Mum would kill me. You always say that! You’ve been threatening to move closer for ages. But then you'd miss out on all the cool stuff happening in Leeds. And Mum’s probably just being dramatic. She always is. How’s she doing, by the way? Still obsessing over the garden gnome collection? Don’t even get me started. She’s added three more. Three! Apparently, Bertram and Agnes needed some company. It’s getting a bit ridiculous.
