Apparently, it’s "festive.” I’m saving it for Christmas, just to torture myself. So, marketing, huh? Still saving the world, one flawlessly branded campaign at a time? Something like that. It’s… intense. We’re launching a new online learning platform next month. The pressure is on. Honestly, it feels like I’m living on caffeine and spreadsheets. What about your project coordinating? Still wrangling the spreadsheets for  your  lot? Exactly. Different spreadsheets, same level of frustration. We’re trying to implement a new CRM system. You wouldn’t believe the resistance we’re getting. People are terrified of change, even if it’s for the better. I spent half the morning explaining why “clicking the green button” isn’t inherently evil. People are baffling. Tell me, have you heard from Liam lately? Liam? Not really. Why? Just… I saw him at a party a few weeks ago. He looked… well, he looked happy. With someone else. Oh. Right. I… hadn't realized. It's been a while. Good for him, I suppose. Bit of a shock, though. I know. I felt awful crashing his happiness, but I thought you deserved to know. He seemed… genuinely settled. Definitely moved on. Honestly, it probably should have happened ages ago. Remember that time he tried to build a bookshelf with only a rubber mallet? Oh god, yes! The entire living room was covered in sawdust and veneer. It ended with me ordering one from IKEA. He was  terrible  at DIY. It's probably been the best thing for us both. Definitely. You’re better off without someone who can’t tell a Phillips head from a flathead screwdriver.

Right, Earl Grey then? Or do you fancy a splash of something stronger, lass? This Cambridge air does get right into your bones. Earl Grey’s grand, thanks, Ben. Though, honestly, I’ve been craving a good cuppa Yorkshire Tea all week. Feels like it’s been ages since I’ve had a proper brew from home. Aye, well, Yorkshire Tea's a bit… intense for a Monday morning. Besides, ANON’s got a real thing about it staining the china. Remember what happened with her grandmother’s Royal Doulton? Oh, don't remind me! She practically had a heart attack. Still, a bit of staining never hurt anyone. Adds character, eh? Like that pot plant in the corner there. Lookin’ a bit peaky, that one. That's Agnes. She's been a bit temperamental lately. I think she's missing proper sunlight. I’ve been rotating her around the windows, trying to give her some love. Honestly, plants are more demanding than my PhD supervisor sometimes. Aye, they are. My Gran used to have this jungle in her front room - ferns and orchids and practically a small palm tree. She knew all their names and their needs. I tried, you know, to keep a spider plant going when I moved to London, but it just… withered. Poor thing. I’m convinced it was the processed food. Probably was. You were living on ready meals and instant noodles for a good six months, weren't you? Speaking of food, ANON’s been experimenting with a new tagine recipe. Apparently, it involves apricots and preserved lemons. Sound appealing? Apricots and preserved lemons? That’s a bold combination! Is she sure about that? My Mam would have a field day criticising it. Vaguely… it involved a very public lecture on the correct spice ratios. ANON tells me she’s been watching a lot of Ottolenghi lately. Inspired, she says. Remember that pasta dish we used to make in halls? Just pasta, pesto, and a tin of chopped tomatoes. Absolute heaven after a lecture.

Speaking of impressive, did you catch that comeback from Ronnie O’Sullivan at the World Snooker? Brilliant stuff. His potting was sublime. Reminds you of a time when skill was paramount, rather than all this strategic nonsense. I did indeed! A masterclass, Gwyn, absolutely. He’s got that… that  je ne sais quoi , hasn’t he? An innate talent that just… flows. I’ve always admired the precision and concentration required. Completely different world from lecturing on Victorian literature, I suppose. Though, I suspect both require a form of intense focus. True enough. Different disciplines, same mental rigour. My niece, Megan, she's just finished her application to join the police force. The pressures they face… It's a difficult profession, requiring a different kind of intellectual strength, wouldn't you agree?

Right, so, this is… this is the current state of affairs. It's a bit of a mess, innit? I've been trying to get my head around this grant application for ages. It's for the research project, you know, on Northern dialects and language change. "A bit of a mess" is putting it mildly, Liam. It looks like a paper explosion. What's the big hurdle? Is it the budget breakdown again? You were moaning about that last week. It’s more than the budget now, mate. The budget's almost sorted, just need to finalise the equipment costs. Right, so you’ve got your initial surveys, transcriptions… and is this a phonetic analysis chart? Looks like you’ve been busy. Yeah, loads of it. Transcribing old dialect recordings is surprisingly tedious. And the phonetic analysis is… well, it's a slog. But I'm thinking Davies wants me to specify  how  I'm going to ensure the data is representative. Like, how am I avoiding bias in my participant selection? Ah, the sampling problem. Yeah, that's fair. It’s a constant worry with dialect studies. Everyone ends up just talking to their Gran, doesn’t it? Exactly! My Gran's a goldmine of Lancashire phrases, but she's hardly a representative sample of the entire Northern population, is she? I’ve tried to diversify – targeted ads on community pages, contacted local historical societies… But it's still tricky. Okay, so, you need to emphasize that. Show you’ve  considered  the limitations. Maybe… acknowledge upfront that the study  might  skew towards a certain demographic and then explain  why  you believe that skew doesn't fundamentally invalidate the findings. Focus on the broader trends you're analysing. Yeah, you’re right! I’ve been so bogged down in defending every single participant that I forgot to frame it properly. It's about outlining the limitations  and  explaining why those limitations don't negate the overall picture. Exactly. And quantify it, if you can. “While the sample includes 68% female participants residing in rural areas, the qualitative data gathered consistently reflected…” You know, give specifics, make it sound… scientific.

…and then Mr. Henderson, bless him, tried to explain the water cycle using a biscuit and a napkin. It was… chaotic. But the kids were absolutely captivated. Honestly, sometimes the best teaching moments are the unexpected ones. Sounds stressful. You look it too. Long day? You have no idea. It’s Year Two. They're at that age where logic and impulse wrestle constantly. But, you know, it's rewarding. What about you? Any near-misses with rogue spreadsheets today? Just the usual. Trying to convince people that slightly higher research spend equals significantly better investment opportunities. The eternal struggle. It's funny, though, thinking about Mr. Henderson and his biscuit water cycle... reminds me of a dream I had last night. Absolutely bonkers. Daddy? Story time? Just a tick, sweetheart! Daddy was just telling Mummy about a dream. With dinosaurs! Is there a dinosaur? Not quite dinosaurs, love. It was... I was presenting a proposal, right? To a room full of penguins. And they kept interrupting me to ask for fish. Like, demanding it. And the slides were all pictures of squirrels. Penguins and squirrels? That’s wonderfully absurd. You really need to relax more. Tell me about it! But it felt… significant, you know? Like, a metaphor for something. Probably just needing more sleep. What about you? Any dream adventures lately? Actually, yes. I dreamt I was swimming in a giant bowl of jelly. Strawberry jelly. And I kept finding little lost socks in it. It was surprisingly calming, until a giant spoon started chasing me. Jelly? I like jelly! Red jelly! See? Even your dreams are more appealing than mine! Though, red jelly sounds messy. I dreamt I flew to the moon! And there were bouncy castles on the moon! Wow! That's fantastic, mate! A bouncy castle on the moon - brilliant! That’s better than penguins and squirrels, that's for sure. They always have the best dreams, don’t they? So full of imagination. It's a shame we lose some of that as we get older. You’re right. It is. Speaking of things we want… You know I’ve been thinking. We should get a dog. A dog? Really? We’ve talked about this before. It's a lot of responsibility, especially with the kids and your work. I know, I know. But I keep picturing it. A little golden retriever, running around in the garden… It’d be good for the kids, teach them responsibility.

Right, okay. Just… just let me adjust this. Honestly, I thought I’d broken it. Stupid rock. Seriously, who puts a rock that big on a walking path? Aye, well, some folk dinnae think, do they, Ben? You're lucky it's just a sprain, an' nowt worse. You were hopping like a mad thing back there. Did you get it checked properly at A&E? They can be a bit rushed, can’t they? Yeah, they did an X-ray. Said it was a grade two ankle sprain, needs icing and rest. Gave me a boot thing to wear. Feels like I'm walking in a Michelin Man tyre. Michelin Man is a grand description! Did they give you any painkillers strong enough to actually  do  somethin’? They gave me paracetamol once when I had a migraine. Paracetamol! Like that's gonna shift a brain-splitting headache. They gave me some codeine-based ones. Said to take two if the pain gets bad. But I’m trying to avoid those if I can. All that wooziness... not ideal when trying to work. Aye, I know what you mean. They leave you feelin' like you're floatin' away. Still, A&E were packed, weren’t they? All those folk waitin’… Did you see that poor lass with the arm? Looked like she’d fallen off a bike. Yeah, it was mayhem. I felt a bit bad, feeling sorry for my sprain when there were people with genuinely serious injuries. I felt guilty even taking up their time, to be honest. Don't be daft, Ben. You were hurt! You should get treated. Besides, that's what A&E’s for. It’s a right disgrace though, the waitin' times. Me mam was waitin' for six hours last month with a dodgy chest. Six hours! It’s terrible. The NHS is under so much pressure. I feel like I should be doing something about it, but… what can I do? Well, you're an engineer, aren't you? You could design better hospital layouts, maybe? Less crowded waiting areas, more efficient triage systems… use your skills for good! Always thinkin' up grand schemes, don't you? Always. It’s on my ‘to do’ list after I've mastered walking again. Right now, it's more a question of mastering getting  into  the car without looking like a newborn giraffe. Aye, you look a proper state.

…and honestly, Nigel, the state of education now. It’s just… a world away from when I started. Endless testing, targets, all the pressure on the kids. Where’s the joy gone? Joy? Joy’s for retirement, Arthur. You’re meant to be preparing them for the brutal realities of the modern world! Though, I understand your point. It  does  seem rather… regimented. Still, you managed to produce some fine young minds, didn't you? Remember young Emily? Went off to Cambridge, didn’t she? She did. A bright spark, that one. She sent a lovely card last Christmas, actually. Said she was still using the critical thinking exercises I set her. Makes a teacher feel a bit worthwhile, you know? So, how's the new venture going, Nigel? Still grappling with the logistics of importing artisan cheeses from France? Grappling is an understatement. Arthur, you wouldn’t believe the paperwork. Mountains of it. The EU regulations, even post-Brexit, are a nightmare. I spent three hours yesterday just wrestling with a form about lactose content. Lactose! Imagine. But the cheese… oh, the cheese is worth it. We’ve got a delightful Comté, a proper Roquefort… customers are already raving about them at the market. Good to hear! It's a brave move, leaving the insurance business after all these years. Takes guts, that. Did you tell Charles and Margaret about it? Not yet. I was waiting for things to be a bit more solid. Don’t want to inflict any anxieties on them, especially Margaret. She worries enough as it is about everything. You know how she is - a walking weather report. Anything remotely ominous and she’s convinced the world is ending. Indeed. She’s a gem, though. Loyal as the day is long. Speaking of the world ending… did you see that report about the rising sea levels? Brighton's going to be underwater within fifty years if they don't do something drastic. Saw it. Gloomy stuff, isn't it? Reminds me of that film, 'Waterworld'. Though, I can't imagine Kevin Costner setting up a stall selling Brie and Camembert in a flooded Brighton Marina. You have an odd outlook on potential catastrophes, Nigel. Though, you’re right, it would be a sight to see. Still, it's worrying. My grandson, Thomas, is obsessed with climate change. He’s trying to get the school to introduce more sustainable practices.

You know, this place is surprisingly…pleasant. I wasn’t expecting much from a pub called The Guardhouse in Woolwich, to be honest. The exposed brick is a nice touch, isn't it? It is. Much better than that awful Wetherspoons we tried last time. Though, I'm still not convinced about those weird, vaguely nautical paintings. Is that a mermaid riding a lobster? It might be. You're probably right. Let’s not dwell on the artwork. What are we having to eat? I’m starving. That admin work really takes it out of a man, you know. Endless spreadsheets and…well, endless spreadsheets. I was thinking fish and chips. Classic pub fare. Or maybe that shepherd’s pie looks good. They had a board outside. Fish and chips is always a winner. Although, I did see something about a venison burger. That’s tempting, actually. Bit fancier than I usually go for, though. Oh, you’ve developed a taste for game, have you? Remember when you swore off anything that wasn’t a chicken nugget when we were at university? Don’t remind me! Edinburgh student life was…a simpler time. Mostly fuelled by instant noodles and desperation. University was a better experience when you were around, though. Remember those late-night debates in the common room? Oh goodness, yes. Arguing about post-structuralism until 3 am. I think we nearly drove the poor hall warden insane. I’m still trying to recall most of what we were even discussing. Precisely! And yet, we felt incredibly intelligent at the time. Right, fish and chips it is then. Safer choice. More fuel for discussing… Happy Valley, did you finish it? Just last night! Absolutely brilliant, wasn't it? That final episode... the tension was unbearable. I literally held my breath. I know! Sarah Lancashire is just phenomenal. The way she conveys that simmering anger and resilience… It’s gripping. That whole series felt so authentically bleak and Northern. Agreed. It’s so well-written too. And the cinematography... those grey, rain-soaked streets. Perfect atmosphere. Did you notice the music? That haunting cello track? Yes! It really amplified the mood. Speaking of music, I'm glad they weren’t blasting some awful chart music. This pub actually has a decent playlist. Something mellow. It’s a bit chilly in here, isn’t it? I should have grabbed my coat. I'm regretting leaving it in the car now.

Golden dust, eh? Sounds like you were livin’ the high life, brother. Morocco, right? You did mention somethin' about that. So, was it worth the bother then? All that flyin' and gettin’ yourself lost, like you usually do. Worth it? Absolutely! It was transformative, actually. Not just the landscapes, which were breathtaking, don't get me wrong, but the people. The colours...it just shakes you up a bit, you know? Forces you to see things differently. And the photography opportunities… phenomenal. I’ve got some shots I’m really excited about. Aye, I can imagine. You were always good wi' a camera. Remember that lot you took o' Gran at the Highland Games? Still got those framed on me wall, I do. Though, she did complain about you gettin' too close when she was tryin' tae sling the caber. She  did ! A right scandal it was. Said I was distracting her. But honestly, the expressions on people's faces at those events are gold. Morocco was a bit different. More about capturing the stillness, the quiet moments. I spent ages just sittin' in a courtyard, watchin' the sunlight shift on the walls. Sounds peaceful. A far cry from yer busy Director o' Studies life, I'd reckon. You're teachin' philosophy now, aren’t ye? That’s a wee bit different than stackin’ boxes, eh? It is, undeniably. But there's a surprising overlap, actually. Both involve problem-solving, analysis, trying to make sense of... well, everything. Though one involves a lot more paperwork. And a lot less lifting. How are things at the warehouse going? Still trainin’ up the new recruits? Aye, keeps me busy, it does. Got a young lad called Euan just started. Fair enough chappie, but a bit… easily distracted, I’d say. Keeps starin' oot the window at the rain. Typical Scottish weather, eh? They’re practically born lookin' at grey skies. Did you tell him to appreciate it? It's character-buildin'. Character-buildin' is exactly what I told him. Said he’d be missin’ the sunshine if he didn't. Though, to be fair, there hasn't been much sunshine  to  miss lately. Proper dreich it’s been. Makes you yearn for that golden dust you were talkin' about. It really does. I was thinking about that just the other day. Even Edinburgh feels a bit… muted right now. All this dampness. I’ve been trying to edit my Morocco photos, to recapture some of that warmth.

Honestly, this week feels like it's going to be a marathon, not a sprint. Between the garden club meeting and sorting out that antique dresser, I'm already feeling knackered. Mum, you always say that, and you always manage to get everything done! Garden club sounds… stimulating. Antique dresser? Serious business. Stimulating is one word for it. The hydrangea competition is tomorrow, and Mrs. Higgins is  determined  to win again this year. You know how she is. And the dresser… well, Aunt Maureen wants it for her granddaughter's room, but it needs a good going over. Dust, polish, maybe a new handle or two. Right. Sounds like a full day's work. Anyway, mine isn't exactly a picnic either. Little Leo’s been having a phase where he refuses to share any of his building blocks, and Emily keeps trying to eat glue sticks. The joys of reception class! Oh, bless ‘em. You're a saint, love. Still, at least you get to shape little minds. I'm just shaping hydrangeas and dusting old wood. Have you made any progress with the nursery? Have they called about the waiting list? Not yet, no. I called them again yesterday, and the woman on the phone just said they were still "reviewing applications." It’s so frustrating! I feel like I’m constantly chasing shadows. Honestly, Mum, I’m starting to panic a bit. Daniel is wonderful, of course, but he works long hours. I need somewhere reliable for little Poppy. I know, pet. It’s awful. Don’t you worry, something will turn up. Keep pushing them. Persistent is good. Perhaps I’ll give them a ring myself, anonymously, and see if I can shake something loose. You know I'm good at getting things done. You and your unofficial interventions! Please don’t! They might think I'm trying to pull strings. But thank you. It’s just… it feels so important to get it right. It’s Poppy's first major step away from us, you know? I do know, love. Believe me, I remember when you were that little. It feels like yesterday. Though you were a much better-behaved child than Leo, it sounds. Building blocks disputes at three? Honestly! He's just… passionate! And Emily's not  eating  glue sticks, she just… likes the smell. Apparently. So, what about the television this week? Anything good on?

Honestly, this risotto is divine, Anon. You've really outdone yourself. Though, I still think you need a lighter hand with the Parmesan. It's fighting with the lemon. Aye, well, relax, Chloe, it's just grub. And Anon's a good cook, even if she does drown everything in cheese. Speaking of fighting, how's the production controller life treating ya? Still grappling with rogue widgets? Rogue widgets are a daily occurrence, Maisie. But I've actually managed to streamline things a bit. My boss is quite pleased, which is a rare victory. But the politics! Don't even get me started. There’s this new intern, fresh out of uni, and she's trying to reinvent the wheel. Claims my processes are "outdated" and "inefficient." Says she's bringing "innovative solutions." Sounds like a right pain. People think knowing stuff is the same as  having  ideas. I know how to lay bricks, doesn't mean I can design a skyscraper. Sound advice, Liam! Fresh out of uni, are they? They always think they’ve got all the answers, don't they? Remember when I tried to re-organise the catering at that tech conference last year? Complete chaos. Ended up with everyone wanting beetroot sandwiches. Beetroot! Nightmare fuel. At least rogue widgets don’t involve vegetables. So, Liam, still at the building site? Anything interesting going on there? It's alright. Bit of a grind, like. Big job on just outside of town, new housing development. Loads of bricklaying, bit of pointing, mostly just carrying stuff. It’s honest work, though. Pays the bills. But it’s the uniform, innit? They give us these fluorescent vests, bright orange, and they’re  awful . I look like a giant traffic cone. I know the feeling. My work uniform used to be a navy blazer and pencil skirt. Felt like a walking corporate spreadsheet. At least you get fresh air. Speaking of clothes, I need your honest opinions. I have a work event next week - a conference drinks reception – and I’m having a mini-existential crisis about what to wear. Should I go classic LBD, or something a bit more…statement? I’ve been eyeing this emerald green jumpsuit… Emerald green jumpsuit?! Get it! Definitely get it! You’d look stunning, Chloe. You carry it off, you’ve got the confidence for it. LBD is a bit…safe, isn’t it?

"Children, aren't they? Always a bit of chaos. Though, Doreen deserves a bit of a relax, poor love. Rheumatism's been playing up something awful lately. You’ve got the kettle on, Arthur?" "Aye, Margaret, just put it on. Strong as you like, like you always ask. Though, really, we’ve got enough Yorkshire Tea in the cupboard to sink a battleship. Bought a whole crate at the reduced price last month. Didn't know what I'd do with it all, to be honest, but a bargain's a bargain, eh?" "A crate, Arthur? That  is  a significant investment. Reminds me of when young Timothy, back when he was knee-high to a grasshopper, insisted we stock up on rhubarb. Wanted to make crumble every other day. We practically  lived  on rhubarb for a whole summer. Good times, though, good times." “Rhubarb crumble  is  lovely. Though, I always preferred a little ginger in mine. Gives it a bit of a… kick. It's important to have a little something different, isn't it? Sometimes tea itself can be rather… monotonous, can't it?” She paused, adjusting her cardigan. “Although, even the most commonplace things can be special if you simply appreciate them, I suppose. Like a good, strong cup of tea on a dreary afternoon.” “Agnes, you always have a thoughtful observation to make, don't you? I quite agree. It's the ritual, really, isn’t it? The warmth of the cup in your hands, the smell… it’s comforting. More so than anything else these days.” “Comforting’s right. Used to have a cuppa every morning before… well, before. Now it’s just… well, just what I do. Keeps the chill out, that’s what it does. Although, I'm thinking I might try a different blend for a change. Seen some Earl Grey in the shop. Never had it before, mind you. Seems a bit… fancy.” “Fancy? Arthur, Earl Grey is perfectly respectable! It’s just bergamot – a citrus fruit. Gives it a lovely, fragrant aroma. You should try it. Actually, I used to bring it with me when I marked essays. A little touch of civilisation amidst the teenage angst, you see.” He chuckled. "It is quite pleasant, Earl Grey. Though, for me, it’s not really a ‘comfort’ tea. More of an occasional treat. I prefer something a little… robust. Something that’ll stick to your ribs, you know?

Honestly, I think this rosemary and garlic is  divine . What do you think, Rhys? Right good, it is! Proper tasty. Though, a bit more gravy wouldn’t go amiss, wouldn’t it, love? Always with the gravy, Rhys! You’d drown everything in it given half a chance. It’s wonderful though, Anna. You've really outdone yourself this time. Absolutely fantastic, really. Proper comfort food after a long day. London felt like a different planet entirely. It’s just nice to have everyone together. How was your day, Mark? Did you manage to sort out that issue with the student? Eventually. It required a lengthy discussion about plagiarism and proper citation. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if they even  read  the guidelines. And then there’s the CRB checks… the bureaucracy! It’s a nightmare getting everything processed in time. Tell me about it! I had Brenda from accounts on my back all day about a training budget discrepancy. Honestly, these spreadsheet warriors… they’d rather argue about a decimal point than actually improve anyone’s skills. Sounds lively. My day was… less thrilling. Dealing with customer complaints. Mostly about delivery times, you know how it is. Though one bloke phoned up furious because he’d ordered a left-handed hammer. Said it was discriminatory. A left-handed hammer! Oh, Rhys, you’re incorrigible. That’s brilliant! Honestly. So, Mark, you were in London. Anything exciting happen? See any good art? Actually, yes. I went to the Tate Modern. There was this protest happening outside, quite a boisterous one about climate change. But inside, there was a really compelling exhibition of contemporary sculpture. Really thought-provoking stuff. You’d like it, Anna. Very minimalist, a bit like that artist you showed me last year. Oh, I’d love to go! Maybe we can plan a weekend trip? Find a nice hotel, properly posh this time, not that Travelodge nightmare we endured in Bournemouth. Remember that? The noise! And the wallpaper… like a flock of angry pigeons had attacked it. Rhys was snoring like a walrus. I do  not  snore like a walrus! I merely… breathed deeply. After a long drive. And after a pint or two at the pub on the way. A few pints, yes. Which brings me to a slightly uncomfortable topic. We were discussing CRB checks, and proper protocols... Should we really be letting you drive back to Wales after a potential long night out, Rhys?

Honestly, I’m wrecked. The airport queues were a nightmare. Did you miss me loads? Liv! You're back! Proper missed you, yeah. You look exhausted though. Holiday go well? Smells amazing in here, by the way – what’s cooking? It was... complicated. Beautiful, mostly. Saw some incredible sights in Greece, but the flight… ugh. This smells like you actually cooked something substantial. Not just instant noodles for once. It’s stew, right? Lamb stew. Your favourite. Figured you'd need some serious comfort food after battling the hordes. So, spill! Greece? Sun, sand, handsome locals? Don't leave out the juicy details. Okay, okay. Sun, definitely. Sand, breathtaking. Handsome locals… well, one, maybe. He was a windsurfer. Kept saving me from drifting out to sea. Bit intense, honestly. Turns out, he was married. Classic, right? Oh my god, Liv! You're pulling my leg! A married windsurfer? Seriously? You didn’t! I swear! Found out when his wife, a very angry woman with a sunhat and a very large handbag, came screaming down the beach. Let's just say, the romance ended swiftly. Anyway, aside from that, it was mostly exploring ruins, trying to avoid sunburn, and eating way too much feta. You are a magnet for drama, aren't you? I'm glad you had a good time overall though. It sounds lovely. Did you see your auntie Eleni? I know you were excited to see her. Yeah, Auntie Eleni was brilliant. She dragged me to this tiny taverna, miles from anywhere, where they served the most authentic moussaka I’ve ever tasted. She’s still going strong, though she keeps dropping hints about me settling down. Apparently, all the eligible Greek bachelors are clamouring for a mental health nurse! Oh, here we go. The auntie matchmaking routine. Don’t listen to her. Focus on the feta. So, work stuff? Anything exciting happening there? Mrs. Davies is still making me photocopy things in Comic Sans if you can believe it. Seriously?! Comic Sans? That woman. Don’t even get me started. Work's been… busy. We’re trying to get the new outreach program for young adults with anxiety off the ground. It’s a real challenge finding funding, but it's vital. It's been a bit tougher than I anticipated, to be honest. I’m feeling a bit burned out. That sounds really rewarding, though. And important.

Honestly, the planning application for that old Miller's cottage is driving me mad. They want to knock it down and build five townhouses. Five! It’s utterly ridiculous for a village the size of Little Puddleton. It  is  a bit much, isn’t it? But you know Mrs. Hawthorne's got serious connections. She's on the Parish Council, and her husband used to bankroll half the village fete. They’ll fight tooth and nail. Exactly! And the design…it's just…bland. Modern boxes jammed onto the green. No consideration for the character of the place. I drafted a response to the council – a fairly strongly worded one, I might add – but I’m not sure it'll make a blind bit of difference. Don’t be disheartened. Every little bit helps. Did you mention the impact on local infrastructure? Parking especially. We already struggle with that when the cricket club has a tournament. Yes, and the sewage system! Little Puddleton's drains are Victorian, for goodness sake. Five new houses…it’s a recipe for disaster. Right, I need a break from planning applications. How are you feeling? Still worried about Liam? Terribly. I spoke to Sarah this morning. He had a tough night, apparently. The chemo is really taking its toll. He's vomiting constantly and they've had to adjust the dosage. Oh, love. That’s awful. Is he…is he still optimistic? That’s the thing. He  says  he is. He’s putting on a brave face, naturally. But Sarah’s clearly worried. She said he's finding it harder to get out of bed, even forgetting things sometimes. Little things, but…you know. Cancer really is the cruelest thief. It steals so much more than just physical health. Remembering things… that’s terrible. Have they talked about palliative care options? I know it’s a difficult subject, but… They touched on it, briefly. He's resisting. Wants to fight it, obviously. And I understand that. But Sarah said he’s agreed to see a specialist next week, someone who can talk about managing symptoms and quality of life. It’s a start, anyway. It is. And it’s good that Sarah’s pushing him gently. She’s a rock. Listen, I’ll call her later. Just check in, see how they’re doing. Maybe offer to drop off some groceries or something. That would be lovely, thank you.

Honestly, the instant noodles situation in the communal kitchen is just… abysmal. They’re always empty.  Always . Like, I stock them, I buy a whole box, and within two days, they've vanished. And it's not like they're being eaten thoughtfully. There's just discarded packets everywhere, a lake of lukewarm, salty water in the sink. It’s disgusting. I’ve started labelling them with "Resident Life Support - Do Not Touch!" but even that doesn’t seem to deter anyone. Aye, I know what you mean. Students, eh? No respect. It's the same with the milk. Buy a two-pint, gone by the mornin'. You'd think they were all going through a dairy growth spurt. Though, you'd have thought labelling would work. You'd think. I had a right mare with a lad last week tryin' to nick a sausage roll out o’ the staff room. Told 'im where to go, I did. A sausage roll?! Seriously? That’s brazen! I once found a single, half-eaten banana abandoned in the microwave. Not even puttin' it in a bag first! The absolute state of it. It was melting into the carousel. I had to scrub it for a good ten minutes. I’m starting to feel like a glorified cleaning lady, not a Resident Life Support Officer. Tell me about it. Security’s not all glory and flashing lights, you know. Mostly, it’s pickin' up litter and remindin' folks to put their rubbish in the bins. You’d be surprised how many forget. Or choose to leave it right next to the bin, just... refusing to move it an inch. I had someone argue with me last Tuesday about whether a crisp packet constituted 'rubbish'. Said it was ‘recyclable materials pending assessment’. I just stared at him. Oh, bless. “Pending assessment.” That’s a new one. My biggest gripe, though, apart from the perpetual noodle shortage and the abandoned fruit, is the late-night noise. Like, some people seem to think these are nightclubs, not student apartments. I get complaints constantly. It’s a constant juggle between tryin’ to be understanding and tryin’ to enforce the quiet hours. Aye, the noise. That's a right pain. We get tumble dryers crankin' at 3 AM – who does that? And the music, dearie me. Bass so loud, you can feel it through the floor. I've had to move residents a couple of times to get some peace and quiet.

…and honestly, most of my cohort at uni are scattered all over the place now. One’s in Berlin teaching English, another’s backpacking through Southeast Asia, it's mad. Makes you feel a bit… adrift, doesn’t it? Like everyone’s forging paths you didn’t even consider. Drifting’s alright, love. Beats being stuck. I drifted for years, you know. Ended up in Antwerp for a bit, back in the eighties. Can’t say I ever  wanted  to be there, mind you. Package tour, that was. Bruges was lovely though. Proper charming. Antwerp? Really, David? I didn't know that! What was it like? Was it before they really cleared up the quays? Aye, before all the fancy shops and whatnot. Grittier, I’d say. Less to do, more… character, if you get my meaning. Didn’t speak a word of Flemish, of course. Managed fine with a bit of pointing and smiling though. Tried to learn some, I did. Didn't stick, though. Never been much for languages, me. Always preferred a good rhyme. Easier to remember! “Rain, rain, go away, come again another day…” you know? Classic. Proper childhood rhyme. But seriously, Antwerp? Why a package tour to Belgium? Well, I wasn’t exactly over-burdened with options back then, was I? Needed a change of scenery. Felt like I was just… circling. Trying to find somewhere to land, like a lost seagull. It's so hard to find somewhere to feel like you belong, isn’t it? I was thinking about Christmas markets this year. There’s a lovely one in Birmingham, apparently. Thinking of dragging the boys along. Oh, yeah! I saw something about that. It’s supposed to be really festive. Wonder if they'll have those little gingerbread hearts again? I always get one for Finn. He's obsessed. Though, honestly, the traffic getting into Birmingham… it’s a nightmare. Birmingham traffic...  shudders  Reminds me of trying to get into Herne Bay shopping centre on a Saturday. Absolute chaos! Still, I do enjoy a bit of shopping. Remember that little antique shop just off the high street? Wonderful things in there. Oh, yes! Such treasures. Actually, speaking of things I'm looking forward to, it's young Liam’s birthday next month. Turning eight! Can you believe it? Where does the time go? Seemed like only yesterday I was changing nappies… I know, right?

Ugh, school was mental today. Mr. Davies went on and on about the Equality Vote. Feels like everyone's talking about it. And what did he say, love? Sounds like you could use a biscuit. He was basically trying to convince us it's, like,  the most important thing ever . Said it was about fairness and making sure everyone has the same chances. Which, yeah, I get. But honestly, he made it sound like we were personally responsible for centuries of inequality just because… well, because we exist. Bit dramatic, aren’t we? Davies is just doing his job, trying to raise awareness. It  is  important, you know. More important than a lot of people realize. But he kept bringing up Ireland, you know, the Troubles. Saying it was a prime example of inequality. It just felt… awkward. Like, I’m learning about the Tudors and Shakespeare in history, not… that. It’s connected, though, isn’t it? Equality isn't just about gender or race. It's about national identity, too. About people feeling they have a voice and are valued. Think about what it must have been like, growing up in Northern Ireland during that time - feeling isolated, discriminated against… I suppose. Still, it’s a bit far removed, isn’t it? I mean, I'm in Bristol. Everything's pretty chill here. Don’t be so sure. Inequality exists everywhere, sweetheart. Maybe not in the same, obviously violent way as the Troubles, but it’s there. How about that girl, Chloe, in your class? Always seems to get picked on. Chloe? Yeah, she’s a bit weird, I guess. Always wearing those… massive hats. See? That’s a form of inequality. Teasing, exclusion… they all chip away at someone's sense of worth. It’s the little things that add up. And the vote is about making sure those little things don’t become big, systemic problems. So, what's this Equality Vote even  about ? It sounds like it's got loads of different angles. Liam was saying his mum's campaigning for something to do with marriage equality. Liam’s mum's a good woman. Yes, it's a vote on a series of proposals aimed at strengthening protections against discrimination. Marriage equality is one of them, absolutely. But also things like equal pay for equal work, better access to education for disadvantaged communities, that sort of thing.

Honestly, Harold, you’d think with all those lovely tools you've got, you’d be building a miniature castle, not just fiddling with bits of wood! What are you even  doing  with that skew chisel today? Well, Doreen, it's a bit of a tricky bit, this. I’m trying to shape the curve on this… this fancy foot for a little stool. For the grandkids, see. They're always wanting somethin’ new. Can’t be lettin' ‘em think Grandad’s gone soft, can we? Though, between you and me, this bead cutter is givin' me a right bother. Keeps chippin' the edges, the pesky thing. A bead cutter, eh? Are you using the right speed, Harold? Too fast and it’ll certainly chatter. And have you indexed the cutter correctly? It’s easy to overlook. I used to have to deal with similar issues at the training centre; machinery always caused a headache. You know, precision is everything, even in childcare. Tidiness, organization… it all reflects on the learning environment. Oh, David’s always got a technical explanation for everything, doesn’t he? It's good, mind, but sometimes a bit much over lunch. Harold, dear, you need to eat something. You're looking peaked. Did you manage to get some of those apples from Mrs. Higgins’ allotment? Aye, Doreen, got a whole bag. She gives 'em to me, bless her heart. Said I look as if I need "a proper bit of sustenance." These sandwiches are lovely, though. Sarah makes a mean egg mayonnaise. Egg mayonnaise is a classic. Though, you know, if you want a  really  good egg mayonnaise, you need to whip the yolks first – it makes it lighter, airier. And a touch of Dijon mustard, just a tiny bit. Elevates the whole thing. See? Even lunch isn't safe from David’s improvements. Honestly, it's like he's coaching a Michelin-star chef! It’s good, David. Don't you worry about that. Though… remember that episode with Percy? Oh, please, Harold, not Percy. Not the hamster. Well, I can't just forget it, can I? Little blighter got himself in a right pickle. Sarah found him in the microwave. In the  microwave ? Harold! Were you attempting… something? No, no! Blimey, David! It was an accident. I was just… warming up a bit of squash for his supper. You know, he likes it a bit warm.

Honestly, Eleanor, this interest rate hike is just another kick in the teeth. I'm starting to think these banks are actively trying to squeeze every last penny out of us. Don't start moaning, David. You know it's cyclical. And besides, at least we're not facing the sort of debt some young people are drowning in these days. Remember that article about Laura’s niece? Apparently, she’s got over £50,000 in student loans. Fifty thousand! Good heavens. When I started teaching, the fees were a pittance. Though, of course, back then, a house cost a reasonable amount, too. Not like these prices now. Absolutely ridiculous. I saw a two-bedroom flat in Islington the other day – over a million! A million! For a flat? You could buy a small castle in Scotland for that! Which, incidentally, is another thing I’ve been looking at. Maybe we should… you know… David, are you suggesting we uproot ourselves and move to Scotland? With the cat? Not immediately! Just exploring options. The property market here is just... unsustainable. And your mother’s been rattling on about the Scottish Highlands again. It's planted a seed, I admit. Plus, I've always been fascinated by that mirror-writing thing. Remember Leonardo da Vinci? I read an article about it, how some people naturally write backwards. A delightful eccentricity! It’s linked to neurological things, apparently. Keen observation. My nephew, the neurologist, was explaining it to me once. He says there's a surprising overlap with dyslexia sometimes. Fascinating. Did you see that story in the news? About the cat who saved its owner from a house fire? Such a brave little thing. Yes! Absolutely heartwarming. Though I do think the papers rather sensationalize these things. Still, good for the cat. It reminds me of Mrs. Higgins’ ginger tom, Bartholomew. He used to bring her dead mice… strategically placed on the doorstep, of course. Utterly mortifying. My grandmother had a cat like that. Called him Satan. Ironically. She swore he was possessed. Speaking of mortifying things, did you catch any of the American political debates? Utter chaos. Avoided them like the plague. Honestly, the level of vitriol is just… draining. I’d rather grapple with a particularly tricky cryptic crossword clue. This one’s got me stumped: "Crimson reflection a culinary deception ." "Beetroot?" Of course! Beetroot! You’re a lifesaver, Margaret.

Honestly, you two. Look at this kitchen. It’s a disaster! Crumbs everywhere, Lego scattered like landmines… and you’ve barely touched your books. But Mum, I'm building a new Ninjago city! It needs  all  my attention! Zane is having a problem with his ice palace. And I’m defending my Minecraft world from creepers! They’re  everywhere ! I need to build a stronger wall. A diamond wall! A diamond wall? Seriously? We talked about this. Reading time was meant to be… well, reading time. Not battling digital monsters and constructing fantastical cities. But Mum, Ninjago is educational! It teaches teamwork and problem-solving! Zane has to use science to build his palace, you know. Ice physics! Ice physics, huh? And what about problem-solving when it comes to tidying up, eh? Because right now, the biggest problem facing this kitchen is the sheer volume of plastic bricks and digital chaos. But Minecraft helps me with creativity! I’m designing a whole underground kingdom! It’s got lava farms and hidden tunnels and… and everything! It’s way more creative than… than… reading. Oh really? More creative than imagining dragons, wizards, and entire new worlds sparked by words on a page? Books are full of more worlds than you can shake a stick at, darling. They just require a slightly different kind of imagination. But Mum, the Ninjago characters have backstories! And special moves! And they fight evil! It's exciting! And wizards in books fight evil too! Brave knights, clever detectives, resourceful explorers… Think of Hermione Granger, or Harry Potter! They solve problems, travel to incredible places, and become heroes, all through the power of words. Creepers are  really  close… I need more TNT. Right. TNT. Look, I'm not saying you can't play your games. I get it – they’re fun. But everything in moderation, remember? It's about balance. We need to give those lovely books a chance too. They're not  boring , they're just different. So, can I finish building Zane's palace? It’s  really  important. Fine. Finish Zane's palace. But just for another half an hour. Then, we’re all reading. I’ve got a new mystery novel that I think you might both enjoy, actually. It's got a secret garden  and  a missing cat. A cat?! Does it have to fight creepers? No creepers involved, I promise. Just a very clever detective trying to solve a very puzzling case.

Honestly, Mum, the traffic getting here was  awful . I swear, Birmingham’s become a permanent car park. I was late opening the store, and Mr. Davies was giving me the stink eye. Oh, don't let him wind you up, love. He's always got something to moan about. Was it as bad as last time we came? Remember that gridlock on the A38? Last time was legendary! I think we spent an hour going about fifty yards. I nearly started taking pictures for Instagram just to document the absurdity of it all. #BirminghamTraffic #SendHelp. You and your Instagram, Liv. I was just stressed. This store manager life is… a lot. It's not all like, samples and discounts, you know? Dealing with staff issues, stock takes, complaints… it's exhausting. I know, sweetheart. It's a big responsibility. But you're doing brilliantly. Mr. Davies is lucky to have you. You always were a grafter. Remember helping me at the Christmas market when you were little? You practically ran the hot chocolate stall! Trying to convince you that the gingerbread men  needed  more icing, mostly. That wasn’t exactly a responsible business decision. Memories! Speaking of memories, Mum, weren't the sunsets in Cornwall absolutely incredible? I’ve been editing the photos, and they're just… wow. I think I’ve got at least twenty that are worthy of the 'Gram. They were stunning, weren't they? Especially that one from Porthleven - the way the light hit the water... proper magical. I was thinking of printing a few and putting them up in the hallway. It’d brighten the place up nicely. That would be lovely, Mum. I took loads of pictures of the Minack Theatre too - it was amazing to see a performance right on the cliffs. Although, I nearly fell over trying to get a good angle! You nearly took me with you! I ended up spending half the play checking on you! Honestly, I thought I was going to have to carry you both back to the car. Very funny, Liv! I was fine. Just a little… enthusiastic about capturing the perfect moment. So, what are we doing today? Anything planned? Well, I was thinking we could pop into Lichfield Cathedral. It's been ages since we’ve been, and I know you both appreciate some decent architecture. Then maybe a wander around the shops? I need to get a new scarf, the one I bought last year fell apart.

Right, my turn. Seven of clubs. Your go, Chloe. And seriously, this sandwich is  awful . Tuna and cucumber? Who puts cucumber in a tuna sandwich? You’re being dramatic, Liam. It's fine. My chicken and mayo is way worse. It's all dry. Honestly, I’m regretting choosing lunch here. Mum’s sandwiches are always better. Tell me about it! My dad makes these monster cheese and pickle ones. Mountains of pickle. It's a war on my mouth. You know, I was watching that documentary about the Falklands the other night… reminds you how lucky we are to not be, you know, fighting somewhere. Yeah, well, fighting over tuna and cucumber is bad enough, isn't it? Okay, your turn again. But seriously, the school's going mad, isn't it? Those new prefects are a nightmare. Tell me about it. Amelia thinks she’s Queen Elizabeth. Always sniffing around, writing down everything. She reported Jacob for, like, accidentally bumping into her.  Accidentally!  And didn’t she make him scrub the toilets as punishment? Ridiculous. He’s probably still traumatized. They need to be more approachable, you know? Like, actually  help  people, instead of just policing. Exactly! And it’s not even just Amelia. Rhys is just… aloof. Doesn’t seem to care about anything. It’s like they both think they're too good for everyone else. It's always the ones who try the hardest to be perfect who are the worst, isn’t it? Remember last year when we were watching  The Crown ? That’s what Amelia’s like. Desperate to be regal. Speaking of TV shows, did you guys see the new episode of  Space Force ? Steve Carell is hilarious. My little sister is obsessed with it. She keeps making spaceship noises. I haven’t seen it yet. Been busy trying to finish this history essay. It’s about the impact of colonialism on Nigeria. It’s… heavy. You know, thinking about all that stuff that happened… people being treated so unfairly… Yeah, it is. It’s crazy to think it all happened not that long ago. Sometimes, when I walk around London, I feel like I'm surrounded by ghosts of the past. Like, all the buildings are whispering stories. My grandad served in the army, you know? In Germany. He never really talked a lot about it, but my mum said it was tough.

Honestly, Mr. Davies is  killing  me this year. I swear, he thinks we're all about to win Nobel Prizes in Physics. Tell me about it! My head’s swimming with equations. Did he actually make us derive the laws of thermodynamics  again  yesterday? Again! And with even more complicated examples. He’s obsessed with projectile motion. Like, we get it, things go up and then they come down. Is there really any point in calculating the trajectory of a particularly complicated pineapple? A pineapple? Seriously? He’s got a weird sense of humour. Mrs. Peterson in English, though, she's a lifesaver. She let us have a free period today just to read. Oh, brilliant! What did you read? I was finally getting into 'Wuthering Heights'. Heathcliff is such a…complicated character. I started 'Pride and Prejudice' again. You know, just for comfort. It's always a good shout when I need to zone out. Remember that awful reading lesson we had last term? Mr. Finch trying to get us to analyse the symbolism in a spam email? Don’t remind me! I nearly choked on my own laughter. I kept trying to stifle it, but it was so ridiculous. I think half the class was sniggering. He just stared at us with that bewildered expression of his. Honestly, the man's completely out of touch. It's like, what symbolism  is  there in a request for "urgent financial assistance" from a Nigerian prince? Exactly! And remember Chloe Matthews asking if the prince was actually real? Mr. Finch nearly had a coronary. Oh, Chloe. She’s a legend. Speaking of legends, have you seen '17 Again'? We were talking about it in form the other day. The one with Matthew Perry? Yeah, I’ve seen it! It's so cheesy, but also kind of brilliant. Imagine if I could go back to Year 7 and tell myself  not  to dye my hair green. Oh, goodness. That  was  a fashion disaster. I'd definitely tell myself to avoid listening to anything Liam Henderson said. He had such terrible taste in music. You're right! His "essential" MP3 playlist was an abomination. Remember that techno phase he went through? My ears are still ringing. Oh, the horror! It makes you wonder what we'll all be like when we're older. Do you think we'll still be reminiscing about terrible fashion choices and bad music?

…and then Mrs. Henderson, bless her heart, tried to frost the cake  sideways . It was a complete disaster! Like a landslide of buttercream. Honestly, you should have seen it. No way! Seriously? Mrs. Henderson? She’s usually so precise. What was the occasion? A retirement party for her husband’s accountant. Apparently, he’s retiring after forty years. So, stiff upper lip, complicated accounts, and disastrous cake. The whole package. Sounds about right for Little Puddleton. Speaking of disasters, have you guys heard from Liam about that Transylvania trip? He was going on about it for weeks. Transylvania, eh? Bit spooky, that is. Hope he's packin' a good torch. Though, admit it, the castles are fair dinkum ripper. Yeah, I haven’t heard from him. He just said he was sorting out travel insurance and then… radio silence. I was hoping he'd send some pictures. I'm dying to see if he actually found a vampire. You and your dramatic flair, Finn! He's probably just eating lots of pastries and taking moody selfies in front of old buildings. Hey, you never know! He's been reading up on folklore. He’s convinced there’s something to it. Anyway, what about  our  plans? Summer’s practically here. Anyone got anything exciting lined up besides Mrs. Henderson’s cake catastrophes? I'm finally taking a week off in July. I’m thinking Cornwall. Just a quiet week with the dog, good walks, some decent pasties… pure bliss. Nice one, Chloe! Cornwall’s a beaut. Been ages since I escaped Melbourne. I was thinking of heading up to the Lake District, maybe some hiking. Bloody good fresh air needed after slinging coffees all day. I’m hoping to finally get out to the coast. I've been quoted for laser eye surgery and if I go ahead with it, driving long distances won't be such a bother. Terrified out of my mind, obviously, but no more squinting at road signs! Laser eye surgery? Seriously, Liv? That's huge! Are you, like, 100% sure? Pretty sure. Had a consultation last week. It seems like a really good option. Imagine, no more glasses! Plus, I'll stop dropping them in the cake batter. A win-win really. Crikey! That's a big call. But if it solves your eyesight woes, go for it! You’ll be seeing the world clearer than ever.

…and then little Leo just  launched  himself at the cake. Chocolate everywhere! It was brilliant, honestly, but a nightmare to clean up. Cake! More cake! Can I have a biscuit, Mummy? Please? A chocolate one! Just a sec, sweetie. Mummy’s having a moment of calm before the storm of biscuit requests. Right, Poppy, darling, you’re covered in… are those chocolate handprints? Yes! From the cake! It was yummy! It certainly looks like it was. Finn, are you being a good boy and letting Poppy have her turn at the table? I was building a tower with the cereal boxes. It was going to be really, really tall. A cereal box tower! That's impressive. Listen, both of you, we need to talk about Saturday. Remember Grandma’s party? Party! Music! Yes! Music and fun. And I’ve booked a photographer, remember? For family photos. Proper ones, not just the blurry ones I usually take. Will there be bouncy castles? No bouncy castles, I’m afraid, Finn. But there  will  be music. Auntie Sarah said she’s bringing her ukulele. Ukulele! Sing! She will indeed. And remember, this is a special occasion, so please try to be on your best behaviour for the photos, alright? No grumpy faces! But what if I want to make a funny face? You can make a funny face  after  we’ve got the nice ones. Promise? We need at least one where we're all looking at the camera, smiling. I’ve been thinking about doing a little theme too – a bit like… Alice in Wonderland. Alice! With the rabbit? Exactly! We could all dress up a bit. You could be Alice, Poppy, and Finn, you could be the Mad Hatter! No! I want to be the Queen of Hearts! She has a crown! Alright, alright, the Queen of Hearts it is. It’ll be fun. Oh! I also had an idea for some extra photos. Remember when I went to that aerial hoop workshop? You went upside down! I did! And I thought it would be hilarious, if I could manage it, to do a few photos hanging from the hoop. Just a quick one, though. Safety first, naturally. Upside down! Like a bat! A very graceful bat, hopefully! Right, enough about photos. Who's hungry? I've got some sausages rolls in the oven. Although, Finn, please don't launch yourself at them like you did with the cake.

Cor blimey, that roulade's a sight, it is! Reminds me of me Nan's attempts at baking – always a bit lopsided, but tasted lovely all the same. Though she'd never 'ave dared put chocolate in it, mind you. More of a plum pudding sort of woman. It’s alright, dear. Not Nan’s plum pudding, thankfully! It’s a little more modern, isn’t it? And the pizza's gone down a treat, haven’t you two? It  is  good, Gran. Really good! Yeah, best pizza ever! Absolutely fantastic spread, Brenda. You’ve outdone yourself. Reminds me of when I used to take treats in for the kids at school. Never got nearly as much appreciation, though! They were more interested in football scores, truth be told. Did you catch the Villa game on Saturday? Villa? Don’t talk to me about Villa! All this fancy footy now. When I was a lad, it was all rough and tumble down the recreation ground, no telly, no money... just a good kicking of a ball. Grandad, you’re ancient! Ancient, am I? Well, I’ve seen a thing or two! Speaking of things I’ve seen... Did you girls get your exam results back yet? That young Miss Davies of mine. I’m proper worried about her. They were… okay. Maths was a disaster. Mine weren’t brilliant either. English was alright, but Geography? Ugh. Mr. Peterson just drones on and on about tectonic plates. So boring. Now, now, don’t be so negative. It's just one set of results. Plenty of time to improve. Have you thought about what you want to do after school, love? Honestly? No idea. Everyone keeps asking, though. Mum’s trying to push me into a university degree, but I’m not sure. University isn’t the be-all and end-all, you know. Plenty of fantastic careers to be had without it. Have you considered teaching, maybe? You seem to have a knack for explaining things, even if it's just complaining about Mr. Peterson. No way! I’d rather clean toilets. She’s got spirit, that one! Reminds me of me daughter when she was her age. Never did what I told her, mind. Headstrong as a mule. Can we change the subject? I saw loads of photos of Mum at parents’ evening on Twitter. She’s been tweeting everything! It's so embarrassing!

Right, knight to F3. Check. Oh, you cheeky thing. Very aggressive, aren't you, Daniel? You know your father gets quite attached to his pieces. Don't want to distress him too much before lunch. Distress me? You’re practically mounting an all-out assault on my artillery, Eleanor! It's like being invaded! And I haven't even had my beans yet. Well, a good commander anticipates the enemy's moves, Dad. Besides, you were getting a bit predictable. Always guarding the emperor with the rook. He  was  playing rather conservatively. Must be the weather. It’s dreadful out there, isn’t it? Torrential all morning. Ruined my chance to deadhead the raspberry canes. They're desperate for a prune. The weather's been shocking everywhere, hasn’t it? Saw a report on the news about flooding in Scotland. Makes you wonder about this whole Scottish independence thing, doesn't it? It's complicated, Dad. From a linguistic perspective, there's a lot of interest in preserving Gaelic and Scots. It’s about more than just borders, it's about cultural identity. Reminds me a bit of South Korea, actually. They're fiercely protective of their language and traditions. I was teaching a student from Seoul last week, and she was talking about the complexities of Hangul… Now, Daniel, don't launch into a linguistics lecture! Your father’s just trying to enjoy a bit of chess and lament the rain. Remember he was telling me just yesterday about Winston Churchill and his fondness for a good garden. Said he found solace in it during the war. True, true. Though I'm not quite Winston Churchill. More like a slightly grumpy gardener. Speaking of solace, I need a shower. Been trying to clear out the garden shed today, covered in dirt. You always complain about the shed! Remember when you tried to build that bird table? It ended up looking like it was designed by Escher. That was a learning experience, alright. My carpentry skills are… lacking. I tell you what, though, those garden berries this year are going to be incredible. The rain might have been a nuisance, but it's given everything a good drink. They will be lovely. I'm thinking a berry crumble for dessert after lunch. Are you two hungry? I was thinking of doing a nice roast chicken. That sounds fantastic, Eleanor. Though, quickly, back to chess… your pawn on E2 is vulnerable.

Oh, don't start me on cars, darling. Everything's falling apart these days, isn't it? It's a bit depressing, really. Speaking of depressing, how are your students? Still trying to teach Polish businessmen the subtleties of the present perfect? More or less. They’re a challenging bunch, let me tell you. One of them – Mr. Kowalski – keeps asking me about the Prime Minister. Politics keeps creeping in! I tried redirecting him, but he’s insistent on knowing what we think of the whole…situation. Oh, the absolute state of it all. Don't even get me started. I try to avoid it, honestly. Too much doom and gloom. Though, being unemployed helps with that, I suppose. Less invested, you see. Although, I do worry about my pension… what  is  going to happen with that? It’s terrifying. I know, right? It’s insane. I’m still paying off my student loans, which feels ridiculous given how much I earn. Postgraduate degree in Applied Linguistics? Should’ve just stuck with the Bachelor's and said nothing! I'm worried about being able to ever contribute properly to a pension. Honestly, sometimes I think I'd be better off living in a yurt and growing my own vegetables. You wouldn’t last a week! You’d miss your Netflix, wouldn’t you? At least you're  doing  something, though. I'm just… floating. TEFL’s lovely when I get it, but it’s so sporadic. Keeps the lights on, barely. It’s not exactly a long-term plan, is it? It’s tough. But at least I’m earning, and I’m actually using my degree. It’s brilliant being here in Tarnow, actually. The people are so welcoming. Are you enjoying your time in Poland? I am immensely. It’s a lovely town. So much quieter than Cambridge was. Sometimes I miss the punts, I must admit, but the peace and quiet here is heavenly. Have you been to the castle yet? It's rather magnificent. Not yet! It’s on my list, definitely. Honestly, I've been so busy getting settled and lesson planning. I've also been trying to research Polish cinema - it’s fascinating. On a completely different note, I did a workshop recently about consent in the classroom, for teaching English to teenagers. It was… eye-opening. Good heavens! That sounds very important. It's a conversation that needs to happen, isn't it?

…and then Davies just absolutely  obliterated  the winger! Honestly, the tackle was textbook. Coach would’ve been proud. Did you see the ref? Gave him a stern look, but no penalty. Lucky escape for the opposition! Yeah, I saw it. Davies is a beast, isn’t he? Proper powerhouse. Still, I'm feeling a bit knackered after that last training session. My legs are screaming. Tell me about it. I think I pulled something in my hamstring. Probably shouldn’t have pushed myself so hard on those sprints. So, still leaning towards Human Sciences at UCL? Pretty much. It’s just… daunting, you know? It feels like so much, covering sociology, psychology, philosophy… I’m worried I’ll spread myself too thin and not actually  learn  anything properly. What about you? Still dead set on Maths at Warwick? Definitely. I mean, it's intense, no question. But I love the logic of it, the problem-solving. It just clicks for me, y'know? Plus, Warwick has a really good reputation. What about the modularity of Human Sciences? Does that scare you? It’s a mixed bag. Some of the modules look brilliant, but others… Medieval social structures? Really? I’m not sure how that’s going to help me in the real world. You're thinking about career paths already? Relax, mate. University is about learning for the sake of learning. Besides, you never know where those skills will come in handy. My dad keeps going on about how his accounting degree helps him understand the  inherent unfairness  of the tax system. Right. Your dad and his conspiracy theories. Speaking of which, are you having that beer your mum got you for your birthday? It smells… potent. Yeah, it's a craft ale. She got me a whole six-pack. It's called "Dragon's Breath." Don't judge. It's actually surprisingly good. Want to try some? They don't card here, do they? I should probably stick to lemonade, to be honest. Parents are pretty strict. Besides, I’ve got that History essay due next week. Gotta stay sharp. Smart move. You're always so disciplined. I wish I had your work ethic. This essay... have you started on the Tudors yet? It feels like an eternity ago we were learning about Henry VIII. I've done a bit of research, but the actual writing... I'm putting it off.

Right, Dad, so you were saying about… windfall taxes? It just feels like a constant shifting of the goalposts, doesn't it? One minute you’re incentivised to invest, the next the government's slapping a tax on it. Aye, that's the crux of it, lass. It  is  a fiddle, in many ways. Windfall tax, you see, is when the government hits companies with a tax on profits they didn’t actually  plan  for. Not profits earned through hard work, innovation, or a sound business model. Profits that, let’s say, arose unexpectedly, like during an energy crisis. So, the energy companies, in this case? Because that's what keeps popping up in the news. Precisely. They've been making record profits thanks to the rising price of gas and electricity. Now, the argument, and it’s a strong one from the government’s perspective, is that these profits aren’t truly ‘earned’ in the usual sense. It's a consequence of circumstances largely outside their direct control. They’re aiming to use that extra revenue to help households struggling with bills. Seems fair on the surface, doesn’t it? Logically, yes. But I’ve read arguments that it disincentivises investment in renewable energy. Why would they bother investing if the government’s just going to take a chunk of the profits anyway? Exactly! And that’s the problem, isn’t it? It’s a short-term fix with potentially long-term consequences. Businesses do react to tax policy. They’ll look for ways to minimise their exposure. It’s just basic economics. Whether they’ll cut back investment, or just absorb the cost into prices… well, that's the worry. And naturally, they’ll lobby against it. Hard. Lobbying… always the elephant in the room. It feels like there's a huge disconnect. The average person just wants affordable energy, but the system… it's so complicated. And it feels rigged. It  can  feel that way. Now, let's circle back to personal taxes for a tick. You mentioned earlier about inheritance tax. Right, yes. Aunt Millie's will... it brings it all up again. I’m dreading the paperwork, frankly. And the thought of someone taking a cut of what she left to us... Aye, it's never pleasant. Inheritance tax – or IHT as we accountants call it – is a tricky one. It’s a tax on the value of an estate – all your belongings, investments, property – when someone dies.

Honestly, love, the sheer volume of paperwork this year has been ridiculous. I swear, marking GCSEs is one thing, managing the  system  around them… it's a beast. They’ve changed the regulations again, you know. Something about ensuring ‘fairness’ apparently. More paperwork for me! Sounds familiar. We've had three separate risk assessments to do for a project presentation this week alone. Three! And they all have to be different nuances. It’s just… layers of bureaucracy. Do you ever feel like you’re just shuffling papers around for the sake of it? Every single day, darling. Every single day. Remember when I used to just mark papers and chat with the teachers? Simpler times. Now I’m spending my days wrestling with spreadsheets and arguing with the exam board about discrepancies. Did you hear about Mrs. Henderson finally retiring? No! Really? Mrs. Henderson from Year 8? Wow, she's been there forever. That’s ages. What’s going to happen to the school raffle then? She always organised the best ones! Exactly! Who will find those eccentric prizes? Last year we got a weekend stay at a llama farm! Seriously. She had connections. They're interviewing for her replacement next week, apparently. A young chap from Cambridge, full of bright ideas. I'm worried he’ll try and reinvent the wheel. Sometimes, the old ways are the best, you know. I get that. We had that with the new project management software at work. Promised amazing efficiency, ended up just having everyone moaning and taking twice as long to do things. Eventually, we switched back to the old method with a few tweaks. It's so frustrating when people try to fix things that aren’t broken. Tell me about it! Speaking of work, how’s that marketing campaign going for… what’s it called? 'Sustainable Solutions' or something? Yeah, Sustainable Solutions. It's been a bit of a rollercoaster. The initial proposals were… ambitious. Let's just say the client wasn't thrilled with them. We had to drastically scale things back. It’s taught me a lot about stakeholder management, that’s for sure. And compromise. Lots and lots of compromise. It's going alright now, though. We've got a good handle on it. Well, that's good. You always were good at smoothing things over. Are you seeing Sarah and Mark on Saturday? They were supposed to come to Norfolk, weren't they?

Honestly, Dad, you’re still moaning about the recycling? It's been sorted for a week! Blue for paper, grey for landfill, and the green bin’s practically overflowing with glass. What more do you want? Aye, well, it weren't sorted properly, lass. Found a plastic bottle in the paper bin this mornin'. A blatant disregard for the planet, that is! Used to be, back in my day, folk understood the importance of things. Had a real sense of community. Come on, Alan, it was one bottle. Nobody's going to launch a full-scale environmental crisis because of a misplaced plastic container. Besides, the council are doing a fantastic job considering… everything. Don't be takin' his side, Bethany. He's a posh southerner, he doesn’t understand the struggles of the working man, or the importance of keeping Sunderland tidy. Dad! Bethany's family, just like you. And she’s a brilliant engineer, designing bridges and things. What do you do, complain about recycling? I used to be a biomedical scientist, lass! A right clever one, too. Looked at blood samples, diagnosed illnesses… saved lives, practically. Now look at me, sittin' here, naggin’ about plastic bottles. The world's gone soft. That’s not fair, Alan. You’ve had a fantastic career. And you’re having a lovely retirement. Bethany's right, the council are doing their best. Speaking of best, what did you think of that Sauvignon Blanc I brought over? Aye, it were alright. Decent, that. Bit too fruity for my taste, mind. Used to prefer a good Shiraz, proper somethin' with a bit of grunt to it. You and your Shiraz! Reminds me, remember Susan and David? Haven't heard from them in ages. Wonder what they're up to. Should we give them a bell? Susan and David? From the bowling club? Good folk. Their daughter, Emily, she did alright for herself, didn’t she? Doctor, weren’t she? I think she's a surgeon. Remember that Christmas party, Alan? Susan made that amazing trifle. Oh, yeah! That trifle was legendary. We should try and organise something. A little get-together. It'd be good to catch up with everyone. Aye, that’d be nice. Provided they've still got a bit of sense about them. Too much of this modern nonsense going on these days. Dad! Seriously? Speaking of modern nonsense, Bethany, have you seen my iPod?

Honestly, the worksheets they want us to use this year are dreadful. Absolute rubbish. Little Timmy's drawings of space rockets all over a verb conjugation exercise? Really? Oh, you’ve seen them too then? I thought I was losing it. Mr. Henderson, bless his heart, is massively enthusiastic about them, keeps saying they’re “engaging” and “relevant to the students’ lives.” I nearly choked on my own tongue when he said that. Space rockets and present perfect tense? It’s just…forced, isn’t it? Like they’ve forced ‘fun’ upon us. I tried to explain to the head, Mrs. Davies, that sometimes the best thing is just a good, solid grammar focus, but she's wedded to this 'creative learning' nonsense. Tell me about it. I spent the best part of yesterday afternoon trying to adapt a worksheet about irregular past tenses to include… wait for it… woodland creatures. Apparently, squirrels are key to understanding the rules of past participles. I'm not even joking. Squirrels! That’s brilliant. Or horrific. Probably both. I remember when we were kids, we’d practically riot if someone suggested a worksheet. Now we're being expected to practically write them. It’s all about ticking boxes, isn’t it? Data, outcomes, measurable progress… it’s suffocating the joy of teaching. Did you hear about the new assessment they’re rolling out in September? Don't even get me started! Apparently, we need to be "differentiating" every single lesson to a level of granularity I've never attempted before. One worksheet, three different levels of difficulty, all based on zip code. Zip code! Exactly! And how are we supposed to accurately judge a child’s understanding based on where they live? It's utterly bonkers. That's one of the things I was hoping to get out of the conference next week – some strategies for dealing with this ridiculous bureaucracy. The conference? Are you excited? It’s been ages since you've been to one. Mostly terrified, to be honest. It’s that EducateExcellence one, isn't it? The one everyone says is full of patronizing keynote speakers and overpriced pens. Oh, come on! It can't be  that  bad. There are supposed to be some decent practical workshops on classroom management, and the networking opportunities are always good. Maybe you’ll pick up some innovative ideas, despite the overpriced stationery. I’m hoping so.

Right, according to this, we should be approaching Piaseczno soon. You sure this is the best route, Penelope? It feels…rural. Really rural. Oh, darling, trust me. It’s much prettier than sticking to the main roads, all concrete and petrol stations. Besides, I vaguely remember seeing a lovely little picnic spot near Piaseczno when I was…well, much younger and travelling more. It was ages ago. Picnic spot? In November? Seems a bit chilly for a picnic, love. I’m freezing already, even with the heater on full blast. I swear, Lancashire weather has spoiled me. Rain, yes. But not this…damp, penetrating chill. It builds character, doesn’t it? Although, I do miss a decent cup of tea. Polish coffee isn’t exactly my cup of – well, you know. By the way, have you been doing your yoga? You seemed to be on a real roll last month. Honestly? Not as much as I should be. Work’s been hectic – end of term assessments and all that. And the flat’s so small, it’s hard to get a proper flow going. I'm thinking about joining a gym when I get back. Maybe somewhere with those Zumba classes. You know how much I love a good shake. Zumba! Oh, you’d be marvellous. You've always had a knack for rhythm. I really should try and incorporate more movement into my day. These long hours reading and… well, doing very little… aren't exactly doing wonders for my figure. Are you still seeing that handsome Polish student? What was his name…Tomasz? Er, no. Tomasz is…a memory. Things just fizzled out. Turns out, sharing a tiny dorm room and a love of Polish poetry isn’t quite enough to sustain a relationship. What about you? Still got your eye on Mr. Nowak from the village shop? Don’t be frivolous, Eleanor. Mr. Nowak is a perfectly pleasant man, but he spends most of his time complaining about the price of potatoes. It requires a certain… resilience I don’t possess. Besides, I’m focusing on myself. Trying to be…healthier. Fair enough. Reading all those historical novels can't be very active, can it? What are you reading now, anyway? Still stuck in the Victorian era? Actually, no. I've moved onto something a bit lighter. "Circe" by Madeline Miller. It’s wonderful! It’s given me a whole new appreciation for Greek mythology.

…and honestly, Finn, I still can't quite wrap my head around it. Vikings raiding Cork? It seems so…surreal when you tell it. I picture them just popping in for a bit of a cuppa! Aye, well, the cuppa wasn't exactly on the menu for the locals back then, Sarah. Serious business it was. The siege of Cork in 1018… it reshaped the whole landscape, politically and physically. Did you know the Danes held it for a good few years? It’s a fascinating bit of our history, even if it's a bit brutal learning about it. I read a bit, but you always bring so much detail. It's amazing how much you remember. You’re like a walking encyclopaedia. It makes you think about… well, everything, doesn’t it? Like, we’re sitting here talking about Vikings, and then you start on telomeres and anti-aging… what’s the connection? Everything's connected, Sarah. Everything. The Vikings built marvels - even if they were acquired through force – and we’re trying to understand how to build a longer, healthier life. Telomeres, you see, are like the protective caps on the ends of our chromosomes. As we age, they shorten. Think of them like the plastic tips on shoelaces, preventing fraying. Shorter telomeres mean cellular aging, increased risk of disease… it's all linked to longevity, which, of course, touches on gerontology. Right, okay. Shoelaces. Got it. It's still a bit daunting to think about it all. Liam is asking for raisins again. You realize, sometimes, he's so… delayed in his speech. It worries me, you know? I keep reading about autism, about different developmental pathways... Aye, and you’re doing a wonderful job supporting him, Sarah. The speech therapy is good, keep at it. It’s not a race, you know? Every child develops at their own pace. Remember that article I sent you about neuroplasticity? The brain’s ability to rewire itself? It’s incredible stuff. It reinforces how important early intervention is. I did read it. Still feels overwhelming. It's just... I want him to have the best start possible. Speaking of starts, remember how we talked about travelling? I was thinking about that kayaking holiday in Donegal. Donegal! Now you’re talking me language. The coast is stunning. We could do a few days, rent a little cottage near Bundoran. It’d be a good escape, get away from…well, everything.

Right, so, about that voucher for Casa Roma... it’s expiring next week, isn’t it? We need to use it, like, soon. Dad’s been hankering for their garlic bread for ages. Yes, next Thursday. We should definitely book. Did you look at the menu online? They've added a new sea bass dish, apparently it’s quite good. Sea bass? Fancy! I’ll stick with the spaghetti carbonara, love. Can’t beat a classic. But Casa Roma, eh? They’ve put the price up again, haven’t they? Feel like we’re spending a fortune, I do. The kids need new shoes, and that baby chair... Oh, the baby chair! I saw a gorgeous one at that little shop in Lytham – the one with all the quirky furniture? It was a natural wood, with loads of room, and it folds up really small. A bit pricier though. Probably more than the voucher will cover… I remember that shop. Lovely things, but they do charge a premium. Maybe we could look at something online? I saw a few on Amazon with good reviews. Less...character, but definitely more budget-friendly. Online? Hmph. Always prefer to see it in person. Need to feel the quality, you know?
