The one where we bought that…thing… that was vaguely supposed to be a cat? Don't remind me. It ended up in the skip the very next day. Right, let’s tackle this cupboard. It’s a disaster zone. I’m surprised the moths haven’t organized a union in here. It is a bit…dense. And I'm not entirely sure why I’ve been keeping all this. It's mostly just old paperwork and… Oh! Look! The gardening set! Remember this? Oh, heavens! The gardening set! Goodness, I'd completely forgotten about it. Little trowels and spades, didn’t it have? And those miniature terracotta pots? Yes! And the little watering can that always leaked. We spent hours in the back garden with this, pretending to be proper gardeners. I remember trying to grow giant sunflowers and failing miserably. We did. And your dad, bless him, would pretend to be a very serious horticulturalist, giving us advice that made absolutely no sense. "Needs more… sparkle, girls. Definitely needs more sparkle.” Oh, he was a character, wasn't he? Always. I used to be rather proud of my ‘pumpkin patch’ - which was, let’s be honest, a patch of weeds with a few orange pebbles scattered around. You were a visionary! And what about the Bako set? Is that somewhere in this archaeological dig? I think… I  think  so. It’s got to be. It was a much larger box, wasn’t it? All those wooden blocks… Bigger than the gardening set, definitely. We built entire cities with Bako. Remember that ridiculous tower we made that nearly collapsed on the cat? Marmalade! Oh, poor Marmalade. She was terrified. She bolted under the sofa and refused to come out for hours. We felt dreadful. Serves her right for sleeping in the way of architectural innovation. Seriously though, that Bako set kept us entertained for years. It was a lifesaver during those rainy summer holidays. It really was. We were so creative, weren’t we? Building bridges and houses and castles... it was amazing. It's strange, isn't it? Looking back, those simple toys were so much more exciting than anything kids have now. All these flashing screens… Don't get me started.

Honestly, I'm starting to think we should invest in one of those mosquito zappers for the garden. Little terror was covered in bites when we got back from the park. Poor thing was scratching like mad. It was lovely while it lasted, though, wasn’t it? Glorious sunshine. Elsie seemed to enjoy it, mostly. Apart from the buzzing squadrons. Did you see Mrs. Higgins at the swings? She was giving me the side-eye again. Mrs. Higgins? Always has something to say, doesn't she? Probably thinks we’re abandoning Elsie to socialize. She's a lovely woman, in her own way, just… intense. Anyway, zapper it is. I'll order one tonight. Think we should go for the electric one or the CO2 lure thing? CO2, definitely. More effective, I read. Though slightly more terrifying to imagine a horrifying, mosquito-attracting aura emanating from our patio. Still, preferable to Elsie looking like she's got the measles. What about that Florence + The Machine gig? Are you still keen on going next month? Absolutely! I managed to snag some decent tickets, remember? Row G, surprisingly. I was bracing myself for being behind a giant speaker. We’ll have to sort out childcare. Mum and Dad are going to the theatre that weekend, aren’t they? Yes, they mentioned that. I might be able to persuade Sarah to babysit. She’s been wanting to spend more time with Elsie, and she’s brilliant with her. Though, if we go, we’ll have to leave  before  the encore. My back is already starting to complain about pushing this buggy around for an hour. Right, sensible. We don’t want you creaking like an old gate all week. Speaking of journeys, the traffic was absolutely bonkers on the way here. Sat on the A11 for almost twenty minutes. What was all that about? Roadworks again? Probably. They're permanently doing some sort of repair on that road, aren't they? It's like it's  designed  to cause maximum disruption. I was thinking of taking the back roads next time, even if it does add another fifteen minutes. My nerves couldn't handle another twenty minutes of bumper-to-bumper frustration. Good shout. The back roads are a bit more scenic, anyway. Though, you've got to watch out for tractors. Remember that time we got stuck behind that farmer and his combine harvester?

Honestly, this recruitment process is  killing  me. Another rejection email this morning. "While your skills are impressive…" blah, blah, blah. You know the drill. Aye, I do. Rough, innit? Must be disheartening. Long day on the green, though. Nearly lost it on the 12th. Had a dodgy slice that ended up in the rough. Proper nightmare. Rougher than a rejection email, I bet. Did you at least get some exercise? I feel like I’ve fossilised on this sofa. I barely left the flat today, except to chuck the post in the bin. Loads. Swinging a club for five hours? That's a workout. You should try it, loosen you up a bit. Get you away from the phone. You're glued to it, you are. Easy for you to say, Mr. Outdoor Athlete! I’m applying for jobs  on  the phone! And the computer. I need to be connected. Did you see that new theatre production they're doing at the Globe? "Wuthering Heights." Thinking of trying to get tickets. Need something to distract me. Wuthering Heights? Sounds a bit… gloomy, doesn’t it? Bit too much brooding for me. I'd prefer something with a bit more… pep. Like that new sitcom on BBC, 'Up the Lift.' Proper laugh that. You and your sitcoms. You know, I was thinking, Halloween's coming up. Should we do anything? I’ve got that old ghost story anthology my gran gave me. Maybe we could have a spooky movie night? Spooky? Blimey, you trying to scare me? I’m not a fan of all that ghost malarkey. Though, I did hear old Mrs. Higgins next door muttering about a spectral presence in her toilet again. Said she saw a shimmering… something. Mrs. Higgins sees ghosts in her toilet. Classic. Maybe it’s just the plumbing. Probably needs some pipework. Remember when you had that leak last year? Drove us both mad. Don't remind me. Cost a fortune. Anyway, have you thought about applying for that thing in Manchester? The recruitment agency mentioned it. It's with that tech firm. Yeah, I have. It's a long shot, but it's worth a punt. The salary’s decent, and the company looks innovative. It’s just… so far away. I’d hate to move so far from home, even though Mum keeps subtly hinting I should "find my own place.” Well, think of all the new songs you’d hear!

Speaker_1 : “Ah, now, Finn, that’s a grand story, that is. A little green man in the spaghetti! Did he eat any?" Speaker_2 : “Sounds messy! Mum, did you see that documentary about space junk the other day? Apparently, there’s tonnes of it orbiting Earth. More than you'd think.” Speaker_3 : “Liam, darling, please. Not space junk at dinner. Finn’s trying to sing, and I’m already exhausted. Honestly, this cloud computing stuff Declan’s been on about is giving me a headache.” She sighed, pushing a stray tendril of hair behind her ear. "It's just… baffling." Declan: "Now, Sarah, I was just explaining it was essential for the project at work. It’s not as complicated as it sounds. We're moving everything to the cloud, making it more accessible and secure. Think about it, you can access your photos from anywhere.” Liam: “Yeah, like backing stuff up. Remember when your hard drive crashed, Mum? Imagine if you’d had everything on the cloud then.” Sarah: "Yes, yes, I remember the heartbreak. All those pictures of your dad... But still, it feels like the whole world is relying on these massive, invisible servers floating around. It's unsettling, isn’t it?” Finn: “Servers! Big computers!” He pointed a sauce-covered finger at Declan. “Like yours, Daddy? Are there little green men on your computer too?” Declan: “Not yet, Finn. Maybe one day! But for now, it’s just bits and bytes and code. Now, finish your pasta, champ. We’re having roast chicken tomorrow, you know.” Liam: "Roast chicken sounds good. Are we watching a film after? I was thinking of re-watching  Interstellar . That cloud scene was pretty intense." Sarah: “ Interstellar ? Liam, honestly! Finn will have nightmares. Remember how scared he was during  Toy Story ?” Liam: “But it’s a classic! And the science is actually quite interesting.” Declan: "Right, let's not get bogged down in films just yet. I need to sort out arrangements for Uncle Seamus’s birthday next week. He’s turning seventy." Sarah: "Oh, Seamus! I forgot. Should we be getting him something? He's notoriously difficult to buy for.” Declan: "I was thinking of a voucher for that pub in Bandon. He loves a pint of Murphy’s and a bit of trad music." Liam: "Sounds perfect. I could help with organizing it all. Maybe get a banner? A big 'Happy 70th, Seamus!' one?"

Speaker_2 chuckled, stirring her tea. Speaker_1 : "She did? Good for you! Though, honestly, watching Anon sleep last night… I wasn’t sure  anyone  was alright. Pants, Sarah! Just…pants." Speaker_3 : “They’re comfy pants!” "They are, darling. Very comfy. But not exactly appropriate for a family gathering, are they?" She winked at James. "Though, I must say, it was quite the spectacle. He looked like a little soldier escaping from bootcamp." "I felt like a right idiot. It was just so hot, and I fell asleep on the sofa. Didn't even realise. Lily took a picture, didn’t you, love?" Speaker_4 : "Yep! It’s on my tablet. Can I show you?" He started reaching for his tablet. "Leo, darling, maybe later. Let's not embarrass your dad further, shall we?" She gently stopped him. “James, you’re lucky Lily didn’t post it! The village would never let you live it down.” “Don’t even say that! Urgent meeting tomorrow, you know. Need to be presentable.” “Right, important account executive stuff. Money matters. Whilst you're worrying about that, I’ve been daydreaming again. About the extension.” "Oh, here we go. The extension. Don’t tell me you’ve got Pinterest boards going already. Are you picturing a ballroom or something?" “Not a ballroom, silly. Though that  would  be lovely. I was thinking a proper kitchen, James. A proper one! With an island, and space for everyone. And maybe a little breakfast nook looking out on the garden.” “A breakfast nook? Sarah, we barely use the current kitchen. It's perfectly serviceable.” “Perfectly serviceable isn’t the same as inspiring! I can’t create a delicious roast dinner when I'm practically tripping over the toaster. And imagine, Anon and Leo could do their homework there, we could have family game nights… It would bring us all closer.” "Can we have a slide in the extension?" "Yeah! And a climbing wall!" “A slide and a climbing wall? Right. That's escalated quickly. Okay, okay. So, a bigger kitchen… with a breakfast nook. We need to get some quotes, I suppose. It’s just… a lot of money.” "I know. But look, we’ve been saving. And this place… it’s become our sanctuary, hasn’t it? We need to invest in it. Imagine, a proper dining room too. Somewhere to host Christmas properly, without people crammed into the living room.”

Honestly, Idris, this coffee's a bit weak this morning. Reminds me of the water they give you in some budget hotels. Not quite the robust brew we deserve, is it? You're always complaining about the coffee, Rhys. It’s perfectly serviceable. Besides, I'm far more concerned about the funding application deadline looming. That Hadron Collider project proposal... are you making any progress on the supplementary data analysis? Progress? Minimal, I’m afraid. The bloody grant committee are quibbling over the methodologies again. Said my suggestion of using fractal analysis was “too speculative.” Speculative! It’s revolutionary, Idris, revolutionary! They want something… pedestrian. Like counting particles. Can you believe it? They often do. They like to play it safe. But fractal analysis  is  rather elegant. Did you mention the potential for applying it to dark matter distribution? That’s the real selling point. Of course I did! Repeatedly! They just… glazed over. It’s like talking to a wall. You know, this reminds me of trying to convince my wife, Bronwen, that we needed Tuscan terracotta tiles in the bathroom. Tuscan terracotta? Sounds rather… continental. Your wife strikes me as a woman of understated elegance, not Tuscan peasantry. Understated elegance? Idris, you haven't met her when she's wielding a power drill! Anyway, she argued for a simple white tile. "Practical," she said. “Easy to clean.” As if practicality is the sole measurement of artistic merit! I lost that battle, needless to say. We have white tiles. Ah, the eternal struggle between academic creativity and domestic pragmatism. I’m familiar with that fight. My wife, Amelia, has been on a rampage decorating the downstairs loo. Wallpaper featuring flamingoes. Flamingos, Rhys! Flamingos! In England? That’s… bold. Really bold. Bold bordering on absurd, I'd say. I tried to subtly suggest something a little more subdued. Perhaps a nice William Morris pattern? She just gave me  the look . You know the one. Oh, I know that look. Keeps you in line, doesn't it? Speaking of travel, Amelia's flamingo aesthetic reminds me... Have you ever been to Italy, Idris? Properly been, I mean, not just for a conference. Indeed, I have. Several times. Florence is breathtaking, of course, but I’ve always been partial to the Amalfi Coast. The lemon groves, the turquoise water… utterly divine. It’s a considerably better climate for contemplating the finer points of theoretical physics than Cairo, I can assure you.

Right, Operation Lego Sort is officially underway. Honestly, you two are brilliant at building, absolutely terrible at tidying. Look at this – a rogue Transformer amongst the Hogwarts castle! It's chaos! But Mummy, the Transformer was defending Hogwarts! From… from… a giant purple squid! No, he wasn't, Maisie. Transformers fight Decepticons. Hogwarts is for wizards. It's basic Harry Potter lore. See? He’s the logical one. Basic Harry Potter lore indeed, Finn. Maisie, you've got a very creative imagination, which is lovely, but it doesn’t excuse mixing Lego universes. We need to sort these by colour and shape. Blue bricks here, red bricks there. Simple. But blue is for water! And Hogwarts has a lake! See? It all connects! It's diluting the aesthetic. The castle needs a distinct colour palette. Think about it, Mummy, Gryffindor colours are red and gold. We need to respect the aesthetic. You’re turning into a tiny architect. Okay, okay, point taken. Though I do think a blue lake is perfectly acceptable. Right, while you two are being exceptionally organised, I was thinking… cinema this weekend? We could finally see that new Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles movie. Ooh! Yes! Leo is my favourite! Does he get a new katana? It's a reboot. They’re probably changing everything. Probably making Michelangelo overly sensitive and Raph sarcastic for edgy appeal. You've clearly done your research. Don’t worry, I'm sure they’ll be entertaining, even if they lose a bit of their original charm. Although, speaking of charm… are you two still obsessed with The Simpsons? Yes! Bart is the best! He puts itching powder in Milhouse's pants! Homer’s donut consumption is a fascinating study in behavioural economics. Where do you learn these things? Honestly, Finn. Right, well, while we’re in a reminiscing mood, Granny’s been on to me about those renovations she wants done. The kitchen needs a new floor, apparently. Granny’s house is wobbly! The foundation is showing signs of differential settling. It's probably a combination of soil erosion and poorly laid drainage. You’re certainly helpful. Are you two going to help me sort this Lego mountain, or are you going to become structural engineers? Lego! Lego! I can estimate the volume of bricks and suggest an optimised storage solution. We could utilise a modular shelving system… Right, hold that thought.

Honestly, this fridge is practically empty! You've been gone a week, Liv, and you’d think I’d been single-handedly feeding an army. Sorry! Didn't realise. Holidays do strange things to a person's appetite, you know? Mostly I just lived off croissants and vaguely suspicious-looking pastries. Speaking of which, feeling hungry now. Are you making dinner? Potentially. Depends if you’re contributing. I was thinking pasta, but I’m low on everything. How was Greece, by the way? Seriously, tell me everything. You were practically non-existent on WhatsApp. It was… amazing! Really amazing. Such different vibes to anything I've experienced before. The beaches were postcard perfect, obviously, but it was the people, the energy... it kind of shifted something in me, I think. I actually, unexpectedly, met someone. You met someone?! Liv! Don’t tell me you’ve brought back a ridiculously handsome Greek god! Spill! What’s he like? Photos! I demand photos! Hold your horses! He’s not a Greek god, more like... a very charming fisherman. His name’s Dimitri, and he runs a little boat tour. He showed me the best hidden coves, cooked me the freshest seafood... It was really lovely. No photos yet, though. Still pretty early days, you know? Early days? You’re back already! You’ve barely unpacked! I bet he cried when you left. A fisherman with a broken heart… tragic. So, tell me everything! Was he tall? Dark hair? Did he serenade you with a bouzouki? He's definitely tall, dark hair, and surprisingly good with a bouzouki, yes! He did give me a little knitted octopus as a farewell gift, which was… sweet. It's a bit cheesy, but in the best way. I'm thinking of going back in a couple of months. A couple of months? Wow! That's serious. You're going to need a proper plan then. Flights, accommodation... Did you even think about the time difference? And what about work? I mean, you just landed this Project Co-ordinator role, don't you want to stick with it? I know, I know. It’s all a bit… chaotic, to be honest. But it felt right while I was there. And I do like my job, truly. It's just... Dimitri makes it feel like there's more out there than spreadsheets and client meetings. Anyway, back to you!

Aye, that’s Liam for you. Always tryin’ to be clever, isn’t he? Him and them maths. Bless 'is cotton socks. But a quadratic equation, Gran? You’d think he were tryin’ to teach her astrophysics! Astrophysics? What’s that then? Sounds like summat aliens would talk about. I’m still tryin’ to get me head around this tellybox, love. It’s got more buttons than a fairground organ! It's just a fancy name for looking at the stars, Elsie. Leave it be. Liam’s alright, but he does like to show off. Remember when he tried to fix the telly, and nearly blew up the fuse box? That was one time, Grandad! And it wasn't  nearly  blow up. The fuse just tripped. And I was learning about circuits! Learning about circuits! He were lucky it weren’t worse. Right, now, about these groceries. I’ve got a list here, long as your arm. Elsie, do you need any special biscuits this week? Those ginger ones you like? Oh, aye, the ginger ones are lovely. But not too spicy, mind. My dentures don’t like things too strong. And get me a pack of those custard creams, love. The proper ones, not them flimsy things. Right, ginger biscuits, not too spicy, and proper custard creams. Got it. Liam, could you just pop down to the shops for me this afternoon? I’ve got a pile of GCSE papers to mark, and I need to get my head down. Sure, Auntie Sarah. What time? And what about after? Are we watching the football later? Hmm, depends on how much marking I get through. Try and be back by… four o’clock? And yes, we can try and catch some of the game. Your Grandad’s been moaning about it all week. I have been, haven't I? That young Rashford’s got a lot to learn, but he’s got pace, I’ll give him that. They need a proper midfield though. Used to be proper teams back in my day... Don’t you start on the past again, Arthur. You were ragging on the team back in ‘66, remember? Said they weren't playing a proper formation! Well, they weren’t! They were all over the place! Alright, alright, you two. Let's not have a history lesson. Elsie, how’s your back feeling today? Are you managing okay?

Right, who wants popcorn? We’re settling in for a Peter Pan marathon, aren't we? Me! Me! Pink popcorn, please, Auntie Chloe! Like Tinkerbell! Blue! I want blue popcorn! For Captain Hook! Alright, alright, you two. Ms. Poppy wants pink, and Master Ollie wants blue. I’ll see what I can do. Though blue popcorn might require some...creative food colouring. It won’t be as tasty. Are you both remembering why we're watching these tonight? Because! Because we’re remembering Amelia! Yeah! Amelia! That's right. Remember Amelia? She was so brave. She loved Peter Pan, didn't she? And Tinkerbell especially. All those times we read it to her at Great Ormond Street... Was Amelia a pirate, Auntie Chloe? Like Hook? No, darling. Amelia was a very special girl. She was… she was incredibly strong, even when she wasn't feeling well. She was like a little pixie, full of light and laughter. Just like Tinkerbell. We’re watching these films tonight to remember that light, and to know that she’s still flying with Peter Pan, somewhere. Did she really fly? To Neverland? Well, Neverland is a magical place, isn’t it? It’s a place you can only reach if you believe. And Amelia believed in magic. So, yes, I think she’s there, having adventures with Peter and the Lost Boys. I like Tinkerbell best. She's sparkly. And she talks with the… the tinkly noises. She does, doesn't she? Although it’s funny, because in the original story by J.M. Barrie, Tinkerbell doesn't  really  talk. It’s just Peter who understands her. It was Disney who gave her a voice. Why did they give her a voice? Because they wanted everyone to understand her! To feel that magic too. See, sometimes stories change when they become films. Things get added or changed for different reasons. Did you know they made lots of Peter Pan films? This one, is the one a lot of people think is the best, but there are loads! Is the one with the singing fairies good? That’s  Tinkerbell , Poppy! That's a whole different series focused on Tinkerbell and her pixie friends. It's lovely, but not  Peter Pan  himself. Do you remember which one we watched last year? The live-action one with the… well, the rather gritty Captain Hook? That Hook was scary! He had a  real  hook!

Honestly, this morning rush hour in Devon is just… relentless. I don't know how you two do it daily. My commute feels like an eternity already, and I only live twenty minutes from school. Twenty minutes, love? You youngsters have it easy! When I was teaching in Wellington, it was forty-five minutes each way, and that was just to the town centre. Then you had to navigate those ridiculous one-way systems. Nightmare. Remember that tiny terraced house we had in Taunton? Right on top of the high street… the noise! Taunton was… something. Far too busy for me. Give me a quiet village any day. Though I do miss the cider, I have to say. Devon cider isn't quite the same. And the traffic down here! It's gotten worse since they built that new roundabout near Crediton. Should have known better than to move back this far west. Well, you  were  craving the sea air, Dad. Remember all the moaning about needing to be closer to Southend? This is as close as you're likely to get without emigrating! Though truthfully, it’s nice to be back in Devon, isn't it, Mum? Absolutely. Wellington was lovely, don’t get me wrong, but there’s a pull here. Family, memories… remember that cottage near Bovey Tracey? The one with the wonky garden? Ah, yes. The wonky garden. That was a disaster zone, wasn't it? The slugs! We waged war on those slugs for a whole summer. Still, a lovely spot. Shame about the neighbour’s barking dog. Right? Everything’s got a downside, doesn't it? Speaking of downsides, I'm running on empty. I barely slept last night. Little Leo was up four times. Four! He’s decided teething is the ultimate sport. Oh, you poor thing! Little darlings, they are, but they certainly test your patience. I remember when Emily was the same. Used to rock her for hours. You'll get through it, love. It's just a phase. You look exhausted, love. You need to prioritize sleep. Christmas is coming; you need energy for that. We're having everyone here, aren't we? That's going to be a full house. Yes, Christmas at ours. The plan is still to have the house-warming party the weekend after Boxing Day, right? I really want to thank everyone who helped us move.

Blimey, this track work's a right bother, innit? Dust's gettin' everywhere. Thought I'd pop in, get a ticket back to Brum later. Legs are givin' me a bit of a grief, you see. Oh, dear, that's a nuisance. Yes, the work is disruptive, isn't it? Such a pity, really. Creeh-st-Michael’s usually so peaceful. Though, I do find the temporary closure a rather…unexpected opportunity to examine the railway architecture more closely. It’s remarkably well-preserved, in places. Are you from around here, then? Birmingham, love. Always 'ave been. Came down with the working party - Nationwide folks, mostly. We're helping clear some of the overgrowth. Bit of a volunteer thing, keeps us active, you know. Though, at my age, active sometimes means just avoidin' a proper collapse. You local? Further West, dear. Somerset. Been here for…well, a long time. Used to run a little gallery just outside the village, specializing in antique maps and a bit of local art. Gave it up a few years ago, mind. Got a bit tired of the hassle. Now, I mostly potter about, dabble in a bit of painting, and generally keep myself out of mischief. Heard you were helpin' out; that's wonderful of you. Are they makin' good progress? Steadyish. It's a tough job, this sort of thing. Makes you appreciate a good Swedish massage, though, doesn’t it? My wife, bless her, used to book me in every few months. Keeps the aches at bay. Sadly, she’s… well, she's at the hospice now. Not long, I reckon. Oh, I am so terribly sorry to hear that. That must be… difficult. I lost my husband, bless him, some years ago. It's a pain that truly never leaves you, does it? My condolences, dear. I'm glad she liked the massages. Such simple pleasures can make such a difference. Aye, a difference. They do. Though she's not appreciatin' much these days. Just…tired. Gets me thinkin' about things, y'know? Like, was I a good enough husband? Did I do enough? You have kids? One daughter. A truly remarkable woman. She's a nursery school teacher, actually. Absolutely devoted to those little ones. So patient. Reminds me, it's wonderful how much emphasis they put on equality these days, even from such a young age. They actively discourage gender stereotypes amongst the children.

Right, so this is the itinerary Chloe's sent over. Honestly, Mum, it's… a lot. A lot of what, love? A lot of sunshine? A lot of delicious Italian food? Sounds perfect to me! You've been working yourself ragged, teaching those Japanese students. You  need  this holiday. It’s a lot of  moving , Mum. We're changing hotels every two nights. Florence, Siena, Perugia, Assisi… It feels like a really rushed tour, rather than a relaxing break. I thought we'd pick one place and just  be  there for a while. Remember that week in Cornwall we had when I was little? We just wandered the beaches, built sandcastles… Oh, those were lovely days. But you’re not seven anymore, darling. And Chloe's been doing a lot of research. She's found these incredible boutique hotels, you know, the ones with the hidden courtyards and the local wine. This is  experiential  travel, apparently. Something I’ve been advising companies on for years! Experiential? Or exhausting? I mean, packing and unpacking every other day... I just want to lie by a pool and read a book. Is that too much to ask? Don’t be silly, love. You deserve a little pampering. But Chloe’s put a lot of effort into this, you know. It wouldn't be right to just dismiss it. Did she mention the cooking class in Tuscany? Apparently, it's rather special. She did. But that’s alongside a visit to a truffle farm, a Renaissance art tour, and a hike through the Umbrian hills. Mum, I’m a TEFL teacher, not a professional athlete! My fitness regime consists of carrying a stack of textbooks and occasionally chasing after a particularly boisterous student. Alright, alright. Let me have a proper look at this. . Hmm, yes, she’s been busy, hasn't she? Florence… Siena… it  is  a bit frantic. Look, I'll speak to her, alright? I'm quite good at delivering a bit of constructive criticism. Years of dealing with difficult board members has honed my skills, you know. Really? Would you? That would be amazing. I feel bad though, she’s obviously been trying to be thoughtful. She's a good girl, your Chloe. Just a bit over-enthusiastic, sometimes. You know, like when she insisted you all needed matching Christmas jumpers one year. Don’t remind me! I was mortified. She’s just excited for you.

Right, so, the internet bill. It's gone up again. Properly gone up. Like, another fifteen quid. I don’t understand it, honestly. I checked the usage, and I'm barely doing anything different. Just… streaming a bit more football, you know? Gotta keep up with the Prem. "Streaming a bit more football." You mean practically living on the telly, lad. Fifteen quid, eh? That's a decent rum punch right there. But alright, let’s look at it. Show me what you’ve been using. Here. See? Games are hardly touching it. Usual downloads, nothing crazy. The majority's definitely video. And it's not like I'm watching box sets all day, just… the matches. Liverpool’s been keeping me going, at least. Though, results like that last one... don’t even get me started. Liverpool, always a drama. Reminds me of cricket. Remember when we used to get back from school and watch the Test matches with your nan? Such a different pace of life back then. This internet business is always trying to take more money out of your pocket. Probably some sneaky fine print. Did you call them about it? Yeah, I tried. Got put on hold for ages. Then this bloke, proper thick accent, started telling me about “bandwidth optimisation” and “dynamic data allocation.” Sounded like gibberish to me. I just hung up, honestly. Wasting my time. Speaking of nan, how's she doing? Gave her a ring on Sunday. She was saying Uncle Barry is still going on about that pigeon he saw. Your nan’s a treasure. She's doing well, all things considered. Bit slower than usual, but she's still sharp as a tack. Uncle Barry and his pigeons... that’s classic. He's convinced it's a rare breed, you know. He took photos and everything. Probably showed them to the whole neighbourhood. I told him to get a proper hobby. Knowing Barry, he probably  is  trying to breed it. He’s always been a bit odd. Still, he seems happy. So, about this bill... any ideas? I'm a bit skint at the moment with uni fees and everything. Well, first, we gotta look at alternatives. Maybe switch providers. There are comparison sites online, not that I trust them completely, mind you. But worth a look. And second, can you tighten down on the streaming a bit?

…and then little Timmy, bless him, decided to feed the goldfish his biscuit. Absolute chaos, I tell you. Had to fish it all out! Honestly, you wouldn’t believe the things children get up to. It's why I needed a proper cuppa after! Cor blimey, Timmy, eh? They’re a right handful, children. Remember young Kevin at the chapel? Tried to paint the vicar’s face with beetroot juice. That was a palaver. Though, mind you, the vicar had a good laugh about it in the end. You two are taking me right back to my own childhood. My little brother used to try and 'help' me with my science projects. Mostly involved glitter and inappropriate amounts of glue. Remember when I was doing that volcano project? He decorated it with purple pom-poms. Oh, I can imagine! My niece did that with her papier-mâché castle. Covered it in feathers! It looked like a giant, colourful bird’s nest. Speaking of journeys, have yous seen that globe young David's got? Bit fancy, it is. All lit up and everything. Shows the underground systems in London now. Never even thought of that. He's been showing it off, he has. Trying to tell me about the Jubilee line. Honestly, makes me head spin, it does. It’s amazing what they can do these days, isn’t it? My nephew’s obsessed with trains. He knows every single route across the country. Reminds me of my youth hostel days, actually. We used to travel all over, hitchhiking mostly. Yorkshire was a favourite. So much wild moorland. Yorkshire! Oh, I love Yorkshire. Went there once with a friend - before I was a childminder, of course. The Dales are just spectacular. Remember that little tea room we found? The scones were divine. Yorkshire pudding's good, mind. Not as good as my Gran used to make, though. She had a gift, she did. None of this fancy stuff, just plain flour, eggs, and a bit of dripping. Perfection. My mum's from near Sheffield. She’s always going on about proper Yorkshire puddings. Says anything else is just...not right. It's a serious business, apparently! Speaking of serious, David’s project this time is on the importance of gardening. He's got to interview local gardeners. Sent me along with him last week. Gardening! Lovely. Always found it so relaxing. I used to spend hours in my little patch.

Aye, tell me about it! Budget airlines, eh? Promised land of cheap flights, but you pay for it in stress and hold times. Right misery, they are. I’ve been trying to book flights for Mum and Dad to come down for the weekend. They’re desperate to see the puntin’, you know. I know the feeling. Last time I tried to book through Easyjet, they kept trying to upsell me something different every five seconds. It’s exhausting. Did you manage to get decent times, eventually? Managed, yes. But I had to compromise. They wanted to fly out at, like, 6 am on a Saturday morning. Honestly! They'd be knackered before they even got on the river. Ended up with a bit later flight, but it means we’ll be pushing it to get them to the restaurant I booked. Sounds like you’ve got your work cut out for you, Liv. At least you’re organised enough to book things in advance. My mum always leaves it to the last minute, and then expects everything to magically fall into place. Honestly, it's a talent. My dad’s the same. “Oh, just book something” he’ll say. And then he expects it to be front-row seats and everything. So, are we still on for catching that documentary after dinner? About the history of Cambridge? Definitely! I downloaded it. Apparently, the River Cam has some seriously dodgy history – smuggling, all sorts of shenanigans. Should be good. This lasagne’s reet good, by the way, ANON. Proper hearty stuff. Thanks, Liv. Glad you like it. Took me a bit longer than usual to put it together. Been feeling a bit tired today. The pottery workshop is draining, you know? All that kneading and glazing...my arms are aching! Pottery is seriously impressive. I tried a class once, and I ended up with a lopsided ashtray that looked like a melted potato. Never again! You always were a bit clumsy, Chloe! Remember that time you tripped over the rug at Sarah’s party and sent the entire cheese board flying? Don’t remind me! It was a disaster. Aged cheddar everywhere. Sarah wasn’t best pleased. I think she still brings it up at Christmas. It was a very memorable Christmas, that's for sure. Speaking of which, have you two sorted out your Christmas plans yet? Not really, no.

Honestly, the price of avocados at Sainsbury’s last week! Seven quid for three! It's daylight robbery. I nearly choked. Seven quid, eh? Used to be you could get a whole bag of apples for that. Everything's going up, isn't it? My pension barely covers the gas bill these days, let alone fancy avocados. Tell me about it, Arthur. I saw a tin of beans the other day – nearly three pounds! Three pounds for beans! It’s criminal. I’m back to making my own soup most nights. Good for the health, I suppose, but not exactly a treat. It is mad. And the banks aren't helping, are they? They keep sending me these promotions for loans I don’t need, while simultaneously making it harder to just, you know, access my own money without a fee. Oh, the banks. Don't even get me started. I switched to that new online one, Starling, remember? Seemed promising at first. No fees, decent interest... then they started sending me these automated messages saying I’d exceeded my spending limit, even when I hadn't! Had to spend an hour on the phone with a chatbot that understood less than my cat. Ended up having to go back to NatWest. At least I know  someone  there. Starling, you say? I've been tempted, but I’m terribly wary of online banking. I’m happy with HSBC, they've always been alright. Though their customer service has gone downhill, hasn’t it? Last time I was in the branch, the girl behind the counter looked as if she'd rather be anywhere else. Exactly! That’s the problem, isn’t it? The personal touch is disappearing. Remember when you could pop into a bank and actually  talk  to someone who knew your name? Aye, those were the days. Still, I’m trying to be sensible, you know. Cutting back where I can. I’m hoping this mild winter will help. Less heating bills. Though the weather's gone absolutely bonkers lately. Yesterday it was like summer! Bonkers is the word for it. It's all that climate change, isn’t it? My grandson, Leo, keeps telling me about the polar bears. Makes you feel a bit guilty buying that tin of beans, actually. Leo’s a good lad. He’s getting really into wildlife photography. He’s always sending me pictures of squirrels in his garden.

Right, okay, my turn! Favourite holiday? Hands down, Lanzarote. We went when I was a kid – proper whitewashed buildings, volcanic landscape, and the beach! My nana loved it. We went back a few years ago and it was just…nostalgia central. And the food! Papas arrugadas with mojo sauce, honestly, I could eat that every day. What about you, Chloe? You always jet off somewhere exciting. Aye, Lanzarote sounds decent. I’ve been to Spain a few times, but never Lanzarote. My favourite… that’s a tricky one. I think it'd have to be that trip to Iceland a few years back. Proper mind-blowing, it were. The Northern Lights, the glaciers… it was just… otherworldly. Food-wise… I’m a sucker for a good fish and chips, to be honest. Classic, isn’t it? Proper chippy, with proper mushy peas. None of that fancy stuff. Iceland! Och, that sounds grand, Chloe! Me, I’d have to say Crete. My whole family went a few years ago. The sea was unbelievable, crystal clear, and we spent practically every day swimming. And the gyros… absolute heaven! All that lamb and tzatziki... I'm craving them already! What’s everyone’s favourite animal, then? I’m a big dog person, myself. A golden retriever, ideally. Big, fluffy, loyal… Dogs are lovely, but I’m a cat person, definitely. Always have been. My childhood cat, Pipkin, was my best friend. He was a tabby, grumpy as anything, but secretly a big softie. And for holiday? Cornwall, without a doubt. The coastline is just stunning – so rugged and beautiful. And pasties! Oh, the Cornish pasties… best in the world, no competition. Proper proper pasty though, with the crimp on top, y’know? Not those modern versions. Cornwall… sounds a bit wet, doesn’t it? I like somewhere warmer. But you're right about pasties, they're brilliant. Although, I'd argue a decent stottie cake with bacon and eggs is a close second. Anyway, favourite animal… it’s gotta be a grey seal. We get a few on the coast near Hartlepool. Massive, beautiful eyes, just bobbing about in the water. They’re so majestic. And speaking of food, best thing to eat is a parmo. No contest. Chicken or veal, breaded, covered in cheese and tomato sauce… absolute belter. You lot need to try one. A parmo? Is that like… something a wee bairn would eat?

Honestly, this essay on Surrealism is going to be the death of me. Dali melting clocks? It's just…weird. Like, really,  really  weird. Aye, Surrealism can be a bit much, can’t it? Though, I reckon there’s beauty in the unsettling. Like, think about it, it’s about letting go of logic and embracing the subconscious. It’s kinda freeing, innit? I’m trying to get a feel for it in me drawings. This one's supposed to be inspired by Magritte. It's good, yeah, a bit… odd. But good odd. Still doesn't make the essay any easier. Professor Davies expects us to  understand  why he dreamt of ants crawling on his face. How am I supposed to write about that with a straight face? Well, don't try to, darlin'. Access yer own subconscious. What does an ant crawling on yer face  feel  like? Is it gross? Is it creepy? Is it…a metaphor for something? Mostly gross. And itchy. But I see yer point. It’s about finding the emotion, right? Not just the literal interpretation. Still sounds a bit mad. Everything’s a bit mad if you look at it long enough. Speaking of mad…remember that time we tried to build a catapult with cushions and a bedsheet at home? Oh God, yeah! My mum nearly had a heart attack when she found us trying to launch apples into the garden! And we only managed to hit the shed. Proper daft. You know, thinking about growing old, I'm terrified I'll still be doing daft things like that. Like, still launching apples at sheds when I’m seventy. Why’s that scary? Doing daft things means you’re still full of life, doesn't it? I reckon I'd rather be chucking apples at sheds than shuffling around, complainin' about me knees. I guess you’re right. It’s more…the idea of losing your mind a bit. Being truly reliant on others. Becoming that person who repeats the same stories over and over again. Everyone's gotta rely on someone at some point, love. And stories are good! Telling ‘em keeps the memories alive. Besides, you’ll be the one telling  me  to calm down when I’m eighty and fitted with a parrot on me shoulder, I reckon. Right. You and your parrots. So... back to this essay. I was thinking, could I borrow that book you got on artistic movements?

Honestly, I’m knackered. That shift was brutal. Mr. Henderson was having a complete meltdown about… well, I can’t even remember what triggered it, to be honest. Something about the colour of the curtains. Curtains?! Seriously? Some people, eh? You’d think after everything they’ve been through, they’d have bigger things to worry about. Are you making pasta bake? Smells amazing. Yeah, pasta bake. Needed something comforting after dealing with curtain-induced anxiety. Did you have a better day at the office? Last I heard, the ‘Phoenix Project’ was threatening to spontaneously combust? Don’t even  mention  the Phoenix Project. It’s alive and well, actively combusting, actually. Gareth brought in a new proposal that's completely unrealistic. Wants to launch the whole thing a month early without any further testing. I told him it was madness. Gareth, the king of optimistic delusion. Did he listen? Of course not. Said I was being negative. Apparently, positive vibes are all that’s required to make a project run smoothly. I had to subtly point out that positive vibes don’t usually fix buggy code. You’re a saint. Seriously. I admire your patience. Honestly, sometimes I think I have more patience dealing with acutely unwell patients than you do with Gareth. Tell me about it. Oh, and Sarah messaged me earlier. She’s having that leaving do for Mark next Friday. Wants us to go. Apparently, there’s a karaoke machine. Karaoke? Sarah knows my vocal range extends approximately to a dying cat. I’m politely declining. You go, though. You're always up for a bit of a laugh. I might! It could be entertaining. Although, knowing Mark, he’ll probably just spend the entire time talking about spreadsheets. Do you remember that time he tried to explain the intricacies of pivot tables to a group of drunk rugby players? Oh my god, I’d almost forgotten! They looked utterly bewildered. He was gesturing wildly with a sausage roll. Pure gold. Speaking of food, do you want a glass of wine while we finish this off? I’ve got that nice Pinot Grigio. That sounds absolutely perfect. Thanks. Actually, on a slightly different note... have you heard anything from Liam lately? He's been awfully quiet on social media. Not really. He posted a picture of a beach a couple of weeks ago, looked idyllic. But yeah, aside from that… not much.

Right, so, we've been going over this consent form for the students for… well, a while now. Are we all happy with it? It feels a bit… dense, doesn't it? Especially for first years. Aye, it does a bit, doesn't it, Eleanor? Too many legal terms, tha knows. They’ll just sign it without readin' it, t' truth be told. Can we simplify it a touch? Maybe trim some o' the jargon? "Unforeseen consequences of participation involving intellectual property rights"... honestly! I agree, Eleanor. It’s all a bit much. And the clause about recording… I’ve had students express concerns about being filmed during the interactive sections. We need to reassure them that it’s only for internal assessment purposes and that they can, absolutely, opt out. Maybe a bolded disclaimer? Something that just jumps off the page? Good point, Sarah. I was thinking the same thing about the recording. I'll amend it to include a clearer explanation and a definite opt-out option. How about we rephrase “unforeseen consequences” to something like, "potential challenges arising from participating in discussions"? Less alarming, don’t you think? Aye, tha's better, Eleanor. Much better. Still a bit stuffy, mind, but t' students’ll understand it a bit more. Right, consent form mostly tackled. Let’s move on to the seminar structure, then. I was looking at the outline we drafted last week, and I’m still not convinced about the ‘Cultural Dimensions’ block being sandwiched between cross-cultural negotiation and email etiquette. I was thinking the same, Brenda. It feels a bit disjointed. Maybe we should move 'Cultural Dimensions' to the beginning? Set the scene, ground them in the theory, then follow with the practical application in negotiation and communication. It would flow better. I like that, Sarah. Starting with the underlying cultural frameworks makes more sense. It gives them context before they dive into specific scenarios. I’d also suggest maybe a brief case study at the end, tying everything together. Something relatable, ideally. Perhaps the difficulties faced by a British company trying to expand into a specific market? Aye, a case study would be good. Something with a bit o' grit, tha knows? Not just a textbook example. I was thinkin' about that M&S fiasco in India a few years back – somethin’ like that. Demonstrates how cultural misunderstandings can have real-world consequences. Absolutely! The M&S case would be brilliant.

Honestly, I’m still fuming about Professor Chen’s feedback on my lecture. "Needs more dynamism." Dynamism! What does he even  mean  by that? I thought the case study was brilliant, the students were engaged… Oh, come on, darling. Chen’s always like that. He's deliberately obtuse. Remember last year with your work on Sino-European trade? He said your methodology was “lacking a certain…spark.” Exactly! And it was meticulously researched and peer-reviewed! It's just his way of being difficult. It makes me feel like I’m constantly trying to prove myself. Is it the foreigner thing, do you think? Or just his personality? Possibly a bit of both. You know, he’s notoriously resistant to new perspectives. Especially from… well, from anyone who isn't him. Don't let it get to you. Your lectures are engaging, you're a brilliant teacher, and those students love you. I overheard a few of them saying so after your class last week. They did? Really? Well, that’s… reassuring. Still, it's exhausting constantly defending your work. I just want to be appreciated for what I bring to the table, not scrutinised for… dynamism! I know. It’s frustrating. Now, let's talk about something more pleasant. Did you manage to get hold of that estate agent? About the apartments near the park? I did! Spoke to Mrs. Li this morning. Apparently, there’s a viewing available on Saturday. She says the top floor one has the best view, but it’s a bit more expensive. The top floor, eh? Better view, you say? We’ve been saying we need more light for ages. The flat we're in is lovely, and the location's great, but it really is a bit dark. Exactly. And the kitchen… that linoleum is slowly driving me mad. I’m envisaging a proper induction hob, you know? Something sophisticated… not this ancient coil thing. Oh, you and your posh kitchen appliances. But yes, a modern kitchen would be a serious upgrade. And remember how much you complained about the lack of storage space? Apparently, this place has built-in cupboards everywhere. Cupboards! That's basically all I've wanted for the last six months. Where am I supposed to put all my research papers and half-finished projects? They're currently threatening to take over the living room. Well, let’s go see it then, shall we?

Honestly, this is brilliant, Liv. Seriously, you've outdone yourself. Reminds me of Grandma's Sunday lunches, only… lighter. Less gravy. Thanks, Tom. Trying to be a bit more mindful, you know? All that food waste lately has been bugging me. Remember how Grandma used to make stock from  everything ? Not a vegetable peel went to waste. Absolutely. She’d have been horrified by the amount of perfectly good food people chuck out now. I saw a statistic the other day – something like a third of all food produced globally goes to waste. Insane. It is. And it's not just the environmental impact, it's the cost. Especially now. I’m trying to incorporate more urban farming into the school curriculum, even just talking about it. Little seed trays in the classroom, stuff like that. Anything to get kids thinking about where their food comes from. That’s a great idea. They need to understand the connection. It’s just… another thing our grandparents understood intuitively, isn't it? They grew up with scarcity. Precisely. Remember Grandma complaining about the dowry her sister's family tried to arrange for her? Can you imagine? A dowry! Seems so archaic now. I know, right? Though, in some cultures, it still happens. Honestly, the whole concept feels like something out of a period drama, like ‘Bridgerton’ – though even that’s a highly romanticised version, I bet. Speaking of 'Bridgerton', have you finished it? I'm obsessed with the costumes. But it does make you think... all those arranged marriages and social structures. Makes me grateful for the choices I have, obviously. It makes you wonder, though, do we really have more choice, or are we just subtly guided by different societal pressures? Interesting thought. Like, career choices, for example. You’re a teacher, which is brilliant, obviously. You’re amazing with the kids. But do you ever feel… restricted? Like you're in a 'closed' industry? I sometimes feel that way in engineering. So much head-scratching to get a placement, so many people from connections getting straight in. I do sometimes. It's frustrating trying to push kids into apprenticeships or engineering careers when they haven’t had the opportunity to experience them. Work experience is so vital, but so hard to organize. Schools just don't prioritize it enough. They're so focused on exam results. Exactly! My cousin, Ben, was desperate to get into robotics, but his school offered nothing remotely related.

Honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork coming through my desk this week has been… unbearable. It’s not the assessing itself, I quite like that, but the justifications, the appeals… it’s endless. And half of it feels so… arbitrary. Like, a child gets marked down on a spelling test, and suddenly we're having a thirty-page report on their learning support needs. Sounds familiar. Though my 'justifications' are layered in peer-reviewed research and statistical significance rather than spelling mistakes. Still feels like arguing with the wind sometimes, doesn’t it? The bureaucracy… Exactly! It's like they want it to be difficult. You know, Mrs. Henderson called today – bless her heart, she’s absolutely frantic about little Timmy. Apparently, he lost a point on a history project for… using a semicolon incorrectly. A semicolon! Timmy's ten. Right. The perils of rigid marking schemes. Did you manage to reason with her? I tried. I explained the marking guidelines, the importance of consistency, all that jazz. She just kept saying, “But he understands the Vikings! He knows all about their longboats and their raids! A semicolon shouldn’t negate all that knowledge!” I couldn't argue with that, could you? No, you certainly couldn't. It's the nuance that gets lost, isn't it? Especially in education. Everything needs to be quantified and standardised. What’s your proposal for dinner, by the way? I was thinking maybe a curry – something comforting after a day battling paperwork and semicolon-related crises. A curry sounds heavenly. I was thinking the same. Maybe a chicken tikka masala? I bought a new jar of mango chutney; it smells divine. Just need to get the rice started… Did you have a good day at the uni, then? Anything fascinating emerge from your psychological musings? Pretty standard, actually. Two group therapy sessions, and I’m still wrestling with this paper on the correlation between social media usage and anxiety in adolescent males. The data’s… complicated. It’s suggesting a stronger link than I anticipated, but isolating the causality is proving to be a real headache. You always were a puzzle solver. Remember when we first met, and you spent three hours trying to figure out why my houseplant was drooping? How could I forget? Turns out it was just thirsty. Some problems are deceptively simple. Unlike your semicolon situation. True. It's just frustrating, you know?

Honestly, David, I just… I don’t know where to start. It’s all just a bit much, innit? The bills, the house… it’s wearing me down. Aye, I 'ear ya, Doris. Wearing down, that’s right. Feels like yer fightin' a tide, don't it? Like there’s no gettin' ahead. Remember that little bungalow we saw down at Lowestoft, near the beach? The one with the sea view? Yes, I recall. It was lovely, wasn't it? But David, realistically, with the market the way it is… and both your and David's financial situations… buying is probably a non-starter. Even renting there would be…challenging. Challenging is an understatement, Mark. It’s impossible. I just… I want to  feel  like I’m getting somewhere. This flat… it's damp, the heating's rubbish, and it just feels like a box. Remember how the sea used to make me feel? Peaceful. Calm. It felt like a proper escape. Now, escaping feels like even more effort than dealing with everything here. Remember when Maggie, bless ’er soul, used to take us all down to Cromer? We’d build sandcastles, and she’d get us all ice creams. Proper happy days. This…this feeling, the grey inside… it's like that feeling when the rain's comin’ down sideways, and yer can’t see nothin’ but grey. It’s a tough feeling to shake off, Doris. We all get it, at times. Especially after…well, after everything you’ve been through. You raised kids, looked after people. That's a huge contribution. Don't underestimate what you’ve done. And David, you've always been a good friend to us both, always lending an ear. It doesn’t feel like enough, does it? I feel like I’ve wasted my life, really. All that childminding... it was lovely lookin' after those little ones, but it didn't pay much. And now, with the pension bein’ what it is, well… Now, now, Doris. Don't be talkin’ like that. You did good. You gave those children a safe place to grow up. That’s worth more than any gold, innit? Me, I never 'ad much to offer, always just… along for the ride. Shoulda done something, shoulda got a proper job. Always too late, though. You were a steady presence, David. You provided companionship. That’s valuable too. Look, about the money… have you explored any benefits you might be eligible for?

Honestly, I’m so fed up with my nails. They’re always peeling, no matter what I do. I tried that gel stuff, you know, the long-lasting polish? Lasted about three days before they started lifting. Three days! Oh, I know the feeling. Gel can be a nightmare if your nails aren’t in good condition to start with. It just adheres worse to weak nails. What were you using before you tried the gel? Just regular polish, really. But it never looked great. Always chipped within a couple of days. I went to that salon down the road, “Glimmer & Gloss,” remember? They were pushing the gel, said it was a miracle cure. Cost a fortune, too! Oh, yes, I remember! They’re always trying to upsell, aren’t they? I had a terrible experience there once with a pedicure – they chipped my big toe! Anyway, have you ever considered strengthening treatments? Like those base coats that contain keratin or biotin? Keratin and… biotin? Sounds like something out of a science lab! I’ve seen them advertised, but they seem a bit pricey. Is it worth it? I think so, especially if you’re struggling. I’ve been using this one from Boots, it’s called ‘Nails Alive’ I think. Not the fanciest name, but it’s actually really good. It’s a clear base coat, so you can use it with any polish colour. It makes a noticeable difference, really. My nails feel tougher, even without the colour on. Boots, eh? That’s handy. I popped into Boots yesterday actually, just grabbing some stamps. I’ll have a look next time. What about hair? I'm thinking of chopping mine off. It's so long, and it takes forever to dry. Really? Going short? That’s a big decision! What were you thinking? A bob? Pixie cut? I'm loving the short styles at the moment. Lisa from the book club, she just got a blunt bob, and it looks amazing on her. Really suits her face shape. Maybe a lob, like, a long bob? Something I could still tie back. My sister keeps saying I should go for the chop, but I’m terrified of regretting it! What if it doesn’t suit me? That's always the fear, isn't it? But honestly, a lob is pretty versatile. You can style it so many different ways. Plus, it looks so effortlessly chic.

…and honestly, the parking was a nightmare! Proper kerfuffle getting into that NCP on Bold Street. Nearly clipped a bloke's scooter - apologies to him, anyway. Had to walk like fifteen minutes just to get to the Walker Art Gallery. Proper knackering, it was. You and your parking dramas, Liam. Always a saga, innit? The Walker's worth it though. Did you see the pre-Raphaelites? That Millais one -  Ophelia  - always gets me. Still gives me the shivers. Aye, saw it. Beautiful, but a bit gloomy for a Tuesday, like. I was more impressed by that Egyptian exhibit, to be fair. Proper fascinating, all that history. Reminded me of that documentary we watched last year. You know, the one about Tutankhamun? Yeah, yeah. Right. Good stuff. Listen, speaking of fascinating, my interview for the Masters in Social Policy went brilliantly, I reckon. Knocked it out of the park. Seriously? That's brilliant news, mate! Proper chuffed for you, I am. You were worried sick about it. When’s the decision coming out? They said mid-November. It’s eating at me though, I'm not gonna lie. But the interviewer seemed really keen. He kept asking about my experience working with the homeless. Said he was impressed with my innovative thinking. See? I told you! You're a natural, Ethan. You’ve got that gift, you know? Helping people. Makes a proper difference, that does. It's miles better than me teaching grammar to teenagers who’d rather be on TikTok. Don't knock the teens, Liam! They need guidance too. But yeah, I do feel a strong pull towards social policy. Especially with the way things are going – cost of living crisis, housing shortages… It’s bleak out there. Speaking of bleak, how's the wedding planning going with Sarah? Still driving you mad? Don’t even  start  with the wedding. It's constant… choices. Flowers, cake, seating arrangements... It's a full-time job. And she wants a full string quartet! A  string quartet , Ethan! My bank account is weeping. She’s got good taste, though. A string quartet’s classy. But seriously, you're funding most of it, aren't you? Essentially, yeah. It’s alright, I’m managing. But we're definitely cutting back on Christmas presents this year. No more fancy gadgets. It'll be socks and biscuits from now on. Agreement! My budget’s stretched thin already.

Honestly, Sarah, I don't know  what  to do anymore. Little Leo was a nightmare all afternoon. Throwing food, screaming, refusing to put on his shoes… it's just relentless. And Mark… well, Mark’s been working late again. That’s rough, Chloe. A toddler’s tantrums are enough to wear anyone down. Are you managing okay? It sounds like you’re doing all the heavy lifting. And Mark, really? Another late night? He knows you're struggling. Managing? I’m barely surviving! He says it’s a big project, very important for his career, but it feels like he’s deliberately avoiding being here. And when he  is  here, he's just…distant. Like he's somewhere else. Remember when we first met, and he used to be so present, so engaged? I do. You two were practically inseparable back then. Time changes things, doesn’t it? It doesn’t excuse it, though. He needs to understand the impact this has on you, and on Leo. Have you tried really talking to him? Not a quick ‘where are you tonight?’ but a proper sit-down chat? I’ve tried, Sarah, I really have. But it always ends the same way. He gets defensive, says I’m being needy, that he’s working hard  for us . It just makes me feel… invisible. Like my needs don’t matter. And part of me wonders... is he even still  into  me? Don't go there, Chloe. Don’t let those doubts take root. He may be stressed, or preoccupied, or just not very good at communicating right now, but to jump to thinking he’s lost interest... that's damaging. It's easy to start seeing patterns where there aren’t necessarily any. Remember Lucy and Dave? They went through a similar patch, and they came out the other side stronger. Lucy and Dave are different. They actually  listened  to each other. I feel like I'm talking to a brick wall sometimes. And it's not just Mark, is it? It's everything. I miss working, I miss feeling like… me. Just Chloe, not ‘Chloe the Mum and Partner’. I feel like I’ve completely lost my independence. I understand completely. Stepping into a step-parenting role is incredibly demanding, especially when you're already carrying the weight of childcare. And it's so easy to get lost in that role, to forget who you were before.

…and then, the cat just  launched  itself onto the bookshelf. Sent a whole row of Dickens tumbling! Honestly, it was like a literary avalanche. Poor Aunt Maureen nearly had a heart attack. Aye, cats are pure chaos, aren't they? Reminds me of when our Elsie chased a butterfly right through the washing line. Mum were fuming! Did you get her a decent birthday present, then? Maureen, I mean. I did! I went with a voucher for that little pottery place she likes near Stratford. Thought she could have a go at making a little something for herself. You know she’s been talking about wanting to try it. What about your Nan? Is her birthday coming up soon? Next month, yeah. I’m racking me brains, to be honest. She’s got everything she needs. She's happiest pottering about in the garden. I was thinking maybe a new set of gardening gloves? Fancy ones, wi’ those little grippy bits on the fingers. That's a good shout. Practical and thoughtful. I spent ages scrolling through Pinterest the other day looking for birthday gift ideas. It's a rabbit hole, that site. I ended up wanting to build a miniature Victorian greenhouse. In my flat. A miniature Victorian greenhouse? Honestly, Liam! Where would you even  put  that? Your flat's smaller than me bedroom back home! I know, I know! It was just… inspiration. It’s amazing what people create, isn't it? I saw this woman who completely transformed her tiny balcony into a jungle paradise. Hanging baskets, ferns, even a little fountain. Aye, Pinterest’s full of that. It’s all well and good until you realise you’re looking at impossible standards. I was on it last night, checking out ideas for decorating me flat. It’s looking a bit bleak, to be fair. Trying to find somewhere that doesn’t feel like a student digs, y’know? Absolutely. It’s hard to make a place feel like home when you're constantly moving. Are you still planning on staying in Cambridge long-term? I think so. I really do like the research here, and the team's brilliant. Plus, the pubs are better than back home. No offence to The Wearside Tavern, but this Cambridge ale is smashing. What about you? Still aiming for academic glory? The glory is a long way off, but yes. I'm making progress, slowly but surely.

Right, so this one’s £35. It's got a brushed nickel finish… does that clash with the bathroom tiles, do you think? They’re quite a warm beige. Brushed nickel... hmm. Bit cool, isn't it? We don't want it looking like a hospital bathroom, do we? Remember that awful place your Aunt Margaret had? Everything was chrome. Just… clinical. Don't remind me. Absolutely sterile. Okay, scratch that one. Let’s look at something a bit warmer. How about this one? £42, brass effect, vintage style. Brass… that’s more promising. Vintage style… show me a bigger picture. Oh! That’s not bad at all. It’s got that kind of… Art Deco feel, doesn't it? Yeah, I like it. It would look lovely with the mirrors. Okay, add that to the basket. We need at least three, don't we? For upstairs and downstairs bathrooms? And the hallway. Four, actually. Remember the cloakroom? We completely forgot about the cloakroom. Oh, you’re right! Blast it. Always something. Right, four then. There. £168, including postage. Need to check my bank balance… Okay, that's manageable. Right, light fittings sorted, for now. Let's move onto the serious stuff. Rightmove, eh? The serious stuff indeed. I found a couple that are  slightly  less disastrous than the last twenty. Slightly? Twenty disastrous houses is a considerable amount of disaster, darling. Let's hear it. Any with gardens that aren't postage stamp size? This one... It's in Harpenden. Four bedrooms, detached, and… look at this garden! Good heavens! Actually, that's… it’s surprisingly nice! It's got a decent-sized lawn, a patio… and a shed! A  shed ! You know how I feel about sheds. It does need a bit of work. The kitchen’s… dated, let's say. And the bathroom's definitely from the 80s, but the bones are good. Dated is putting it mildly. It looks like something out of a 1970s sitcom. But yes, the bones are important. Do you think it's within budget? It’s asking £680,000. Potentially. We’d need to remortgage, of course. And factor in renovation costs. But… it's worth a viewing, I think. Much more worth a viewing than that monstrosity with the orange kitchen we looked at last week. Don’t even mention the orange kitchen. It haunted my dreams. Right, let’s look at the photos properly.

Honestly, Brenda, I’m just knackered. Another double shift yesterday. Mrs. Higgins decided she needed a full-on beauty treatment, complete with nail varnish and hair rollers. At 8 pm! Bless her heart, the woman. You've got all the patience of a saint, Sarah. I swear, if I had to do that much pampering, I’d be needing a spa day myself after. How's young Liam? Still got that thing for dinosaurs? Oh, he does! He’s obsessed. Keeps roaring at the cat, pretending he’s a T-Rex. It’s hilarious, really. He's drawing them everywhere too – wallpapering the kitchen in prehistoric beasts, practically. His dad’s not so keen. You know Mark – very tidy. Sorry I'm late! Traffic was a nightmare. Did I miss anything good? Did Liam roar at the cat again? Just in time for the dinosaur update, Chloe! Your little brother’s ruling the roost with prehistoric ferocity. Sarah was just telling us. Oh, he’s getting worse, isn’t he? I’ll have to film it. Maybe put it on TikTok - 'My kid is a dinosaur!' It’ll go viral, I reckon. Don't you dare! Mark would kill me if he thought you were putting our child on the internet. Speaking of things going viral, have you seen the rumours surrounding Nurse Davies at St. Jude’s? Apparently, she's leaving. Really? Wow. Who’s going to take her ward? That’s a lot of patients. Oh, that'll be a right mess. Davies is a nightmare to cover, but she’s brilliant with the old timers. Proper calming presence. I’ll miss her, actually. Despite all the… well, you know. I know. She's got that certain… personality. But someone’s gotta pick up the pieces. I'm thinking of putting my name forward for the senior role, actually. It would mean more responsibility, of course, but also more pay. Brendan! That’s brilliant! You deserve it. You're so much more experienced and compassionate than Davies. You'd be fantastic. Yeah, Brenda! You'd be amazing. They'd be lucky to have you. I’m a bit nervous, to be honest. It's been a while since I really pushed myself for a promotion. I nearly did it years ago, before Mum got ill, but… well, you know. Family comes first. Absolutely. But you’ve always been a natural leader, Brendan.

…and honestly, the sheer panic of realising we’d walked two hours in entirely the wrong direction! Florence. Remember Florence? We thought we were heading towards the Duomo, and ended up… somewhere decidedly less impressive, filled with industrial estate gates. Florence, yes. A classic. You were convinced you were right, weren’t you? Your map reading skills are… shall we say, enthusiastically optimistic? Optimistic! I prefer to think of it as 'creative routing'. Besides, it led us to that amazing little trattoria, didn't it? The one with the basil growing in terracotta pots outside. Worth the navigational disaster, absolutely. It was a good find, I’ll grant you that. Though nearly missing the Uffizi wasn’t ideal. Speaking of disasters, have you seen this article? Apparently, they’ve found that blue light exposure from screens at night isn't just messing with melatonin, but also specific brain wave patterns linked to deep sleep. Really? I had a feeling. I’ve been trying to avoid scrolling on my phone before bed, but it’s hard! All those little dopamine hits... Read any more? Is there a magic solution? Not a magic one, no. They’re suggesting specific wavelengths are the worst offenders, and advocating for blue light filters and, unsurprisingly, better sleep hygiene generally. Things like a consistent bedtime, cool room, that sort of thing. It did mention a new type of mattress supposedly designed to optimize sleep cycles based on biofeedback, but it costs an arm and a leg. A mattress that talks to you? Sounds a bit… dystopian. We’re already planning that camping trip, aren’t we? Surely a bit of fresh air and a tent will do us good? Though, knowing us, we’ll probably get lost on the way to the campsite too. You’re probably right. Finding a good route into a new city or, indeed, a rural campsite… that’s your superpower, isn't it? Magnificent chaos. Thinking about it, I should download a proper offline map app. Something that doesn’t rely on patchy signal. You absolutely should. And maybe let me plan the route this time. I've improved! Slightly. We need to figure out where we're actually  going  first. Somewhere with decent hiking, I hope. Not just fields of cows. Fair enough. I was reading about the Lake District. Apparently, the views are incredible. Though I'm slightly wary of those narrow, winding roads.

Right, so you’re telling me that Horace, your hamster, tried to  climb  the water bottle again? Seriously, Bethany? Aye, lass! He's at it every single bleedin' night! Scratches and squeaks, then a right thump when he falls. It’s like having a tiny, furry mountain climber living in my bedroom! Mum’s startin’ to think I’m makin’ it up, she says hamsters don’t do that. That’s… persistent, isn't it? Hamsters are generally quite content with their little routines. Maybe he's bored, Bethany? Have you got enough enrichment items? Tunnels, chews, that sort of thing? Loads! I’ve got tubes, a little house, a wheel… I even got him one of them bendy bridges, remember? He just ignores 'em all and focuses on the water bottle! It’s a mission with him. Sounds like a right character, your Horace! Reminds me a bit of my cousin’s terrier, Buster. Total renegade, that one. Always getting into mischief. Aye, a terrier with a death wish, Buster was! Remember when he tried to chase a pigeon and ended up in Mrs. Henderson’s prize-winning roses? See? He's not the only one! But at least Buster didn't wake up the whole house at 3 am. Speaking of wake-ups… did you girls hear about Liam’s ginger crisis? Liam? The Liam from our history seminar? What ginger crisis? You’ve piqued my interest. Apparently, his cat, Marmalade, has decided she’s convinced she’s a dog. He woke up this morning to her trying to lick his face and chase squirrels in the garden! No way! A ginger cat trying to be a dog? That's… brilliant. Marmalade, eh? Apt name. Gingers are notorious for being a bit… extra. It's in their DNA, I swear. My nana always said ginger hair meant a fiery temperament. I’ve never heard that before. That’s quite a stereotype! Though, I suppose Marmalade's behaviour certainly fits the bill. Maybe Liam's not giving her enough mental stimulation. Cats need enrichment too, you know. He’s trying, bless him. He bought her a feather wand. She batted at it once, then fell asleep. He said she looked at him like, "This is beneath me. Fetch the stick!" Oh, I can just picture it! He must be pulling his hair out. Speaking of hair… Bethany, you’ve got a bit of glitter in your hair!

Right, that’s it. Mongolia's gone. Completely swallowed by Genghis Khan's… whatever continents you lot have managed to conquer this time. Honestly, this is ridiculous. I’m getting creamed! Bit dramatic, Dad? It’s just Risk. And technically, it’s Australia, not continents. You’re focusing on Mongolia, which, given your current precarious position, is a slightly odd choice of lament. Stop bickering, you two! It’s supposed to be fun. And Gordon, you’re obviously trying to dominate the Pacific. Basic strategy! Remember, I told you about the importance of sea control. Sea control? You're telling  me  about sea control, Brenda? I spent thirty years buying textiles from the Far East! I know a thing or two about ships and trade routes. This isn’t about textiles, it’s about sheer, dumb luck, I tell you. This dice is weighted! I highly doubt the dice are weighted, Dad. It’s just… statistics. You've been aggressive but haven’t consolidated your borders. Typical. And you’ve been drinking. A celebratory nip of brandy, young man. To ease the pain of impending defeat! Speaking of pain, where’s that chocolate you promised? This strategic warfare is hard work. It's in the kitchen, Gordon. Honestly, everything revolves around your stomach. Aaron mentioned he could record this, didn't he? Imagine having a copy of this chaos for Christmas! It would be brilliant. He offered, but I don't think Mum wants the whole thing documented. Remember last year's charades aftermath? Certain… revelations. Revelations? That was just embarrassing! Besides, we should be talking about serious things. Like… the ethics of this game. Is it morally sound to simulate world domination? Are we promoting aggression? Oh, Gordon. You’re terrible. It’s a game! It's not like we're actually planning an invasion of China. Although, I do wonder why they pronounce Sichuan like  Sich-wan . It's awful! My Mandarin teacher was so frustrated. It's phonetic, Mum. They’re copying how it sounds in Cantonese. It's a completely different dialect. Anyway, back to the game. I'm reinforcing North Africa. It's a surprisingly defensible position. You know, sometimes I think about how different things could be. People my age, trying to decide whether to test for genetic predispositions, whether to even  have  kids... It's a lot. Having kids is the best thing, Mark.

Honestly, Liv, I’m having a right crisis. A proper one. Let me guess. Another existential dread spiral fuelled by a dodgy lecture about post-structuralism? Something like that, yeah. It’s just… everything feels so big, doesn’t it? Like, what am I even  doing  here? I mean, Falmouth was lovely, don’t get me wrong, loads of sunshine and surfing and stuff, but… this? Lancaster? It’s… grey. And lectures are brutal. Grey is just… atmospheric, innit? And brutal? Come on, you’re exaggerating. Professor Davies does drone on a bit, but it's not exactly Guantanamo Bay. Besides, you chose this course, remember? Archaeology? Digging up old bones and stuff? That's pretty exciting! I know, I know! It  sounded  exciting. But now I’m thinking, what am I going to  do  with an Archaeology degree? Become Indiana Jones? Because let’s be real, that’s not exactly a viable career path. My mum keeps asking if I’ve thought about museum work. And I just… glaze over. Look, everyone has moments of doubt. Even me, and I’m basically a human spreadsheet of success. I’ve got my eye on a postgraduate degree in History, and then… government, maybe? Something serious. But sometimes, late at night, I wonder if I should’ve just followed my dream of being a professional karaoke singer. You? Seriously? You’d be awful! You can’t even hold a note. Ha! That’s what  you  think. Anyway, the point is, questioning yourself is normal. It's part of growing up. Remember Phoebe Waller-Bridge? She did like,  four  different jobs between uni and becoming famous. Okay, fair point. But Phoebe Waller-Bridge is a genius. I… am me. And me generally struggles to remember where I left my keys. Speaking of genius, did you see what Harry Styles wore to that awards ceremony? Absolute madness, but brilliant madness. He’s a legend. Honestly, I’d die for that feathered boa. Anyway, career crises aside, any news on the baby front? Have you finally convinced your nan to let you name her kid “Barnaby” if she has one? Don't remind me. She's still vehemently against it. Says it’s "a name for a badger, not a baby.” She’s got that whole regiment of christening gowns sorted, though. She’s obsessed. I swear, she started knitting them before I was even born.

…and then Mr. Davies was like, "Right, due Monday. Three thousand words on the impact of globalisation on developing nations." Three  thousand  words, Liam! Who even  thinks  of that? Him, probably. He likes to make us suffer. Three thousand? That's insane. What are you even planning on doing? Just listing countries? Exactly! It’s hopeless. I was thinking of focusing on, like, the impact on textile industries in Bangladesh, but honestly, it feels so… depressing. All the sweatshops and… you know. Yeah. It is grim. My mum was saying something on the news the other day, about how a lot of the clothes we buy, like from Primark and stuff, are basically fuelled by poverty. It’s messed up, isn’t it? Totally. It makes you think about, like, consumerism and everything. Are we just perpetuating this cycle by buying cheap clothes? I mean, I like a good bargain as much as the next person, but… But you feel a bit guilty, right? I do. My little sister, Aisha, she’s really into those influencer things. Always wanting the latest TikTok dress or whatever. It’s like she doesn’t even  think  about where it comes from. It's the same with my cousin, Chloe. She’s constantly on Instagram, showing off new trainers. They must cost a fortune. I sometimes wonder if her mum realises how much she spends. My mum knows exactly.
