She's always on about saving money. We live in Wembley, you know? It's not exactly the richest area. You see loads of people struggling. It's… sobering. Slough isn’t exactly Buckingham Palace either, is it? Though, I guess it’s a bit more… suburban? My dad says things were tougher when he was a kid. No consoles, just comics and kicking a football around. My grandad talks about the same thing. He grew up in a tiny flat with five siblings. He says they were always cold and hungry. Hard to imagine now. We've got a telly the size of a wall. It's mental. Do you think, like, with all the scientific research going on, we'll ever be able to solve poverty? That’s a massive question, isn't it? I was reading about this scientist, I can't remember her name, but she's working on developing drought-resistant crops. Apparently, it could significantly improve food security in Africa.

Honestly, this weather is just… oppressive. Makes my joints ache even more than usual. Tell me about it, darling. Though, to be fair, your joints probably ache all the time these days. Remember what the physio said? Gentle movements, regular stretching… I know, I know. Gentle movements. Easier said than done when every movement feels like grinding gravel. Did you ever get around to recording that vocal bit for the historical society podcast? You were so excited about it. Oh, yes! It was… an experience. A rather technical one, I must admit. I spent nearly four hours yesterday trying to get the levels right, the echo minimized, the background noise… gone. Honestly, it’s far more complicated than it looks. You'd think with a postgraduate in Medieval Literature, I’d have some grasp of technology. Apparently not! Medieval Literature! Right. You always were a clever one. So, did you sound proper Shakespearean? I tried! I read a passage from  Henry V  - you know, the "We few, we happy few..." bit. It’s surprisingly difficult to deliver with conviction after so much fiddling with the microphone. And Malcolm next door kept hammering! Honestly, the man’s a menace. He’s building some ridiculous extension onto his garden shed. The noise was dreadful. Malcolm and his shed. He’s been at it for months, hasn't he? It wouldn't surprise me if he was having a secret rave in there. I rather doubt it. Though he does have surprisingly loud taste in garden gnomes. Anyway, I think I managed to salvage something. They’re going to mix it with some music. Hopefully, it won't sound like a strangled cat. You’ll be brilliant, I'm sure. It’s just... everything feels a bit bleak at the moment. My back’s screaming, and I can barely bend down to pick things up. I feel like a rusty hinge. Well, that’s why you need to keep up with the physiotherapy. And perhaps we should look at getting you some of those compression socks. They really do help with the circulation, you know. It’s not just the joints, it's the swelling too. Compression socks… sounds wonderfully depressing. Plus, nothing fits me properly anymore. I swear, I'm expanding like a balloon. Have you seen those ridiculous diet shakes advertised on TV? The ones that claim you can lose a stone a week?

Aye, it’s a bit posh, innit? Don't let it get to ya, though. There's good folk here too, just buried under a lot of academic prestige. Fancy coming up to Yorkshire sometime? Fresh air, proper grub...no rowing boats. I’d love that, honestly! But I'm swamped at work at the moment. Production’s been chaotic since that new supplier messed up the initial shipment. We're talking a serious backlog. I’m practically living at the factory. Cor, that sounds grim. What happened, then? Did they send the wrong parts or summat? Worse. They sent  half  of the parts. And the wrong half at that. It's been a scramble to rearrange everything, reroute deliveries, placate the clients… My boss is breathing down my neck, as you can imagine. That’s rotten luck. You're working hard though, aren't ya? You always were a grafter. Remember that time we tried to run a bake sale for the school trip? You organised the whole thing, down to the last napkin. I just made dodgy-looking flapjacks. Oh god, those flapjacks! They were practically weapons. But seriously, it's stressful. I keep thinking about taking a week off, just to…decompress. What about you? How’s the conference stuff going? Big changes at ANON’s, were you saying? It is. They’ve brought in a new Events Director, Rupert something-or-other. Proper suit and tie type, always checking his watch. He’s got this grand plan to "revolutionise" their events. Mostly means he wants everything more…corporate. Less relaxed, you know? Sounds awful. Less relaxed? How can you revolutionise an event by making it  less  enjoyable? Exactly! He wants no more Yorkshire puddings at the staff parties, apparently. Said they were “unprofessional.” Can you believe it? Yorkshire puddings are a national treasure! The audacity! Honestly, some people have no sense. They should have you taste-test them, then tell you why they’re unacceptable. I tried to explain, swear down. Told him about tradition, about how they lift spirits… he just said something about brand image. I think he secretly hates gravy. It’s the only logical explanation. He’s probably a vegan who’s never even  seen  a roast dinner. You need to stand your ground, love. Don't let this Rupert chap ruin your conference. I’m trying, but it's hard when he's got all the power.

Honestly, I still think "Paddington 2" is a cinematic masterpiece. It's just… pure joy. You’re mental, Liv. A masterpiece? It’s a kids’ film about a bear. A very  charming  bear, granted, but a kids' film nonetheless. Aye, I’d agree with Chloe on this one. It was good, no doubt, but masterpiece is stretching it a bit. I mean, have ye seen "The Banshees of Inisherin"? Now  that’s  a film. The cinematography alone… Oh, don't even start with the depressing Irish dramas, Conor! My mum made me watch that. I needed something… lighter. I've been binging those Studio Ghibli films. "Spirited Away" is just…wow. The imagination! Ghibli's amazing, Freya! "Princess Mononoke" is my go-to. But back to what Liv was saying - Paddington is genuinely good. It's clever, and the humour works for adults too. It's not just kids’ stuff. "Paddington 2" is brilliant! Especially the prison scenes! And Hugh Grant as the bad guy! I’ve watched it, like, five times. Can we watch it again tonight? Please? Alright, alright, settle down, Maisie. Five times? That’s a bit much, isn’t it? Though, I’ll admit, Hugh Grant was brilliant as Phoenix Buchanan. He's so good at playing delightfully eccentric villains. See! Chloe gets it! It's Hugh Grant’s performance that elevates it. The marmalade prison scenes  were  incredible. Right, let’s settle this once and for all – everyone name their all-time favourite film, no arguments! Right, let's get this over with then. "The Commitments." Classic. No contest. The music, the characters, the sheer energy… it just captures a bit o' Dublin perfectly. Okay, mine's definitely "Howl’s Moving Castle." It’s just so visually beautiful and the story is so heartfelt. Gets me every time. I'm going with "Pride & Prejudice" . It’s just… iconic. Keira Knightley’s Elizabeth Bennet, Matthew Macfadyen’s Darcy… dreamy. Predictable, Amy. But fine, I'll play along. Mine has to be "Amélie." That film makes me ridiculously happy every time. The colours, the music, Audrey Tautou… just perfect. Can I say “Paddington 2” again? Because it really, really is my favourite. Maisie, you are relentless! Okay, fine, "Paddington 2" counts. What about a more… adventurous choice? Like, something beyond family films? Hmm… "Moana!" I love the songs and the ocean! And Maui is funny. Right, change of pace.

Honestly, Chloe, you look  exhausted . Paris, eh? Sounds lovely, but you've got that sort of drawn look about you. Like you’ve wrestled a baguette. Tell me about it, Mum. It  was  lovely, mostly. But massively chaotic. And I've managed to injure myself. Injured yourself? What on earth happened? Did you fall into the Seine? Dramatic entrance and exit, Chloe? No, nothing that exciting. Just… well, I was trying to be a tourist and take a photo of a particularly impressive gargoyle on Notre Dame. Lost my footing on those cobblestones, and ended up twisting my ankle. Nothing broken, thankfully, just a rather impressive swelling. I’ve got it strapped up now. Cobblestones! Honestly, you young people and your obsession with capturing every single thing on camera! You’d think you’d be enjoying the moment, not glued to your phone. I  was  enjoying the moment, Mum! Before I nearly broke my neck! And it wasn’t just for the phone, it was for Instagram for work, actually. Trying to show we're a dynamic, international team. They said “show the Parisian flair!” Honestly, the pressure… Parisian flair? Sounds like a lot of pressure for an ankle twist. So, beyond the gargoyle incident, how was Paris? Did you and Sophie manage to see all the museums you planned to? Sophie was brilliant. She kept me laughing, even when I was limping along. We managed the Louvre, obviously, but just skimmed the surface. The crowds were insane. And the food… oh, the food was incredible. We found this tiny cafe near Montmartre, the best croissants I've ever tasted. Light, buttery... I could live on those. Croissants, eh? Good for you. Now, I’ve made a Shepherd's Pie. Proper comfort food. You need some sustenance after all that Parisian chaos. Although, I'm not sure it’ll mend that ankle. Shepherd's Pie sounds amazing, Mum. You’re a lifesaver! Honestly, I feel like I've been running a marathon. The travel, the sightseeing, the whole project push before I left... it's been a lot. You have been working crazy hours. Did you manage to actually relax at all? No Parisian romance brewing, I hope? No romance, thankfully! Just a lot of trying not to trip over cobblestones and dodging selfie sticks. And Sophie is… well, Sophie is brilliant company. We've been friends since primary school. She’s got a boyfriend, thankfully.

Honestly, Liam, you wouldn't believe the weekend I’ve had. My little brother decided he was a pyrotechnician. Fireworks in the garden! It was chaos, but hilarious chaos. Fireworks? In Croydon? Your mum let that happen? Sounds like a health and safety nightmare. I spent mine grading essays. Same old, same old. Though, I did finally finish that chapter on passives in the British National Corpus. Tedious, but fascinating to see how much we rely on them. Passives… ugh. Students  hate  them. Especially when I’m trying to explain why “The report was written by me” is technically correct, but sounds a bit… awkward? I'm a supervisor now, you know? At Primark. It's a bit of a change from my postgraduate studies. Wow, a supervisor! That’s a big step up from just retail assistant. Gemma, congratulations. How’s it going? Are you enjoying the extra responsibility? It’s... interesting. More paperwork than I anticipated. And dealing with staff issues. I had to have a slightly awkward conversation with someone yesterday about… well, let's just say adherence to company policy wasn’t their strong point. Not a drama, but it’s definitely not Chaucer. Speaking of which, I’ve started dipping my toe into some creative writing myself. Just short stories, nothing serious. Need a creative outlet after dealing with customer complaints all day. That’s brilliant! What kind of stories? Are they related to your linguistics background at all? I’ve been trying to work on my novel, but progress is slow. Referencing properly is a nightmare. I keep slipping into first person narration accidentally. Actually, yeah, quite a bit of linguistics sneaks in. I’m doing a story about a linguist trying to decode a lost Malaysian dialect. It's mostly an excuse to research cool linguistic theories, to be honest. Oh! I saw a photo of you on the department’s Instagram page. You were at that musical in Chichester, weren’t you?  Wicked ? I was! It was fantastic. Absolutely blew me away. Chichester Festival Theatre does it right. It’s a perfect day out - theatre, a bit of exploring, and decent coffee afterwards. You should come with me next time. I was thinking of seeing something else in a few weeks. I’d love to! That sounds wonderful. I've been so swamped with work and family stuff, I haven't had much time for theatre.

Right, so you’ve got the rice in, yeah? And the water needs to be… like, at least twice the amount of rice. Grandma always said, "drown the little blighters." Drown the little blighters, eh? Sounds intense. Honestly, I just usually buy ready-cooked. It’s easier with Leo. He tries to ‘help’ and ends up throwing sticky rice everywhere. It’s a battlefield. Easy’s boring, though! Once you know how, it’s dead simple. See, you gotta put the lid on tight, like this. Not too tight, but… snug. And then you crank up the heat, right until it’s boiling, then you turn it right down to a simmer. Can’t lift the lid while it’s simmering, or all the steam escapes and it goes all sticky, see? Right, simmer. Got it. So, what are we having with the rice, then? I saw you sorting through the freezer. I got some vouchers for that new Indian place, “Spice Paradise.” Thought we could use one. Nah, didn’t fancy Indian tonight. Got this chicken curry paste. Found it on offer. Thought we’d do a quick one. Proper easy. And I’ve got some frozen peas and sweetcorn. Gonna chuck those in. Need to remember the salt, though - last time it tasted like cardboard. Cardboard curry? Ouch. They really under-season things these days, don't they? Everything seems to be lower salt, lower fat… It’s just bland. Though, that jalapeno relish you got last week was amazing. Gave Leo a right kick! He loved it, didn’t he? Nearly cried. Good kick, proper spicy. Should’ve got more. You know, I saw this documentary about jellyfish the other day. Mad, innit? They’re basically just… pulsing blobs with stingers. And some of them have like, faces. Kind of. Deformed ones, obviously. Jellyfish with faces? Honestly, this world is getting weirder by the minute. Everything's got a weird twist. Even the food. You know, I was looking at that chicken in the fridge earlier and it just... didn't look right. Like it was about to go off. Oh yeah? Which bit? Don't tell me I've got dodgy chicken. I was planning on having it in the curry. Just... the colour. A bit greyish around the edges. You know how it is. And it smelled... not right. I think we should bin it, honestly.

Right, everyone dig in! I made a proper shepherd’s pie tonight, needed a bit of comfort food after that shift. Mrs. Henderson was having a right moody day. Sounds like a nightmare, Rach. Anything exciting happenin’ at uni then, El? You've been quiet all evening. Not really, Liam. Just the usual. History’s proving a bit of a slog, honestly. So much detail. I feel like I’m drowning in dates and names. And everyone’s obsessed with that new docu-series on Netflix, 'Royal Scandals'. It’s all they’re talking about. Tell me about it! I cleared my schedule tonight just to binge the first three episodes. It’s properly addictive. Honestly, the stuff they’ve dug up… scandalous. You should watch it, Liam. Nah, not really me thing. All that posh nonsense. Give me a good crime drama any day. Still nothing on then, is there? Job-wise, I mean. Liam, we've talked about this. You need to keep applying. Just because you didn’t get that apprenticeship at the shipyard doesn’t mean there aren’t other options. You've got a degree! Aye, a fancy piece of paper that's good for nothin’ round here. Everyone wants experience, Rach. How can I get experience if no one’s givin’ me a chance? Feels like I’m stuck in a rut, like I'm just… goin' nowhere. Don’t say that, Liam. You’re talented. Remember that amazing presentation you did on Victorian social reform? That was brilliant! Yeah, brilliant for a university lecture hall full of people who don’t care whether I’m alive or dead. It doesn’t pay the bills, does it? Mum’s gettin' worried, you know. Mum's always worried, Liam. That's just Mum. But she’s right to be concerned. Have you looked at… I don’t know, volunteering somewhere? It could look good on a CV. That's a good shout, Chloe. There's a charity shop down by the market always looking for helpers. Or you could offer your time at the community centre. They have all sorts of activities. Volunteering. Right. Just what I need. More… nothin’ that gets me closer to a paycheque. I'm feelin' proper down, to be honest. Don’t. Please don’t. You’re being dramatic. And besides, you cooked us all a lovely dinner last week. Those sausages were brilliant.

Speaker_1 : Honestly, a nightmare? You looked so chipper setting up this morning! All smiles and perfectly positioned name cards. Speaker_2 : Aye, well, projecting an image, isn't it? Gotta make it look smooth for the clients. Truth is, behind the scenes, it was chaos. The AV wouldn't cooperate, Ms. Hawthorne kept rearranging the seating plan every ten minutes, and the catering almost didn’t arrive. Nearly had a full-blown wobble, I did. Ms. Hawthorne?! Oh, bless. That woman is a force of nature. I remember when she tried to tell the florist  exactly  which shade of pink the roses needed to be. It was terrifying. Did you manage to get everything sorted in the end? Eventually. I had to charm the AV guy with promises of lukewarm tea, bribe the caterers with a box of biscuits, and practically wrestle Ms. Hawthorne into letting the seating plan stay put for five minutes. Worth it though, the feedback has been good. Head of marketing was chuffed, apparently. See? You’re a star, Eleanor! All that hard work pays off. Bet you deserve a massive glass of wine. Speaking of, is there any left in that bottle? There is. Another one? Don’t mind if I do. You know, this is lovely, Eleanor. Proper home cooking. Reminds me of… well, never mind. Reminds you of what? Come on, spill. Just… my mum’s Sunday roasts. She used to make the best gravy. Thick as you like. Nothing fancy, just proper, honest gravy. Right. Well, I'm trying to emulate her – proper gravy is key, isn't it? So, you need a lie-down after a conference like that, definitely. Do you ever get chance to… relax, properly? Not just recovering from work, but… doing something you enjoy? Not much, lately. I've been… wandering. You know, around Cambridge. It’s alright. Gets me out. Wandering? Sounds a bit lonely. You used to love football. Aye, well, the knees aren’t what they used to be. Can’t exactly be sprinting about anymore. Doctor says I need to do more exercise, but... it’s hard to get motivated. I know it is. But honestly, even a short walk every day makes a difference. Fresh air, a bit of sunshine… It’s good for the soul. I’ve started doing yoga, actually. Sounds daft, I know, a proper Yorkshire lass doing yoga, but it’s surprisingly good for your back.

Right, I’m off to my room. This clearing up is boring. Don't be so dramatic, Leo. It's a family effort. Just put your plate in the dishwasher, love. And please, could you clear the table? Dramatic much? Just like your Instagram posts, eh? All filters and angles. It’s art, Dad! And it's about creating a vibe. Besides, everyone does it. Yeah, definitely. My feed's looking pretty good this week. Got a load of likes on my new drone shots. Drone shots, eh, Ethan? Anything interesting in them? Anything…historical? Knowing your fascination. Just the old church in the village, Mum. It's just, like, really cool architecture. Speaking of historical… I was reading something interesting the other day. About Hitler’s moustache. Did you know it wasn't always that little toothbrush thing? Apparently, he initially had a much grander, more walrus-like affair. Dad! Seriously? We just finished dinner. Can we  not  talk about Hitler? Just a little historical fact, Leo. Adds a bit of colour to the man, doesn't it? It's amazing how much someone's appearance shaped their public image. It makes you think, doesn't it? It does, actually. Though I think that’s a rather…insensitive comparison. Let’s stick to slightly less weighty topics, shall we? How was tennis practice today, Leo? You seemed pretty down before dinner. It was okay. Mark's got a new girlfriend. She’s, like,  really  good at tennis. Better than me. Well, that's just motivating, isn’t it? Gives you something to work towards. Competition is good. Exactly! Healthy rivalry. I remember when I was younger, competing with my cousins in Korea. We'd play Go for hours, arguing over every single move. It sharpened your mind, you know? Go? What’s Go? It’s an ancient board game, Ethan. Really complex. Actually, Leo, when you've cleared the table, fancy giving it a go? I can teach you the basics. Uh… I don't know. I’m busy. Don't be like that. It might be a nice change of pace from Instagram. Besides, a bit of face-to-face interaction can't hurt, can it? Easier said than done, Mum. Now, Ethan, how's the photography project coming along? Have you managed to get those close-ups of the wildflowers? Yeah, mostly. The lighting was tricky this afternoon.

Honestly, Mum, I still can’t believe you’re getting  another  sofa. You just got rid of the last one! Aye, well, it were knackered, lass. Right saggy in the middle. And this one’s electric recliners! For yer Grandad, mind. He’s been grievin’ about his back somethin’ awful. It'll be grand for him. Don't you start fussin' about, Sarah. Your mother’s doin’ a good thing. My back ain't gettin' any younger, ya know. And modern comfort is a blessing. I know, Nan, I’m not  fussin’ , I’m just… financially baffled. Between the sofa, the new TV unit… are you sure you can afford all this? Don’t you worry yer pretty little ‘ead about it. Got a bit of savings, and Grandad’s offered to chip in. Besides, I've been doin' overtime. Remember I told you about that new placement at Meadowbrook? Bit hectic, but the extra pennies are worth it. Meadowbrook is always hectic. So, are you taking the scenic route again, Mum? We’ve been driving for ages. Aye, figured we'd go past the tip. Need to get rid of that old armchair from the spare bedroom. It's been standin' there for years, gatherin' dust. Fancy having a clear out yourself, Sarah? Maybe. I'm drowning in clothes anyway. Remember how Bethany’s mum offered to do a load of my washing last week? I felt awful, totally relying on her. Don't be daft, love. Family helpin’ each other is what we do. Remember all those Christmases at Auntie Maureen’s? Half the family endin’ up sleepin’ on her floor. Aye, and Uncle Barry and his dodgy presents. Remember that knitted owl he got you, Sarah? It looked like a mutant pigeon! Oh god, yes! I still have it somewhere, buried deep in a box. I can’t believe he thought that was a good gift. Speaking of presents, have you heard from Emily? How’s her partner doing? Still struggling? Poor lad. It’s gettin’ worse, isn’t it? The dementia’s takin’ its toll. Emily's a saint, she really is. Always puttin’ others first. She's been talkin' about getting him into a proper care home. It’s heartbreaking to hear. It just… reminds you what’s comin’, doesn't it? It does, dear. It truly does. My Elsie… well, you know. We don’t talk about it much now, but… it's a thief, that disease.

Honestly, love, I just don’t know what to do. It's all a bit mad, isn't it? Redundancy at my age! After thirty years at the school… thirty years! Mum, you told me about it on the phone, but hearing you say it like that… it's awful. Are you sure they can’t offer you anything else? Maybe a different role? They said they’ve restructured, you see. Apparently, with the new exam boards and online marking, they don't need an Examinations Manager anymore. Said my role’s being absorbed by someone else. Absorbed! Like I’m some bit of equipment they can just… chuck in a cupboard. That’s ridiculous. You’re brilliant at that job. Remember all those times you saved the day with a last-minute query about results? Absolutely indispensable. Don't let them make you feel like you're not. Easy for you to say, innit? You’re climbing the ladder, saving the world with your project coordination. I’m stuck. I’ve got bills to pay, you know. And Grandad needs his weekly visit. He gets so morose if I miss one. He’ll understand, Mum. He loves you regardless. And look, about the bills… have you looked at job agencies? There must be other secondary schools in Norfolk needing someone with your experience. Plus, you've got your pension savings, right? We can sit down and properly look at the finances when I come up next weekend. Next weekend? Oh, you coming for the Saturday? Lovely! I was thinking we could pop over to that new garden centre. They’ve got those amazing succulents at the moment – you know how much you like them. And afterwards, maybe we could try that new Thai place? I’ve heard good things. Sounds perfect! I'm free Saturday. Just gotta see if I can shift my weekend gym class. I'm determined to try that new HIIT one, it’s supposed to be killer. You still going to yoga? Still going, dear, though my knees aren't what they used to be. Honestly, bending over to pick up a dropped pen is a momentous occasion these days. Perhaps I need to cut back on the biscuits... Speaking of, are you still scoffing those ginger nuts every afternoon with a cuppa? You know you should switch to fruit. They’re comforting! And Grandad likes me to bring him one too.

This is a bit… mushy, Mum. And why’s it got, like, bits of carrot in it? It’s a vegetable medley, love. Good for you. And stop moaning, you’ll be complaining if there’s  not  carrots. Little Finnigan here seems to be enjoying it. Finn’s just banging things. He doesn’t actually  taste  anything. Anyway, summer hols are nearly here. We need to figure out what we’re doing. Boredom is a serious threat. I know, love. I’ve been thinking. We could try and make the most of the weather, yeah? Maybe a few trips to the swimming pool? Swimming’s alright, I guess. But it’s always packed. Last time, I spent more time dodging splashing than actually swimming. Remember you nearly lost me in the paddling pool last year? Don’t exaggerate, darling. You were only playing hide-and-seek! And this year will be different. We’ll go at quieter times. Perhaps mornings? Mornings are… early. And what about stuff to do? Like, proper stuff. Not just splashing around and getting carrot in my dinner. Well, Anya from next door said they’re having a barbeque next weekend. We could pop over. Finnigan will love seeing the dog, Buster, won't he? Anya’s barbeque? That’ll involve awkward small talk. And probably veggie burgers. You’re such a drama queen. There’ll be proper burgers too, I’m sure. Besides, it’s good to see people. You’ve been glued to that guitar all week. I am getting better, though! I can nearly play that riff from… what’s it called… the one with the robots? “Neon Genesis Evangelion”? The Japanese one? Yeah! That one. I downloaded a tutorial. It's really hard to understand though. That bloke's speaking so fast! Japanese is a tricky language. All those different tones. Have you been practicing your chords properly? Yeah, mostly. I think I need to learn a new one to do that part. Maybe I should look online again. I saw something about summer holiday job opportunities too, did you know? Jobs? You’re barely thirteen! What kind of job were you thinking of? I don’t know! Like, helping Mrs. Henderson with her garden, maybe. Or washing cars. Earn a bit of pocket money. That’s… actually a good idea. It’d teach you responsibility. And get you out of the house.

Nah, proper weird ending, innit? I reckon they could've wrapped it up a bit smarter. Like, what was the point of the ferret? The ferret was symbolic, Finn. Clearly. Representing… the inherent absurdity of… modern existence. Right, because a ferret’s gotta have a deeper meaning, does it? You and your postgrad brain. Honestly, sometimes I think you overthink everything. Remember that time you tried to analyse the symbolism of baked beans? They  are  intrinsically linked to British identity! And consider the textural contrast… the smoothness of the sauce, the firm snap of the beans… You're mental, you are. Speaking of contrasts, my dentist appointment’s tomorrow. Proper looking forward to that, I am. Not. Oh, that’s rough, isn’t it? Dr. Patel isn’t exactly known for his gentle touch, is he? He tries to make conversation, but it's just… awkward. Last time, he spent fifteen minutes detailing his prize-winning roses. Roses? Seriously? Mine just grunts. "Open wider." "That's your problem." Like I'm a garden or a faulty engine. Thinking about it, I need a proper holiday, don’t I. Somewhere with sunshine and no dentists. Definitely. Fancy a trip? We were talking about Greece the other week… Santorini, maybe? Though, knowing us, we’d probably end up getting lost in some tiny village and arguing about the authenticity of the gyros. Probably. Although, I did find a Citibike scheme in Athens. Could be right good for exploring. Less chance of ending up lost if we've got wheels. Did you ever manage to get your hands on one of those Citibikes here, by the way? Tried, mate. Absolute nightmare! The app crashes constantly, and half the docks are empty. It's a public service failing, I tell you. It's like they  want  you to walk everywhere. Tell me about it. Anyway, changing the subject – finished that new Faulkner you were raving about? "As I Lay Dying"? Yeah, finally. It’s… intense, isn’t it? The stream of consciousness is relentless. Took some getting used to, but the language is incredible. Proper poetry, in a way. Sounds a bit heavy for me. I’m more of a quick-read kind of fella. Got into this comic series, "Saga," actually. Brilliant artwork, proper bonkers story. You should check it out. Comics, eh? Not really my thing, usually. But I’m open to suggestions.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails! It's relentless. Every single parent wants to know  everything  about every single thing. And the safeguarding forms! Don't even get me started on the safeguarding forms, Mum. It’s a minefield. Sounds intense, love. But you always were brilliant at explaining things. Remember when you had to explain quadratic equations to me? You made it… almost fun. Oh, don’t remind me! Your face! You looked like you were contemplating abandoning your studies and becoming a sheep farmer. I probably was! But seriously, little ones are a handful, aren't they? Year One, I presume? That's why I'm so glad I finally got the job at St. Mary’s. It’s closer to home, a lovely school, and the headteacher seems genuinely supportive. Much better than my placement last summer. St. Mary’s is lovely, isn’t it? I remember Mrs. Henderson teaching me French there. Goodness, that feels like a lifetime ago. So, how are the children settling in? Any little terrors already? A few! Little Leo keeps trying to eat the crayons. And Emily practically lives in the sandpit. But mostly, they’re sweethearts. It's so rewarding, seeing them learn and grow. Though, I did have a small meltdown yesterday trying to get them all to sing "Twinkle Twinkle Little Star" in tune. It was utter chaos! Teaching patience, I imagine? It’s a skill, that one. Now, tell me, have you booked anything for your holiday yet? We were saying about maybe going to Cornwall… Not yet, Mum. I’ve been so busy with the job hunt and settling in, I haven’t had a chance. Cornwall sounds lovely, though. Somewhere with a beach would be amazing. Little Thomas would love paddling in the sea. Absolutely. We could look at somewhere near Newquay, maybe? They’ve got some beautiful little coves. And we could do some proper coastal walks. Fresh air and pasties - what more could you want? That sounds perfect. Although, Dad might moan about the lack of golf courses. Your father! He always finds his golf, doesn't he? Right. I'll start having a look online. And speaking of things to plan, did you hear from Auntie Carol about the Christening? Not yet. I messaged her last week, but no reply. I was hoping to sort out guest lists soon. It all feels a bit… overwhelming.

Honestly, the marking! It's relentless. I swear, they’re deliberately trying to wear us down. Year 11 GCSEs are just… a different beast these days than when I started teaching. The pressure on them, and therefore on us, is just immense. Tell me about it! I've got a particularly tricky class of Year 8s, bless their hearts. They’re brilliant, full of energy, but focusing them on French grammar is like herding cats. I tried a role-playing activity about ordering food in a restaurant - complete chaos! One boy started pretending to be a chef who only spoke Klingon. Oh, that’s brilliant! You have to find the humour, don't you? Otherwise, you’d just collapse. At least you're teaching a language, something creative. Mine's just History. Endless dates and battles. Though, I did introduce a short video clip from a documentary on the Vikings the other day, and they were actually engaged. For a whole ten minutes. A miracle, I tell you. Ten minutes? That  is  a miracle! I'm envious. I'm trying to get more interactive elements into my lessons, but it’s hard to find the time to prepare them all. You’d think with a postgrad, it would come naturally, wouldn’t you? Don't be silly. It's a constant learning curve. By the way, how's Barnaby doing? Still causing havoc in the garden? Oh, Barnaby! He's discovered roses. Apparently, they're excellent to dig under and then roll in. My prize-winning ‘Peace’ rose is currently covered in mud and dog hair. He's utterly shameless. But I couldn't stay mad at him for long, could I? He just looks at you with those big, brown eyes. I know exactly what you mean. My Millie, she’s getting old now, about 13 in human years, is the same. Gives you  that  look, and all is forgiven. Are you still using that new dog shampoo you were talking about last Christmas? The one with the shea butter? Yes! It’s wonderful! It actually  does  make his fur softer. I ended up buying it for my mum too, for Rupert. He's always complaining his hair is dry. It's ridiculous. He’s a dachshund, what’s he expecting? Men! My nephew, Jamie, is trying to convince me to invest in some sort of… beard oil subscription box.

…and then the chulent just  exploded  in the oven! Honestly, Mum nearly had a heart attack. It was all over the extractor fan, a sticky, sweet, lentil-y mess. Could you imagine? Passover and a chulent catastrophe! Blimey, Chloe! You're having a laugh, innit? That's mental. Least it weren’t the matzah balls. Those are sacred. Indeed, Daniel. Matzah balls represent dedication to the tradition. Though, I confess, my grandmother’s were always a bit… dense. Like little dumplings of disappointment. My nan's were a bit too fluffy, personally. Vanished in your mouth before you even tasted them. Anyway, Chloe, sounds like you've got your work cut out for you this year then. All that cleaning... Tell me about it, Tom. But Mum insisted on making two. "Just in case,” she said. Of course, both ended up volcanic. At least the charoset looks decent. I used Pomegranate molasses this year, thought I'd try something a little different. Pomegranate molasses? Fancy! My Nan always just used apples and walnuts. Proper old-school. I’m starving though, Chloe, seriously. When are we getting to the gefilte fish? Daniel, be patient. We’re savoring the atmosphere. It’s lovely to have everyone together. This Seder feels particularly… connected, somehow. After everything. Mum’s right. It does. Remember last year, when Aunt Miriam kept insisting she’d taught Elijah how to say ‘L’Shana Haba’ah’ in Hebrew, and he just kept saying, “Banana Haba’ah”? Oh, God, yes! He was convinced it was a joke! I spent the whole evening correcting him. Though, to be fair, it  is  a bit tricky for a five-year-old. He’s a spirited one, that Elijah. Reminds me of your grandfather, actually. Always had a twinkle in his eye, and a mischievous sense of humour. He'd have loved this charoset. He adored anything with pomegranate. Speaking of food... anyone else dreaming of Italy right now? I saw this amazing documentary about Bologna, all those cured meats and freshly made pasta… makes a bloke miss his Nonna's cooking, you know. Bologna! Oh, stop it, you’re making me hungry. We were meant to go last spring, you remember? Then… well, you know. Do you think we’ll ever make it? Definitely. France first, though, I reckon. I've been meaning to take Sarah to Paris for ages. Just wander the streets, eat pastries, maybe catch a film at La Cinémathèque Française.

Honestly, I thought "The Crown" was going downhill this season. All that palace intrigue felt a bit… forced, didn’t it? Like they were desperately trying to manufacture drama. I agree, actually. The earlier seasons had such a grounded, observational quality. This one felt almost theatrical. Though, I did enjoy the portrayal of Thatcher. Imelda Staunton was brilliant. I loved it! I know some people moaned, but I thought it was gripping. I’m a sucker for historical drama, you know? Though, I do wish they'd shown more of Diana's friendships. She couldn’t have  just  been Prince Charles' problem, could she? No, dear, of course not. But they have a narrative to maintain, don't they? Speaking of gripping, has anyone been following "Happy Valley"? Sarah Lancashire is phenomenal. Oh, "Happy Valley"! Absolutely. Catherine Cawood is such a complex character. The writing is just superb, so bleak, so real. It’s a masterclass in slow-burn tension. I was practically chewing my fingernails during the latest episode. I’ve started it, but I’m only a few episodes in. It's a bit… intense, isn't it? I need something a little lighter sometimes, especially after a long week crunching numbers. Well, you know me, I’m always knitting. It's my therapy. I'm working on a chunky blanket at the moment – a sort of wonky chevron pattern. It’s taking forever. Sarah’s helping, bless her, she’s a dab hand at crochet. Sarah? Your niece? Good for her! I've been trying to get back into crocheting myself. I started a scarf a few months ago, a lovely moss stitch, but I got distracted by a new book. Speaking of which… I'm reading “Lessons in Chemistry” at the moment. Have you heard of it? Vaguely… it’s the one about the female chemist, isn’t it? It's been everywhere online. I'm trying to reduce my screen time, though. I've switched almost entirely to eBooks now. It's so much easier to carry around, you know? eBooks? Oh, I just can't do it. The  smell  of a book, the feel of the pages… it's part of the experience! I can't imagine curling up with a cup of tea and an eBook. It’s just not the same. I'm with you on that, Jane. There’s something so… tactile about a physical book.

Honestly, this is… quaint. Like something out of a museum. You’re telling me we’re using  this  while we’re in Finland? A country practically built on technology? Aye, lass. Quaint’s the word. But reliable. And, importantly, it works. Remember why we chose these, eh? No fancy apps, no data spying, no endless notifications. Just phones. For talking. I remember. You were waxing poetic about privacy and escaping the digital vortex. But still! Look at it! It's… beige. And tiny. How am I supposed to text anyone? I’m used to thumbs that stretch across a six-inch screen! You'll adapt. Remember that old mobile phone you had when you were a teenager? The one that only did calls and texts? This is a step back, but a deliberately chosen one. Right, let’s get these settings sorted. Have you managed to find the contact list yet, Liv? It's not intuitive, Professor Lehmann. Not at all. This thing is operating on a different logic entirely. “Menu,” “Options,” “Tools”… it’s like navigating a labyrinth. I need to add Mum and Dad's numbers at least. They’ll be worried sick if they can't reach me. Right. See this little icon? The one that looks like a contact book? Tap that. Then, scroll down to “New Contact.” Now, breathe, Liv. It's simple, once you get the hang of it. Remember, these phones don’t do autocorrect. Spell everything carefully. Right, right. Mum… M-U-M... Oh, for goodness sake, it's already added her as “MU.” Honestly! This is a pain. And there's no photo option? Are you serious? Nope. No photos. Part of the charm, I’d say. Keeps it uncluttered. See, I’ve got the emergency services programmed in. That’s crucial. In case you get properly lost in the wilderness. Finland's a beautiful country, but it's easy to wander. Thanks, Dad. That’s exactly what I needed to hear. I’m not planning on wrestling a bear. I just want to check Instagram occasionally. Which, obviously, isn’t happening. Instagram. That's the point. This is a digital detox. Remember the plan? We’re here to immerse ourselves in Finnish culture, not to be glued to our phones. Now, Dad's number... let's get that in. And I’ve pre-loaded the address of the cabin. Just tap “messages” and then “new message” if you need to send it.

But Dad, a Red Panda is way better than a cat! They're like, fluffy and climb trees and eat bamboo! Cats just… sleep. And occasionally cough up hairballs. Now, Leo, be nice to Mr. Whiskers. He’s a perfectly lovely cat. And remember, you had a goldfish once, and you forgot to feed it. That was  one  time! And it was a really stressful week with exams! Besides, Red Pandas are endangered! We could, like, adopt one! Adopt a Red Panda, love? Where would we keep it? In the garden? Imagine Mrs. O’Malley’s face if we had a Red Panda swinging from her bird feeder! Woof woof! See! Even Finn likes dogs better! Malamooches, specifically! Big, fluffy Malamooches! They're like, giant, furry clouds. I saw one on YouTube, it was wearing a tiny hat. So cute! Finn’s obsessed with dogs at the moment. He’s always trying to make Mr. Whiskers bark. He doesn't seem to get that cats don’t bark. Well, he's two! He's learning. Anyway, about the party… are we still having it at the community hall? I sent Liam a message, and he said he was definitely free. Yes, the community hall is booked. I spoke to Mrs. Doyle, and she said she’d be able to help with the decorations. We need to think about a cake, though. What kind does Liam want? Chocolate, definitely chocolate. With extra sprinkles. And maybe one of those edible images? The one of a spaceship? We’ll see. It's all a bit much, isn't it? A spaceship cake… Right, after the party, we need to start looking at holidays. I was thinking maybe Ireland again, maybe County Clare this time? I liked County Cork! But Clare sounds good too. We could go to the beach. And… do you think we can bring my laptop? I want to edit some videos I took. We’ll see. It’s your cousin Sarah's birthday trip as well to think about. And we really should try to fit in some time to watch those Japanese films you like. You’ve been talking about them for ages. Yeah! Kurosawa! The Seven Samurai is brilliant! Do you think Finn would like it? Probably not. He's more interested in pulling my hair at the moment. He’s just discovered he has hands, you know. He's a menace sometimes.

…and then Auntie Maureen tried to deep-fry a turkey! Honestly, the smoke alarms were going off for a good half hour. It was a right state! Never been a Christmas like it, that's for sure. Deep-fried turkey? That’s… ambitious, even for Maureen. My Lola used to make this incredible leche flan for Christmas. Creamy, jiggly, just perfect with a bit of cinnamon. Did you ever have anything like that at your Christmases, Chloe? Leche flan? Sounds lovely, really. We mostly had roast beef, Yorkshire puddings, and sprouts. Loads of sprouts. My dad's obsessed. We'd dress the tree, Mum would be stressing about the timings of everything, and me and my brother would be nicking the Quality Street. It was always a bit chaotic, but in a good way, y’know? Oh, Christmas! My dear, those were truly special days. We always had a goose, a beautiful, plump goose, stuffed with apples and sage and onion. My husband, Arthur, would carve it, and my mother would oversee the gravy – she was very particular about the gravy! We'd have flaming pudding, of course, set alight with brandy. Such theatricality! It’s all so subdued now. Flaming pudding! Reminds me of the time I tried to recreate it for the grandkids and nearly set the curtains on fire. Young Emily just stared at me, absolutely horrified. We switched to chocolate Yule logs after that. Much safer. Though, I did once spend Christmas in the Bahamas, back in '72. Now  that  was a Christmas! Sun, sand, cocktails... no goose in sight. The Bahamas at Christmas? Seriously? That sounds amazing! Barrow-In-Furness is a bit…grey in December. Snow’s lovely, but mostly it’s just cold and damp. Imagine! Tropical Christmas versus Yorkshire puddings. It’s quite a contrast. My family always brought a bit of the Philippines to London. We’d have Noche Buena - a huge feast! Hamon , pancit , rice cakes… everything’s sweet and savory at the same time. It’s a bit much for some people, but I love it. It connected us to home. Connecting to home...that's what Christmas is all about, isn’t it? Arthur’s family were very traditional. Carols around the piano, readings from Dickens… all very proper. My own family were a bit more bohemian. My mother was an artist, you see, and we’d often have travelling musicians staying with us during the holidays.

Honestly, that shepherd’s pie was divine, Anne. Absolutely divine. You really outdid yourself. Oh, thank you, David. It’s a classic, isn’t it? Thought we needed something comforting after all that rain we've been having. Glad you enjoyed it. Comforting is the word! It’s exactly what I needed. This is wonderful, Anne. Honestly, I used to make a dreadful shepherd’s pie. Ends up gluey and grey. You've got the secret touch. It’s all in the mash, really. A generous knob of butter, a little cream, and not overworking it. Simple tricks, really. Speaking of tricks, did you see last night's "Detective Davies"? Absolutely brilliant deduction in that last scene. I was completely thrown off. Oh, I adored it! That twist with the antique clock… masterful. Davies is just getting better and better. Though, I must admit, I find the lead actress a bit… wooden. I don't mind her. She’s understated. It allows Davies to really shine. I’ve been transcribing a writer’s memoir this week, and the level of detail some people put into describing facial expressions is astounding. You’d think a flicker of an eyebrow could solve world peace. You and your transcription work! Always finding some fascinating detail. Is it a particularly juicy memoir? It's alright. Nothing scandalous, thankfully. It's a biography of a garden designer. Plenty of descriptive prose about roses and herbaceous borders but not much drama. Keeps me busy. Are you swamped at the office, David? Overflowing, as usual. They’re reorganizing again - apparently, “synergy” needs to be achieved. Which usually translates to “more work for the same people.” I swear, management speak is its own language. Oh, the corporate world. I’m glad I escaped that particular rat race. Though, chasing deadlines for a book can be just as stressful in its own way. I’m still wrestling with the middle section of my novel. The plot’s stubbornly refusing to cooperate. You'll crack it, Eleanor. You always do. Remember that ridiculous historical romance you wrote? Even  that  ended up being surprisingly good. Please don't remind me! That was a dark period. Desperate times called for desperate measures – needed the money after my divorce, you know. Speaking of desperate times, how’s your Kindle doing, Anne? Have you loaded it with anything good for your commute next week? It's doing splendidly!

Honestly, Arthur, you're being daft. Absolutely daft. You can't just  ignore  the letter. It’s from the council! Council letters. Always bad news, them. Always wantin' somethin'. Probably wantin' more taxes, they do. More taxes on nothin'! Arthur, let’s just have a look at it, shall we? It’s on the table. Eleanor, could you fetch me my reading glasses? I appear to have misplaced them again. Already on it, darling. Here you are. Honestly, you'd lose your head if it wasn't attached. Right. Let’s see… "Regarding proposed changes to local green spaces…" Hmm. It seems they're suggesting re-zoning the field behind your cottage, Arthur. Re-zonin'! What for? Another one of them 'luxury developments', I reckon. Posh flats for foreigners, no doubt. Ruinin' the countryside. Don’t jump to conclusions, Arthur. It could be anything. A community garden, perhaps? A little park for the children? Though, heaven knows, there aren’t many children around Costessey anymore. It does mention the possibility of a "mixed-use development" and "improved community facilities." Sounds like housing, Arthur, but potentially with some added amenities. And it asks for residents' feedback. Feedback! What good is feedback? They never listen to us, do they? Remember that time they wanted to put that concrete monstrosity of a roundabout on the High Street? We all complained, we did! And what happened? They built it anyway! That was years ago, Arthur. And you were rather strident about your position. Perhaps a more… diplomatic approach would be better this time. Eleanor's right. Ignoring it is the worst thing you can do. They’ll just assume you’re content. The letter suggests a meeting next Tuesday at the village hall. Tuesday? Tuesday's my Bingo night! I can't miss Bingo! Doreen's been saving me a lucky seat. Arthur! Seriously? You're prioritising Bingo over potentially losing the field you look out on every day? Well, Doreen spends ages gettin’ me a nice cuppa and a digestive biscuit. Proper good, them biscuits. And I’m gettin’ quite good at Bingo, you know. Got a full house last week! Alright, alright. Let’s not argue about Bingo, Arthur. We'll work something out. Perhaps I could go on your behalf? I'm rather good at speaking my mind, and I know you're worried about the character of the area. You? Go to a council meetin'?

Right, so, final decisions on the Leaving Do for Horace? He’s officially retiring next week – feels a bit mad, doesn't it? Been here since dinosaurs roamed, practically. Almost. I’ve confirmed The Eagle, upstairs room. They've got that great view of King’s College Chapel. Initial headcount’s hovering around forty, give or take a few late additions. Should we stick with buffet or explore something a little fancier? Buffet’s fine, innit? Keep it simple. Horace always said he hated a faff. Less time faffing about, more time for a pint, wouldn’t you say? I’ve already put feelers out for some decent local beer. Worthington's if we can get it. Worthington's is ambitious, Sarah. But I'll check. I’ve been looking at the decorations – should we go traditional Cambridge blue or something a bit more… celebratory? We could do a 'Horace through the years' photo slideshow, too. "Celebratory" sounds excellent, Amelia. And absolutely, a slideshow is essential! We need to embarrass him a little bit, you know, celebratory embarrassment. I've got a few photos from the ELT conferences over the years – some truly glorious fashion choices. Oh, that's brilliant, Eleanor! I'll dig through the archives too. Right, food then. Buffet seems the sensible option. Any dietary requirements floating around? I think Janet in accounts is still gluten-free. And Mark from Sales is firmly vegan, as always. Keep them happy, eh? Though, secretly, I bet he sneaks a sausage roll. Right, noted. I’ll make sure to flag it to the caterers. Speaking of flagging things, has anyone seen that poor bumblebee trapped in the window of the stationery cupboard? It's been buzzing frantically for ages! Oh dear! I just walked past. It's quite distressed. Perhaps we should do something? Absolutely. I’ll grab a piece of stiff card and try to gently guide it out. It’s awful seeing them like that. Reminds me of that time I was working at Aylesbury Wildlife Centre… we had a swallow trapped in the main hall. The relief on its face when it got out… That's a lovely story, Sophie. But let's focus on the bee for now. It looks like it needs rescuing immediately. We wouldn’t want a little ecosystem collapse on our hands because of a stationery cupboard! Eleanor’s right. Let’s get the bee sorted.

Honestly, I am  so  over history. Like, seriously. Romans? Egyptians? What good is knowing about pharaohs when I’m trying to figure out my algebra homework? You say that now, but remember last week when Mrs. Davies was going on about Hadrian's Wall and you were, like, actually interested? You were asking about the logistics of building it and everything. That was  before  she announced the essay. Five pages on the social impact of Roman bathhouses! Five pages! Who even cares about Roman bathhouses? People washed in them, obviously. End of story. Okay, dramatic much? It’s probably not as bad as you think. You're good at essays, remember? You always write really vivid descriptions. Vivid descriptions of lukewarm water and mosaics? No thanks. I’d rather be learning… I don’t know… astrophysics. Literally anything else. What about you? Is double science still driving you up the wall? Oh, you have  no  idea. Mr. Peterson is being extra… Mr. Peterson. He keeps deducting marks for ‘lack of enthusiasm’ now. Like, how enthusiastic can you be about titration when you’re trying not to spill acid all over yourself? Ugh, I remember that lab. Nearly lost an eyebrow because of a rogue splash. He’s a nightmare, that man. Did he actually give Emily a detention for asking a sensible question yesterday? He did! Can you believe it? Emily asked if the indicator solution actually  worked  on all acids and he went ballistic. Said it was ‘disruptive to the learning environment.’ Honestly, I think he just doesn't like being questioned. Textbook power trip. You’d think a science teacher would embrace inquiry. Anyway, at least you’re learning something useful. I'm learning how to write convincing arguments about the average temperature of Roman bathwater. Okay, that does sound terrible. Have you started it yet? Absolutely not. I’ve been avoiding it like the plague. I was hoping to procrastinate until the last minute and then pull an all-nighter fuelled by chocolate and pure desperation. You know, the classic student method. Honestly, that's your usual M.O. It's surprisingly effective though, isn't it? Just don’t pull it too much; your mum gets a bit worried when you’re up until three in the morning. Tell me about it. She left me a note on my bed this morning saying "Please prioritise sleep." With a little smiley face.

Honestly, this risotto is… well, it’s something. Not exactly what I was expecting after all that talk about ‘authentic Italian’. I thought it was alright, Mum. It's not Nonna’s, obviously, but it’s a Tuesday night dinner, not a Michelin star review. And I did follow the recipe pretty closely. It’s fine, love. It's got flavour. Besides, the bread is lovely. You made that, didn’t you? Garlic and rosemary are always a winner. Bread doesn’t compensate for bland risotto, Daniel. It’s just… lacking something. Maybe Parmesan? I’m probably just hungry. This restaurant needs a decent gravy boat. You lot wouldn't understand, working in your offices. Oh, here we go. 'Working in offices'. It's just as tiring as your sales job, Mum. My admin work at the university isn't exactly a walk in the park. Especially with the modular grading system this year. Absolute chaos. Oh, paperwork. Different kettle of fish entirely. You’re pushing buttons, love. I'm dealing with actual people and their actual needs. And trying to meet quotas. Honestly, Brenda from accounts nearly gave me a heart attack today. Complaining about the new coffee machine! Brenda? Seriously? She's always complaining about  something . Remember that time she moaned about the stapler? Don't remind me! It never ends. Anyway, speaking of chaos, how’s your project going, Daniel? Still wrestling with the new logistics software? Pretty much. It's a nightmare. The training was useless. I spent half the morning just trying to print a report. And the head of logistics keeps changing his mind about the entire workflow. It's constantly shifting. I swear, I'm going to need a holiday just to recover. You deserve one. Have you booked anything yet? You've been saying you need a break for months. I've been looking. Nothing concrete yet. Somewhere warm, preferably with a beach. Somewhere I can just... switch off. Maybe Spain? Spain’s lovely. We went to Benidorm once. Awful, though. Far too many stag dos. You need somewhere quieter. Maybe the Algarve? Your sister went there last year and said it was beautiful. The Algarve is nice. Or how about Greece? Santorini is stunning, but maybe a bit pricey. I’ll look into it. Need to get the budget approved first, mind. Head of logistics is being particularly tight-fisted this quarter.

Honestly, Chloe, I'm knackered. Mrs. Henderson's place was a disaster. Her grandson apparently had a party while she was away. Cake everywhere! Sticky floors… you wouldn't believe it. Oh dear, that sounds awful! I’m glad I don’t have to deal with that. Though my flat can feel like a teenage battlefield sometimes. How are Liam and Maisie doing? Still causing chaos? Liam’s alright, mostly. It’s Maisie… Honestly. She got detention this week. Again. Apparently, she was laughing during a history lesson about the Battle of Hastings! Can you imagine? Laughing! The Battle of Hastings? That's a bit insensitive, even for a teenager. What did they say to her? Well, Mrs. Davies – you know, the new history teacher – she’s very strict apparently. Sent her straight to detention. Maisie’s been moaning about it non-stop, saying she had plans to go to Sophie’s. Oh, that’s rough. Sophie’s parties are legendary, aren’t they? She’s got a good head on her shoulders, that Sophie. Still, detention is detention. Did you speak to Mrs. Davies? Sometimes a bit of communication can smooth things over. I did, briefly. She wouldn’t budge. Said it was disrupting the class. I tried explaining Maisie gets… distracted. You know? It's hard to know sometimes. It's just... everything's feeling a bit much lately. I can imagine. Listen, before we spiral into teenage angst, how are  you  doing? I was so worried after your last appointment. Has there been any… news? They're running more tests, Chloe. Another scan next week. The oncologist says it's stable for now, which is good, obviously. But… you know. This waiting is the worst part. It feels like I'm living on borrowed time. Don't say that. You're not. You're being incredibly strong. And you have so much to live for – Liam, Maisie, all your friends... And honestly, you’re a rock. You always have been. Have you been going to those yoga classes? I’ve tried. It’s hard to find the energy some days. But I'm trying to make myself. They say it helps with the… the  stuff , you know? The side effects. Absolutely. Little things. Every little thing helps. I was thinking, maybe I could come with you sometime? Give you a bit of company? That would be lovely, actually.

Right, so, another three essays due by Friday. Joy. Honestly, I'm starting to think I should’ve just stuck with cleaning toilets back home. At least that was predictable. Don't be daft, Chloe! You've got a first-class degree, almost. You can't be thinking about toilets! Besides, bartending wasn’t exactly a picnic, was it? Late nights, dodgy customers... Aye, but it was  my  dodgy customers. And I knew roughly when I’d be home. This uni lark’s all over the place. You’re alright, though, Liv? How's the criminology course going? Still dreaming of arresting villains? It's good, yeah. Really interesting actually. We had a guest lecturer last week, a former detective. Proper fascinating. Though, honestly, finding a proper job afterwards is the bit that worries me. Everyone says the market's saturated. What about you, after the masters? Still thinking about Hull? Hull's always home, innit? Always. But I'm not sure about going back to bartending full-time. It’s alright for a bit of money, you know, to tide me over, but... I was thinking about maybe doing some freelance copywriting. I’ve been doing bits and bobs for mates, building a little portfolio. Copywriting? That sounds… posh. Seriously, that's brilliant! You’ve always been good with words. Remember that ridiculous poem you wrote for Mrs. Higgins' birthday in Year 8? Don’t remind me! That was mortifying. Still, it got me a box of chocolates, so can't complain. Right, but getting actual  paid  to write… is that even a thing? It feels a bit fanciful, like something posh Southerners do. It absolutely is a thing! Loads of businesses need content for their websites and social media. You could do it online, from anywhere. Imagine, you could work from a cafe in Barcelona! Now you’re just teasing! Barcelona's a bit far fetched, even for a daydream. I'd probably end up working from my mam's kitchen, eating Eccles cakes and stressing about deadlines. Hey, there’s nothing wrong with Eccles cakes! And stressing about deadlines is just part of the writing process. Seriously though, you've got the skills. You’re witty, you're observant… you can spin a yarn like nobody's business. Thanks, Liv. Means a lot. It's just… back home, everyone expects you to do what your parents did. My dad was a roofer, my grandad was a roofer...

…and then the parrot just started reciting the shipping forecast! Honestly, Brenda, you should have seen it. The look on Mrs. Higgins’ face was priceless. She thought she was losing it. Oh, that’s brilliant, David! A parrot and the shipping forecast? You’re making me cry! My nephew, Liam, tried to teach his budgie to say "Yorkshire pudding." All it learned was "budgie." Utterly useless for a Sunday roast, that one. Shipping forecast parrots. You've got a good one there, David. Reminds me of my uncle. He tried to teach a pigeon to deliver messages. Ended up just chasing squirrels. More entertaining than efficient, though. Ach, pigeons and parrots. You're coddin' yourselves. Me holidays, they were always about the sea. County Donegal, that's where I grew up. The air, the smell of the salt...it clings to yer soul, ya know? Not like this dry, grey Salford. Agreed, Moira. There's something about the sea air. Where are you planning on going this year, Moira? Still Donegal? I was considerin' it, aye. But me daughter, she’s been on at me to see Dublin. Proper theatre, good museums, a bit of a city buzz. Haven't been back in years, not since I left for England. It'll be good to see the family, of course. It's just a bit… overwhelming, big city life. I know what you mean. I went to London last year to see my sister. Lost myself three times within a five-mile radius. Absolutely overwhelming. I’m sticking firmly to Scarborough this year. Nice, quiet beach, fish and chips, a bit of bracing wind. Can’t beat it. Scarborough, eh? Nice choice. I’m leaning towards the Lake District. Need to escape the city, you know? Get some fresh air, walk a bit. Maybe even try some climbing. Though I'm not sure my lung capacity is up to a proper ascent of Scafell Pike. Climbing? You? You’ll be needing a Sherpa, lad! Though, I applaud the ambition! I’m heading to Greece this year. My wife, Eleanor, is obsessed with ancient history. So it’s Athens, Delphi, the lot. I’ll likely spend most of the time in a taverna, sampling the local wine. Research, you see. Essential research for a husband. Essential research, you say? Sounds suspiciously like a holiday to me. Greece is lovely, though. Just be careful of the stray cats.

Honestly, did you SEE that tackle, Liam? Absolutely rank! Should’ve been a red, no question. Hmm? What tackle? I was just trying to finish up this paragraph on the impact of… never mind. Which one are you on about now, Maisie? They’re all questionable, aren't they? Ref’s having a right mare today. The one on Barnes! Five minutes ago! Straight through the back of him! The lad was practically airborne! They’re letting ‘em get away with murder, aren’t they? It’s the Newcastle way, innit? Always getting done over. Always getting done over, eh? Classic Geordie perspective. It's a competitive sport, Maisie. There’s a lot of physicality. He probably just mistimed it. Mistimed it? He  launched  himself at him! You’re just saying that because you're from Brum and you probably support Villa. Always biased, you are. Guilty as charged. But I'm trying to be objective. It was a clumsy tackle, not malicious. Besides, Villa aren’t even playing today, so my loyalties are purely focused on witnessing this… spectacle. Spectacle? It's a disgrace! Right, I'm starving. Fancy some kebabs after this? There’s that good place down the road, the one that does the cheesy chips extra good. Kebab sounds brilliant. I’m fuelled entirely by caffeine and revised economic models at the moment, proper food is desperately needed. Their falafel is surprisingly good, you know. Don’t just go for the doner. Falafel? You and your healthy eating. You're trying to turn me into some kind of quinoa-loving vegan, aren't you? I’m a girl from Sunderland, Liam! I run on chips and gravy and meaty goodness. I'm just saying, broaden your horizons! It's good for the soul. Though, I admit, cheesy chips are hard to resist. Especially when you’re watching a game that's this… eventful. They're really playing hard today, aren’t they? They are. And they're still down a goal! This is a nightmare. You wouldn’t believe the stress I go through watching these matches. My poor mam worries sick every time. She’s convinced I’ll have a heart attack before I’m thirty. You're a tough cookie, Maisie. You’ll be fine. Just breathe. It's only a game, honestly. Though, I understand the passion. It's the same with economics, in a way.

Right then, that’s a bit strong, Grandma. You didn’t add enough milk again, did ya? Never you mind, lad. Strong tea keeps you awake. You need to be sharp, you’ve got all them projects swirling about in your head. Manchester’s always been a busy place, innit? Not like it used to be, though. All these fancy flats goin’ up… Mum, don’t start reminiscing about the old days again. He’s got a meeting this afternoon, remember? Liam, honestly, you barely touched your biscuit. It’s Brenda’s famous ginger snaps, you know she only makes them for special occasions. Sorry, Mum. Just a bit distracted, I suppose. That Henderson project is being a right pain. They keep changing the scope. It’s like trying to build a house with moving foundations. Moving foundations? What’s that then? Sounds like somethin’ out of a war film. Oh, I used to love those war films! "The Dam Busters" – now  that  was a film. Richard Attenborough, proper acting. Remember seeing it at the Odeon in Withington, practically every week. Mum, you've told us the "Dam Busters" story a thousand times! Liam's talking about work. Mum’s right, it  is  a good film, though. I watched it with my mate, Dave, last week. Got a new projector, proper cinema experience in his garden. Speaking of which, he’s got this electric bike now, a proper fancy one. Goes like the wind, he says. I’m thinking of getting one myself. Good for getting around the city, avoids all that awful traffic. Electric bike? What’s wrong with a proper bike? I used to cycle everywhere when I was a lass. Up to Chorlton, to the market. Used to be a blooming market there! Now they've got all these… these… organic stalls… full of kale. Who needs kale? Give me a good turnip any day. Mum, that's because you were a teenager when the market changed. It's not all kale, there's still decent fruit and veg. Liam, are you seriously considering an electric bike? It feels a bit…uncharacteristic. You're usually all about the performance cars. I know, I know. But the congestion charge is getting ridiculous, isn't it? And the parking…don’t even get me started. Plus, it's better for the environment, right? Trying to be a bit more responsible. Responsible!

Honestly, Leo, you’ve barely touched yours! It's Pancake Day! What's wrong? Are they not sweet enough? I put extra syrup on. Too… fluffy! I like 'em! Good!  munching sounds  See, Leo? Barnaby's enjoying his. It's just a pancake. Don’t be fussy. You were so excited about making them this morning. Remember all the whisking? I wanted chocolate chips! You forgot the chocolate chips! I didn’t forget! We ran out! We'll get some for next week. Right now, eat your pancake. We need energy for the school assembly this afternoon. Mrs. Davies is doing a really interesting talk about ecosystems. Will there be animals? Probably pictures of animals, Barnaby. And maybe videos. We talked about ecosystems in class, remember? Like how plants and animals all depend on each other. Miss Lewis said we’re learning about the Romans next! That’s better. The Romans are good too, darling. But understanding how nature works is important too. Speaking of important, I'm worried about a few children in my class. It’s heartbreaking, really. Some of them… they come to school clearly not having had breakfast, and their packed lunches are practically empty. It makes you think, doesn't it? Does that mean they don’t get pancakes? Well, some of them might not. It’s a stark reminder that not everyone has the same… well, everything. It’s hard to concentrate on long division when your tummy is rumbling, isn't it? Sometimes they even look at your children’s lunches with… I don't know… a sort of longing. It’s awful. I'm sharing my berries with Barnaby. That’s lovely, darling. Sharing is wonderful. That’s why it’s important to be kind. Right, so, after the assembly, how about we pop into town and get that Science Museum trip booked? I saw they have a special exhibit on space exploration. You two would love that. Flying through space, seeing planets… Can we see aliens? Perhaps! It’s possible! We’ll have to look very carefully. And afterward, we can pop into a bookshop and look for a new Green Knowe story. You both adore those. The one with the talking cat! That’s the one. Though, before any of that, little teeth need brushing! And hands need washing, especially after all this yummy pancake syrup. Can we go to the beach after that?

Honestly, this isn’t as good as last time. They’ve really cut back on the peanuts, haven’t they? Nah, it's fine. Perfectly acceptable takeaway. Don’t be so picky, Chloe. Besides, we’ve got bigger things to worry about than slightly fewer peanuts. Did you see that article about the rising cost of…everything? You and the news, Liam. Always doom and gloom. I'm enjoying the sweet and sour. You know, it’s really strange thinking about Aunt Susan’s funeral. It feels like it’s still so recent, but apparently it’s been nearly three weeks. It has. I’m still trying to process it, to be honest. She was so… vibrant. Can you imagine her in all that somber black? She’d have hated it. Absolutely. She would have wanted a rave, not a wake. Remember that time she tried to teach Grandpa how to do the Macarena at Christmas? Oh god, yes! He looked positively mortified. Speaking of mortified, did you guys hear about Sarah and Mark? Apparently, she found out he’d been texting his ex again. No way! Seriously? That’s awful. Poor Sarah. I hope she kicks him out. They’ve been together for ages! That's rough. It wouldn't surprise me, though. He always seemed a bit flaky. Has anyone seen the housemates lately? I haven't seen Alex in ages. Alex is working overtime. Apparently, his boss needs him to finish some emergency paperwork, something to do with a new agricultural subsidy. It’s dull stuff, if he describes it, which he never does. Speaking of agricultural stuff, I've been wrestling with this blight issue on the experimental wheat crop. It's a nightmare. You wouldn't believe the complexities involved. Sounds thrilling, Tom. Pass the fortune cookies, please. I need some wisdom. "A storm is coming. Seek shelter." Creepy! Probably just means the weather forecast for tomorrow is awful. Actually, did anyone catch that new Bob the Builder film? My niece kept nagging me to take her. Bob the Builder? Seriously, Liam? You're not seriously suggesting you saw a film about a cartoon builder? I didn’t  see  it, I endured it. For the niece, obviously. It was… surprisingly intense. Clearly, there's a deep existential crisis underpinning Bob’s construction activities. You're pulling my leg, right? Swear on my life. Anyway, what about the England cricket?

Oh, my goodness! Mrs. Higgins was always a character. My mum used to say she lived in a world of her own making. Did Mr. Bailey ever play along? He did, he did. Baited her right along. Old Bailey, a sly one he was. He'd nod and say, "Indeed, Martha, are they particularly stylish hats this year?" Kept her entertained for hours. You youngsters wouldn’t understand the patience needed in those days. We relied on a bit of gentle amusement. It’s lovely hearing these stories, Grandpa. Makes you realise how much the village has changed. Remember when we were little and Mrs. Peterson used to leave out plates of biscuits for everyone after school? Absolutely! Chocolate digestives, always. A lifeline. My mum used to say Mrs. Peterson practically raised half the village. She was a saint. Saints are rare these days. Everything’s so… rushed. Nobody takes the time to sit and chat over a cup of tea. Though, you’ve all brought some lovely cakes, haven't you? Are those Rice Krispy Cakes, Eleanor? Yes, Grandpa. I made a batch this morning. Thought you'd enjoy them. Very good. Very good indeed. Reminds me of my mother's. She'd make them for the children after school. Different recipe though, used to have a dash of lemon zest. Makes all the difference, that does. Speaking of differences, did you see that article about Google's deal with HMRC? Apparently, they’re only paying a fraction of what they should in taxes. I did! It’s infuriating, isn’t it? Multi-billion pound companies getting away with sweet nothing while small businesses struggle. It feels like a rigged system. It always has been, Eleanor. Always has been. When I was an accountant, you'd be surprised the loopholes you could find, even with the best intentions. Though those were slightly different times, of course. Less… global. It just feels unfair, doesn’t it? Especially when you see the impact on services like education. Remember when the school was trying to fundraise for new computers? I do. It took us months. And even then, we only managed to get a few refurbished ones. It's something I worry about constantly, you know. The future for my pupils. Worrying never solved anything, my dear. Action does. Though, what can one little teacher do against a giant like Google? True. It’s just… everything feels so complicated these days.

Right then, Operation Dragon Drawing is officially underway! Let’s see if we can make these look even remotely… dragon-y. Leo, you’re in charge of scales. Poppy, you’re the head, obviously. Big, fierce head. But dragons have  lots  of heads, Mummy! Like, five! Five heads! Boom! Boom! Like a monster! Well, this one just has one, sweetheart. We're keeping it simple. It’s for Chinese New Year, remember? It has to be a lucky dragon! Though, five headed dragons  would  be pretty impressive, wouldn't they? Reminds me of something I read about in a book… it was about the planets, actually. Did you know some scientists think there might be planets circling other stars with  multiple  suns? Imagine that! Five suns! Five suns! Would it be really hot? Hotter than… than the oven when you're baking? Probably a lot hotter! Much, much hotter. Speaking of things that are hot, anyone fancy some dumplings after this? I’ve got some frozen ones - easy peasy Chinese feast! Dumplings! Yes! With soy sauce! Definitely with soy sauce. And maybe some spring rolls? Although, drawing dragons is hungry work. It needs fuel! Leo, are those scales looking fierce? You’re doing a great job, clever clogs. Mummy, look! I gave him sparkly eyes! So he can see all the planets! Sparkly eyes! Brilliant! He’s a very observant dragon. Good for spotting any mischievous spirits trying to spoil the celebrations. Speaking of celebrations, school's putting on a little performance next week. You’re both playing your instruments, aren’t you? Poppy, your piano piece is lovely. It's so calming, isn’t it? It's about the moon. And stars. Boom! Boom! My drums are  much  louder! I’m playing a warrior song! You certainly are, my little warrior! Honestly, sometimes I wonder where you get all that energy. You'd be amazing at aerial hoop. Remember when we saw that demonstration at the village fete? Yes! Spinning in the air! Like a sparkly… dragonfly! Dragonfly… boom! You’re both wonderfully chaotic. Now, back to our dragon. I was thinking, maybe we could add some little clouds around him? Like he’s flying through the sky? Leo, what do you think? And can we put glitter on the clouds? Lots and lots of glitter? Of course, we can put glitter on the clouds. It's a Chinese New Year dragon; it needs to be fabulous!

"You're winding him up, aren't you, Liam? About poor Uncle Barry. He’s obviously mortified." Chloe, fresh from a morning baking session, gave Liam a playful nudge. "He just wants to appreciate the Colosseum!" "Appreciate it with a feathered hat, apparently," Maya said, laughing from across the small, wrought-iron table. She ran a hand through her curly hair. "Rome is wild. The heat’s a bit much though, isn’t it? Not complaining, mind, just saying." “Yeah, it’s a scorcher, alright,” Mark, the Australian barista, agreed, taking a long sip of his beer. “Reminds me of a summer back in Perth, but drier somehow. Less humidity.” He had a slight accent that hinted at years spent just outside of Australia. Liam: "He did try to rearrange the pigeons, though. Said they were blocking the view. Uncle Barry, bless him, thinks he can control nature. The poor tour guide looked like he was about to cry.” Chloe: “Honestly, you guys are brutal. He’s family! He’s probably just having a bit of a culture shock. How’s the Airbnb treating you all, by the way? Mine was… an experience. Tiny, but with a view of a brick wall. Romantic, right?" Maya: "Mine's a bit better! Little balcony overlooking a courtyard. Got a lemon tree, even. Makes for a lovely breakfast, honestly. And the owner, Signora Rossi, is an absolute sweetheart. She keeps feeding us biscotti. I’m going to roll home eventually." Mark: "Glad to hear it. My place is pretty basic, just need a bed and somewhere to crash after long shifts. This city never sleeps, it seems." He gestured to the bustling street outside the bar. “So, dinner tonight? What are we thinking? Something traditional, or fancy and touristy?" Liam: "Traditional, definitely. I'm starving for some proper pasta. Somewhere not near the main tourist drags… somewhere the Romans actually go, you know?" Chloe: "I'm in. I’d love to try some authentic cacio e pepe. I attempted it yesterday, and... well, let's just say it was a learning experience. My kitchen’s covered in pecorino romano." She grimaced good-naturedly. Maya: "I know a place, actually. Near Trastevere. My cousin recommended it – Luigi’s. Apparently, the handmade pasta is legendary. Bit of a trek, but worth it, she says. I’ll send you the address.” Mark: “Luigi’s sounds good. I’m in.

Honestly, arranging this hen do for Chloe is proving to be a nightmare. She wants glamping, a pottery workshop,  and  a vintage clothes market. All in one weekend! Chloe does love a bit of chaos, doesn’t she? Sounds like a lot to juggle, though. Have you found a glamping site that allows for pottery? That feels pretty specific. It  is  ambitious! I’m still working on these little keychains for the guests, by the way. Thought it would be a cute little something.
