What about just booking the pottery workshop for the Saturday and doing a separate day trip to a vintage market? Spread it out a bit? Yeah, trying to cram everything into one weekend is just a recipe for stress. And probably budget-blowing! Remember when we tried to bake three different types of cake for Sarah’s birthday? Complete disaster. You’re right. I’m probably biting off more than I can chew. The vintage market is negotiable, I guess. Glamping feels important to her, though. She’s been talking about it for months. Found this place near Rutland Water, looks gorgeous, but it’s £300 a night! Ouch. That’s steep. Maybe suggest a slightly less fancy option? There are loads of campsites that have a "glamping" vibe – yurts, bell tents, that kind of thing. It would still fulfill the wish without breaking the bank. Totally! And speaking of money, did anyone see that gorgeous fabric at the craft fair last week? That peacock print, I was thinking of making some scrunchies for the goody bags… if I ever manage to find the time! Oh my god, yes! The peacock print was stunning! I was tempted myself, but I'm still trying to use up my stash. I'm working on a batch of little embroidered patches for people's bags - a little inside joke referencing Chloe’s terrible puns. That's brilliant, Jess! Actually, good idea. Goody bags. I hadn’t even thought that far ahead. What should go in them besides your patches and Ali’s keychains? Little face masks? Or those miniature scented candles? Always a winner. Keeps everyone happy and relaxed, which will be crucial for surviving Chloe's weekend of activities. Maybe some of that really cheap Prosecco? For a little pre-pottery fuel? Jess, you are a menace. But tempting! We  do  need to keep spirits high. I’m starting to feel genuinely worried about the glazing process.

Right, so, I’m thinking a bit more paprika in this. It needs a bit more…oomph, innit? Feels a bit bland, even with the smoked paprika. Mmm, sounds good. Don't go overboard though, remember what happened with Grandma’s stew last Christmas? She practically breathed fire for a week. Alright, alright, lesson learned. Subtle paprika boost. You're studying like a maniac, aren’t you? Big test coming up? Yeah, final assessment for the TEFL course. Gotta nail this if I want to actually get a decent job abroad. Still thinking about Spain, you know? Valencia specifically. The climate sounds unreal. Spain, eh? Proper adventure. You’ll love it. Me, I’m just stuck here designing brochures for garden gnomes. Thrilling, I know. Still, at least I'm earning. How's the flat hunting going? Still looking at those dodgy places near the train station? Ugh, don't remind me. Found one yesterday that smelled suspiciously of damp cat. Seriously, you wouldn’t believe some of this student accommodation. Think I’m just going to bite the bullet and increase my budget. Maybe look around Ruzafa, a bit further out. Probably a good shout. Your health’s worth more than saving a few quid. Speaking of health, how are you feeling? Still struggling with that cough? It’s…better. Still a bit of a wheeze, mostly at night. I reckon it’s just the changing weather. I’ve got that awful hayfever kicking in as well. Honestly, this time of year is a nightmare. Tell me about it. I’ve been sniffling like a leaky tap for days. Should’ve waited before coming round, sorry. Didn’t want to risk infecting you further though, thought the soup would cheer you up. Don't worry about it. The soup smells amazing, actually. What is it, anyway? Hungarian goulash. Tried a recipe I saw online. Wanted to make something hearty, you know, get some warmth in you. Needed a change from the usual pasta and beans diet. You ever tried making goulash before? Never. Too much effort! I’m more of a microwave meals kind of guy, if I'm honest. Though, I’ve recently been trying to be more adventurous. Remember that disastrous attempt at paella I made last month? How could I forget? The rice was rock hard, and it tasted like seawater. Don't remind me! I need a professional to teach me the ropes.

…and honestly, Patricia, finding those felt-tip pens for the cards – a crucial mission. Remember how excited we were about felt-tips in primary school? The smell of them alone! Oh, goodness yes, Penelope. The rainbow ones! And the way Mrs. Hawthorne, bless her, would insist on using them  responsibly . “No swirling, girls! Think of the vibrancy!” As if a seven-year-old could resist swirling a hot pink felt-tip. Absolutely not! I’m still traumatised by that felt-tip rule. Right, shopping list then. Biscuits are essential, naturally. And teabags – Earl Grey, specifically. Don't you dare buy anything else, Patricia. Wouldn't dream of it. And some of those little cream crackers, Penelope? The ones with the salty edge. Perfect with a slice of cheddar. We need some apples too. Granny Smiths, I think. Granny Smiths it is. What about a loaf of that sourdough from the bakery on Albion Street? It's ridiculously good. And… Oh! Remind me to get calendar fobs. Remember how Aunt Mildred always used to get us those awful ones with kittens? Floral wallpaper and everything. Oh, the horror! We’d use them for the back of the cupboard, not for the wall! This year, let’s get something…slightly less offensive. Maybe something with Impressionist art? Much better. They have some lovely ones at the craft fair next week, I think. Speaking of craft, do you remember when Miss Davies made us decorate hockey sticks in Year Four? With glitter and feathers! Oh, yes! And the chaos! Everyone getting glitter everywhere. I’m fairly certain half the class had glitter in their hair for a week afterwards. Mine certainly did! I can still smell that awful glue. My hockey stick looked like a particularly flamboyant parrot. Mine looked like a disco ball. It was mortifying. You know, it's funny, thinking back to school… I remember wanting to study sound recording at university. Completely obsessed with the idea of capturing sound. You did, didn’t you? For a little while. You had such a passion for it. I remember you buying that reel-to-reel recorder; it was enormous! It was! Terribly heavy to lug around. And then computers came along. Everything changed so quickly. Do you recall the absolute monstrosity that was the Commodore 64? Goodness, yes! A beige brick. But fascinating, in a way. And the loading times! Waiting what felt like an eternity for a game to load.

Honestly, it’s lovely here, isn't it? So much calmer than London. I can actually hear birds singing! It's a bit of a shock to the system after the constant hum of the city. Absolutely, darling. You've landed yourself in paradise. Holsworthy’s got such charm. And the people are so friendly. We bumped into Mrs. Treloar just this morning, she practically adopted you already! Said you must pop over for a scone. Scones already, are we? Sounds delightful, though I’m trying to resist the temptation of endless baked goods. My waistband thanks you. It's...different, isn't it? After Southend, I mean. Not quite the bracing sea air, that’s for sure. Well, the fresh air is  here , just a different kind. More…country air. And the hills! You'll love the walking, you really will. There’s that local walking group, the ‘Holsworthy Ramblers,’ apparently. Quite a dedicated bunch. Want to join? Oh, they're a good bunch. Bit serious, perhaps. But you’d get to see some proper countryside. I went with them once, ended up slightly lost amongst the gorse bushes. Highly entertaining for everyone  but  me. Lost in gorse bushes? That sounds precisely the sort of adventure I require. It’s a far cry from the council estate back home though. I’m having to adjust, you know. It's not just the scenery, it's...the pace of life. People actually stop to talk! In Southend, you get a glare if you make eye contact before rushing past. Exactly! And the DIY! You’re going to need to get involved in that. Mr. Peterson next door is a retired builder. He's offering to help with the fence. Apparently, the last one was practically falling down. Peterson’s a gem. Bit grumpy, but a good bloke. And his wife makes the best apple crumble you’ll ever taste. You'll be getting free crumble deliveries in no time. Have you found that nice little pub, 'The Dragon's Breath' yet? Gets rather busy on a Friday. That’s the one! Had a pint there last night. Decent ale, good atmosphere. It’s a bit pricey, though. That’s something to consider on the pension, isn't it? Less crumble, more pints, perhaps? Don't be ridiculous, Dad. You can have both! How's your tax return going? Are you managing alright with all the new forms?

Honestly, Liam, another fleece blanket? Mum’s going to kill us if we end up with three. Aye, well, it were on sale, Rach. Proper bargain. Like, twenty quid off. Couldn't miss it, could I? Winter's comin’, lass. Gotta be prepared. Prepared for what? Hibernation? You haven’t left this room in three days except to grab a Pot Noodle. That's a bit harsh, isn’t it? And it weren't just a Pot Noodle. It were a spicy one. Massively different. Besides, I been lookin’ for jobs online. Honest. Online? Still? Liam, you’ve been ‘looking’ since… well, since you finished uni. That's, what, two years now? And you applied for what? "Professional Gaming Enthusiast"? Seriously? It were a genuine listing! They wanted someone with experience in competitive online games. I'm good at FIFA. Top tier, even. It’s a skill, Rach! A transferable skill! Right. A transferable skill to… what? Sitting on the sofa all day? Honestly, Dad's shaking his head at you from the kitchen, you know. He just said something about ‘wasted potential’ and ‘wanting to see a bit of effort’. Don't remind me. He's always on about ‘effort’. It’s not that easy, is it? Everything's automated now. Robots doin' all the jobs. What's a lad from Whitehaven supposed to do? Whitehaven’s producing somethin’ alright: a mountain of fleece blankets and a son who hasn’t paid a bill in six months. Look, I put some real jobs on your email earlier. Warehouse assistant, delivery driver… even something at the garden centre. A garden centre? I’d be stood about weeding all day. I’d rather wrestle a badger. You’d probably lose to the badger. Just look at them, Liam. Please. Anything's better than scrolling through Amazon lookin’ for discounted home furnishings. Speaking of, did you see that thing Sarah posted on Facebook? About that new smart fridge? A smart fridge? What's that then? Does it order your beer for you? Basically. It can tell when you're running low on milk or eggs and orders them online. It even suggests recipes based on what's inside. It's ridiculous! And costs more than my entire rent. Ridiculous, aye. Fancy that. Back in our nan's day, a fridge just kept your sausages cold. No fripperies. Still, it’d be handy.

Honestly, it’s coming together so much better than I imagined. You’ve really made it feel like a home, ANON. That rug really pulls everything together, doesn't it? It does, love! A proper bit of colour, too. Takes the biscuit, really. And that sofa… comfy as anything, isn’t it? A far cry from that old thing you had before. Yes, well, it's a vast improvement. Spent a fortune on it, mind you. But worth every penny. Needed something robust. You know, ready for… well, for us. And the dogs, naturally. Speaking of robust, how's the heating situation looking? You mentioned you were tackling that yesterday. Still freezing in the mornings, are we? Well, it's… complicated. Took the cover off the boiler, had a proper look, and… it's a right mess, innit? Some of those pipes are practically fossilised. I think I’m going to need to get a proper plumber in. DIY won’t cut it this time. Oh dear. That’s a shame. You’re usually so handy. I’ve got a contact, a chap called Dave. He does a decent job for a reasonable price. I can give you his number. That would be brilliant, Siobhan. We don’t want you freezing through the winter. By the way, I brought lunch. Ploughman's, as requested! Cheddar, pickle, bread, apples… the works. You’re an angel, love! Always thinking of me. Sit down, sit down. It smells absolutely marvellous. Always happy to oblige! Got a bit more time now I’m semi-retired. So, ANON, you were saying about that coastal walk you were planning? Where were you thinking of going? I was thinking of heading out towards Hartland Quay on Sunday. The weather forecast looks reasonable. We could pack a picnic, make a day of it. Hartland Quay… lovely. Bit of a steep climb back up, though, isn't it? My knees aren't what they used to be, you know. We'll take it easy, Dad. Plenty of stops along the way. And I'll carry the heaviest bits of the picnic. Speaking of carrying things, have you had a look at that sideboard you wanted? The one from that antique shop in Bude? I went in yesterday. It's a beauty, it really is. Oak, solid as a rock. A bit of a fixer-upper, but nothing I can't handle.

That was lovely, honestly. Your roast chicken is getting seriously impressive, Ben. Definitely better than my attempts. Years of practice, love. And a bit of help from YouTube, if I'm honest. Don't tell Mum. She’d never let me live it down. So, massively better than your attempt last week, then? The one that resembled charcoal? Okay, okay, you win on the chicken front. Drastically better. Though, to be fair, the smoke alarm did add a certain…ambiance. How was your day, by the way? You were awfully quiet at dinner. Not the usual frantic recounting of research findings. It was… frustrating, to put it mildly. I've been wrestling with this dataset all week, trying to isolate a clear correlation between social media usage and anxiety in adolescents. Everyone  thinks  there's a link, naturally. But the numbers… they just aren't cooperating. That sounds awful. Is it a design flaw, do you think? Something with the methodology? I've checked and double-checked everything. The sample is good, the questions are validated... I think it's just...noise. So much confounding data. They’re all hanging out online, chatting about different things, influenced by so many factors... Honestly, I'm starting to question the whole premise. Maybe there isn't a direct causal link. That's tough. You put so much effort into these projects. It's disheartening when the data doesn’t support your hypothesis. Remember that time I was trying to implement that new assessment system at work? I was convinced it was the  answer  to everything, all efficiency and streamlined processes. Then the teachers revolted. Ah, yes. The great assessment system rebellion. I still remember you coming home absolutely livid, ranting about stakeholder management. Livid doesn't even cover it! They felt like I was trying to deskill them, reduce them to robots ticking boxes. It was a total misreading of… well, of everything, really. Professor Davies pulled me aside and said I needed to spend more time listening to the people who were actually  doing  the work. She was right, of course. Sometimes the answers aren’t in the spreadsheets; they’re in conversations. That’s a good point. I'm so focused on the statistical significance, I might be missing the human element. Maybe I need to go back to the initial interviews we conducted and re-examine them with a different lens.

That lamb was lovely, wasn't it? Proper Sunday dinner this, thanks to you, David. Better than the hospital canteen, that's for sure. Glad you enjoyed it, love. It's what I do, innit? Though, honestly, sourcing decent lamb these days is a right pain. Keeps goin' up. You’d think with Brexit…well, makes no sense. Brexit's a rabbit hole nobody needs to go down on a Sunday, Dad. Seriously. Can we talk about something lighter? Like, did Gran ever tell you about the time she tried to teach a squirrel to do tricks? Oh, that! You youngsters wouldn't believe it. She bought a little harness and everything. Tried to get the poor thing to jump through hoops. It ended up biting her. Proper nipped her, it did! Remember, Margaret? Oh, I do! She was flustered for days, covered in iodine. Said it was a sign the squirrel disapproved of her methods. Such a character, Mum. Always had a story. Though she did make a right mess of the garden trying to attract wildlife. Wildlife's a nuisance, frankly. I had a robin building a nest in my guttering last year. Had to cover the whole thing in mesh. Nearly bankrupted me, the cost of everything. And don't even get me started on pigeons! Ruining my newly painted eaves… Arthur, that’s a bit harsh, isn’t it? They’re just trying to survive. Speaking of survival, did you hear about young Timmy Henderson down the road? Lost his job at the warehouse. Hard times for everyone. That’s awful. It’s getting harder and harder to find anything secure. Makes you wonder what the future holds, doesn’t it? I’m just freelancing as a copywriter at the moment, which is fine, but it's feast or famine. I’m seriously considering looking at a permanent position. You should, love. Secure work's worth its weight in gold these days. Especially with the way things are going. It's just…everything’s so expensive now. Even with me earning, it's a struggle sometimes. I was looking at replacing the boiler, but frankly, I'm scared to even get a quote. Tell me about it. Training to be a Nurse Practitioner is costing a fortune. All these top-up fees… and don’t even get me started on childcare. Little Alfie's running me ragged, but I’m determined to see it through.

Aye, this scone is a bit dry, isn’t it, Anon? Not quite up to your usual standards, love. Though the jam’s lovely. Proper strawberry jam, that. Dry scones are a sign of the times, lass. Everything's rushed these days. Back in my day, you got a scone still warm from the oven, practically leaping out of the tin. My mother – God rest her soul – she used to bake them every Saturday. Proper Lancashire scones, they were. Heavy, ye ken? Not these… these are like eating sawdust. They're perfectly fine, actually. And Anon, you really shouldn't apologise. Scones are notoriously difficult to get just right. I had a disastrous attempt myself last week. They were flatter than a pancake. Pancake scones! Now that’s a thing I’d like to see. You’re a consultant engineer, aren't you, Finn? Surely you can apply some kind of structural integrity principle to baking. I assure you, even precision engineering doesn’t conquer the unpredictability of flour and baking powder. It’s a very humbling experience, attempting to bake. Humbling? Baking's a craft, boy! A proper skill. Used to be every woman knew how to bake, how to knit, how to darn a sock. Nowadays, folks can’t boil an egg without looking it up on their… their whatchamacallits. Phones. He's right, Finn. There’s a real loss of traditional skills, innit? My gran used to make the best pasties you ever tasted, from scratch. Never a shop-bought ingredient in sight. I suppose so. Though, I think we’ve gained other skills. Technical skills, problem-solving... Technical skills. What good are technical skills when you can't make a decent cup of tea or a pie crust that doesn't crumble at the slightest touch? I tell you, the world's gone soft. Oh, get off your high horse, George. You’ve been saying that since I was knee-high to a grasshopper. Remember that trip to Spain, though? You complaining about the paella being too… exotic? That paella was an insult to seafood! Overly seasoned, drowned in rice… no respect for the ingredients, that’s what it was. Proper Lancashire seafood pie is the only way to enjoy fish. Well, I’ve always wanted to go to Spain. Portugal too. The architecture, the history… and, of course, the food. I’m a bit of a foodie, actually.

Right, so, the feedback on Module 3 was... robust, to say the least. Apparently, the students found the Derrida section utterly impenetrable. Robust is putting it mildly, darling. My inbox looked like a war zone. "Confused," "overwhelmed," "what on earth was that about?" – the usual suspects. Did you see the one who said it felt like being “thrown into a philosophical blender”? Oh, I love that. A philosophical blender. I might steal that. But seriously, we need to do something. I spent ages trying to break it down, but seemingly, it didn’t land. We can’t just abandon it, though – it's crucial to understanding deconstruction. Perhaps we need to find a different entry point? I was thinking the same. Maybe less direct theory, and more applied examples? Instead of diving straight into  Of Grammatology , we could start with some pop culture – a critically analysed ad campaign, a popular song… something they can latch onto. Think about how we explained structuralism last year; using fashion trends made it so much easier for them to grasp. Good point. Something concrete. A music video, perhaps? Something with layered meanings, easy to dissect... Hmm, Billie Eilish maybe? She’s complex, visually striking, and there's a lot to unpack. Perfect! We could even build a little task around it. "Deconstruct a Billie Eilish music video" – sounds significantly less daunting than "Discuss the implications of Derrida's concept of  différance ." Exactly! And we could pair it with a shorter, more accessible reading related to semiotics. To give them the grounding before they tackle the more challenging stuff. Okay, I’m feeling slightly more optimistic about this now. What about the seminar discussion on Woolf? I’m worried it’s going to devolve into a massive existential angst session. They  will  go there, inevitably. But we’ve prepared for that. The key is to guide them towards specific textual examples. Remind them about the stream-of-consciousness technique and how it reflects the fragmented nature of experience. And I’ve found that prompting them with questions about Mrs. Ramsay's relationships helps steer the conversation away from purely personal musings. True. We did have a good framework. Right, classes... almost there. Actually, I'm starving. Have you thought about what we're having for dinner? I'm craving hotpot. Hotpot sounds amazing! I saw a new place down the street, apparently they have really authentic Sichuan broth.

Honestly, this coffee machine is a menace. It's been spitting out lukewarm, half-brewed sludge all morning. I'm starting to think it's actively plotting against me. Oh, you and your dramatics, love. It's just a machine. Probably needs a good descaling. My own never gave me much trouble, no. Though, teaching quadratic equations is far more stressful than a dodgy coffee machine, I’ll tell you that. Descaling won't fix everything, Sarah. These things are built to fail now. Planned obsolescence, that's what it is. Keeps the economy ticking over, apparently. Exactly! Everything's designed to fall apart just when you're getting comfortable. Which reminds me, we  need  to sort out those removal quotes. They're higher than I expected. Storage costs especially… ridiculous. They are, aren’t they? I had a look at a few online, and they nearly made me choke on my tea. Where are we thinking of storing the bulk of the furniture anyway? Is Derek happy with that unit in Penrith? Penrith’s fine. He assured me it's secure and dry, and they have CCTV. More important than a fancy address, that. Though, the sheer cost... it’s a bit depressing, isn't it? Paying to keep things we  own  locked away. Depressing is the word. I'm trying to rationalize it – it's only for a couple of months while we get settled. But every pound spent on storage feels like a pound not spent on, you know, actually enjoying ourselves. Well, you’ve earned a bit of enjoyment, haven't you, dear? You’ve been working your fingers to the bone. Though, all this moving… it does make you think, doesn’t it? All the accumulated… stuff. A life’s worth of things. Reminds you of the fleeting nature of it all. All this striving, all this collecting… Ultimately, it’s just boxes. Don’t get philosophical on me, Michael. I’m stressed enough as it is! Speaking of striving, have you seen what's happening with the Labour leadership? It's such a mess. Oh, don’t even start me on politics. It’s enough to drive a person to drink. Though, I have to say, I’m wishing they had grasped the nettle years ago and truly reformed. So much talk, so little action. It's disheartening. It’s the same old story. Promises, promises.

…and then Mrs. Goldstein actually  insisted  I cater her nephew's bar mitzvah using only… pineapple. Pineapple! Can you imagine? Kosher rules, right out the window. I had to politely explain that wasn't exactly… permissible. Blimey! Pineapple on a bar mitzvah spread? That's mental, innit? I’d have walked. My nan would've given me a right telling off if I’d even  considered  it. She’s got this encyclopedic knowledge of kosher law – you ask her anything, she’ll know. You're telling me! My mum’s the same. It’s like a family religion. Although, the bar mitzvah thing… that’s a new one. Listen, did you guys see that canal boat going down the Thames the other day? Massive thing. Looked like something out of a period drama. Crikey! A canal boat on the Thames? That  is  a sight. Reminds me a bit of the Murray River back home, though the Murray's a bit wider, naturally. Not exactly canals, though, more like big, slow-moving rivers. We used to go camping along the Murray when I was a kid. Proper good times. Speaking of rivers… I was thinking about nicknames. We're all here on holiday, pretending to be someone else, right? We said we’d pick pseudonyms. I’m still stuck. "Evie" feels a bit… bland. Yeah, we need something proper. I'm thinking "Riff." Short, sharp, London-y. What about you, Chloe? You haven’t offered up one yet. I’m thinking about it! It’s hard. Don’t want anything too silly. Maybe… “Willow”? It feels kind of calming, y’know? Like being by a riverbank. Willow's lovely! Suits you. I’m gonna go with "Digger." Classic Aussie. Can't go wrong with Digger. It's my granddad's name, too. Digger! That’s brilliant. Riff and Willow and Digger… and Evie. Still working on that one. So, holiday so far? Anyone managed to visit any decent clubs? I was hoping for something a bit underground, you know? Not just the tourist traps. Nah, been too busy eating. And arguing about pineapple. Reckon we should hit up Fabric? I went there once, years ago, it was mental. Good music, proper vibe. Fabric's a bit too much for me, I think. I like somewhere more chilled. Have you guys ever been to that little Italian place down Brick Lane? "Bella Luna"?

Honestly, this Tinder thing is a right shambles, isn't it? Like, I swiped right on five lads last night, proper decent looking ones, and not a single message. Nothin'! Tell me about it, love! It’s a desert out there. I had one guy message me, "U up?" at 2 AM. Like, seriously? Is that your best effort? I blocked him quicker than you can say "Scouse." Oh, don't even start me on the questionable messages. I got one asking if I was good at… baking. Baking! Like, what does that even have to do with anything? I'm studying engineering, for goodness sake! Likely just trying to get you to bake him a cake, Derby girl. Low effort romance, that is. It’s a plague, innit? I've been sticking to lads I know from uni, less hassle. Aye, sensible. Although, even the uni lads are a bit… lukewarm. Like Mark from my lectures? Nice enough, I suppose, but zero spark. Proper dull. See, that’s it, isn't it? It’s all just lukewarm. All lads seem to be playing it safe these days. Nobody’s bold. Nobody’s… exciting! Remember when you could just, like, talk to someone in a bar and boom! Potential romance? Those days are gone, lass. Now you need a carefully curated profile, a witty bio, and lightning-fast responses. It’s exhausting! My housemate, Chloe, she’s obsessed with it. Spends hours taking selfies. Chloe sounds intense. Uni’s getting to her. Speaking of housemates, how's yours, Beth? Still playing her ukulele and singing off-key at 6 AM? Don't even mention it! Honestly, I’m half tempted to move out. It’s not just the ukulele, it’s the… everything. The constant snacking, the leaving dirty mugs everywhere, the interpretive dance sessions... Interpretive dance? Now you’re just winding us up! Honestly, Sarah, your life sounds like a sitcom. I wish it was a sitcom! It's more like a slow, torturous reality. I told her yesterday, "Beth, for the love of Pete, can you keep it down when I'm trying to revise for my history essay?" And she just… wiggled her eyebrows and started humming. Classic Beth. You’ve gotta lay down the law, Sarah. You're the one living with her, right? You need to be strong! Strong is right. Tell her to find a different hobby.

Honestly, Marjorie, this news is just… dreadful. Another rise in benefits! They're bleedin' us dry, they are. And for what? To line the pockets of some bloke in Westminster, I reckon. Now, Arthur, don't go gettin' yourself worked up again. It's not helping your blood pressure. They have to manage the country, don’t they? Things cost money. Managed it right into the ground, more like. Look at this, Marjorie. Another report about the state of the roads. Potholes the size of craters now! A civil engineer couldn't fix all this with a lifetime supply of tarmac, I tell you. And the blame? "Unforeseen weather conditions." Unforeseen? We’ve had rain for centuries down here! It's shoddy planning, plain and simple. See? See what I mean? They don't care about us ordinary folk. It's all London and the south-east. Norfolk gets forgotten about entirely. Remember back in the day, Arthur? The council used to be proper. Kept things shipshape. Now? It’s just… chaos. You’re remembering the 1960s, dear. Things change. And blaming everything on London isn’t productive. There’s good and bad everywhere. Though, I must say, I agree about the roads. Nearly lost a wheel on my bicycle just last week. Productive? Marjorie, with all due respect, we're talking about the infrastructure crumbling around us! They're cutting corners everywhere. Remember that bridge they built over the River Wensum five years ago? Had to be closed for repairs within a year. A year! A proper bridge, constructed correctly, wouldn't need repairs that quickly. And the television! Don't get me started on the television listing. Nothing on but…reality shows and talent competitions. Back in the day, you got proper dramas.  Dixon of Dock Green , that was a show! Something to actually think about. Oh, Arthur, you and your nostalgia.  Dixon of Dock Green  was a bit… quaint, wasn’t it? I quite enjoy the talent shows. Gives people a chance. Though, I do agree, there’s a severe lack of quality drama on the BBC these days. It used to be the standard, didn't it? Now it’s all just… manufactured emotion. Manufactured emotion! Precisely! It's all designed to manipulate you. And don't even get me started on the political coverage. It's just endless bickering and point-scoring. No one actually addresses the real issues.

Honestly, David, this is lovely, really it is. But I'm still a bit tired. That meeting with the historical society was… something. Tired? Sounds intense. What happened? You looked a bit flustered when you got in. And you haven't even touched your peas! Peas are essential for a balanced diet, you know. It’s about the proposed development on the old brewery site. They want to build flats, luxury apartments, the whole nine yards. And apparently, they’ve got planning permission already. Luxury apartments? In Lichfield? Bit much, isn't it? Who's going to buy them? Oil tycoons come to admire the cathedral? Apparently, there’s a huge demand. Property developers have convinced the council. The problem is, the brewery site is historically significant. It's been a brewery for over two hundred years! And they’re going to demolish the original building, saving only the façade, and slapping some shiny glass boxes in front of it. It’s… jarring. So, I was arguing against it, trying to explain the importance of preserving this part of our history. And did you get anywhere? You always were a good debater, remember those school prize-givings? Not really. They had a planning consultant there, all suited and booted, spouting jargon about ‘urban regeneration’ and ‘market opportunities.’ It was like arguing with a brick wall. Mrs. Higgins kept interrupting, saying it would bring “vital investment” to the town. Honestly, David, sometimes I feel like shouting. Don’t fret, love. You did your best. Those councils, eh? Always listen to the money first. How's your sister doing, by the way? Any news from Emily? Oh, Emily's fine. Still trying to get little Thomas to stop eating crayons. She sent some pictures today – he’s got a masterpiece on his face. It's rather charming, actually. She’s starting to think about coming back for Christmas. That’d be lovely. It’s been far too long. Speaking of charming, did you catch that episode of 'Midsummer Murders' last night? The vicar was particularly amusing. Oh, yes! The one with the antique book dealer? Absolutely brilliant. Though I do think they’re running out of ideas. It’s become a bit predictable, hasn’t it? A bit, perhaps. But it’s comforting, isn’t it? Familiar faces, a quaint village, a dastardly murder... perfect evening fodder. My meetings today were a right slog, I’m telling you.

Honestly, this damp is dreadful. My sinuses are playing up again. Poland in October… you’d think it wouldn't be this miserable, wouldn’t you? Back in Cambridge, it's usually… well, you know. Grey, but drier. Aye, it’s baltic, isn’t it? Worse than Bury, even. At least Bury has decent chippies to cheer you up. Tarnow's cuisine... let's just say I've been mostly living on Polish supermarket soups and hoping for the best. Though, I did find a surprisingly good pierogi place the other day. You should try it. Distracts from the, you know… everything. Distraction is key these days, isn’t it? Especially with… with all of this. Granddad… it’s just… I keep expecting him to pop round for a cup of tea and complain about the football. I know. It's proper gut-wrenching. My nan would’ve hated seeing you like this, flitting about halfway across Europe. Though, I suppose she’d be proud you’re teaching English – she always said you were clever as a whip. Clever doesn’t pay the bills, does it, love? TEFL is… a stopgap. A slightly less depressing stopgap than staring at the wallpaper in Cambridge. Though, I confess, I do enjoy it when I have a class. It's… a purpose. What about you? Still loving teaching? Mostly. There are days, definitely, where I want to chuck it all and open a little bakery somewhere. Somewhere sunny. Like... Greece maybe. Picture it: fresh bread, olives, sunshine... No marking essays. You and your escape fantasies. Don’t we all have them? I’ve been scrolling through Facebook, embarrassing myself, I know, looking at old school friends' holiday photos. Barbados, Australia… all those perfectly curated lives. Makes you feel a bit… adrift. Don't do that to yourself. Those pictures aren't real, not really. It's just the highlight reel. Remember Sarah Henderson's 'perfect' wedding? Turns out her husband’s a nightmare. You're right, of course. It's just... this funeral, going back... It feels like a return to a life that isn't mine anymore. A life where I had… expectations. A job, a house, stability. Now… Poland. Tarnow. It's surprisingly… calming, on some level. But also intensely lonely. I get it. It's a weird feeling, isn't it? Being somewhere that isn't home, but also realising that 'home' might not be what it used to be.

Honestly, this Earl Grey is surprisingly decent for a pub. I was expecting something… dustier. Innit? I thought the same. You'd think they’d only stock lukewarm beer and flat Coke. Glad we opted for tea, eh? Needed something to calm my nerves after that morning. Tell me about it. My dissertation is breathing down my neck. I swear, if I have to read another paragraph about post-structuralist interpretations of Victorian poetry, I’m going to scream into a pillow. Oh, bless you. That sounds… intense. My morning wasn’t quite existential dread, but a client basically accused me of making their product sound “too interesting.” Apparently, beige sells better than vibrant. Beige sells better? Seriously? What even  is  that product? Concrete sealant. For driveways. They wanted it to sound…functional. Like, utterly devoid of personality. I tried to sneak in words like ‘durable’ and ‘reliable,’ but apparently, that was still too much flair. Oh my god, you’re joking! That’s brilliant, in a tragically absurd sort of way. It’s like, they're actively trying to make their product unappealing. Honestly! It's draining, though. Copywriting gigs can be a real mixed bag. One day I'm crafting emotionally resonant ad campaigns for sustainable clothing, the next I'm struggling to make concrete sound exciting. At least you're  doing  something creative. I’m mostly just debugging code for surveys. It’s fine, pays the bills, but doesn't exactly set the world on fire. Though, I did manage to fix a particularly nasty error today involving a miscalculated margin of error. Felt pretty good, actually. See, that’s a skill! A valuable one. I’m useless with anything technical. Remember when my laptop crashed and I nearly had a meltdown? You practically had to live at my flat for a week. That was… memorable. Your sense of despair was truly theatrical. Anyway, speaking of living at someone’s flat… have you heard from Chloe and Liam? They were supposed to be moving in together last month. No! I haven’t. They’ve been pretty radio silent. I thought they were getting on alright. I mean, they seemed smitten at Sarah’s wedding. Exactly! I thought they were on track. I messaged Liam a couple of weeks ago, just a casual ‘how’s it going?’ and he sent back a brief, vague reply about "logistical hurdles." Which isn't exactly reassuring.

Honestly, you two! Six AM? What on earth possessed you to be bouncing around like that? But Mummy! The sun’s up! And Barnaby was doing a flip! A really big one! I almost caught him! Nearly did a handstand too! Nearly. That’s the important word, isn't it? Right, okay. Six AM. Not ideal. But it’s Saturday, so I suppose… are you both starving? Yes! Hungry! Want pancakes! With sprinkles! Red ones! Lots of them! Red sprinkles it is. Pancakes are happening. Barnaby, darling, could you please,  please , try to be a bit quieter before Mummy's properly awake? My head feels like it's full of cotton wool. Sorry, Mummy. I was practicing my tightrope walk! We're going to be circus performers! Are you now? That's fantastic! You’re both very ambitious. Speaking of things we’re going to do... remember that Neon Moon event we talked about? The one in Cambridge next weekend? Ooh, yes! The sparkly one! Can we go, Mummy? Please? We're trying to book tickets, love. It's proving popular, but I’ve got my eye on a few slots. It would be lovely, wouldn't it? Fairy lights and music… Will they have juggling? Can I learn to juggle like a real circus performer? Possibly! I’m sure there’ll be demonstrations, at least. And we can get you some juggling balls. We'll practice! But first, pancakes. Right, let's get this kitchen moving. Barnaby, could you fetch the flour? I’ll get the sprinkles! Red ones! Perfect. Now, I was reading something interesting the other day about… …Australian slang. Apparently, they say 'G'day' instead of hello. G'day! G'day, Mummy! G'day, Barnaby! G'day! Is that like saying ‘Good morning!’? Pretty much. And they say 'arvo' instead of afternoon. Fancy that. It makes you wonder how language changes. I wonder if, a hundred years from now, people will be saying something completely baffling to me. Maybe we’ll all be speaking Martian! And juggling with our toes! Now you’re getting carried away! Though, juggling with your toes… that  would  be impressive. Okay, flour and sprinkles, please. Restocking the pancake supplies is paramount. Afterwards, we can look at those Neon Moon tickets properly. I’m thinking Saturday afternoon might be the best. What do you think? Yes! Saturday afternoon! Can we wear our sparkle dresses? Absolutely. You both look lovely in your sparkle dresses.

Right, another twenty minutes or so, I reckon. And this blasted A30… it’s a ribbon of grey misery, isn’t it? At least the scenery’s improving now we're heading north. Less… palm trees, more sheep. Don't be such a grump, Rhys. It's a perfectly decent road. And the palm trees were a fleeting novelty. Though, you’re right, the Welsh hills are much more… comforting. Speaking of comforting, did you see what's happened with that new housing development proposal in Penryn? They’ve completely ignored the local concerns about flood risk. Seriously? That's outrageous! I read about that online. Locals are saying the ground isn’t stable enough, and it’s going to end up with houses underwater. Developers just don’t care, do they? Exactly, Matthew! It's the same story everywhere, isn’t it? Profit over people. Pure and simple. Remember that debacle with the wind farm near Pontypridd? The council promised minimal impact, and the noise… well, it drove old Mrs. Evans absolutely round the bend. It's deeply frustrating, isn't it? And the planning system is so convoluted. It’s almost impossible for ordinary people to properly challenge these decisions. Politicians promise reform, but… nothing ever changes. It’s like a revolving door. It feels like everything is rigged against anyone who isn't connected to the right people or has a massive bank account. It's just… depressing. Shouldn’t there be more power for local communities to decide these things? There  should  be, Matthew. There absolutely should. We had a similar fight when I was a kid, trying to stop a quarry being built on Pen-y-Crug. My grandfather, bless his soul, was a firebrand. Spent weeks at council meetings, waving geological surveys around, arguing until he was blue in the face. Didn't win, of course. They still opened the quarry. But he fought. That's what matters. Your grandfather sounds like a remarkable man. It's inspiring, really, knowing people stood up for what they believed in, even when it felt hopeless. My own grandfather was more… resigned. He always said, “The trains run on time, Eleanor. What can you do?” A very British attitude, I suppose. Avoiding confrontation. So, Rhys, you were a young kid back then? What did you think of all that? I was barely ten, Matthew, but I remember the smell of the dust from the quarry, the constant rumble of the trucks.

Right, so, rewind. We were just discussing… dragons, weren’t we? Leo, you insisted the dragon  had  to breathe custard. It was a  very  sticky dragon, Mummy! And he tickled people with it! It should have been raspberry. Custard is boring. Dragons need raspberry breath. Much more intimidating. Intimidating? Leo, you are a font of wisdom. Raspberry dragon breath. I love it. Much better than my initial suggestion of… uh… lavender. Not very scary, is it? Now, Elara, what did the princess do when the raspberry dragon appeared? She… she gave him a biscuit! A really big one. With sprinkles. A biscuit with sprinkles? Brave princess. Very brave. Leo, what do you think? Should the biscuit have been chocolate or vanilla? Chocolate. Definitely chocolate. Raspberry dragon deserves chocolate. It’s a compromise. So he’s still scary, but also… appreciated. Appreciated. That’s a good point. It's important for even fearsome dragons to feel appreciated. You know, that reminds me… I'm thinking of going to the Linton Book Festival next weekend. They've got Helen Moss doing a talk. Who’s Helen Moss? Is she a princess? Not a princess, sweetie. She writes stories. Wonderful stories. Really silly ones, and some rather clever ones too. Her stories are often about slightly mischievous, but ultimately good-hearted, characters. Like your raspberry dragon, maybe? Does she write about proper dragons? Ones that breathe fire, not raspberry? Sometimes. But she writes about all sorts of things, Leo. Fairies, goblins, talking animals... even slightly grumpy teacups. It’s all rather fantastical. I thought it might be nice to take you both, if you’re interested. Can we meet a real dragon? I’m afraid I can’t promise a real dragon, darling. Though, who knows, perhaps one of the authors will  be  a dragon in disguise! What kind of books does she write? Are they scary? Not really scary, Leo. More… adventurous. And funny. She writes a series called ‘The Curious Case of…’ – they’re about a little girl who finds hidden portals to different magical worlds. They're brilliant. I read them when I was younger, and they sparked my love of storytelling. Maybe it'll spark yours too. Can we get a book with sprinkles on the cover? We can certainly look! Probably not sprinkled, but there  are  lots of lovely covers. Maybe one with a dragon. Or a biscuit. Or both!

Honestly, I’m still getting my head around this cultured meat thing. “Shmeat,” they’re calling it. It just sounds so…clinical. Like something out of a dystopian novel. Clinical, yeah, but potentially amazing. Think about it, Chloe, no more factory farms. No more animals enduring… well,  everything  they endure. Isn't that worth a little clinical jargon? It’s a massive leap, though, isn’t it? We're talking about completely redefining how we get our protein. It’s a bit… unsettling. I mean, growing meat in a lab? Feels a bit like playing God. Playing God is what we've been doing for centuries with selective breeding! And don’t even get me started on the ethics of abattoirs. I volunteered at an animal sanctuary last year… it was horrific. Seeing the fear in their eyes… Exactly! And hunting, while seemingly "natural," is still inherently violent. It's just a different kind of manipulation. At least with cultured meat, you theoretically control the whole process. True, but the environmental impact of  growing  it needs to be considered. I’ve read some worrying stuff about energy consumption. They said it will take a huge amount of power. Which is a valid point, definitely. But surely it’s still less impactful than raising cattle? Think about the deforestation for grazing land, the methane emissions… Precisely. And what about people who claim it's ‘unnatural’? Like, eating a carrot isn’t natural. Agriculture itself isn't natural. We’ve been manipulating nature to survive for millennia. It’s complex, isn’t it? It's all intertwined. The environment, animal welfare, human nutrition… I'm just struggling to wrap my head around it. It feels like moving away from something tangible, and towards… something else entirely. I know what you mean. It’s like, I like cooking with real vegetables, feeling the texture, smelling the herbs... It's a whole sensory experience. Replacing that with a lab-grown patty feels… sterile. But consider the potential. Imagine a world where everyone has access to affordable, ethical protein. Plus, you could completely control the nutrient profile. We could all be taking fewer vitamin tablets! I've been feeling run-down lately, and the B12 supplements are expensive. Speaking of tablets... I'm thinking of trying that new algae-based omega-3. Apparently, it’s much better absorbed than fish oil. Oh, really? I’ve only ever tried the fish oil capsules.

Honestly, this washing machine is going to be the death of me. It’s taken three attempts to get these towels even vaguely clean. Three! And they still smell faintly of damp dog. Well, Buster does shed, doesn't he? You can’t expect a fluffy Samoyed to be completely odourless. You’d think after all these years, you’d be used to it. And you know, I think we need to run a service on it. It’s probably full of fluff. You guys are stressing me out. I’m trying to decide which streaming service to subscribe to next. So much choice, so little time, right? Netflix is obviously done, Disney+ is alright, but is Apple TV really worth it? Apple TV? For what? More pretentious documentaries about fruit? Honestly, darling, your money would be better spent on fixing this infernal machine! Very funny, Dad. I'm looking at Ted Lasso, you know. Apparently, it's brilliant. Mum, have you seen it? Oh yes! Absolutely charming. Reminds me a bit of Uncle Barry’s attempts at motivational speaking, bless him. Remember at his wedding, he tripped over the flower girl and kept insisting he'd “landed the confetti gracefully?” Don't remind me! The poor girl burst into tears. Wedding photography was a nightmare that day. Trying to hide Barry’s face-plant from every possible angle. Still makes me shudder. Weddings are so stressful. Sarah and Tom are starting to fight already, just thinking about planning theirs. Apparently, the seating arrangements are a war zone. Aunt Carol insists her cousin must sit next to the vicar, and Tom’s best mate is refusing to sit anywhere near his ex. Sounds familiar! You know, it’s amazing how much drama can be squeezed into one family gathering. Speaking of drama… Did you see what Brenda posted on Facebook about the Christmas decorations? She's already put hers up! In November! Brenda? Honestly! That woman lives in her own world. She’s probably got a full-scale reindeer army guarding her front lawn by now. She’s got such a peculiar way of speaking too. Remember when she tried to order a “large portion of chips” in Scotland? They kept asking her if she meant “chips” or “fries”! She got so flustered. That’s so funny! Language differences are wild, aren’t they? I was talking to a client in Australia last week.

Honestly, Mum, butterfly forks are ridiculous. Who even  needs  a fork that looks like a butterfly? It’s just… extra. Oh, come on, Ollie. They're charming! Aunt Penelope brought them back from a trip to Russia, remember? She said they're very popular there for children’s parties. A little bit of whimsy with your supper. They  are  quite cool, actually. I like the wings. Can I have one, Mum? Of course, Leo. There's plenty to go around. Though, I do hope you're not planning on playing with them instead of eating your spaghetti. Seriously though, Russia? Butterfly forks? It's a bizarre combination. What else did Aunt Penelope bring back? Bear-shaped tea cosy and a matryoshka doll that sings polka? You’re being dramatic! She brought back some beautiful scarves, a few amber necklaces, and yes, a rather kitsch but adorable matryoshka doll. She insists it sings, though I’ve never actually heard it. She said it's only activated by a very specific musical note. Can we call Aunt Penelope? Maybe she can make it sing! Maybe later, Leo. Right now, I think we should observe the two minutes’ silence for Remembrance Day. It's nearly eight o’clock. Oh yeah, right. Forgot. It's important, Ollie. Let's all take a moment to remember. Leo, you too. It's for all the people who fought for us. Right then. That was a proper silence, well done. Now, spaghetti time! Best silence ever! Look, I’m a butterfly knight! Don't be daft. It still feels weird eating with this thing. It's just a fork, dear. Besides, it's almost your birthday, Ollie! We’re having a special supper. Speaking of birthdays, Leo’s turning thirteen next month. We need to start thinking about what he wants to do. Laser tag! Definitely laser tag. And cake. Lots of cake. Laser tag again? You had laser tag last year. And the year before that. It’s awesome! Well, we can certainly look into it. Ollie, what about you? Thinking of grand plans for turning seventeen? Not really. I’m just hoping to pass my history exam. Honestly, Mrs. Davies is  killing  me with all the Russian Revolution detail. Tsarist Russia, Bolsheviks, Lenin… it’s a headache. It  is  complex, but fascinating, isn’t it? It's easy to see why Aunt Penelope picked up those butterfly forks.

…and then little Timmy insisted the Roman soldier's helmet was his actual helmet. Had to explain, very carefully, that it was just for dressing up. Honestly, marking these history exams is exhausting. So much misinformation! Dinosaur! Roar! Can I have a biscuit, Mummy? Please? Yes, darling, dinosaurs are brilliant. And yes, Leo, in a minute. Let Mummy finish telling Auntie Chloe about my day. Chloe, you wouldn't believe the things these kids think! I know about dinosaurs! Triceratops! See? She's well-informed. Anyway, Chloe, remember we were talking about holidays? I’ve been looking at Cornwall again. Padstow looks lovely, lots of little coves. Cornwall! Seashells! Seashells! Can we build a castle? A  big  castle, Mummy? With a moat? Absolutely, Leo. A huge castle. We’ll need buckets and spades. It’s just... I’m a bit worried about the allergies again. Remember last time with the cream teas? Honestly, your face… All itchy! Itchy! Right. So, I’ve been researching allergy-friendly bakeries in Padstow. Apparently, there’s one called ‘The Gluten-Free Gull’ that’s supposed to be amazing. They even do dairy-free scones. Fancy that! Scones! Exactly! Now, Chloe, what do you think? Cornwall? Or should we stick to something a bit closer to home this year? I was thinking maybe a few days down on the South Coast…perhaps near Brighton. Adventure Island is always a winner. The kids adore it. Adventure Island! Rollercoaster! Rollercoaster! And candy floss! Yes, all the sugar you can handle, darling. Though perhaps not  too  much. Chloe? Brighton’s good. But Cornwall’s got that… that feel. That salty air. Remember that V&A exhibition we went to last year, the one focused on Cornish pottery? It really got me thinking about the history, you know? All those generations crafting beautiful things from the clay. Absolutely! You're right, it  was  amazing. I loved the stories behind the pieces. We could even combine it with a coastal walk. Get some proper fresh air. Mummy, can we see mermaids in Cornwall? Well, darling, mermaids are very shy. But we might be lucky and spot one! Or maybe just find some really beautiful sparkly shells that  look  like they belong to a mermaid. There are some lovely beaches near Newquay, I remember seeing pictures. Big waves too… if we're feeling brave. We’d have to keep a close eye on you two, wouldn't we?

…and then Mr. Davies actually  stopped  the lesson to tell me I was fidgeting too much! Fidgeting! Like, what's the point of sitting still for an hour when you're basically being force-fed quadratic equations? Seriously? Davies is always on about posture. My mum says he probably spent too long sitting in libraries as a kid. Makes him bitter. Bitter’s an understatement. It felt like a personal attack. Honestly, I was just trying to sharpen my pencil. It was blunt! And I needed it to, you know,  solve  the equations! It’s a vicious cycle. Tell me about it. History's been brutal this week. Mrs. Patel's gone full-on essay mode. Three essays already! And they're all like, five pages minimum. I'm drowning in primary source analysis. Five pages?! You're joking! I’m just trying to remember which Tudor queen married which king. It’s a horrifying mess of beheadings and alliances. It is, isn't it? I'm convinced they all had similar faces too. Blonde hair, pale skin… all just interchangeable queens. By the way, did you hear about Liam? Liam who? Liam from Year 11? The one who keeps trying to race me on his bike? Yeah, him. Apparently, he got detention for arguing with a prefect. Said he was “being unfairly targeted.” Typical Liam. Honestly, he brings it on himself. He’s like a magnet for prefects. Remember that time last term when he tried to convince Mrs. Harding that pigeons were plotting against the school? Oh my god, I’d completely forgotten! He was so serious! Said they were communicating in a secret code. She just gave him a really long lecture about respecting wildlife. She handled it well, actually. But Liam… he just stared blankly. Anyway, are you going to Sarah’s party on Saturday? Definitely! I've been looking forward to it all week. Apparently, they're playing that new superhero movie. The one with the guy who can control water? 'Hydro-Man'? Yeah, I saw the trailer! Looks pretty epic. My sister went last week. Said it was good, but a bit long. That’s fine by me. I’m happy to sit and be entertained for a few hours. I need a break from essay writing. Are you bringing anyone? I was thinking of asking Chloe. Chloe? Really? Isn’t she… allergic to, like, a million things?

Honestly, this road is a nightmare. It's like they deliberately designed it to be as winding and potholed as humanly possible. I’m having to concentrate so hard, I can't even think about the cricket. Aye, well, roads round 'ere nevver were known fer bein' smooth, were they? Least it’s not the A1, that’s a proper beast. Reminds me o’ that time I tried cycling on it…never again. Cycling on the A1?! Seriously? You’re brave, or perhaps utterly mad. I stick to the cycle paths, thank you very much. Speaking of which, have you seen the new bike lane they're putting in down by the river? It looks pretty decent. Nah, dinnae see it yet. Been busy wi' the corpus, you know how it is. Data niggle after data niggle. But a new bike lane sounds lovely! I’ve been meaning to get back on me bike, mind. It's been sat in the shed lookin’ sorry for itself. Used to love tearing around Ryton Pools on it, didn’t I? Fresh air, sunshine… a world away from spreadsheets. It sounds idyllic. I should get out more, myself. Too much time spent in front of a screen, designing bridges and the like. Though, a bit ironically, those bridges need to be built on these… charming roads. Did you catch the highlights of the England match yesterday? Williamson really came through. Briefly! Just saw bits and pieces on me phone during me lunch break. Thought he played a blinder. Reckon they've got a good chance this year, haven't they? Better than last year, definitely. Williamson's got that calm, steady sort of leadership about him. Always reassuring. More reassuring than that bloke we had last year, anyway. Don’t wanna mention him… bad memories. No, best not. He was… a challenging captain, to say the least. Williamson’s much more my style. Solid, dependable, not prone to dramatic outbursts. Like me with engineering - practical and thorough. Which is probably why I'm stuck navigating this… obstacle course. You're a good lad, Liam. Proper sensible. That's why yere mam likes you so much. Though, sometimes you need to let yer hair down a bit, y’know? Come to Sunderland next weekend, we'll go for a proper pub lunch and watch the football. I’ll even try and drag you onto the bowling green.

Seriously? They’re closed? It’s only 8:30! I was  really  craving Sweet and Sour Chicken. Yep. Just checked their website. "Closed for kitchen maintenance. Reopening tomorrow at 12pm.” Absolutely infuriating. I specifically wanted that spicy Kung Pao, too. Kitchen maintenance? At a Chinese restaurant? That’s a new one. Probably just a deep clean, or Brenda’s got the flu again. Remember last time? They were closed for three days because Brenda was convinced she had a dragon’s breath. Dragon's breath? What is that, a cough? Apparently, a particularly potent cough that involves lots of fire and brimstone, according to Brenda. She's a character. Anyway, what are we going to do? I’m starving. Right. Okay, plan B. There’s Golden Dragon down on Elm Street. It's not  as  good, but it’s open. Their General Tso’s is… adequate. Adequate? Adequate isn’t what I want when I’m ordering Chinese! I want vibrant, flavourful, a little bit oily… you know. Sweet and Sour Chicken. Specifics, Elodie, specifics! Okay, okay. But Golden Dragon  is  currently the only option. I’ve scoured all the apps. They deliver too, which is a bonus. Elm Street, huh? That’s a bit of a trek for the delivery driver, isn't it? Be prepared to tip generously. I’m suddenly feeling like noodles. Do they do decent Dan Dan noodles? I think so. I’ll check. Yes, they do. And they have proper Mapo Tofu! That's for you, Liv. Fine, Golden Dragon it is. But I’m officially adding "kitchen maintenance at my favourite Chinese restaurant" to my ever-growing list of life’s disappointments. It's right up there with rainy summer holidays and… burnt toast. Cheer up, Ben. At least we  have  options. Remember that time we were stranded in that tiny village in Scotland and the only food available was… haggis? Don’t remind me. That was a low point. I think I’m still traumatised. You were! You refused to eat anything for the rest of the day. So, should I order the Dan Dan noodles, then? Do you guys want anything to share? Spring rolls? Samosas? They seem to do a surprisingly good selection of sides. Samosas? That’s not really Chinese, is it? It's near enough, isn’t it? Just trying to broaden our horizons. Honestly, Ben, you're being so fussy tonight.

"Tell me about it, Karl. I hear you. It’s not just the sheer volume, is it? It's the complexity. People coming in with layers of need, social issues mixed with medical ones. It's a minefield." “Exactly! It’s a total restructure needed, isn’t it? They’re patching things up with plaster, but the foundations are crumbling. Back in my dad’s day, a visit to the doctor was a proper consultation, you know? Now? Fifteen minutes, shove you out the door. No time for nuance, no time to actually  listen .” "My sister, Brenda, she's a cleaner at the Royal. She says the atmosphere is awful. All stressed and snappy. Used to be camaraderie, she says, but now… it's every person for themselves. She says staff are leaving in droves. Wanting to move away from the area entirely." “Leaving the area? That’s dire. It’s a bleedin’ crisis, isn't it? Reminds me slightly of the post-war period, only without the blitz to explain the chaos. Though, admittedly, dealing with overstretched public services feels its own kind of… bombardment." "You know, I was reading this paper the other day, quite clever actually, on the impact of austerity on the NHS… fascinating stuff but simultaneously utterly depressing.” "Papers won’t fix it, Karl. It needs government intervention, serious cash. And a bit of common sense, to be honest. Speaking of needing help… have you noticed Mrs. Henderson next door? She’s been leaving her bins out for days again. Honestly, the smell is… potent, to put it mildly." “Mrs. Henderson, you say? Ah, yes. The one with the seventeen cats, if I recall correctly? I’ve tried to overlook it, you know. She’s a bit… eccentric. But the bins… you're right. It's not pleasant. My daughter, Anya, complained about it the other day. She was having a friend over." "Eccentric is one word for it. Rude is another. She gave me a right lip when I politely suggested she might want to take the bins in. Something about 'mindin' her own business.' I said, 'It  is  my business when it's stinkin' up the street, love!' " Margaret laughs, a hearty Liverpool laugh. "Ah, classic. You handled that brilliantly, Margaret. She's a tough nut to crack, that one. You know, living here in Liverpool 8, you get used to… colourful characters. Back in Germany, things were so... regulated.

"Aye, they do love to keep us on our toes, don't they, Arthur? The licensing folks. Bit relentless, aren’t they? Though I suppose they’ve got a job to do. Reminds me of the bureaucracy I have to deal with at the university. Paperwork, paperwork, paperwork. Nobody wants it, but there it is.” He paused, taking a sip of the weak tea Arthur offered. “You’d think with all the fancy AI they've got, they could automate that sort of thing, eh?” "AI? What’s that then? Sounds like somethin' the Russians cooked up. Used to be, you'd complain to the manager, sorted right out. Now, you’re fightin’ computers and letters. It’s a bleedin’ disgrace, that's what it is. Not like back in me day, when a fella could walk into a factory and get a job.” He sighed heavily. “Used to work at Dunlop. Good money, steady work. Now, what's a lad supposed to do?" “Times have changed, haven’t they? The textile industry, manufacturing... gone mostly. My own father, a German engineer originally, ended up working in a car factory just outside Liverpool. Hard graft, but it provided, you know? It's tough seeing people struggling, especially when it's through no fault of their own. I was marking essays the other day - some brilliant students, really bright kids, but facing a world with far fewer opportunities than we did.” “Opportunities! Don’t talk to me about opportunities. Look at ‘em, comin’ over here, takin’ our jobs….” He trailed off, muttering under his breath. “Now, Arthur, let’s be careful with that kind of talk. Immigration's a complex issue. It’s changed the city, certainly, but in many ways, it’s enriched it. Brought new life, new businesses. And not all of those people are ‘taking’ jobs. Many are creatin’ them. My students come from all over the world – Ukraine, Nigeria, China. They’re here to study, to contribute.” "Contribute? They get handouts, that's what they do. Welfare, the lot. While folks like me, who’ve struggled all their lives, get a pittance. Do you know what they sent me last week? A letter telling me my heating allowance's being cut! Cut! In this weather! They should be helpin’ the old, not squanderin’ it on… well, never mind." He waved a dismissive hand. "It  is  frustrating, isn’t it?

Honestly, I still can’t quite believe how quickly this project spiralled. We started with a relatively simple analysis of learner corpora feedback and now we're building a whole AI-powered diagnostic tool. Aye, tell me about it. I've been drowning in transcript requests, trying to keep up with the demand for specific language features. It’s like everyone suddenly wants to know about the nuances of prepositions. Who knew? It’s fascinating, though, isn’t it? Seeing the data actually visualise the struggles learners face. My work on identifying consistent error patterns is yielding some really insightful results. Did you see the initial report on the overuse of ‘make’ and ‘do’ by Spanish speakers, Sarah? Absolutely. It's sobering, actually. Reminds you how much we take language for granted. I've been focusing on the semantic shifts in learner language, particularly with idioms. It's a proper rabbit hole! Rabbit hole’s right! I’m dealing with commissioning content for the new series – trying to find authors who can explain this stuff in a way that’s engaging and doesn’t sound like a linguistics lecture. It’s harder than you think, making grammar engaging. Tell me about it. American students seem to particularly struggle with the perceived dryness of ELT materials. It’s a constant battle to find a balance between accuracy and appeal. My American upbringing probably helps, but even I have to be mindful of cultural references. It’s just… relentless, isn’t it? Feels like we're all battling the same tide of data and deadlines. Especially with the push for more personalised learning. How  do  you tailor materials to individual learner needs when you’re dealing with thousands? That's where the diagnostic tool comes in, hopefully. If we can accurately identify their pain points, we can recommend targeted resources. It’s ambitious, I know. Though, accuracy is the key, isn't it? I worry about over-reliance on AI. We need to remember the human element – the intuition, the understanding of context. An algorithm can spot a pattern, but it can't explain  why  a learner might consistently use 'say' instead of 'tell'. Definitely. That’s what I'm trying to convey to the authors. You can't just throw a list of rules at someone. It needs to be explained with engaging examples, stories, something that resonates. I had one suggest explaining the difference between ‘say’ and ‘tell’ purely through a flowchart.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of content on TikTok is overwhelming. I mean, I get why people are hooked, it’s designed to be, but wading through endless dance trends and lip-syncing just to find something genuinely interesting? It feels exhausting. Aye, I know what you mean, don’t I. It’s a bit like trying to find a decent pasty in a Cornish holiday resort - buried under a mountain of tourist tat. It’s got its moments, mind, but it’s mostly nonsense. I’ve been trying to get me niece, Maisie, into a bit of proper telly, you know? Something with a bit of substance. Maisie's still a kid, isn't she? What’s she into? Oh, she's fourteen now, nearly fifteen. Used to be obsessed with those teen dramas, typical thing. Now she's got a bit cynical, you know? Says everything’s been done before. Hard to impress these young ‘uns! I was trying to steer her towards  Slow Horses  on Apple TV. Thought she'd appreciate the dry humour.  Slow Horses  is brilliant! Gary Oldman is phenomenal. You should definitely push that one. It's got that proper British bleakness, doesn’t it? Very different from the American stuff, all sunny and perfect. Speaking of different cultures, I was reading an article the other day about the influence of Korean dramas on global storytelling. Apparently, they’re completely reshaping the formula. Really? Korean dramas, eh? I’ve heard a bit about 'em, mostly from Mrs. Finch down the village. She’s gone absolutely mad for them, all subtitles and whatnot. Says they're far more complex than anything we produce. She’s not wrong. The emotional depth, the intricate plotting… It’s fascinating. It makes you think about how much our culture – British culture, Western culture in general – shies away from raw emotion on screen. It’s all subtle glances and witty banter. That's fair, innit? We're a reserved bunch, us Brits. Don't want to make a fuss. I’m trying to encourage my students to be a bit more expressive in their essays, you know? They’re terrified of showing any kind of passion. I tell 'em, "Just let it flow! Don’t be afraid to sound a little… emotional!" They look at me like I’ve grown a second head. I can imagine! Teaching can be brutal sometimes.

Oh, aye, I bet! Poor Liam, trying to impart wisdom on that one. Gran doesn't need quadratic equations, pet, she needs a nice cup o’ tea and a sit down. He's a good lad, though, wanting to help. It wasn't going well, alright? She kept asking about it being something to do with sheep farming. Apparently, roots in maths are like growing crops. It was…confusing. Sheep farming! That's a good one, that is. Remember when your dad tried to explain fractions to me using slices of cake, love? I thought he was just being generous! Aye, a generous man, your dad. Always sharing the cake. We used to get some good slices. Remember that Victoria sponge he made for the church fête, Hilda? Won first prize, it did. It did, didn't it? Though I think Mrs. Higgins’ scones may have bribed the judges. Honestly, Malton’s always been full of a few sneaky ones. Right, now, about the heating. Arthur, are you warm enough? Aye, love, I’m alright. It's a bit much, actually. Turning it right up like that. Burns a hole in your pocket, that does. We turned it down a bit, Gran and Grandad. It's on about medium now. Liam checked the thermostat - he's got a knack for that sort of thing, you know. Probably all that maths he's studying. Thermostats! Fancy things. Back in my day, you just opened a window or put on another layer. Simple as that. We didn’t need all this technology. Less fuss, too. Aye, times change, don’t they? Speaking of fuss, has anyone sorted out the tea and biscuits? I thought I’d made some of those ginger snaps you like, Grandad. Ginger snaps? Oh, that’d be lovely, Hilda. Lovely. Put a bit of extra cream on mine, mind. Don't you start, Arthur! You'll be wanting a whole tin! I can get the tea, Auntie. And I think I saw some shortbread in the cupboard. Is that alright, Gran? Perfect, pet. Whilst you’re doing that, I'll see if I can find those old photos of you two when you were young. We haven’t looked at them in ages, have we? Remember that holiday in Scarborough, Arthur? You insisted on wearing that ridiculous striped jumper. It was fashionable! Everyone was wearing striped jumpers in '62!

Honestly, look at this one. Remember that disastrous attempt at karaoke in Chengdu? You were  convinced  you could nail Whitney Houston. Oh, don't remind me! It's a miracle anyone still speaks to me after that. Though, I maintain, I was perfectly in tune. It was the microphone's fault! Terrible acoustics. The acoustics were fine. You were… enthusiastic. And slightly off-key. But that’s what made it brilliant, wasn’t it? Look at poor Mei’s face in the background. She’s practically cringing. She’s such a sweetheart. She’s been asking about us constantly. I promised her we'd send more photos. These are mainly for reminiscing, aren’t they? A bit of a nostalgia trip. Definitely. Being here feels… surreal sometimes. Like we're living in a film. Especially now, after all this time. It doesn’t feel like ten years since we first came out here. No, it really doesn’t. Remember how overwhelmed we were then? All the language barriers, the food... I think I spent the first week living exclusively on apples. I was convinced every other fruit was poisonous. You were a sight. And the scooters! You nearly had a nervous breakdown trying to navigate those. I still can’t believe you managed to rent that motorbike. Necessity breeds bravery, darling. Besides, I wanted to explore the countryside. And I did! Though I may have ended up in a rice paddy more than once. Speaking of exploring, are we still thinking about that trip to Yunnan next spring? Absolutely. I was just looking at some articles about it last night. The Stone Forest is supposed to be incredible. And the tea plantations – imagine the smells! We could even do a photography workshop. You’d love that. Oh, I would! It would be so nice to focus on something creative again. Lecturing is demanding, you know? It's satisfying, of course, seeing the students progress, but it leaves little mental space for anything else. Tell me about it. Marking essays about the complexities of post-colonial literature... it drains the soul sometimes. Do you think Eleanor and Mark are settling in alright in Edinburgh? I haven’t heard from them in ages. I spoke to Eleanor last week. They're doing well, all things considered. Mark's missing the Sichuan food terribly, unsurprisingly. Eleanor says the weather is a bit of a shock to the system - very grey!

Honestly, last night was… a lot. Like, a  lot  a lot. My head is still throbbing. Tell me about it! I think I aged five years. Remember Liam trying to do that ridiculous dance move? The one he saw on TikTok? Don't remind me! I swear, the whole pub went silent. Poor bloke. He seemed so confident beforehand. Did you see Chloe filming it? She’ll be posting it online before lunchtime, guaranteed. Definitely. She's obsessed with her Insta stories. You know, Mum keeps going on about how I need to be more ‘present’ and less glued to my phone. As if  she  doesn't spend half her day on Facebook looking at recipes. Mums, right? Always the experts on everything. Mine’s been lecturing me about my ‘lack of hobbies’ again. Apparently, going out Saturday and Sunday isn’t a hobby. It’s a ‘waste of potential’. Potential for what, exactly? Becoming a nun? My nan's the same! Always asking about boyfriends and future husbands. Like that's all that matters. Speaking of which, did you hear anything back from, what's his name…Josh? The one you were chatting up at the football match? Oh, erm… not really. He said he’d text me, but… crickets. I'm probably reading too much into it. It was just a bit of friendly banter, innit? I mean, he did seem pretty keen. Well, don’t beat yourself up about it. There are plenty of fish in the sea, or, you know, plenty of lads at Uni. Don’t let one rejection ruin your entire week. More sausage roll? Thanks. I need the carbs. Need to fuel up for that History essay due on Friday. I’m dreading it. Professor Davies is brutal. Oh, I know! I overheard him grilling poor Ben about the Tudors last week. Honestly, he's terrifying. I’m sticking to Psychology. At least Freud’s theories are interesting. And much less likely to involve memorising dates. True. Speaking of interesting, did you see that video of that golden retriever rescuing a cat from a tree? It was all over Twitter. Made my day, honestly. Give me animals over people sometimes. I'm thinking of getting a hamster. Oh my god, don't! Remember what happened with Auntie Sheila's hamster? It chewed through  everything . Her sofa, her wallpaper… even her dentures! Seriously? Okay, maybe not a hamster then.

Right, so Nana’s definitely coming next Saturday, then? I've booked the table at The Heron Inn, you know she likes it there. Gets a decent view of the river. Aye, Saturday's good. Sorted my bits and bobs for her. Got her favourite lemon drops, too. Hope she’s feeling alright, mind. Last time I spoke, she seemed a bit… withdrawn. Oh, she's fine, dear. Just getting on, isn’t she? It's lovely to have her visit. It’s been too long since we’ve all been together. This peas and chips is just perfect, isn’t it? Comfort food. Absolutely. She’ll love it. I cleared a space for her in the living room so she doesn't have to squeeze in. Though, knowing Nana, she’ll probably end up commandeering the armchair with the best blanket. She always does. Stubborn as an ox, that one. Remember when she insisted on driving all the way from Sheffield, despite me begging her to let me pick her up? Oh, goodness, yes! And the state of her car! I swear, I needed therapy after cleaning it. But you can’t deny she’s got a good head on her shoulders, even now. She gave me some truly brilliant mathematical insights when I was a child. Sharper than most of my students, I can tell you! That's a scary thought! So, everything’s in hand then? Transport, food, Nana-proofing the house? I just want to make sure she has a really good time. It’s been a tough year for her, with Uncle George… Aye, a tough one indeed. We need to be sensitive. Don’t want to bring up too many memories. Though, she does like reminiscing, doesn’t she? Brings out a whole load of stories. She does. And some of them are wonderful. Remember the one about her and Granddad trying to build a shed in the garden and it ended up collapsing halfway through? Oh, yes! Covered in sawdust and laughing their heads off. Nana swore it was Granddad’s fault, and he blamed the wonky foundations. Classic. It’s just… sometimes I wonder, with all this reminiscing, if we're avoiding the difficult bits. Like, George's issues… Were there things we could have done differently? Oh, Thomas. Don’t go down that road again. We’ve been over this a thousand times.

Honestly, Dad, you nearly gave me a heart attack! I swear, you were wielding that mug like a medieval weapon. Now, now, Ellie, don't exaggerate. It was a clumsy movement, that’s all. I was just reaching for a digestive and…well, accidents happen. Besides, you’ve got insurance, haven’t you? You could have aimed slightly better, Mr. Davies. It’s a miracle it didn’t shatter completely. At least it’s just a crack, right? And Ellie’s right, insurance should cover it. Though dealing with that is its own special kind of nightmare. Don’t you worry, dear. It’s easily fixed. I know a chap, Brian from down the road, he fixes everything. He even tried to fix my washing machine once – didn't quite work, but he tried! It’s a shame though, that laptop. Lovely thing. You’ve been using it for your studies, haven’t you Ellie? Yes, Mum. It’s a disaster. I have an essay due next week! But yeah, Brian, that’s a thought. Though I need something more immediate. Maybe a cup of tea will calm me down. This is really nice, Liam. Thanks. Glad you like it. I was dithering about what water to use. Fiji? Icelandic? Tap? It's a surprisingly existential dilemma. Tap water’s perfectly fine, lad. Waste of money buying all that fancy bottled stuff. They all taste the same anyway. Remember when they used to have those Crystal springs ads? All that mountain spring nonsense. I always thought the French water tasted nicest. Badoit, that was the one.
