But it’s extortionate, isn't it? We've been moaning about the bin strikes, imagine paying that much just for water! Speaking of which, I need to remember to get some more rubbish bags. The last collection was chaos. Tell me about it! I’m trying to get my head around this old Blackberry my gran gave me. She said it was a "useful tool." It’s practically a museum piece! She's trying to show me how to set it up. Blackberry? Wow, that's taking things back a few years. Have you tried voice recognition software? It's pretty useful, though sometimes it gets the words completely wrong. I was trying to dictate an email the other day and it wrote "a purple rhinoceros" instead of "a crucial rehearsing"— a baffling outcome!

Right then, let’s see… Man City lost! Can you believe it? 2-1 to Wolves. Absolute shambles. Honestly, I wasn't expecting much. They haven't been on top form lately, have they? Though, a loss like that… it’s a bit of a downer, isn’t it? Especially being so far away. It is, isn't it? Makes you miss the proper atmosphere, the pub, everyone shouting at the telly. Makes you miss home, I guess. I'm starting to feel a bit…blah, actually. I think SAD might be creeping in. The grey skies here are doing nothing for my mood. Oh, darling, I know  exactly  what you mean. It’s been hitting me hard this year. Poland is beautiful, don't get me wrong, but the winter light... it’s just so relentless. I've been trying to get out for walks, but even that's difficult when it’s tipping down. I saw a woman the other day with a vibrant yellow umbrella - it was the cheeriest thing I’d seen all week. A yellow umbrella! That  is  cheering. I need one of those. I’ve got a black one, practically camouflaged against the sky. Anyway, about home… I got a message from Auntie Maureen this morning. She's asking if I’m coming for Christmas. Says the dogs miss me. Oh, bless her. The dogs  do  miss you. Barnaby, especially. He'd practically chew through the wifi to get a video call. And Maureen, of course, always worries. She does. It’s sweet, but also a bit… suffocating, sometimes. Speaking of worrying though, I'm stressing about Anya's exam results. She’s a bright student, really, but she gets so nervous. I've been working my socks off with her and the others. Practicing speaking, reviewing grammar… it’s intense. Being a teacher is a huge responsibility, isn’t it? You’re shaping these young people’s futures. I remember when I was teaching…well, let’s not go there. Before…you know. It was lovely, but so tiring. Have you considered getting them to do some practice exams? Honestly, simulating the pressure can sometimes make a real difference. I've got them scheduled for next week. I'm trying to keep it low-key, but it’s hard to mask my own anxiety, I think. It's funny, actually. My uncle, he’s started working on a farm just outside Bury.

Aye, right enough! Conference catering, eh? Always a gamble, isn't it? You'd think, for the prices they charge, they could at least get the timings right. Was it a big conference then? It was. International marketing thing. Loads of suits, lots of jargon. Honestly, I felt a bit…out of my depth, to be fair. Just shifting plates and making sure people had champagne. Not exactly rocket science. Sounds stressful, though. Production Controller is stressful enough without having to manage a rogue catering company on top. Did you at least get a decent tip? Don’t reckon he got opportunity for tips, does he, lads? He was runnin' around like a headless chicken! Me own Mam would've had words with them lot, she would. So, Cambridge, eh? Still livin' with yer folks? Yeah, still at home. Not exactly rollin' in it, you know? Pay's alright, but rent prices 'round here are mental. What about you, Chloe? Still in that little flat near the station? Aye, still there. It’s snug, mind. Just about big enough for me and Scruffy. . Right, are you two hungry? I’m thinking pasta bake tonight. I found some proper mature cheddar at the market today, you won’t believe it. Smells amazing, Chloe! Seriously, you’re the best cook. I’m starving. So, Liam, you were saying something about feeling out of your depth? What kind of marketing were they pushing? Just… all the usual stuff. Brand awareness, target demographics, engagement strategies… it was just a wall of buzzwords. I’m good with my hands, you know? I'm building this shed at home for my dad. Feels more productive than fluffing up marketing speak. Aye, practical skills are gold, lad. Can't eat buzzwords, can you? Speaking of practical things… I need to grab a new coat. This one’s seen better days. You wouldn't believe how many times I've had to wear it in the rain. You should check out that vintage shop on Mill Road. They have some incredible stuff - really unique pieces. You’d find something perfect for your style. Oh aye? I'll 'ave a look. I’m lookin’ for somethin’ warm, though. Something I can chuck on when it's blowin' a gale up North. Right, pasta's nearly ready. Anyone got any stories to tell while we eat? Anything interesting happenin' in your loves lives, eh?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of people cramming into that tiny teahouse was ridiculous. It was like Piccadilly Circus on a Sunday afternoon! You wouldn’t believe the queue just for a pot of jasmine. Sounds about right, doesn't it? China, eh? You've been having a grand time, I’d wager. Though, all that hustle and bustle... not really my cup of tea, is it? Give me a quiet afternoon in Devon any day. Somewhere you can actually  hear  the birds. Well, there’s beauty there too, you know. I was lucky enough to get out of the cities a bit. Sichuan province, especially. The landscape is breathtaking. Towering mountains, lush bamboo forests... it's a completely different world. And the wildlife! You wouldn't believe the bears they have in some of the reserves. Absolutely massive. Bears, you say? Proper grizzlies? Reminds me of that documentary we watched about the pandas at Chengdu Zoo. Amazing creatures, pandas. So much bigger than they look in the pictures. I wonder if they ever miss the bamboo forests, you know, being in captivity. They probably do. Although, this reserve I visited had been set up to recreate their natural habitat as closely as possible. And the local guides - brilliant. They were practically encyclopedias of Chinese wildlife. Speaking of guides, I had a Chinese student, Li Wei, on my TEFL course - such a bright spark. She's trying to get a posting in Tibet, amazing ambition. Tibet... now that's a place to see. Always wanted to go, but the logistics… and, well, other things, don’t they? My supervisor, Professor Davies, he’s always going on about the political landscape out there. Makes PhD supervision feel like a picnic sometimes. Davies! Still a stickler for perfect footnotes, I presume? He gave me a right telling off last year for a slightly ambiguous phrasing in a research paper. Anyway, moving on from academics... did you see that lad over there? Just caught a pigeon. Bless him. Typical. Reminds me of my nephew, Tom. Always trying to be a little ornithologist. He’s obsessed with West Ham United at the moment, too. Can't get away from football, can you? No, you can't. Keeps you grounded. Thinking about it, though, his father's got a horrific driving style when we're down in the Isle of Wight. Always honking at people on those country roads.

Right, so we’re still… fifteen minutes out? Honestly, this routing is a nightmare. I swear, every time I let the sat nav decide, it wants to take me through fields and single-track lanes. Aye, well, ya can’t expect it to know the proper shortcuts. You’re used to fancy consultancy routes, aren’t ya? Me mum always said there’s a right way and a quick way, and the quick way’s usually the best. That's... surprisingly practical wisdom from your mum. But I need to be on time, Elara. This meeting with Henderson & Sons is pretty critical. They're considering the entire structural design for the new stadium. It's a massive contract. I ken. You were stressin’ about it all last week. Henderson & Sons, fancy name. Sounds proper posh. Are they like,  really  posh? 'Cos I’m worrited about the dress code. Posh? They’re wealthy, yes. But not ridiculously so. Smart, definitely. They'll want to see competence, not couture. Just... avoid anything too casual. No trainers. And maybe leave the floral scarf at home? It’s lovely, but… It’s me favourite! Me Gran knitted this for me. It keeps me neck warm, ya know. I know, and it suits you perfectly. Just… perhaps save it for the weekend. There's a navy blazer in the boot, remember? I packed it. Oh aye. The navy blazer. Makes me feel like I’m goin’ to a funeral. Don’t be dramatic. It’s a smart blazer. It shows you’re taking this seriously. And seriously is what they want to see, Elara. This could really boost my career. Think about it - the main structure of a brand new stadium! Aye, I’m thinkin' about it. I'm proud of ya, Liam. Really. All that hard work payin' off. You deserve it. Still, a posh meeting… sounds a bit stiflin’. It's not stifling. It's professional. Look, can we just focus on getting you comfortable? Are you alright? You seem a bit quiet. You didn't mention being nervous. I'm just… thinking about me dad, that’s all. He'd have loved to see you with a project like this. He always said you were clever, Liam. Proper clever. I know. He was so proud of you too, Elara. He used to brag about your degree, your intellect... He was incredibly impressed you were working with language corpora.

Honestly, this flu has knocked me for six. I feel like I’ve been run over by a particularly grumpy bus. Aye, tell me about it! My mam's got it bad. Poor lass, she’s been stuck in bed for a week, barely able to lift a teacup. I brought her some Yorkshire pudding the other day – a bit of cheering up, y’know? Didn't touch it, though. Said she couldn’t even  smell  gravy. Rough. My nan caught something similar last year. She spent a fortnight like a zombie. Feel sorry for your mam, though. Yorkshire pudding and no gravy? That's a tragedy. It is! It sounds awful. I’m just trying to power through. This production schedule at work is a nightmare as it is, and now I'm feeling like this. I had to delegate half my tasks to Liam today. He’s alright, but he won’t pick up on the nuances the way I do. Aye, work’s always a faff when you’re poorly. Is Liam a nice lad? He’s… fine. He’s been asking me out, actually. Oh? And? And I said no, obviously! I mean, I can barely remember my own name, let alone deal with a romantic entanglement. But he's persistent. Keeps bringing me coffee and asking if I'm "feeling a bit better yet." Like, yes, Liam, I appreciate the caffeine, but I’m currently operating at 20% brainpower. Persistent lads, eh? They’re a pest! My ex was like that. Always bringing me roses, even when I’d straight-up told him I weren’t interested. Daft as a brush, he was. What were you two arguing about again, love? That's not the point! The point is, I’m ill, I’m swamped at work, and now I have to politely fend off a colleague’s advances. It’s a bit much, isn't it? It sounds like it. Look, if he becomes too much, just be direct. Don’t beat around the bush. A firm "no" is usually pretty effective. Aye, that’s right. Be bold, pet! Don't let him wear you down. Remember what I always say – a Yorkshire lass doesn't take kindly to a bit of mither! Thanks, both. You're right. It's just… tiring. Speaking of tires, I'm exhausted. This conversation, despite being lovely company, is really draining me.

Honestly, Liam from admissions is just… unbearable today. Absolute meltdown over a missing form. A  single  form. Like the entire healthcare system is crumbling because of it. Liam, eh? Sounds about right. Remember that time he got in a right state because someone put the stapler in the wrong drawer? Don't remind me! It was biblical. Honestly, I feel like I spend half my day diffusing his anxiety. And then he blames  me  when things go wrong. He actually said, "Are you sure you checked thoroughly, Chloe?" like it was my fault a piece of paper went missing! People like that just thrive on drama, don't they? It's like a little power trip for them. Is Sarah still off sick? Yeah, still. Poor thing. Apparently, the stress from her last assessment got to her. Burnout, proper burnout. It just underlines how much pressure we're all under, doesn't it? Head of Nursing is suggesting mandatory mindfulness sessions. Mindfulness? Seriously? Sounds a bit… patronising, doesn’t it? Like, "Just breathe, you're saving lives!" Exactly! Like it’s going to magically solve overcrowded wards and understaffing. Though, honestly, five minutes of quiet  would  be a miracle. What about you? How’s the Johnson project going? Still battling Brenda and her spreadsheets? Don't even get me started on Brenda. She’s added three more metrics to the weekly report. Three! I spent all morning wrestling with pivot tables. And then Mark from marketing had the audacity to ask if I could “just pop over” to help him with his presentation. As if I have nothing else on my plate. Oh, the entitlement. Classic Mark. You should have told him to look up "delegation" in the dictionary. I wanted to! I really did. But I just bit my tongue. It’s exhausting, battling with people all the time. Makes me miss… you know. Ben? Yeah. Stupid Ben. Sometimes I think it would have been easier to just stay with him. Less stressful, definitely. Don't do that to yourself, Liv. You're better off without him. Remember how much he used to belittle your career? He didn’t get you, did he? You were always striving, wanting to achieve… he just wanted you to fold laundry and watch reality TV. I know, I know. Intellectually, I know I made the right decision. But emotionally… there are days. Like today, when I’m buried under spreadsheets and Brenda’s tyranny, and I just crave the easy comfort of familiarity.

…and that’s why the Green Man isn't  necessarily  evil, Leo. He’s more…wild. A force of nature. He represents the power of the forest, the changing seasons. He’s not good, not bad, just… is . But Miss Honeybun said the Grims were  always  bad! They stole children and lived in dark caves! Did they have treasure, though? Like pirates? Well, darling, Miss Honeybun is telling a lovely story, a cautionary tale. But stories, like the Green Man, often have layers. The Grims  could  be seen as bad, yes. Hoarding, stealing...not very nice. But maybe they were just scared, desperate even, and hoarding things made them feel safer. Think about squirrels burying nuts for the winter – are they  bad  squirrels? No, they’re just…getting ready. Exactly! Sometimes, what looks like ‘bad’ is just survival. It’s all about perspective, isn’t it? Now, who wants to help me set the table? I’m making shepherd's pie, although I suspect it won't be quite as exciting as battling a Grim. Pirate treasure would be better than shepherd's pie! No treasure tonight, I'm afraid. Although, I  did  find a particularly shiny button in the sewing box earlier. Does that count as treasure? Can I have it? For my story? I’m writing about a princess who lost her button, and it was magical! Of course, love. It’s all yours. So, plates and cutlery? Leo, you put out the napkins. Maisie, can you grab the gravy boat from the cupboard? It's on the top shelf, be careful! I’m a pirate! Pirates climb! Steady on, Captain! Safety first. That gravy boat is heavy. Perhaps I can help. See? Sometimes, even pirates need a little help. That's not bad, is it? No! Helping is good! Miss Honeybun said helping is a kind thing to do. That's right. Now, tell me, what would happen if the Green Man and one of the Grims met? Do you think they'd fight? Or…maybe they’d find something they had in common? Maybe they both like collecting shiny things! The Grim collected gold, and the Green Man could collect dewdrops! That's a brilliant idea, Leo! See? Even two creatures perceived as opposites can have a connection. It’s all about finding the good, or at least the understanding, in everything. But what about…ghosts? Are ghosts good or bad?

"Embarrassing! Like when I tripped over Tippy?" "Exactly like that, love. Luckily, the camera wasn't rolling  that  time. So, Anon, what was the scene about, anyway? Your school's filming a documentary, right?" "It’s about the school's environmental initiatives, isn’t it, darling? They’re highlighting the wildlife garden and the recycling program." "And the bees!" "Right you are, sweetie. And Anon’s playing the lead researcher!" He looks at Anon proudly. "Big responsibility, that." "She was brilliant in rehearsals. Although she did complain about having to pretend to be fascinated by compost." "Well, compost  is  a bit... smelly, innit? Is your leg still bothering you, love? You were limping a bit earlier." Anon: "Yeah, it’s a bit sore. I think I twisted it during the filming. We were running across the field to get a shot of the sunrise, and I tripped on a root." "Oh, you poor thing. Don’t push yourself, darling. Maybe a little ice and a rest is all you need. Did you take any painkillers?" Anon: "Mum gave me some, but they haven't really done much." "Right, well, don't go running any marathons for them then. It's warm enough to sleep with just the sheets tonight, isn’t it? I was freezing last night." "It was! I had to put a blanket back on. I think we’re finally getting some proper summer weather, after all that rain." "Definitely. Makes going to the gym a little more appealing, doesn't it? I’m thinking of hitting the treadmill later. Need to try and burn off some of these doughnuts I’ve been scoffing." "You and your doughnuts! Honestly, you'd think you were training for an Olympic eating competition. Why not just go for a run outside? It's lovely out there.” "I know, I know, you’re right. But the treadmill’s a bit more… reliable. Less chance of getting rained on. And less chance of tripping over roots like someone else did!" He glances playfully at Anon. Anon: "Hey! It wasn’t my fault there was a root there!" “It  was  unfortunate timing, though. Maybe you should be careful when pretending to be a dedicated environmental researcher. Hazards lurk everywhere, apparently.” "Like Tippy!" "Exactly! Speaking of which, where’s Finn?" "He’s building a fort out of cushions in the living room. He's declared it 'Fort Awesome'."

…and honestly, David, the waiting list at the surgery is just getting ridiculous. Three weeks to see Dr. Sharma? It's appalling. I had to practically beg for an appointment because of this persistent cough. Three weeks? Luxury, Arthur! Try getting through to them on the phone. Takes me a good half an hour just to get a recorded message telling me to call back later. It’s a right shambles, the NHS. Always has been, if I’m honest, but it’s got markedly worse lately. You know, I was reading an article in the paper this morning - about the Green Party’s proposals for the NHS. They're suggesting a significant expansion of community health centres, more focus on preventative care… Oh, the Green Party, are they? Good intentions, Arthur, always good intentions. But they haven't got a clue about running a business, let alone a country. Where's the money going to come from? Fairy dust? Well, they’re suggesting a wealth tax, tighter regulations on corporations… It’s about priorities, David. We’re spending vast sums on things we don’t really need, while essential services are crumbling. Priorities, eh? My priority is keeping ‘Brunswick Antiques’ afloat, Arthur. That's a tricky business these days, you know. Especially with that online auction site… it’s eaten into my profits something fierce. Had to let young Liam go last month, bless him. Good lad, Liam. Couldn't afford to keep him. I’m so sorry to hear that, David. The job market is brutal. My niece, Emily, has been struggling to find anything permanent since she graduated. Just a string of temporary contracts. It's disheartening for young people. It is, isn't it? Used to be, a degree guaranteed you something. Now… well, it seems to guarantee you a pile of debt and a lot of disappointment. Speaking of disappointing, did you hear about Margaret and Gerald splitting up? Margaret and Gerald? Good heavens! No, I hadn't. After all these years? What on earth happened? Apparently, something about him spending too much time at boot sales. Margaret says he’s become obsessed with finding vintage bird feeders. Utter nonsense, apparently. She said he was neglecting her completely. They had a proper shouting match at the church fete last Sunday. I heard it from Doris down the road. Goodness. Vintage bird feeders! You wouldn’t think that would be a cause for marital discord.

…and that’s why I’m leaning towards focusing on the mycorrhizal networks in urban woodlands. It seems, on the surface, less immediately groundbreaking than, say, synthetic biology, but the potential for climate change resilience… it’s proper exciting, isn’t it? Aye, sounds dead good, that does. Though, I’m still struggling to get me head round the sheer volume of data you're predicting. Are you sure your algorithm’s going to cope? Remember that crashing incident with the algae project? Let’s not speak of the algae incident. That was a dark week. The algorithm's been revamped, honestly. Triple-redundant now, and I've had Professor Davies look over it. He practically declared it 'fit for purpose'. You know how dramatic he gets. Aye, he is. Right drama queen. Still, good to have his seal of approval. Fancy a pasty? I saw a place just down the street advertising proper Cornish ones. None of that Birmingham muck, neither. "Birmingham muck"? Now, now, Gemma. Some of us are proud of our savoury delights. My nan’s meat and potato pasty recipe is legendary. Though, I  will  admit, the Cornish ones are something special. Alright, pasty sounds brilliant. Suddenly feeling a bit peckish. See? I knew I’d win you over. Speaking of things I’m peckish for, have you seen those new wide-leg trousers everyone's wearing? I keep seeing them on Instagram, and I’m tempted to give them a go. The palazzo pants? Yeah, they're everywhere. A bit… much, aren't they? I think they swallow you whole. Though, you’d probably pull them off. You’ve always had a good eye for fashion. Remember that vintage scarf you scored in Whitby? Oh, shut up! It was a bargain! It’s cashmere, you know. Anyway, I was thinking I could pair them with a nice fitted jumper. Something in forest green, perhaps? Match the plants you're obsessed with. Very sensible. And definitely more your style than, say, a neon pink sequin jumpsuit. Speaking of sensible, have you been keeping an eye on the interest rates? It feels like things are getting tighter. My student loan repayments are already a killer. Tell me about it. I'm trying to build up a down payment for a flat, but it’s ridiculously expensive, even here in Cambridge. I’m thinking of looking into a shared ownership scheme.

"Honestly, your mum still has  everything . Remember that ceramic owl? The one with the wonky eyes? It’s still here." “Of course it is. Mum believes in sentimental value, even when it's questionable. At least she’s making us tea. Though I'm pretty certain the biscuits are the same ones she’s served since 1987.” "A classic. So, you were saying about the student essay? The one on representation in contemporary art?" "Yes! It was… something else. On the whole, the standard was decent, but one student, bless him, genuinely believed Banksy was a collective of trained squirrels." "Trained squirrels? Seriously? That’s… wonderfully optimistic, I suppose. Did he justify it?" "He attempted to. He argued that the squirrels' innate dexterity and camouflage abilities aligned perfectly with Banksy’s guerrilla tactics. He even cited a vague article about squirrel intelligence he found on a conspiracy website." "Good grief. You can’t make this stuff up. At least it’s memorable. Did you mark him down heavily?" “Relatively. I gave him a few marks for originality, and for bravery, frankly. Trying to argue Banksy is a squirrel army takes a certain kind of commitment. It’s just… the scholarship was, shall we say, lacking.” "Speaking of commitment, did you catch that documentary on killer whales the other night? Absolutely incredible. The way they teach their young hunting techniques… it’s a generational knowledge base. Fascinating." "I did! That echolocation stuff is mind-blowing. Though, to be honest, I switched off halfway through. All that talk of dwindling populations and plastic pollution just got a bit depressing. I need something lighter to switch my brain off with." "Like what? More extreme home makeover?" “Don’t be ridiculous. I was thinking something with… ridiculous violence. Purely frivolous, you understand. I started watching that Danish crime drama last week.  Borgen  it wasn’t, but the fight scenes are wonderfully over the top.” “So, you find solace in expertly choreographed brutality?” “It’s a release! After grading essays about the nuances of artistic expression, sometimes you just need to see someone get punched in the face.” "Though, mum would probably faint if she knew I said that." "She'd lecture you about the desensitization of society. It’s a classic mum maneuver." He pauses. “Did you ever manage to find your Blue Peter badge collection? You were talking about it the other day.” "No, still no luck.

That’s a right funny picture, isn't it, Arthur? You look like you're wrestling a badger! Where did we get that from? Oh, that! That was from the hostel, love. Back in '87, I reckon. We had a group of German students, real lively bunch. One of 'em, Klaus, brought his ferret. Tried to sneak it in, he did. Chaos, it was. Ended up with you trying to pry it off my trouser leg! A ferret? In a hostel? You were running a proper establishment then, weren't you? I pictured more of a… a shared dorm situation, not dealing with escaped wildlife. It was a bit of a free-for-all, wasn’t it, dear? Trying to keep order with twenty young people from all over the world. You were good at it though, Arthur. You had a way of just… calming everyone down. Just got used to it, didn’t I? Years of it. Reminds me of my dad’s shop, actually. Constant stream of people, needing something, wanting something. Keeping things ticking over. Hard work, that was. Proper hard work, mind you. Not like some of the youngsters today. My parents worked incredibly hard too. Mum had a little bakery, and Dad ran a hardware store. Long hours, six days a week. It gave me a good work ethic, I suppose. Did your parents have a shop, Arthur? Aye, a greengrocer’s. Costessey market it was. Lovely spot, it was. Good folk. But a tough life. Always the worry about the weather, the price of potatoes... People thinking they're getting a bargain. Always trying to haggle! And the birds! They’d get right in and peck at the fruit, cheeky buggers. Oh, I remember those birds. You used to get so cross, Arthur. Had to protect the livelihood, didn't I? It wasn’t all sunshine and roses, you know. Remember that stink from the abattoir down the road, love? Dreadful! You could taste it in your tea sometimes. I can imagine. We had a meat processing plant near Birmingham when I was a kid. You got used to it, eventually, but the initial smell… pretty overpowering. Science really advanced that industry, didn’t it? Made it a lot less… visceral. Speaking of science, David, did you explain that bit about quantum physics to Thomas last week? He was looking awfully puzzled. I tried! It's tricky, even for adults.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of it is staggering. I’ve been marking essays for this introductory academic literacy module for the last three weeks, and I’m starting to feel like I’m losing the will to live. It’s not necessarily  bad  writing, you understand. It's just…lacking. Fundamentally lacking in the skills we're aiming to build. Tell me about it. I’ve seen a similar trend with my Year 12s, though they have the excuse of being, well, younger. What’s the common failing, then? Beyond the general ‘lacking,’ of course. It’s definitely a lack of clear argumentation, mostly. Lots of description, lots of anecdotal evidence - perfectly valid, but not structured effectively to support a thesis. And the referencing is…creative. Some of them are inventing sources, I swear. Or using sources that are barely relevant. Inventing sources? Good heavens. That's horrifying! It’s a worry, isn’t it? I mean, you'd think a higher education environment would attract students with a certain level of academic rigor. You’d think. But then, I had a student argue that Keynesian economics was fundamentally flawed because his Nan found it confusing. I marked it reasonably, I think, but it just...stuck with me. Oh, I know that feeling. The anecdotal evidence over demonstrable fact. It’s particularly prevalent with students from non-traditional backgrounds, I think. They've learned to value lived experience, which is brilliant, don't get me wrong, but it doesn’t necessarily translate to academic discourse. It needs to be harnessed and directed. Exactly! It's about  how  you use it. It’s not about discarding it entirely, but about supporting it with evidence and logical reasoning. I used to think postgraduate study would automatically equip people with these skills, but clearly, that’s not always the case. Before all this academia, I was in recruitment, remember? Oh yes, you mentioned it briefly. Quite a change of pace from marking essays about citation styles, I imagine. Utterly. You'd be amazed at the writing skills you need in recruitment. Crafting compelling job descriptions, writing persuasive proposals… It's all about clearly communicating a message, and framing it in a way that gets results. We’d have training sessions on persuasive language, writing for specific audiences… Actually, some of the academic writing principles we’re trying to instill now are surprisingly similar.

Speaker_1 chuckled, adjusting a pile of books on the table. "Dead on! You've been pigeon-ed before, eh? It's the worst. They’ve got this smug look about ‘em, like they know something you don’t. I swear, the ones in Manchester are bolder than anywhere else. Once one tried to steal a chip right out of my hand!" He grinned, leaning back in his chair. “Manchester pigeons  are  something special,” she agreed, pulling a textbook closer. “They’re practically fearless. Though, I think Bradford pigeons have a reputation too, don't they, Amelia?” She glanced at Speaker_1. "Oh, yeah, Bradford's got 'em in spades. Proper cheeky, they are. They'll land on your head without a second thought, especially if you're carrying a sandwich. Anyway," she added, noticing Speaker_4 hadn’t spoken. “You haven’t said much. Are you alright?” “Oh, sorry! I was just…processing. You all seem to have very vivid encounters with pigeons. Mine are generally more of the ‘fly away and ignore me’ variety.” She smiled, a hint of shyness in her voice. “I’m Priya, by the way. I’m studying Law, which, ironically, doesn’t seem to cover avian harassment.” "Priya, right? Nice to meet you. I'm Liam. Sales assistant at Sports Direct, mostly wrestling teenagers and dealing with football shirt emergencies. Not as glamorous as law, I’ll admit.” He gave a self-deprecating laugh. “Ellie here,” she announced, nodding towards Speaker_1. "We’re both doing History. It’s… interesting. Lots of dates and dead people. Not quite birds, but equally prone to staring blankly from portraits.” "Trying to keep things lively, I am. Ellie's right – history's grim, but fascinating. I'm Amelia, and I'm doing a Masters in Victorian Literature. Basically, I read a  lot  of sad books about people wearing itchy clothes.” “Victorian Literature! That sounds amazing. I've always loved the Brontës. The bleakness, the passionate turmoil… it's captivating.” She paused. “So, Sports Direct? What’s the most ridiculous thing you’ve ever sold to someone?” “Oh, where do I even  begin ? Probably a full track suit…with matching gloves  and  hat… to a guy who was clearly trying to blend in with a rugby team that wasn’t there. He insisted he was going ‘undercover’. Didn't ask any questions. Honestly, some people.” He shook his head with amusement. “What about you, Amelia?

Nah, not yet love. Been a bit busy with the conference, as you know. Work's been absolutely mental. Trying to wrangle about a hundred tech people who all think they're coding geniuses. It's a joy, it really is. But film? I need a right proper sit down and a massive tub of popcorn for that. How was it? It was  stunning . Visually, it's breathtaking. The world-building is faultless. Paul’s journey feels really earned, and the score… honestly, the score made the hairs on the back of my neck stand up. You absolutely have to see it on the big screen. It's not something you want to watch on a laptop. Right, you've convinced me. Put it on the list. Speaking o' lists, remember Grandad kept going on about wanting to go to a vintage computer fair? Oh God, yes! He was showing me pictures of Commodore 64s again last week. He’s obsessed. Did you manage to find one in decent condition for him? I had a good look.
